statement_text: A em cut of a graph G is a partition of its nodes into two disjoint subsets N_1 and N_2 . title: Treewidth
statement_text: A em tree decomposition of a graph G is a tree T and a collection of bags {X_i | i is a node of T } . Each bag X_i is a subset of nodes of G , and we require: (i) every node of G is contained in at least one bag X_i ; (ii) for each edge of G , some bag X_i contains both its endpoints; and (iii) for all nodes i,j,k of T , if j lies on the unique path from i to k in T , then X_i ∩ X_k ⊆ X_j . The width of a tree decomposition is defined as max |X_i| - 1 , and the em treewidth of G is the minimum width over all tree decompositions.

title: Dynamic graph
statement_text: A dynamic graph G is a sequence of graphs G = (G_i)_ 0 ≤ i ≤ k that share a common set of nodes V . The set of edges of the graph G_i (for 0 ≤ i ≤ k ) is denoted by E (G_i) . The number of nodes of G is n = | V | , and the initial number of edges of G is m = | E (G_0) | . The set of edges ever contained in G up to time t (where 0 ≤ t ≤ k ) is E_t ( G ) = ∪ _ 0 ≤ i ≤ t E (G_i) . A dynamic weighted graph H is a sequence of weighted graphs H = (H_i, w_i)_ 0 ≤ i ≤ k that share a common set of nodes V . For 0 ≤ i ≤ k and every edge (u, v) ∈ E (H_i) , the weight of (u, v) is given by w_i (u, v) .

title: Updates
statement_text: For a dynamic graph G = (G_i)_ 0 ≤ i ≤ k we say for an edge (u, v) that (u, v) is deleted at time t if (u, v) is contained in G_ t-1 but not in G_t ; (u, v) is inserted at time t if (u, v) contained in G_t but not in G_ t-1 . For a dynamic weighted graph H = (H_i, w_i)_ 0 ≤ i ≤ k , we additionally say for an edge (u, v) that the weight of (u, v) is increased at time t if w_t (u, v) > w_ t-1 (u, v) (and (u, v) is contained in both G_ t-1 and G_t ); the weight of (u, v) is decreased at time t if w_t (u, v) < w_ t-1 (u, v) (and (u, v) is contained in both G_ t-1 and G_t ). Every deletion, insertion, weight increase, or weight decrease is called an update . The total number of updates up to time t of a dynamic (weighted) graph G is denoted by φ_t ( G ) .

title: Decremental graph
statement_text: A decremental graph G is a dynamic graph G = (G_i)_ 0 ≤ i ≤ k such that for every 1 ≤ i ≤ k there is exactly one edge deletion at time i . Note that G_i is the graph after the i -th edge deletion.

title: Distance
statement_text: The distance of a node x to a node y in a graph G is denoted by d_G (x, y) . If x and y are not connected in G , we set d_G (x, y) = ∞ . In a weighted graph (H, w) the distance of x to y is denoted by d_ H, w (x, y) .

label: def:approximate_APSP
statement_text: An (α, β) -approximate decremental all-pairs shortest paths (APSP) data structure for a decremental graph G = (G_i)_ 0 ≤ i ≤ k maintains, for all nodes x and y and all 0 ≤ i ≤ k , an estimate δ_i (x, y) of the distance between x and y in G_i . After the i -th edge deletion (where 0 ≤ i ≤ k ), it provides the following operations: Delete u , v : Delete the edge (u, v) from G_i . Distance x , y : Return an estimate δ_i (x, y) of the distance between x and r in G_i such that d_ G_i (x, y) ≤ δ_i (x, y) ≤ α d_ G_i (x, y) + β . The total update time is the total time needed for performing all k delete operations and the initialization, and the query time is the worst-case time needed to answer a single distance query. The data structure is exact if α = 1 and β = 0 .

label: def:approximate_SSSP
statement_text: An (α, β) -approximate decremental single-source shortest paths (SSSP) data structure with source (or: root) node r and distance range parameter R^ d for a decremental graph G = (G_i)_ 0 ≤ i ≤ k maintains, for every node x and all 0 ≤ i ≤ k , an estimate δ_i (x, r) ∈ { 0, 1, ... , lfloor α R^ d + β rfloor , ∞ } of the distance between x and r in G_i . After the i -th edge deletion (where 0 ≤ i ≤ k ), it provides the following operations: Delete u , v : Delete the edge (u, v) from G_i and return the set of all nodes x such that δ_i (x, r) ≤ α R^ d + β and δ_ i+1 (x, r) > α R^ d + β . Distance x : Return an estimate δ_i (x, r) of the distance between x and r in G_i such that δ_i (x, r) ≥ d_ G_i (x, r) , and if d_ G_i (x, r) ≤ R^ d , then also δ_i (x, r) ≤ α d_ G_i (x, r) + β . The total update time is the total time needed for performing all k delete operations and the initialization, and the query time is the worst-case time needed to answer a single distance query. The data structure is exact if α = 1 and β = 0 .

title: Center cover data structure
statement_text: A center cover data structure with cover range parameter R^ c and distance range parameter R^ d for a decremental graph G = (G_i)_ 0 ≤ i ≤ k maintains, for every 0 ≤ i ≤ k , a set of centers C_i = { 1, 2, ... , l } and a set of nodes U_i = { c_i^1, c_i^2, ... , c_i^l } such that U_i is a center cover of G_i with parameter R^ c . For every center j ∈ C_i and every 0 ≤ i ≤ k , we call c_i^j ∈ U_i the location of center j in G_i , and for every node x we say that x is covered by j if x is covered by c^j_i in G_i . After the i -th edge deletion (where 0 ≤ i ≤ k ), the data structure provides the following operations: Delete u , v : Delete the edge (u, v) from G_i . Distance j , x : Return the distance d_ G_i (c_i^j, x) between the location c_i^j of center j and the node x , provided that d_ G_i (c_i^j, x) ≤ R^ d . If d_ G_i (c_i^j, x) > R^ d , then return ∞ . FindCenter x : If x is in a connected component of size at least R^ c in G_i , return a center j (with location c_i^j ) such that d_ G_i (x, c_i^j) ≤ R^ c . If x is in a connected component of size less than R^ c in G_i , then either return bot or return a center j (with location c_i^j ) such that d_ G_i (x, c_i^j) ≤ R^ c . The total update time is the total time needed for performing all k delete operations and the initialization. statement_text: Let H = (H_i, w_i)_ 0 ≤ i ≤ k be a dynamic weighted graph. We say that a path π = le v_0, v_1, ... , v_ell rangle is em persevering up to time t (where t ≤ k ) if for all 0 ≤ i ≤ ell -1 , \[ ∀ 0 ≤ j ≤ t: (v_i,v_ i+1 ) ∈ E(H_j) and ∀ 0 ≤ j<t: w_j(v_i,v_ i+1 ) ≤ w_ j+1 (v_i,v_ i+1 ). \] In other words, edges in π always exist in H up to time t and their weights never decrease.

title: Locally persevering emulator
statement_text: Consider parameters α ≥ 1 , β ≥ 0 and τ ≥ 1 , a dynamic graph G = (G_i)_ 0 ≤ i ≤ k , and a dynamic weighted graph H = (H_i, w_i)_ 0 ≤ i ≤ k . For every i ≤ k , we say that a path π in G_i is em contained in (H_i, w_i) if every edge of π is contained in H_i and has weight 1 . We say that H is an em ( α , β , τ )-locally persevering emulator of G if for all nodes x and y we have d_ G_i (x, y) ≤ d_ H_i, w_i (x, y) for all 0 ≤ i ≤ k , and there are t_1 and t_2 with 0 ≤ t_1 < t_2 ≤ k+1 such that the following hold: There is a path π from x to y in H that is persevering (at least) up to time t_1 and satisfies w_t (π) ≤ α d_ G_t (x, y) + β . For every t_1 < i ≤ t_2 , a shortest path from x to y in G_i is contained in (H_i, w_i) . For every i ≥ t_2 , d_ G_i (x, y) > τ .

Equivalently, there is a choice of t so that the j -th qubit of C lvert t rangle is left in a standard basis state.

paper_title: Zero-knowledge proof systems for QMA

Completeness . For all x ∈ A_ yes , there exists a p( lvert x rvert ) -qubit state ρ such that Pr (V_x(ρ) = 1) ≥ α . Soundness . For all x ∈ A_ no , and every p( lvert x rvert ) -qubit state ρ , it holds that Pr (V_x(ρ) = 1) ≤ β .

statement_text: Suppose that S ⊆ {0,1}^ ast is an infinite set of binary strings, r is a polynomially bounded function, and ρ_x and ξ_x are states on r( lvert x rvert ) qubits for each x ∈ S . statement_text: An interactive proof system (P, V) for a promise problem A is quantum computational zero-knowledge if, for every polynomial-time generated quantum verifier V' , there exists a polynomial-time generated quantum simulator S that satisfies the following requirements. parindent The verifier V' and simulator S agree on the polynomially bounded functions q and r that specify the number of auxiliary input qubits and output qubits, respectively. Let Φ_x be the channel that results from the interaction between V' and P on input x , and let Ψ_x be the channel induced by the simulator S on input x , both as described above. Then the collections {Φ_x: x ∈ A_ yes } and {Ψ_x: x ∈ A_ yes } are quantum computationally indistinguishable.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: thm:main
statement_text: For any constant integer k ≥ 2 and any odd integer p ≥ 1 or p = ∞ , there is an efficient reduction from k -SAT with n variables and m clauses to CVP _p (or SVP _ ∞ ) on a lattice of rank n (with ambient dimension n + O(m) ). In particular, there is no 2^ (1-ε) n -time algorithm for CVP _p for any odd integer p ≥ 1 or p = ∞ (or SVP _ ∞ ) and any constant ε > 0 unless SETH is false.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: thm:all_p_intro
statement_text: For any constant integer k ≥ 2 , there is an efficient reduction from k -SAT with n variables and m clauses to CVP _p on a lattice of rank n (with ambient dimension n + O(m) ) for any p ≥ 1 such that p is an odd integer or p = ∞ ; p ∉ S_k , where S_k is some finite set (containing all even integers p ≤ k-1 ); or p = p_0 + δ(n) for any p_0 ≥ 1 and any δ(n) ≠ 0 that converges to zero as n → ∞ . In particular, if SETH holds then for any constant ε > 0 , there is no 2^ (1-ε)n -time algorithm for CVP _p for any p ≥ 1 such that p is an odd integer or p = ∞ ; p ∉ S_k for some sufficiently large k (depending on ε ); or p = p_0 + δ(n) .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
statement_text: There is an efficient reduction from approximating Max- 2 -SAT with n variables and m clauses to within a constant factor to approximating CVP _p to within a constant factor on a lattice of rank n (with ambient dimension n + O(m) ) for any finite p ≥ 1 .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: thm:cvpp_intro
statement_text: For any 1 ≤ p < ∞ , there is no 2^ o( sqrt n ) -time algorithm for CVPP unless there is a (non-uniform) 2^ o(n) -time algorithm for Max- 2 -SAT. In particular, no such algorithm exists unless (non-uniform) ETH fails.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: thm:maxcut
statement_text: For any 1 ≤ p < ∞ , there is an efficient reduction from Max- 2 -SAT with n variables to CVP _p on a lattice of rank n (and dimension n +m , where m is the number of clauses). In particular, for any constant c > 0 , there is no ( poly (n) · 2^ c n ) -time algorithm for CVP _p unless there is a 2^ cn -time algorithm for Max- 2 -SAT, and there is no 2^ o(n) -time algorithm for CVP _p unless ETH fails.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
statement_text: For any γ ≥ 1 and 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ , the γ -approximate Shortest Vector Problem with respect to the ell _p norm ( γ - SVP _p ) is the promise problem defined as follows. Given a lattice L (specified by a basis B ∈ R ^ d × n ) and a number r > 0 , distinguish between a `YES' instance where there exists a non-zero vector v ∈ L such that | v |_p ≤ r , and a `NO' instance where | v |_p > γ r for all non-zero v ∈ L .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
statement_text: For any γ ≥ 1 and 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ , the γ -approximate Closest Vector Problem with respect to the ell _p norm ( γ - CVP _p ) is the promise problem defined as follows. Given a lattice L (specified by a basis B ∈ R ^ d × n ), a target vector t ∈ R ^d , and a number r > 0 , distinguish between a `YES' instance where dist _p( L , t ) ≤ r , and a `NO' instance where dist _p( L , t ) > γ r .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
statement_text: The Closest Vector Problem with Preprocessing with respect to the ell _p norm ( CVPP _p) is the problem of finding a preprocessing function P and an algorithm Q which work as follows. Given a lattice L (specified by a basis B ∈ R ^ d × n ), P outputs a new description of L . Given P( L ) , a target vector t ∈ R ^d , and a number r > 0 , Q decides whether dist _p( L , t ) ≤ r .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
statement_text: Given a k -SAT formula Φ and constants 0 ≤ δ < ε ≤ 1 , the (δ, ε) -Gap- k -SAT problem is the promise problem defined as follows. The goal is to distinguish between a `YES' instance in which rm val (Φ) ≥ ε , and a `NO' instance in which rm val (Φ) < δ .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
statement_text: Given a k -SAT formula Φ with clauses C = {C_1, ... , C_m} , a clause weight function w: C → Z ^+ , and a weight threshold W , the Weighted Max- k -SAT problem is to decide whether there exists an assignment a to the variables of Φ such that Σ _ rm C_i is sat. by a w(C_i) ≥ W .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
statement_text: Given an undirected graph G = (V, E) , an edge weight function w: E → Z ^+ , and a weight threshold W , the Weighted Max-CUT problem is defined as follows. The goal is to decide whether V can be partitioned into sets V_1 and V_2 such that Σ _ e_ ij ∈ E : v_i ∈ V_1, v_j ∈ V_2 w(e_ ij ) ≥ W .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: def:eth
statement_text: The Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH) is the hypothesis defined as follows. For every k ≥ 3 there exists a constant ε > 0 such that no algorithm solves k -SAT formulas with n variables in 2^ ε n -time. In particular, there is no 2^ o(n) -time algorithm for 3-SAT.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: def:seth
statement_text: The Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH) is the hypothesis defined as follows. For every constant ε > 0 there exists k such that no algorithm solves k -SAT formulas with n variables in 2^ (1 - ε) n -time.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: prop:sparsification
title: Sparsification Lemma,
statement_text: For every k ∈ Z ^+ and ε > 0 there exists a constant c = c(k, ε) such that any k -SAT formula Φ with n variables can be expressed as Φ = ∨ _ i=1 ^r Ψ_ i where r ≤ 2^ ε n and each Ψ_i is a k -SAT formula with at most cn clauses. Moreover, this disjunction can be computed in 2^ ε n -time.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: def:gap-eth
statement_text: The (randomized) Gap-Exponential Time Hypothesis ((randomized) Gap-ETH) is the hypothesis that there exist constants δ < 1 and ε > 0 such that no (randomized) algorithm solves (δ, 1) -Gap- 3 -SAT instances with n variables in 2^ ε n -time.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: prop:gap-sat-sparsification
title: Sparsification for Gap-SAT
statement_text: For any 0 < δ < δ' < 1 , there is a polynomial-time randomized reduction from a (δ, 1) -Gap- k -SAT instance Φ with n variables and m clauses to a (δ', 1) -Gap- k -SAT instance Φ' with n variables and O(n) clauses.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: prop:gap3sat-to-gap2sat
statement_text: For every 0 ≤ δ < ε ≤ 1 , there is a polynomial-time reduction from every instance of (δ, ε) -Gap- 3 -SAT with n variables and m clauses to an instance of ((6 + δ)/10, (6 + ε)/10) -Gap- 2 -SAT with n + m variables and 10m clauses.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: def:piped
statement_text: For any 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ and integer k ≥ 2 , we say that V ∈ R ^ d^* × k and t ^* ∈ R ^ d^* define a (p, k) - isolating parallelepiped if | t |_p > 1 and |V x - t ^*|_p = 1 for all x ∈ {0, 1}^k \ { 0 _k} .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: thm:isolating_implies_reduction
statement_text: If there exists a computable (p, k) -isolating parallelepiped for some p = p(n) ∈ [1, ∞ ) and integer k ≥ 2 , then there exists a polynomial-time reduction from any (weighted-)Max- k -SAT instance with n variables to a CVP _p instance of rank n .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: cor:seth-hardness
statement_text: For any efficiently computable p = p(n) ∈ [1, ∞ ) if there exists a computable (p, k) -isolating parallelepiped for infinitely many k ∈ Z ^+ , then, for every constant ε > 0 there is no 2^ (1 - ε)n -time algorithm for CVP _p assuming W-Max-SAT-SETH. In particular there is no 2^ (1 - ε)n -time algorithm for CVP _p assuming SETH.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: cor:cvp1-seth-hardness
statement_text: For every constant ε > 0 there is no 2^ (1 - ε)n -time algorithm for CVP _1 assuming W-Max-SAT-SETH, and in particular there is no 2^ (1 - ε)n -time algorithm for CVP _1 assuming SETH.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: lem:pmone

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: prop:invertible_suffices
statement_text: There is an efficient algorithm that takes as input any p ≥ 1 , an integer k ≥ 2 , and t^* ∈ R such that det (M_k(p,t^*)) ≠ 0 , where M_k(p,t^*) is defined as in Eq. and outputs V ∈ R ^ 2^k × k and t ^* ∈ R ^ 2^k that define a (p,k) -isolating parallelepiped.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: lem:top_coeff
statement_text: For an integer k ≥ 1 and an odd integer p ≥ 1 , the function t^* mapsto det (M_k(p,t^*)) , where M_k(p,t^*) is defined as in Eq. , is a polynomial of degree at most (k+1)p when restricted to the interval t^* ∈ [-k,-k+2] . paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: cor:non-zero_t

label: cor:no-2-iso-pipeds
statement_text: There is no (2,k) -isolating parallelepiped for any integer k ≥ 3 .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: lem:sum_of_exp
statement_text: For any t^* ∈ R , integer k ≥ 1 , and p ≥ 1 , let f_ k,t^* (p) := det (M_k(p,t^*)) , where M_k(p,t^*) is as defined in Eq. . Then, for fixed k,t^* , f_ k,t^* (p) is a Dirichlet polynomial. I.e., there are some real numbers b_0, ... , b_ r , c_0, ... , c_ r ∈ R (depending on t^* and k ) such that f_ k,t^* (p) = Σ _ i=0 ^ r b_i exp (c_i p) for some finite r .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: cor:non-zero_t_p
statement_text: There is an efficient algorithm that takes as input k ≥ 2 and any p ≥ 1 and either fails or outputs V ∈ R ^ 2^k × k and t ^* ∈ R ^ 2^k that define a (p,k) -isolating parallelepiped. Furthermore, for any fixed k ≥ 2 , the algorithm only fails for finitely many choices of p ≥ 1 .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: thm:most_p
statement_text: There is an efficient algorithm that takes as input an integer k ≥ 2 and any p ≥ 1 and either fails or outputs V ∈ R ^ 2^k × k and t ^* ∈ R ^ 2^k that define a (p,k) -isolating parallelepiped. Furthermore, for any fixed k ≥ 2 , the algorithm only fails on finitely many values of p ≥ 1 . As we observed in Section , the set of failure points necessarily includes all even integers p ≤ k-1 .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: lem:non-zero_t_p_plus_eps
statement_text: There is an efficient algorithm that takes as input any p_0 ≥ 1 and an integer k ≥ 2 and outputs a value t^* such that f_ k,t^* (p_0 + δ) and f_ k,t^* (p_0 - δ) are non-zero for sufficiently small δ > 0 , where f_ k,t^* (p) is as defined in Eq. .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: thm:piped_p_plus_eps
statement_text: For any efficiently computable δ(n) ≠ 0 that converges to zero as n → ∞ and p_0 ≥ 1 , there is an efficient algorithm that takes as input an integer k ≥ 2 and sufficiently large positive integer n and outputs a matrix V ∈ R ^ 2^k × k and vector t ^* ∈ R ^ 2^k that define a (p_0 + δ(n),k) -isolating parallelepiped.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: thm:gap2sat-to-gamma-cvpp
statement_text: For every 0 ≤ δ < ε ≤ 1 and every p ∈ [1, ∞ ) , there is a polynomial-time reduction from any (δ, ε) -Gap- 2 -SAT instance with n variables to an instance of γ - CVP _p of rank n , where \[ γ := (frac δ + (1 - δ) · 3^p ε + (1 - ε) · 3^p )^ 1/p > 1 . \] In particular, when ε = 1 , the corresponding approximation factor is (δ + (1-δ) · 3^p)^ 1/p .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: cor:gap-eth-hardness-of-approx
statement_text: For every p ∈ [1, ∞ ) and 0 < δ < δ' < 1 , there is no 2^ o(n) -time algorithm for γ - CVP _p with \[ γ := ( frac 6 + δ' + (4 - δ') · 3^p 7 + 3^ p+1 )^ 1/p > 1 \] unless randomized Gap-ETH (with respect to (δ, 1) -Gap- 3 -SAT) fails.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: thm:cvp1-hardness-of-approx
statement_text: For every 0 ≤ δ < ε ≤ 1 , there is a polynomial-time reduction from any (δ, ε) -Gap- k -SAT instance with n variables to an instance of γ - CVP _1 of rank n , where \[ γ := (frac δ · (k - 1) + (1 - δ) · (k + 1) ε · (k - 1) + (1 - ε) · (k + 1) ) > 1. \]

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: lem:cvpp
statement_text: For every p ∈ [1, ∞ ) , there is a pair of polynomial-time algorithms (P, Q) (in analogy to the definition of CVPP ) that behave as follows. On input an integer n ≥ 1 , P outputs a basis B_n ∈ R ^ d × N of a rank N lattice L _n ⊂ R ^d , where d = d(n) = O(n^2) and N = N(n) = O(n^2) . On input a Max- 2 -SAT instance with n variables, Q outputs a target vector t ∈ R ^d and a distance bound r ≥ 0 such that dist _p( t , L _n) ≤ r if and only if the input is a `YES' instance.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: thm:max-k-sat-to-high-rank
statement_text: For every p = p(n) ∈ [1, ∞ ) and k ≥ 2 there is a polynomial-time reduction from any (Weighted-)Max- k -SAT instance with n variables and m clauses to a CVP _p instance of rank n + (k - 2)m .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: cor:eth-hardness
statement_text: For every p ∈ [1, ∞ ) there is no 2^ o(n) -time algorithm for CVP _p assuming ETH.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: cor:max-cut-hardness
statement_text: If there exists a 2^ (ω/3 - ε) n -time (resp. 2^ (1 - ε) n -time and polynomial space) algorithm for CVP _p for any p ∈ [1, ∞ ) and for any constant ε > 0 , then there exists a 2^ (ω/3 - ε) n -time (resp. 2^ (1 - ε) n -time and polynomial space) algorithm for (Weighted-)Max-2-SAT and (Weighted-)Max-Cut.

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: thm:k-sat-to-cvp-infinity
statement_text: There is a polynomial-time reduction from a k -SAT instance with n variables to a CVP _ ∞ instance of rank n .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: lem:k-sat-to-svp-infinity
statement_text: There is a polynomial-time reduction from a k -SAT instance with n variables to an SVP _ ∞ instance of rank n + 1 .

paper_title: On the Quantitative Hardness of CVP
label: cor:infinity!
statement_text: For any constant ε > 0 there is no 2^ (1-ε)n -time algorithm for SVP _ ∞ or CVP _ ∞ assuming SETH, and there is no 2^ o(n) -time algorithm for SVP _ ∞ or CVP _ ∞ assuming ETH.

statement_text: Can one maintain an (1+ε) -approximate maximum matching dynamically, with n^ o(1) amortized update time?

paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
label: thm:main
title: Main theorem
statement_text: theorem MainTheorem There is a poly (n, b, frac 1ε) time deterministic algorithm (cref alg:scaling ) that, given a tensor X ∈ V with integer coordinates of bit size bounded by b , either identifies that X is in the null cone or outputs a ``scaling'' Y ∈ G · X such that ds (Y)<ε .

paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
label: def:quantum marginal
title: Quantum marginal
statement_text: Given a matrix ρ acting on H_S ⊗ H_T , where H_S and H_T are Hilbert spaces of dimensions n_S and n_T , respectively (e.g., H_S = C ^ n_S and H_T = C ^ n_T ). Then there is a unique matrix ρ_S acting on H_S , called the quantum marginal (or reduced density matrix) of S , such that tr [ ( M_S ⊗ I_T ) ρ ] = tr [ M_S ρ_S ] for every M_S acting on H_S .

paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
title: Scaling
statement_text: A tensor Y ∈ Ten (n_0,n_1, ... , n_d) is called a ( tensor ) scaling of X ∈ Ten (n_0,n_1 ... ,n_d) if Y ∈ G · X .

paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
label: thm:kempf ness
title: Duality, special case of
statement_text: theorem KempfNess A tensor X ∈ Ten (n_0, ... ,n_d) is not in the null cone if and only if there exists Y ∈ overline G · X such that the quantum marginals ρ_1, ... ,ρ_d of ρ=YY^dagger /Y^dagger Y of the last d tensor factors are given by ρ_i = I_ n_i / n_i .

paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
title: d -stochastic
statement_text: A tensor Y ∈ Ten (n_0, ... , n_d) is called d -stochastic if the quantum marginals of ρ=YY^dagger /Y^dagger Y of the last d tensor factors are given by ρ_i = I_ n_i / n_i for i ∈ [d] .

paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
label: def:ds
title: Distance to d -stochasticity
statement_text: Let Y ∈ Ten (n_0,n_1, ... ,n_d) be a tensor and ρ=YY^dagger /Y^dagger Y , with quantum marginals ρ_1, ... ,ρ_ d on the last d systems. Then we define the distance to d -stochasticity ds (Y) as the (squared) distance between the marginals and d -stochastic marginals, \[ ds (Y) := Σ _ i=1 ^d norm ρ_i - frac I_ n_i n_i _F^2, \] where lVert M rVert _F := (tr M^dagger M)^ 1/2 is the Frobenius norm. Following cref eq:dual-alt-min , we further define the minimal distance to d -stochasticity as \[ dds (X) := inf _ A ∈ G ds (A · X). \]

paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory

title: Deficiency

paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
label: def:ins
title: Deficiency, instability
statement_text: Given a set S ⊆ [n_1] × ... × [n_d] , we define its deficiency as def (S) & := max _ (a_ i,j ) ∈ Γ frac min _ (j_1, ... ,j_ d ) ∈ S ( Σ _ i=1 ^ d a_ i,j_i ) sqrt Σ _ i=1 ^ d Σ _ j=1 ^ n_i a_ i,j ^2 . where we recall that the set Γ was defined in cref eq:abelian 1PSG . paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
title: SLOCC entanglement distillation
statement_text: There is a poly (n, b, frac 1ε) time deterministic algorithm that, given the classical description of a pure quantum state X ∈ Ten (n_1, ... ,n_d) , with integer coordinates of bit size bounded by b , either identifies that X cannot be transformed by SLOCC into a locally maximally entangled state or outputs an SLOCC operation g ∈ G such that ds (g · X)<ε . paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
title: Slice rank
statement_text: A tensor X ∈ Ten _m^d is said to have slice rank-one if it decomposes as the tensor product of a vector and a lower-order tensor, i.e., if there exists a k ∈ [d] , a vector V ∈ C ^m , and a tensor Y ∈ Ten _m^ d-1 such that \[ X_ j_1, ... ,j_d = V_ j_k · Y_ j_1, ... ,j_ k-1 ,j_ k+1 , ... ,j_d . \] The slice rank of a tensor X , denoted slice-rank (X) , is defined as the minimum number r of slice rank-one tensors X_1, ... ,X_r such that X= Σ _ i=1 ^r X_i .

paper_title: (Gap/S)ETH Hardness of SVP
statement_text: For any 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ and any γ ≥ 1 , the γ -approximate Shortest Vector Problem in the ell _p norm ( SVP _ p, γ ) is the promise problem defined as follows. paper_title: (Gap/S)ETH Hardness of SVP
statement_text: For any 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ and any γ ≥ 1 , the γ -approximate Closest Vector Problem in the ell _p norm ( CVP _ p, γ ) is the promise problem defined as follows. paper_title: (Gap/S)ETH Hardness of SVP
label: thm:embedding
statement_text: For any ε ∈ (0,1) , 1 ≤ p ≤ 2 , and any positive integers n and m with m ≥ n/ε^2 , there exists a linear map f : R ^n → R ^ m such that for any x ∈ R ^n , \[ (1-ε)| x |_2 ≤ |f( x )|_p ≤ (1+ε) | x |_2 . \]

paper_title: (Gap/S)ETH Hardness of SVP
label: cor:embedding_reduction

paper_title: (Gap/S)ETH Hardness of SVP

paper_title: (Gap/S)ETH Hardness of SVP
statement_text: For any k ≥ 2 , the decision problem k -SAT is defined as follows. The input is a k -SAT formula. It is a YES instance if there exists an assignment to the variables that makes the formula evaluate to true and a NO instance otherwise.

paper_title: (Gap/S)ETH Hardness of SVP
title: SETH
statement_text: The (randomized) Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis ((randomized) SETH) asserts that, for every constant ε > 0 , there exists a constant k ≥ 3 such that there is no 2^ (1-ε)n -time (randomized) algorithm for k -SAT formulas with n variables.

statement_text: For η ∈ (0,1) and k ≥ 2 , the promise problem Gap- k - SAT _η is defines as follows. The input is a k -SAT formula with m clauses. paper_title: (Gap/S)ETH Hardness of SVP

statement_text: The (randomized) Gap-Exponential Time Hypothesis ((randomized) Gap-ETH) asserts that there exists a constant η ∈ (0,1) such that there is no (randomized) 2^ o(n) -time algorithm for Gap- 3 - SAT _η over n variables. title: When a up P \ machine querying a up BQP \ oracle is not a up P ^ up BQP machine
statement_text: The proof of the Cleaning Lemma uses a up P ^ up Precise - up BQP machine. Let us highlight a subtle reason why using a weaker up BQP oracle instead might be difficult (indeed, in Section we show that the task we use the up Precise - up BQP oracle for is up PP -complete). Let M denote the trivially up BQP -complete problem of determining whether a given polynomial-sized quantum circuit Q accepts with probability at least 2/3 , or accepts with probability at most 1/3 , with the promise that one of the two is the case. Now consider the following polynomial time computation, Π , which is given access to an oracle O_M for M : Π inputs the Hadamard gate H into O_M and outputs O_M 's answer. Does it hold that Π ∈ up P ^ up BQP ? No. Since H violates the promise of BQP, i.e. measuring the output of H yields 0 or 1 with equal probability, the oracle O_M can answer 0 or 1 arbitrarily, and so the output of Π is not well-defined. Having a well-defined output, however, is required for a up P ^ O_K computation, where K is any promise class .

Thus le Grangle _ F precisely encodes this multiplication. We stress that in the notation le Grangle _ F the parameter G determines the support and the parameter F denotes over which field we consider the tensor. Even though all coefficients of le Grangle _ F are 0 or 1, the choice of base field F determines what linear maps are allowed in the restriction preorder ≥ and thus the notion of equivalence and the notion of isomorphism. Crucially, for the monomial restriction preorder ≥ _ M applied to tensors with coefficients that are only 0 or 1, the choice of base field does not make a difference. We consider the structure tensor le Z /3 Z rangle _ F = e_ 0,0,0 + e_ 0,1,1 + e_ 1,0,1 + e_ 2,0,2 + e_ 0,2,2 + e_ 1,1,2 + e_ 1,2,0 + e_ 2,1,0 + e_ 2,2,1 . In general, for any finite abelian group A , the structure tensor le Arangle _ C is isomorphic to the diagonal tensor le|A|rangle , using the Fourier transform on A to diagonalize the multiplication (see, e.g., or for a discussion of this). In fact, for general F , we have underaccent wtilde R (le Z /3 Z rangle _ F ) = 3 because there is a monomial degeneration from the restricted polynomial multiplication tensor to le Z /3 Z rangle _ F , see . It follows for any field F that i _ M (le Z /3 Z rangle _ F ) = 1.08.. and that le Z /3 Z rangle _ F is monomially irreversible.

An alignment can be represented as a bipartite graph, where the nodes are t_1, t_2, ... , t_ d_1 and s_1, s_2, ... , s_ d_2 respectively, and two nodes s_i, t_j are connected with an edge iff f(i) = j . Each node has at most one outgoing edge and the edges do not cross. (See Fig. .) The cost of an alignment is defined to be equal to the number of nodes that do not have outgoing edges plus the number of edges that connect s_i, t_j such that s_i ≠ t_j . Then, In the context of parity functions, there is a PRG that ε -fools sf FORMULA [s] ∘ XOR of seed length ell = O ( sqrt s · log (s) · log (1/ε) + log (n) ). In the context of two-party randomized communication complexity, there is a PRG that ε -fools sf FORMULA [s] ∘ G of seed length ell = n/2+O ( sqrt s · (R^ (2) _ ε/(6s) ( G )+ log (s) ) · log (1/ε) ). paper_title: Algorithms and Lower Bounds for de Morgan Formulas of Low-Communication Leaf Gates
statement_text: An n -variate de Morgan formula is a directed rooted tree; its non-leaf vertices (henceforth, internal gates ) take labels from { rm AND , rm OR , rm NOT }= { ∧ , ∨ , ¬ } and its leaves (henceforth, variable gates ) take labels from the set of variables {x_1, ... ,x_n } . Each internal gate has bounded in-degree (henceforth, fan-in ); the rm NOT gate in particular has fan-in 1 and every variable gate has fan-in 0 . The size of a de Morgan formula is the number of its leaf gates.

paper_title: Algorithms and Lower Bounds for de Morgan Formulas of Low-Communication Leaf Gates
title: Point-wise approximation
statement_text: For a Boolean function fcolon {-1,1 }^n → {-1,1 } , we say that the function tilde f colon {-1,1 }^n → R ε -approximates f if for every z ∈ {-1,1 }^n , \[ | f(z)-tilde f (z) | ≤ ε. \]

paper_title: Algorithms and Lower Bounds for de Morgan Formulas of Low-Communication Leaf Gates
label: thm:approx-polynomial

statement_text: Let s>0 be an integer and 0<ε<1 . Any de Morgan formula Fcolon {-1,1 }^n → {-1,1 } of size s has a ε -approximating polynomial of degree d=O( sqrt s · log (1/ε)) . That is, there exists a degree- d polynomial pcolon {-1,1 }^n → R over the reals such that for every z ∈ {-1,1 }^n , \[ | p(z)-F(z) | ≤ ε. \]

paper_title: Algorithms and Lower Bounds for de Morgan Formulas of Low-Communication Leaf Gates
statement_text: Let fcolon {0,1 }^ n → {0,1 } be a Boolean function. The communication matrix of f , namely M_f , is a 2^ n/2 × 2^ n/2 matrix defined by (M_f )_ x,y :=f(x,y) .

paper_title: Algorithms and Lower Bounds for de Morgan Formulas of Low-Communication Leaf Gates
statement_text: A rectangle is a set of the form A × B , for A,B ⊆ {0,1 }^n . A monochromatic rectangle is a rectangle S such that for all pairs (x,y) ∈ S the value f(x,y) is the same.

paper_title: Algorithms and Lower Bounds for de Morgan Formulas of Low-Communication Leaf Gates
statement_text: Let Π be a protocol that computes fcolon {0,1 }^ n → {0,1 } with at most D bits of communication. Then, Π induces a partition of M_f into at most 2^D monochromatic rectangles.

paper_title: Algorithms and Lower Bounds for de Morgan Formulas of Low-Communication Leaf Gates
statement_text: For every transcript z of some communication protocol, the set of inputs (x,y) that generate z is a rectangle.

paper_title: Algorithms and Lower Bounds for de Morgan Formulas of Low-Communication Leaf Gates
title: ``Number-on-forehead'' communication model; informal
statement_text: In the k -party ``number-on-forehead'' communication model, there are k players and k strings x_1, ... ,x_k ∈ {0,1 }^ n/k and player i gets all the strings except for x_i . The players are interested in computing a value f (x_1, ... ,x_k ) , where fcolon {0,1 }^ n → {0,1 } is some fixed function. We denote by D^ (k) (f) the number of bits that must be exchanged by the best possible number on forehead protocol solving f .

paper_title: Algorithms and Lower Bounds for de Morgan Formulas of Low-Communication Leaf Gates
title: ``Number-in-hand'' communication model; informal
statement_text: In the k -party ``number-in-hand'' communication model, there are k players and k strings x_1, ... ,x_k ∈ {0,1 }^ n/k and player i gets only x_i . The players are interested in computing a value f (x_1, ... ,x_k ) , where fcolon {0,1 }^ n → {0,1 } is some fixed function. We denote by D^ (k - NIH ) (f) the number of bits that must be exchanged by the best possible communication protocol.

paper_title: Algorithms and Lower Bounds for de Morgan Formulas of Low-Communication Leaf Gates
title: Pseudorandom generators
statement_text: Let Gcolon {-1,1 }^ ell → {-1,1 }^n be a function, C be a class of Boolean functions, and 0<ε<1 . We say that G is a pseudorandom generator of seed length ell that ε -fools C if, for every function f ∈ C , it is the case that \[ |Exp _ z {-1,1 }^ell [f (G (z ) ) ]- Exp _ x {-1,1 }^n [f (x ) ] | ≤ ε. \]

paper_title: Algorithms and Lower Bounds for de Morgan Formulas of Low-Communication Leaf Gates
label: def:pac
title: PAC learning model
statement_text: Let C be a class of Boolean functions. We say that a randomized algorithm A learns C if, when A is given oracle access to rm EX (f, D ) and inputs 1^n , ε , and δ , the following holds. For every n -variate function f ∈ C , distribution D supported over {0,1 }^n , and real-valued parameters ε > 0 and δ > 0 , A^ rm EX (f, D ) (1^n, ε, δ) outputs with probability at least 1-δ over its internal randomness and the randomness of the example oracle rm EX (f, D ) a description of a hypothesis h: {0,1 }^n → {0,1 } such that Prob _ x D [f (x )=h (x ) ] ≥ 1-ε. The sample complexity of a learning algorithm is the maximum number of random examples from rm EX (f, D ) requested during its execution.

paper_title: Algorithms and Lower Bounds for de Morgan Formulas of Low-Communication Leaf Gates
label: thm:lb-main
statement_text: For any integer k ≥ 2 , s>0 and any class of functions G , let Ccolon {-1,1 }^ n → {-1,1 } be a function in sf FORMULA [s] ∘ G such that \[ Prob _ x {-1,1 }^ n [C(x)= sf GIP _ n ^ k (x) ] ≥ 1/2+ε. \] Then \[ s = Ω ( frac n^2 k^2 · 16^ k · (R^ (k) _ ε/(2n^2) ( G )+ log n )^2 · log ^2(1/ε) ). \]

title: Computational efficient communication protocols
statement_text: Let tcolon N × N → N . We say that a two-party communication protocol is t -efficient if for each of the parties, given an input x and some previously sent messages π ∈ {0,1 }^ * , the next message to send can be computed in time t(|x|,|π|) ( bot is being output if there is no next message). We say that such a protocol is explicit if t(|x|,|π|)=2^ o(|x|+|π|) .

title: Min-entropy
statement_text: Let X be a random variable. The min-entropy of X , denoted by H_ ∞ (X) , is the largest real number k such that Prob [X=x ] ≤ 2^ -k for every x in the range of X . If X is a distribution over {-1,1 }^aleph with H_ ∞ (X ) ≥ k , then X is called a em (aleph ,k ) -source .

paper_title: On the Complexity of Equilibrium Computation in First-Price Auctions
label: infthm:main-result
statement_text: Computing a (pure, Bayes-Nash) equilibrium of a first-price auction with continuous subjective priors and discrete bids is up PPAD xspace -complete.

paper_title: On the Complexity of Equilibrium Computation in First-Price Auctions
label: infthm:polytime
statement_text: A (pure, Bayes-Nash) equilibrium of the first-price auction can be computed in polynomial time when there is a constant number of bidders, a constant-size bidding space, and continuous (subjective) priors which are piecewise polynomial functions.

paper_title: On the Complexity of Equilibrium Computation in First-Price Auctions
label: def:bayes-nash-equilibrium
title: ε -Bayes-Nash equilibrium of the FPA
statement_text: Let ε ≥ 0 . A strategy profile bm β =(β_1, ... , β_n) is a (pure, interim) ε -Bayes-Nash equilibrium ( ε -BNE) of the FPA if for any bidder i ∈ N and any value v_i ∈ [0,1] , \[ u_i(β_i(v_i),bm β _ -i ;v_i) ≥ u_i(b,bm β _ -i ;v_i) - ε qquad for all b ∈ B. \]

paper_title: On the Complexity of Equilibrium Computation in First-Price Auctions
label: ex:irrational
statement_text: Consider a FPA with n=3 bidders and common priors, whose values are independently and identically distributed according to the uniform distribution on [0,1] ; that is, F_i(x)=x for i=1,2,3 . Let the bidding space be B={0,1/2} . Clearly, this auction can be represented with piecewise-constant density functions (with a single piece) and with a finite number of rational quantities. It can be verified that the auction has a unique equilibrium, where a bidder bids 0 iff her valuation is below frac -1+ sqrt 5 2 ≈ 0.618 ; therefore, the unique equilibrium is irrational. We provide the detailed derivation in cref app:irrational .

paper_title: On the Complexity of Equilibrium Computation in First-Price Auctions
label: lem:charepsilonbne
title: Characterization of ε -BNE
statement_text: Fix an ε ≥ 0 . A strategy profile bm β is an ε -BNE of the FPA, if and only if, for every bidder i and every non-degenerate bid b , u_i(b,bm β _ -i ;α_i(b^-)) ≥ u_i(b',bm β _ -i ;α_i(b^-)) -ε qquad for all b'<b and u_i(b,bm β _ -i ;α_i(b)) ≥ u_i(b',bm β _ -i ;α_i(b)) -ε qquad for all b'>b.

paper_title: On the Complexity of Equilibrium Computation in First-Price Auctions
statement_text: Given ε ≥ 0 , and a strategy profile bm β in a first-price auction with subjective priors, one can determine in polynomial time if bm β constitutes an ε -BNE.

statement_text: Let γ_ell , γ_r, ell , r ∈ [0,1] with γ_ell , γ_r ≥ 1/20 , γ_ell + γ_r < 1 and ell < r . Consider a base gadget with input bidder j and output bidder i , and parameters (γ_ell , γ_r, ell , r) . If γ_ell ,γ_r ≥ 1/3 and j is almost-valid, then i is valid and bm v [i] = (3γ_ell -1) + 3(1-γ_ell -γ_r) frac T_ [2+ell ,2+r] (α_j(1)) - (2+ell ) r-ell pm 6ε.

statement_text: Consider a FPA where the bidding space corresponds to all dyadic rationals of order m , and bidding strategies are represented implicitly according to the white-box model. Then, computing ε -best-responses, for exponentially small ε , is an NP-hard optimization problem.

paper_title: On the Complexity of Equilibrium Computation in First-Price Auctions
label: prop:overbidnonmonotone
statement_text: Let bm β be an exact equilibrium of a FPA. For a bid b_i by player i , let H_i(b_i,bm β _ -i ) denote the (perceived) probability that player i gets the item, given this bid and the bidding strategies by the other players. Then, strategies will always be no over-bidding and monotone non-decreasing except only possibly when the probability of winning is zero. Formally, let v_i be a valuation by player i and b_i=β_i(v_i) . If b_i>v_i , then H_i(b_i,bm β _ -i )=0 ; let v_i,v'_i be valuations by player i and b_i=β_i(v_i) , b'_i=β_i(v'_i) . If v_i<v'_i and b_i>b'_i , then H_i(b_i,bm β _ -i )=H_i(b'_i,bm β _ -i )=0 .

statement_text: For any interval [t_1,t_2] ⊆ [0,1] , any constant θ>0 and any s -sparse matrix A ∈ C ^ N × N with |A| ≤ 1 given by query-access, consider the problem of deciding whether A has a singular value in interval [t_1,t_2] , or A has no singular value in interval (t_1-θ,t_2+θ) . statement_text: For a parameter ζ ∈ [0,1) , we say that we have ζ -sampling-access to a vector u ∈ C ^ N if the following three conditions are satisfied: we have access to an O( poly ( log N)) -time classical algorithm Q _u that on input i ∈ {1, ... ,N} , outputs the entry u_i ; we have access to an O( poly ( log N)) -time classical algorithm S Q _u that samples from a probability distribution pcolon {1, ... ,N} → [0,1] such that \[ p(j) ∈ [(1-ζ)frac |u_j|^2 |u|^2 ,(1+ζ)frac |u_j|^2 |u|^2 ] \] for all j ∈ {1, ... ,N} ; we are given a real number m satisfying |m-|u|| ≤ ζ |u| . We simply say that we have sampling-access to u (without specifying ζ ) if we have 0 -sampling-access.

title: CSP over finite domains
statement_text: The Constraint satisfaction problem is a problem of deciding whether there is an assignment to a set of variables that satisfies some specified constraints. An instance of CSP problem over finite domains is defined as a triple Θ = (X,D,C) , where X = {x_0,...,x_ n-1 } is a finite set of variables, D = {D_0,...,D_ n-1 } is a set of non-empty finite domains, C={C_0,...,C_ t-1 } is a set of constraints, where each variable x_i can take on values in the non-empty domain D_i , and every constraint C_j ∈ C is a pair (vec x _j,ρ_j) with vec x _j being a tuple of variables of some length m_j , called a constraint scope , and ρ_j being an m_j -ary relation on the product of the corresponding domains, called a constraint relation . The question is whether there exists a solution to Θ , i.e. an assignment to every variable x_i such that for each constraint C_j the image of the constraint scope is a member of the constraint relation.

title: CSP
statement_text: A vocabulary is a finite set of relational symbols R_1 ,..., R_n , each of which has a fixed arity. A relational structure over the vocabulary R_1 ,..., R_n is a tuple A = (A, R^ A _1,..., R^ A _n) such that A is a non-empty set, called the universe of A , and each R^ A _i is a relation on A having the same arity as the symbol R_i . For X , A , being relational structures over the same vocabulary R_1 ,..., R_n , a homomorphism from X to A is a mapping φ: X → A from the universe X to the universe A such that for every m -ary relation R^ X and every tuple (x_1,...,x_m) ∈ R^ X we have (φ(x_1),...,φ(x_m)) ∈ R^ A . Let A be a relational structure over a vocabulary R_1 ,..., R_n . In the constraint satisfaction problem associated with A , denoted by CSP( A ), the question is, given a structure X over the same vocabulary, whether there exists a homomorphism from X to A . If the answer is positive, then we call the instance X satisfiable and unsatisfiable otherwise. We call A the target structure and X the instance (or input) one .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: def.rfegen
title: RFE generator
statement_text: The Rational Function Evaluation Generator (RFE) for \(@ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n]\) is parametrized by the following data: A non-negative integer \(k\), the numerator degree . A non-negative integer \(l\), the denominator degree . For each \(i ∈ [n]\), a distinct abscissa \(a_i ∈ @ifstar F \). The generator \(@ifstar G * RFE ^ k _ l \) takes as seed a rational function \(f ∈ @ifstar F (α)\) such that \(f\) can be written as \(g/h\) for some \(g,h ∈ @ifstar F [α]\) with \(deg (g) ≤ k\), \(deg (h) ≤ l\), and \(h(a_i) ≠ 0\) for all \(i ∈ [n]\). From \(f\), it generates the substitution \( x_i gets f(a_i) \) for each \(i ∈ [n]\).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: thm.ideal.generators
title: generating set
statement_text: Let k, l, n ∈ N and let a_i for i ∈ [n] be distinct elements of @ifstar F . The vanishing ideal of @ifstar G * RFE ^ k _ l in @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] for the given choice of abscissas (a_i)_ i ∈ [n] is generated by the following polynomials over all choices of k+l+2 indices i_1, i_2, ... , i_ k+l+2 ∈ [n] : EVC ^ k _ l [i_1,i_2, ... , i_ k+l+2 ] doteq det a_ i_j ^ k & a_ i_j ^ k-1 & ... & 1 & a_ i_j ^l x_ i_j & a_ i_j ^ l-1 x_ i_j & ... & x_ i_j _ j=1 ^ k+l+2 . Moreover, for any fixed set C ⊆ [n] of size k+1 , the polynomials EVC ^ k _ l [C sqcup L] form a generating set of minimum size when L ranges over all (l+1) -subsets of [n] that are disjoint from C , where \[ EVC ^ k _ l [S] doteq EVC ^ k _ l [i_1,i_2, ... ,i_ |S| ]\] for S = {i_1, ... , i_ |S| } ⊆ [n] with i_1 < i_2 < ... < i_ |S| .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: ex.rfe01
statement_text: Consider the special case where k=0 and l=1 . The generator for Van [@ifstar G * RFE ^ 0 _ 1 ] when \(i_1=1\), \(i_2=2\), and \(i_3=3\) is given by \[ EVC ^ 0 _ 1 [1,2,3] doteq 1 & a_1 x_1 & x_1 1 & a_2 x_2 & x_2 1 & a_3 x_3 & x_3 = (a_1-a_2)x_1x_2 + (a_2-a_3)x_2x_3 + (a_3-a_1)x_3x_1. \] For any fixed i^* ∈ [n] , the polynomials EVC ^ 0 _ 1 [S] form a generating set of minimum size when S ranges over all subsets of [n] of size 3 that contain C = {i^*} . As an aside, they also constitute minimal polynomials not computable by read-once formulas, which is consistent with the fact that @ifstar G * SV ^ 1 hits all read-once formulas (see texorpdfstring hyperref [thm.rof] Theorem Theorem ).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: cor.rfe.degree
statement_text: The minimum em degree of a nonzero polynomial in Van [@ifstar Gen@star G * RFE ^ k _ l ] equals l+1 .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: cor.rfe.sparseness
statement_text: The minimum em sparseness , i. e., number of monomials, of a nonzero polynomial in Van [@ifstar Gen@star G * RFE ^ k _ l ] equals binom k+l+2 l+1 .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: cor.rfe.partition-class-size
statement_text: The minimum em partition class size of a nonzero set-multilinear polynomial of degree l+1 in Van [@ifstar Gen@star G * RFE ^ k _ l ] equals k+2 .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: thm.ideal.membership
title: membership test for multilinear polynomials
statement_text: Let k, l, n ∈ N and let a_i for i ∈ [n] be distinct elements of @ifstar F . A multilinear polynomial p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] belongs to Van [@ifstar Gen@star G * RFE ^ k _ l ] if and only if both of the following conditions hold: There are no monomials of degree l or less, nor of degree n-k or more, in \(p\). For all disjoint subsets K,L ⊆ [n] with |K|=k and |L|=l , .partial _ L p |_ K gets 0 is zero upon the following substitution for each \(i ∈ [n] \ (K ∪ L)\), where z denotes a fresh variable: x_i gets z · frac Π _ j ∈ K (a_i - a_ j ) Π _ j ∈ L (a_i - a_ j ) .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: thm.roabp
title: ROABP hitting property
statement_text: For any integer l ≥ 1 , @ifstar G * SV ^ l hits the class of polynomials computed by read-once oblivious algebraic branching programs of width less than (l/3)+1 that contain a monomial of degree at most l+1 .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: thm.roabp.lb
title: ROABP lower bound
statement_text: For any integer l ≥ 1 , any nonzero polynomial in Van [ @ifstar Gen@star G * SV ^ l ] that contains a monomial of degree at most l+1 , requires ROABP width at least (l/3)+1 .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: lem.schwz
statement_text: Let \(@ifstar F \) be field, and \(f = g/h ∈ @ifstar F (τ_1, ... ,τ_l)\) be a rational function in \(l\) variables with \(deg (g) ≤ d\) and \(deg (h) ≤ d\). Let \(S ⊆ @ifstar F \) be finite. Then the probability that \(f\) vanishes or is undefined when each \(τ_i\) is substituted by a uniformly random element of \(S\) is at most \(2d/|S|\).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: prop.rfe-equiv-sv
statement_text: Let l and n be positive integers. There is an invertible diagonal transformation \(A : @ifstar F ^n → @ifstar F ^n\) such that, for any polynomial \(p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n]\), \(p( @ifstar G * SV ^ l ) = 0\) if and only if \((p ∘ A)(@ifstar G * RFE ^ l-1 _ l ) = 0\).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: lemma.vangen-vanishes
statement_text: For every \(k,l ∈ N \) and i_1,i_2, ... ,i_ k+l+2 ∈ [n] , \( EVC ^ k _ l [i_1, ... , i_ k+l+2 ] ∈ Van [@ifstar Gen@star G * RFE ^ k _ l ] \).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: eq.vandermonde-rep
title: Vandermonde matrix
statement_text: For T={i_1, ... , i_t} ⊆ [n] with i_1 < ... < i_t , we abbreviate the Vandermonde matrix built from a_i for i ∈ T in increasing order as A_ T doteq a_ i_1 ^ t-1 & ... & 1 vdots & & vdots a_ i_t ^ t-1 & ... & 1 .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
title: cross inversions
statement_text: For A,B ⊆ [n] , XInv (A,B) doteq |{ (a,b) ∈ A × B mid a>b }| denotes the number of cross inversions between A and B .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: prop.vangen.basic
statement_text: For every \(k,l ∈ N \), \( EVC ^ k _ l \) is skew-symmetric in that, for any \(i_1, ... ,i_ k+l+2 ∈ [n]\) and permutation \(π\) of [k+l+2] , \[ EVC ^ k _ l [i_1, ... , i_ k+l+2 ] = sign (π) · EVC ^ k _ l [i_ π(1) , ... ,i_ π(k+l+2) )]. \] For any S ⊆ [n] with |S|=k+l+2 , EVC ^ k _ l [S] is a nonzero, multilinear, and homogeneous polynomial of total degree \(l+1\), and every multilinear monomial of degree l+1 in \(x_ i_1 , ... ,x_ i_ k+l+2 \) appears with a nonzero coefficient. More specifically, for S = {i_1, ... , i_ k+l+2 } ⊆ [n] with i_1 < i_2 < ... , i_ k+l+2 , EVC ^ k _ l [S] = Σ _ substack Ksqcup L= S |L|=l+1 γ_ K,L · Π _ i ∈ L x_i, where γ_ K,L doteq (-1)^ XInv (K,L) · det (A_ K ) · det (A_ L ).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: def.sunform
title: monomial support and cored polynomial
statement_text: The support of a monomial m ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] , denoted supp (m) , is the set of indices i ∈ [n] such that m depends on x_i . For \(c,t ∈ N \), a polynomial \(p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n]\) is said to be \((c,t)\)-cored if there exists C ⊆ [n] , called the core , such that |C| ≤ c and for every monomial m of \(p\), | supp (m) \ C| ≤ t . For any subset C ⊆ [n] and monomial m = Π _ i ∈ [n] x_i^ d_i , we call Π _ i ∈ C x_i^ d_i the C -part of m , and Π _ i ∈ [n] \ C x_i^ d_i the non- C -part of m .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: prop.lem.vangen-coredform
statement_text: Let \(k,l,n ∈ N \), let \(C\) be a \((k+1)\)-subset of \([n]\), and let I denote the ideal generated by the polynomials EVC ^ k _ l [C sqcup L] where L ranges over all (l+1) -subsets of [n] \ C . Consider a monomial m ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] such that | supp (m) \ C| > l . Modulo I , m is equal to a linear combination of monomials whose non- C -parts have lower degree than the non- C -part of m .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: lem.vangen-coredform
statement_text: Let \(k,l,n ∈ N \), let \(C\) be a \((k+1)\)-subset of \([n]\), and let I be the ideal generated by the polynomials \( EVC ^ k _ l [C sqcup L]\) where \(L\) ranges over all \((l+1)\)-subsets of \([n] \ C\). Modulo I , every polynomial is equal to a \((k+1,l)\)-cored polynomial with core \(C\).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: lem.rfe-hits-cored
statement_text: Let \(k,l,n ∈ N \) and let r ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] be nonzero and \((k+1,l)\)-cored. Then \(@ifstar G * RFE ^ k _ l \) hits \(r\).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: cor-gen-sv
statement_text: Let l, n ∈ N and let a_i for i ∈ [n] be distinct elements of @ifstar F . For any fixed set C ⊆ [n] of size l , the polynomials EVCSV ^ l [C sqcup L] form a generating set of minimum size for Van [ @ifstar Gen@star G * SV ^ l ] when L ranges over all (l+1) -subsets of [n] that are disjoint from C . Here, for any S = {i_1, ... , i_ 2l+1 } ⊆ [n] with i_1 < ... < i_ 2l+1 , \[ EVCSV ^ l [S] doteq Σ _ substack T ⊆ S |T|=l+1 γ'_ S \ T,T · Π _ i ∈ T x_i, \] where γ'_ S \ T,T doteq (-1)^ XInv (S \ T,T) · ( Π _ i ∈ T Π _ j ∈ [n] \ {i} (a_i-a_ j ) ) · det (A_ S \ T ) · det (A_ T ).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: def.degree-pattern
title: degree pattern
statement_text: Let \(J ⊆ [n]\). A degree pattern with domain \(J\) is a \(J\)-indexed tuple \(d ∈ N ^J\) of nonnegative integers. A degree pattern \(d\) matches a monomial m ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] if, for every \(j ∈ J\), \(m\) has degree exactly d_j in x_j . We say that \(d\) is in \(p\) if \(d\) matches some monomial in \(p\). For any fixed \(J\), every polynomial \(p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n]\) can be written uniquely in the form p = Σ _ d ∈ N ^J p_d · x^d where \(x^ smash d doteq Π _ j ∈ J x_j^ smash d_j \) and \(p_d\) depends only on variables not indexed by \(J\). We refer to \(p_d\) as the coefficient of \(x^d\) in \(p\).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: def.extremal
title: extremal degree pattern
statement_text: Let \(K, L ⊆ [n]\). A degree pattern d^* ∈ N ^ K ∪ L is (K,L) -extremal in a polynomial p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] if d^* is the unique degree pattern d ∈ N ^ K ∪ L in p that satisfies both d_j ≤ d^*_j for all j ∈ K , and d_j ≥ d^*_j for all j ∈ L .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: eq.multi-zsub-deriv.sub
title: Zoom Lemma
statement_text: Let \(K,L ⊆ [n]\), let \(p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n]\), and let d^* ∈ N ^ K ∪ L be a degree pattern that is (K,L) -extremal in p . If the coefficient p_ d^* is nonzero upon the substitution x_i gets z · frac Π _ j ∈ K \ L ( a_i - a_j ) Π _ j ∈ L \ K ( a_i - a_j ) qquad ∀ i ∈ [n] \ (K ∪ L) where z is a fresh variable, then \(@ifstar G * RFE ^ k _ l \) hits \(p\) for any \(k ≥ |K|\) and \(l ≥ |L|\).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: prop.multi-zsub-deriv.helper
statement_text: Let \(@ifstar widehat widehat F = @ifstar F (ζ_1, ... ,ζ_r)\) be the field of rational functions in indeterminates \(ζ_1, ... , ζ_r\), let \(V ⊆ @ifstar widehat widehat F \) consist of the rational functions whose denominator has nonzero constant term, and let \(Φ : V → @ifstar F \) be the function that maps each rational function in \(V\) to its value after substituting \(ζ_j gets 0\) for all \(j ∈ [r]\). Let \[ s = Σ _ δ ∈ Δ hat c _δ · Π _ j=1 ^r ζ_j^ δ_j \] where \(Δ ⊆ Z ^r\) is some finite set, and we have \(hat c _δ ∈ V\) for every \(δ ∈ Δ\). If there exists \(δ^* ∈ Δ\) that is minimal in Δ and for which \(Φ(hat c _ δ^* ) ≠ 0\), then s ≠ 0 .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: prop.ideal.membership.degree-bound
statement_text: If a polynomial p contains a monomial of support at most l , then @ifstar G * RFE ^ k _ l hits p . If a multilinear polynomial p in the variables x_1, ... ,x_n contains a monomial of support at least n-k , then @ifstar G * RFE ^ k _ l hits p .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: prop.rfe-homog
statement_text: For any polynomial \(p\), \(p\) vanishes upon substituting \(@ifstar G * RFE \) if and only if every homogeneous component of \(p\) vanishes upon substituting \(@ifstar G * RFE \).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: lem.multi-zsub-deriv.mlin
title: Zoom Lemma for multilinear polynomials
statement_text: Let \(K,L ⊆ [n]\) be disjoint, and let \(p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n]\) be a multilinear polynomial. If \( .partial _ L p |_ K gets 0 \) is nonzero upon the substitution x_i gets z · frac Π _ j ∈ K ( a_i - a_ j ) Π _ j ∈ L ( a_i - a_ j ) qquad ∀ i ∈ [n] \ (Ksqcup L), where z is a fresh variable, then \(@ifstar G * RFE ^ k _ l \) hits \(p\) for any \(k ≥ |K|\) and \(l ≥ |L|\).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: prop.membership-coredform
statement_text: Let \(k,l,n,d ∈ N \), let \(C\) be a \((k+d-l)\)-subset of \([n]\), and let I denote the ideal generated by the polynomials EVC ^ k _ l [K sqcup L] where K ranges over all (k+1) -subsets of C and L ranges over all (l+1) -subsets of [n] \ K . Consider a multilinear monomial m ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] of degree at most d such that | supp (m) \ C| > l . Modulo I , m is equal to a linear combination of multilinear monomials of the same degree as m but whose non- C -parts have lower degree than the non- C -part of m .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: lem.membership-coredform
statement_text: Let \(k,l,n,d ∈ N \), let \(C\) be a \((k+d-l)\)-subset of \([n]\), and let I denote the ideal generated by the polynomials EVC ^ k _ l [K sqcup L] where K ranges over all (k+1) -subsets of C and L ranges over all (l+1) -subsets of [n] \ K . Modulo I , every multilinear polynomial p of degree at most d in @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] is equal to a \((k+d-l,l)\)-cored multilinear polynomial with core \(C\) that is either zero or else has the same degree as p .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: lemma.rfe-hits-multiaffine-coreform
statement_text: Let \(k,l,n,d ∈ N \) with l ≤ d ≤ n-k . Let \(r\) be a nonzero multilinear polynomial of degree d in @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n] that is \((d+k-l, l)\)-cored. There are disjoint sets \(K,L ⊆ [n]\) with \(|K|=k\) and \(|L|=l\) so that \( .partial _ L r |_ K gets 0 \) is nonzero upon the substitution .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: thm.rof
statement_text: @ifstar G * SV ^1 hits read-once formulas.

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
title: grading hypothesis
statement_text: A class C = cup_ k,l ∈ N C _ k,l of polynomials satisfies the grading hypothesis if for every \(k,l ∈ N \) and \(p ∈ C _ k,l \), at least one of the following holds: \(k=l=0\) and \(p\) is nonzero. \(k > 0\) and there is a zero substitution such that the result is in \( C _ k-1,l \). \(l > 0\) and there is a partial derivative such that the result is in \( C _ k,l-1 \).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: prop.zsub-deriv-power
statement_text: Let C = cup_ k,l ∈ N C _ k,l be a class of polynomials that satisfies the grading hypothesis and such that each C _ k,l is closed under variable rescaling. If @ifstar G * RFE ^ 0 _ 0 hits C _ 0,0 then \(@ifstar G * RFE ^ k _ l \) hits \( C _ k,l \) for every \(k,l ∈ N \).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: prop.zsub-deriv-power-variant
statement_text: Let C = cup_ k,l ∈ N C _ k,l be a class of polynomials that satisfies the grading hypothesis. If @ifstar G * RFE ^ 0 _ 0 hits C _ 0,0 then \(@ifstar G * RFE ^ k+l _ k+l \) hits \( C _ k,l \) for every \(k,l ∈ N \).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: lem.rfe-hits-sparse
statement_text: Suppose \(p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n]\) is nonzero and has only \(s\) monomials with nonzero coefficients. Then, for any \(k,l\) such that \(binom k+l+2 l+1 > s\), \(@ifstar G * RFE ^ k _ l \) hits \(p\).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: claim.lem.rfe-hits-sparse
statement_text: For any nonempty set of monomials with fewer than \(binom k+l+2 l+1 \) monomials, there is a sequence of \(downarrow \) and \(uparrow \) operations, with at most \(k\) \(downarrow \) operations and at most \(l\) \(uparrow \) operations, such that the resulting set of monomials has exactly one element.

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: def.smvan1
statement_text: Let \(k,l,n ∈ N \), and let \(S_1, ... ,S_ l+1 ⊆ [n]\) be \(l+1\) disjoint subsets of \(k+2\) indices each. The polynomial \( ESMVC ^ k _ l \) is an \((l+1) × (l+1)\) determinant where each entry is itself a \((k+2) × (k+2)\) determinant. We index the rows in the outer determinant by \(i=1, ... ,l+1\), and the columns by \(d=l, ... ,0\). In each \((i,d)\)-th inner matrix, there is one row per \(j ∈ S_i\); it is \[ a_j^k & a_j^ k-1 & ... & a_j^1 & a_j^0 & a_j^d x_j . \]

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: ex.smvan1.k1l2
statement_text: When \(k=1\) and \(l=2\), \( ESMVC \) uses three sets of three variables each. To help convey the structure of the determinant, we name the variable-sets \(S_1 = {x_1,x_2,x_3}\), \(S_2 = {y_1,y_2,y_3}\), and \(S_3 = {z_1,z_2,z_3}\), and denote the abscissa of \(x_i\) by \(a_i\), the abscissa of \(y_i\) by \(b_i\), and the abscissa of \(z_i\) by \(c_i\). With this notation and using the index ordering, \( ESMVC \) is the following: begingroup renewcommand 1.5 1.5 \[ a_1^1 & a_1^0 & a_1^2 x_1 a_2^1 & a_2^0 & a_2^2 x_2 a_3^1 & a_3^0 & a_3^2 x_3 & a_1^1 & a_1^0 & a_1^1 x_1 a_2^1 & a_2^0 & a_2^1 x_2 a_3^1 & a_3^0 & a_3^1 x_3 & a_1^1 & a_1^0 & a_1^0 x_1 a_2^1 & a_2^0 & a_2^0 x_2 a_3^1 & a_3^0 & a_3^0 x_3 b_1^1 & b_1^0 & b_1^2 y_1 b_2^1 & b_2^0 & b_2^2 y_2 b_3^1 & b_3^0 & b_3^2 y_3 & b_1^1 & b_1^0 & b_1^1 y_1 b_2^1 & b_2^0 & b_2^1 y_2 b_3^1 & b_3^0 & b_3^1 y_3 & b_1^1 & b_1^0 & b_1^0 y_1 b_2^1 & b_2^0 & b_2^0 y_2 b_3^1 & b_3^0 & b_3^0 y_3 c_1^1 & c_1^0 & c_1^2 z_1 c_2^1 & c_2^0 & c_2^2 z_2 c_3^1 & c_3^0 & c_3^2 z_3 & c_1^1 & c_1^0 & c_1^1 z_1 c_2^1 & c_2^0 & c_2^1 z_2 c_3^1 & c_3^0 & c_3^1 z_3 & c_1^1 & c_1^0 & c_1^0 z_1 c_2^1 & c_2^0 & c_2^0 z_2 c_3^1 & c_3^0 & c_3^0 z_3 . \] endgroup

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: prop.smvan1-basic
statement_text: For any \(k,l ∈ N \) and index sets \(S_1, ... ,S_ l+1 \) as in texorpdfstring hyperref [def.smvan1] Definition Definition , \( ESMVC ^ k _ l \) is skew-symmetric with respect to the order of the sets \(S_1, ... ,S_ l+1 \), and the choice of order within each set, in that any permutation thereof changes the construction by merely multiplying by the sign of the permutation. For any order, \( ESMVC ^ k _ l \) is nonzero, homogeneous of degree \(l+1\), and set-multilinear with respect to the partition \(S_1, ... , S_ l+1 \), and every monomial consistent with the partitions appears with a nonzero coefficient. When the sets are ordered as \(S_1, ... ,S_ l+1 \) and the variables associated with S_i are labeled and ordered as \((x_ i,1 , ... ,x_ i,k+2 )\) for \(i=1, ... ,l+1\), the coefficient of \(x_ 1,1 · ... · x_ l+1,1 \) equals (-1)^ (k+1)(l+1) · a_ 1,1 ^l & ... & a_ 1,1 ^0 vdots & ddots & vdots a_ l+1,1 ^l & ... & a_ l+1,1 ^0 · Π _ i=1 ^ l+1 a_ i,2 ^k & ... & a_ i,2 ^0 vdots & ddots & vdots a_ i,k+2 ^k & ... & a_ i,k+2 ^0 .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: thm.smvan1
statement_text: Let \(k,l ∈ N \) and let \(X_1, ... , X_ l+1 \) be \(l+1\) disjoint sets of indices (of any size). The linear span of ESMVC ^ k _ l [S_1, ... ,S_ l+1 ] , over all choices of S_i ⊆ X_i with |S_i|=k+2 , equals the set-multilinear polynomials in Van [@ifstar Gen@star G * RFE ^ k _ l ] with variable partition (X_1, ... , X_ l+1 ) .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: lemma.smvanone-vanishes
statement_text: For every \(k,l ∈ N \) and every choice of \(l+1\) disjoint sets \(S_1, ... ,S_ l+1 \) of \(k+2\) indices each, \( ESMVC ^ k _ l [S_1, ... ,S_ l+1 ]\) vanishes at \(@ifstar G * RFE ^ k _ l \).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: def.smcored
statement_text: Let \(X_1, ... , X_d ⊆ [n]\) be disjoint sets of indices. A polynomial that is set-multilinear with respect to the partition (X_1, ... , X_d) is \((c,t)\)-multi-cored if there exists a set Cdoteq C_1sqcup ... sqcup C_d , with C_i ⊆ X_i , |C_i| ≤ c , such that every monomial m of the polynomial satisfies | supp (M) \ C| ≤ t .

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: lemma.smvanone-multicoredform

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: lemma.rfe-hits-multicored
statement_text: Let \(k,l ∈ N \) and let \(X_1, ... , X_ l+1 ⊆ [n]\) be disjoint sets of indices. Every nonzero polynomial that is set-multilinear with respect to the partition (X_1, ... ,X_ l+1 ) and that is \((k+1,l)\)-multi-cored is hit by \(@ifstar G * RFE ^ k _ l \).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions

statement_text: Let \(Usqcup V = [n]\) be a partition of the variable indices, and let \( M _U\) and \( M _V\) be the sets of monomials that are supported on variables indexed by \(U\) and \(V\), respectively. For any polynomial \(p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n]\) define the matrix \[ CMat _ U,V (p) ∈ @ifstar F ^ M _U × M _V \] by setting the \(( m _U, m _V)\) entry to equal the coefficient of \( m _U m _V\) in \(p\).

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: lem.roabp-char
statement_text: Let \(p ∈ @ifstar F [x_1, ... ,x_n]\) be any polynomial. There is an ROABP of width \(w\) computing \(p\) in the variable order \(x_1, ... ,x_n\) if and only if, for every \(s ∈ {0, ... ,n}\), with respect to the partition \(U = {1, ... ,s}\) and \(V = { s+1 , ... ,n}\), we have \[ mathop rank ( CMat _ U,V (p) ) ≤ w. \]

paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: prop.roabp-homog

statement_text: For any integer l ≥ 1 , every nonzero multilinear homogeneous polynomial of degree l+1 in the vanishing ideal of @ifstar G * SV ^ l requires ROABP width at least (l/3)+1 .

statement_text: Let \(p ∈ Van [@ifstar G * RFE ^ l-1 _ l ] \) be nonzero, multilinear, and homogeneous of degree \(l+1\), let \(Usqcup V\) be a partition of \([n]\), and let \(C doteq CMat _ U,V (p)\). paper_title: Polynomial Identity Testing via Evaluation of Rational Functions
label: prop:ROABP:zero
statement_text: Let p ∈ Van [@ifstar G * RFE ^ l-1 _ l ] be multilinear and homogeneous of degree l+1 . Let Usqcup V be a partition of [n] , and let C doteq CMat _ U,V (p) .
