paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: ranking, inversion, Inv _ · ( · )
statement_text: A ranking ρ of a set X of n items is a bijection from X to [n] . Given two rankings σ and ρ , an inversion of σ with respect to ρ is a pair of items x_1,x_2 ∈ X such that ρ(x_1) < ρ(x_2) but σ(x_1) > σ(x_2) . The number of inversions is denoted by Inv _ρ(σ) . An inversion in an array A of values is an inversion of σ with respect to ρ where σ denotes the ranking by array index and ρ the ranking by value; in this setting we write Inv (A) for Inv _ρ(σ) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: cross inversions, XInv _ · ( · , · )
statement_text: Let ρ be a ranking of X , and A, B ⊆ X . A cross inversion from A to B with respect to ρ is a pair (x_1,x_2) ∈ A × B that is out of order with respect to ρ , i.e., such that ρ(x_1) > ρ(x_2) . The number of cross inversions is denoted by XInv _ρ(A,B) . For two arrays A and B of values, a cross inversion from A to B is a cross inversion from the set of entries in A to the set of entries in B where ρ denotes the ranking by value; in this setting we write XInv (A,B) for XInv _ρ(A,B) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: inversion minimization on trees, MinInv ( · , · ) , Π_ ·
statement_text: Inversion minimization on trees is the computational problem with the following specification: A rooted tree T with leaf set X of size n , and a ranking ρ of X . MinInv (T,ρ) , the minimum of Inv _ρ(σ) over all possible orderings of T , where σ denotes the left-to-right ranking of X induced by the ordering of T . For any fixed tree T with leaf set X , we use the short-hand Π_T to denote the computational problem that takes as input a ranking ρ of X and outputs MinInv (T,ρ) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: leaf set, L ( · ) , and subtree
statement_text: For a tree T , the leaf set of T , denoted L (T) , is the set of leaves of T . For a node v to T , T_v denotes the subtree of T rooted at v .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: thm:main:general
title: lower bound for general trees
statement_text: Let T be a tree with n leaves, and v a node with lvert L (T_v)rvert = ell . The query complexity of inversion minimization on T is at least log _2(Γ( frac ell (n-ell ) n +1 )) . In particular, the complexity is at least log _2(Γ(frac k (k+1)^2 · n+1)) where k denotes the degree of T .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: thm:main:binary
title: lower bound for binary trees
statement_text: For binary trees T with n leaves, the query complexity of inversion minimization on T is at least log _2(n!) - O( log n) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: def:leaf-child-set
title: leaf child set, LC ( · )
statement_text: The leaf child set LC (v) of a vertex v in a tree T is the set LC (v) of all the children of v that are leaves in T .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: thm:main:special
title: lower bound for restricted classes
statement_text: Let T be a tree without nodes of degree 1 such that the leaf child sets have size at most k , at most one of them is odd, and if there exists an odd one, say LC (v^*) , then all ancestors of v^* have empty leaf child sets. The query complexity of inversion minimization on T is at least log _2(n!) - O(k log k) . In particular, the lower bound applies to: perfect trees of even degree k , and full binary ( k=2 ) trees with at most one leaf without a sibling leaf.

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: thm:Mann-Whitney
title: lower bound for counting cross inversions
statement_text: Counting cross inversions from a set A of size a to a set B of size b ≥ a with respect to a ranking ρ of X doteq A sqcup B requires Ω((a+b) log (a)) queries in the comparison-query model, as does inversion minimization on the tree of Figure .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: def:computational-problem
title: computational problem and algorithm in the comparison-query model
statement_text: A computational problem in the comparison-query model is a total function on the rankings of a set X . An algorithm in the comparison-query model can access an input ranking ρ: X → [n] using comparison queries: For given x_1,x_2 ∈ X , test if ρ(x_1)< ρ(x_2) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: def:execution-and-deterministic
title: execution trace, complexity measures D ( · ) and Q ( · )
statement_text: Consider an algorithm A for a problem Π in the comparison-query model. An execution trace of A is the sequence of comparisons that A makes on some input ρ , as well as the outcomes of the comparisons. The complexity D (Π) is the minimum over all possible algorithms for Π of the number of distinct traces the algorithm has over the set of all inputs ρ . The complexity Q (Π) is the minimum, over all possible algorithms for Π of the maximum number of comparisons that the algorithm makes over the set of all inputs ρ .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: adjacent-rank transposition, affected items
statement_text: An adjacent-rank transposition is a permutation τ of [n] of the form τ = (r,r+1) , where r ∈ [n-1] and n denotes the number of items. Given τ and a ranking ρ: X → [n] , the affected items are the two elements x ∈ X for which τ(ρ(x)) ≠ ρ(x) , i.e., the items with ranks r and r+1 under ρ .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: def:sensitivity
title: sensitivity, average sensitivity, s( · )
statement_text: Let Π be a computational problem in the comparison-query model on a set X of items. For a fixed ranking ρ and adjacent-rank transposition τ , we say that Π is sensitive to τ at ρ if Π(ρ) ≠ Π(τ ρ) . The sensitivity of Π at ρ is the number of adjacent-rank transpositions τ such that Π is sensitive to τ at ρ . The average sensitivity of Π , denoted s(Π) , is the average sensitivity of Π at ρ when ρ is drawn uniformly at random from all rankings of X .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: lemma:sensitivity
title: Sensitivity Lemma
statement_text: For any problem Π in the comparison-query model with n items, D (Π) ≥ Γ(s(Π)+2)/n .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
title: permutahedron graph, G( · ) , overline G ( · )
statement_text: Let Π be a computational problem in the comparison-query model on a set X of items. The permutahedron graph of Π , denoted G(Π) , has the rankings of X as vertices, and an edge between two rankings ρ_1 and ρ_2 if Π(ρ_1) = Π(ρ_2) and there exists an adjacent-rank transposition such that ρ_2 = τ ρ_1 . The complementary permutahedron graph of Π , denoted overline G (Π) , is defined similarly by replacing the condition Π(ρ_1) = Π(ρ_2) by its complement, Π(ρ_1) ≠ Π(ρ_2) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: lemma:connectivity
title: Connectivity Lemma
statement_text: For any problem Π in the comparison-query model, D (Π) is at least the number of connected components of G(Π) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: lemma:sensitivity:strong
title: Strong Sensitivity Lemma
statement_text: Consider an algorithm A in the comparison-based model with n items, color each vertex of the permutahedron with its execution trace under A , and let overline H denote the subgraph with the same vertex set but only containing the bichromatic edges. The number of distinct execution traces of A is at least g(deg _ avg (overline H )+1)/n , where g: [1, ∞ ) → R is any convex function with g(x) = x! for x ∈ [n] .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: fact:Boolean
statement_text: Let A be a query algorithm on binary strings of length n . Color each vertex of the n -dimensional hypercube by its execution trace under A , and let overline H denote the subgraph with the same vertex set but only containing the bichromatic edges. Then the number of distinct execution traces is at least 2^ deg _ avg (H) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: claim:encoding
statement_text: Let R denote the set of all rankings ρ that follow a particular execution trace on A , and let d ∈ {0, ... ,n-1} . The number of rankings ρ ∈ R with deg _ overline H (ρ) = d is at most frac n! (d+1)! .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: lemma:k-ary:subtree-sensitivity
title: subtree-induced sensitivity
statement_text: Consider a tree T with n doteq lvert L (T)rvert leaves, and some node v in T with ell doteq lvert L (T_v)rvert leaves. We have \[s(Π_T) ≥ frac ell (n-ell ) n -1. \]

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: claim:k-ary:decreasing-transposition
statement_text: ρ is sensitive to the transposition τ=(r,r+1) if σ_ min (ρ^ -1 (r))>σ_ min (ρ^ -1 (r+1)) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: claim:k-ary:transposition-to-gap
statement_text: For any ordering σ , the number of r such that σ(ρ^ -1 (r))>σ(ρ^ -1 (r+1)) is at least one less than the number of s such that ρ^ -1 (s) ∈ L (T_v) and ρ^ -1 (s+1) ∉ L (T_v) .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: claim:k-ary:gap-count
statement_text: Over a uniformly random ρ , the expected number of s such that ρ^ -1 (s) ∈ L (T_v) and ρ^ -1 (s+1) ∉ L (T_v) is frac ell (n-ell ) n .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: fact:k-ary:balance
statement_text: If T is a tree of degree k with n leaves, there exists a node v in T such that ell doteq lvert L (T_v)rvert = α · n , where frac 1 k+1 ≤ α ≤ frac k k+1 .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: eq:MRInv
title: root inversions, RInv ( · , · , · ) , MinRInv ( · , · )
statement_text: Given a tree T , a ranking ρ of the leaves of T , and an ordering σ of T , a root inversion of σ with respect to ρ is an inversion (ell _1,ell _2) of σ with respect to ρ for which the lowest common ancestor LCA (ell _1,ell _2) is the root of T . The number of root inversions of σ with respect to ρ in T is denoted by RInv (T,ρ,σ) . The minimum number of root inversions in T with respect to ρ is denoted MinRInv (T,ρ) doteq min _σ RInv (T,ρ,σ), where σ ranges over all possible orderings of T .

paper_title: Lower Bound Techniques in the Comparison-Query Model and Inversion Minimization on Trees
label: prop:change
statement_text: Let ρ be a ranking of the leaf set X of a tree T , τ an adjacent-rank transposition, and ell _1 and ell _2 be the affected leaves. Then \[ MinRInv (T_v,ρ) = MinRInv (T_v,τ ρ) \] for all nodes v in T except possibly v = LCA (ell _1,ell _2) . Moreover, the difference is at most 1 in absolute value.

title: randomized query complexity, RQ _ · ( · ) , and distributional query complexity, DistQ _ · ( · , · )
statement_text: Let Π be a problem in the comparison-query model and ε ∈ [0,1] . A randomized algorithm R for Π is said to have error ε if on every input ρ , the algorithm outputs Π(ρ) with probability at least 1-ε . The query complexity of R is the maximum, over all inputs ρ , of the expected number of queries that R makes on input ρ . The ε -error randomized query complexity of Π , denoted RQ _ ε (Π) , is the minimum query complexity of R over all ε -error randomized algorithms R for Π . Let 0.06cm be a probability distribution on the inputs ρ . A deterministic algorithm A for Π has error ε with respect to 0.06cm if the probability that A(ρ)=Π(ρ) is at least 1-ε where the input ρ is chosen according to 0.06cm . The query complexity of A with respect to 0.06cm is the expected number of queries that A makes on input ρ when ρ is chosen according to 0.06cm . The ε -error distributional query complexity of Π with respect to 0.06cm , denoted DistQ _ ε (Π,0.06cm) , is the minimum query complexity of A with respect to 0.06cm over all deterministic algorithms A for Π that have error ε with respect to 0.06cm .

label: def:partition-property
title: partition property
statement_text: A computational problem Π in the comparison-query model on a set X of n items has the partition property if the set X can be partitioned into sets X_i such that for any ranking ρ of X and adjacent-rank transposition τ = (r, r+1) with r ∈ [n-1] , Π(ρ) = Π(τ ρ) if and only if ρ^ -1 (r) and ρ^ -1 (r+1) belong to the same partition class X_i . If every partition class X_i has size at most k , we say that Π has the partition property with class size at most k .

statement_text: Let Π be a computational problem in the comparison-query model on a set X of n items, and ρ a ranking of X . The successor graph of Π on ρ , denoted S(Π,ρ) , has vertex set [n] and contains all edges of the form (r,r+1) with r ∈ [n-1] such that Π(ρ) = Π(τ ρ) , where τ denotes the adjacent-rank transposition (r,r+1) .

The minimum feedback arc set problem is finding the minimum number of feedback arcs induced by any ordering σ . In weighted minimum feedback arc set, each edge from v_i to v_j has a weight w_ ij , and the objective is to minimize Σ _ e ∈ E e_ ij · I [σ(v_i)>σ(v_j)] .

paper_title: Localizability of the approximation method
label: t:idloc

statement_text: Let cal M be any legitimate model of constant-depth circuits and f any Boolean function with n inputs. Suppose that ρ_ O(d^2) (f, cal M ) ≥ s . Then f is not computable by depth d circuits of size s-poly(kdn(2^ m/d +1)) using k arbitrarily powerful oracles of arity m . The constants in the poly( · ) -notation are absolute. We work with a `symmetric' definition of ρ_d , cf. Definitions and , but Theorem holds for `asymmetric' ρ_d as well, if we adjust the parameters appropriately.

paper_title: Localizability of the approximation method
label: d:legmodel
title: Legitimate model
statement_text: A legitimate model (of order n ) of a circuit class cal C is a pair < cal M , overline ∘ ( cal M ) > , where {0,1, x_i mid i ≥ 1 } ⊆ cal M ⊆ cal F _n and overline ∘ ( cal M ) is a set of commutative operations overline ∘ :underbrace cal M × ... × cal M _ m times mapsto cal M , for each ∘ ∈ ∘ ( cal C ) of arity m . We abuse the notation and denote < cal M , overline ∘ ( cal M ) > by cal M .

paper_title: Localizability of the approximation method
title: Approximating circuit
statement_text: Given a legitimate model (of order n ) of a circuit class cal C and a cal C -circuit C with inputs from {x_1, ... ,x_n} , we define an approximating circuit overline C inductively by replacing each gate ∘ (C_1, ... ,C_m) in C by overline ∘ ([[overline C_1 ]], ... ,[[overline C_m ]]) and setting overline 1 :=1, overline 0 :=0, overline x_i :=x_i . Here, [[B]] ∈ cal F _n denotes the function computed by circuit (or approximating circuit) B . In order to simplify the notation, we will assume that B is [[B]] , if it is used in a context which asks for a function.

paper_title: Localizability of the approximation method

title: Error sets
statement_text: Given a legitimate model cal M of a circuit class cal C , we define the error sets of cal M by δ^+_ ∘ (f_1, ... ,f_m):= & ∘ (f_1, ... ,f_m)backslash overline ∘ (f_1, ... ,f_m), δ^-_ ∘ (f_1, ... ,f_m):= &\ overline ∘ (f_1, ... ,f_m)backslash ∘ (f_1, ... ,f_m), δ_ ∘ (f_1, ... ,f_m):= &\ δ^ + _ ∘ (f_1, ... ,f_m) ∪ δ^-_ ∘ (f_1, ... ,f_m), where ∘ ∈ ∘ ( cal C ) has arity m and f_1, ... , f_m ∈ cal M . Further, we let Δ:= {δ_ ∘ (f_1, ... ,f_m)mid f_1, ... ,f_m ∈ cal M , ∘ ∈ ∘ ( cal C ) of arity m}.

paper_title: Localizability of the approximation method
label: d:distance
title: Distance
statement_text: The distance ρ(f,cal M) of a legitimate model cal M of a circuit class cal C from a Boolean function f ∈ cal F _n is the minimal t such that there are tuples < overline ∘ _i , f^i_1, ... , f^i_ m_i > , where m_i is the arity of ∘ _i ∈ ∘ ( cal C ) , i=1, ... , t and f^i_j ∈ cal M , such that for some g ∈ cal M , f ⊕ g ⊆ \ cup_ i=1, ... ,t δ_ ∘ _i (f_1^i, ... ,f_ m_i ^i). If there is no such t , we set ρ(f, cal M ):= ∞ . Razborov defined the distance ρ(f,cal M) as the minimal t such that fbackslash g ⊆ \ cup_ i=1, ... ,t δ^+_ ∘ _i (f_1^i, ... ,f_ m_i ^i) \ \ and \ \ gbackslash f ⊆ \ cup_ i=1, ... , t δ^-_ ∘ _i (f_1^i, ... ,f_ m_i ^i). We use a `symmetric' definition of ρ , which simplifies proofs, but our results work for Razborov's `asymmetric' ρ as well (with an appropriate adjustment of parameters). The asymmetry in Razborov's definition of ρ is used when defining the fusion method, see S .

title: 0-projective model

We say that cal M is 0-projective if the condition * holds: If C is a cal C -circuit with inputs x_j , for j ∈ J ⊆ {0,1}^n , then for each z,y ∈ {0,1}^n , z|_J=y|_Jquad ⇒ quad overline C (z)=overline C (y). paper_title: Localizability of the approximation method
label: t:genloc
title: Localizability of the approximation method for general circuits
statement_text: Let cal M be any legitimate model cal M of Boolean circuits over { ¬ , wedge _2,vee _2} such that overline ¬ := ¬ , and f ∈ cal F _n . em [Localizability with few oracles] Suppose that ρ(f, cal M ) ≥ s . Then, f is not computable by circuits of size s-O(knm) using connectives ¬ ,wedge _2,vee _2 and k arbitrarily powerful, possibly different and noncommutative , oracles of arity m . It is possible to prove Item 1 with Razborov's asymmetric definition of ρ(f, cal M ) , if we adjust the resulting lower bound for the oracle circuits to s-O(kn · max{m, log n}) and conclude that it holds only for circuits with monotone oracles and negations at the bottom. The term max{m, log n} comes from not using DNFs in the proof, which is done in order to keep negations at the bottom. Further, it is possible to avoid the requirement on the monotonicity of oracles and negations at the bottom by using slice functions (and adjusting the parameters appropriately). em [Localizability of 0-projective models] Suppose that ρ(f, cal M ) ≥ s and that cal M is 0-projective. Then, f is not computable by circuits of size s-O(km^2) using connectives ¬ ,wedge _2,vee _2 and k arbitrarily powerful, possibly different and noncommutative, oracles of arity m whose inputs are among {x_1, ¬ x_1, ... , x_n, ¬ x_n} . em [Localizability of projective models] Suppose that ρ(f, cal M ) ≥ s and that cal M is projective. Here, cal M is projective if for each Boolean circuit C over { ¬ ,wedge _2,vee _2} with m inputs x_1, ... ,x_m , for all f_1, ... ,f_m ∈ cal M and each z,y ∈ {0,1}^n , wedge_ i=1, ... ,m f_i(z)=f_i(y)quad ⇒ quad overline C (f_1(z), ... ,f_m(z))=overline C (f_1(y), ... ,f_m(y)). Then, f is not computable by circuits of size s-O(km^2) using connectives ¬ ,wedge _2,vee _2 and k arbitrarily powerful, possibly different and noncommutative, oracles of arity m .

paper_title: Localizability of the approximation method
label: d:ddistance
title: ρ_d(f,cal M)

statement_text: The estimation task for unitary channels is the following: One is given black-box access to a unitary channel by Z ∈ U ( d ) . After applying the unitary channel some Q times, the algorithm should output a classical description Throughout this paper, for ease of exposition we will be treating these descriptions as if they have infinite precision. To formalize our results when numbers can only be specified up to a machine precision ε_ mach , we consider the sets of unit vectors and unitary matrices that can be generated from O( log ^3(1/ε)) -depth quantum circuits. This discretizes these spaces into O(ε_ mach ) -nets by the Solovay--Kitaev theorem. Then, a classical description of a unitary matrix or a unit vector is a list of numbers defining a matrix or vector that need not exactly satisfy the desired constraints, but is ε_ mach -close to an element of the net. When we need to implement a unitary from its classical description, we implement this element. We only care about vectors and matrices up to poly (ε/ d ) error, since this is the magnitude of sampling error from state tomography, which is where these classical descriptions come from. So, if we set ε_ mach to be smaller than this, then the errors from working in finite precision are negligible, and we incur a polylog (1/ε_ mach ) overhead (which is only polylog ( d /ε) ) in time complexity. This issue only affects constant factors in our proofs in a very minor way, and we trust the diligent reader to take note of the required changes. of a unitary widehat Z ∈ U ( d ) . The algorithm may be probabilistic and hence widehat Z should be thought of as a random variable. The goal is to achieve E [ error ( U (Z), U (widehat Z ))] < ε. Again, kl Adam tries to refute her choice, and this time he has two possible lines of attack: either find a directed cycle in P (as before), or show that there are at least two selected kl nodes . He launches both attacks simultaneously by choosing a single subset X of kl nodes , and then presenting kl Eve with two challenges: to charge each kl node positively or negatively according to X (as described in Example ), and to tell each kl node whether the selected kl node belongs to X . paper_title: Classical Verification of Quantum Learning
label: theorem:main-result-agnostic-quantum-fourier-sampling-learning
title: Distributional agnostic approximate quantum Fourier sampling and learning -- Informal
statement_text: Let D =( U _n, φ) be an unknown probability distribution over {0,1}^n × {0,1} , with (known) uniform marginal over {0,1}^n and with (unknown) conditional label expectation φ:{0,1}^n → [0,1] . bf Distributional agnostic quantum Fourier sampling: There is an efficient quantum algorithm that, given a single copy of ρ_ D , with success probability nicefrac 1 2 outputs a sample from a probability distribution over {0,1}^n that is inverse-exponentially close to the squares of the Fourier coefficients of φ = 1-2φ . bf Distributional agnostic proper quantum parity learning: There is an efficient quantum algorithm that properly 1 -agnostically learns parities from an efficient number of copies of ρ_ D . bf Distributional 2-agnostic improper quantum Fourier-sparse learning: There is an efficient quantum algorithm that improperly 2 -agnostically learns Fourier-sparse functions from an efficient number of copies of ρ_ D .

paper_title: Classical Verification of Quantum Learning
label: theorem:main-result-verification
title: Verifying distributional agnostic quantum learning -- Informal
statement_text: There is a class D of probability distributions over {0,1}^n × {0,1} with (known) uniform marginal over {0,1}^n such that: Distributional 1 -agnostic parity learning is classically hard from SQs or random examples, even if the unknown distribution is promised to lie in D . When promised that the unknown distribution lies in D , there is an efficient interactive verification procedure that allows a classical verifier, with SQ or random example access, to verify a distributional 1 -agnostic quantum parity learner, who has mixture-of-superpositions example or QSQ access. When promised that the unknown distribution lies in D , there is an efficient interactive verification procedure that allows a classical verifier, with SQ or random example access, to verify a distributional 2 -agnostic quantum Fourier-sparse learner, who has mixture-of-superpositions example or QSQ access.

title: The GGM tree construction
statement_text: Let Ccolon {0, 1}^n → {0, 1}^ 2n be a circuit. Let n,T ∈ N be such that T ≥ 4n and let k be the smallest integer such that 2^k n ≥ T . The function GGM _T[C]colon {0, 1}^n → {0, 1}^T is defined as follows. Consider a perfect binary tree with 2^k leaves, where the root is on level 0 and the leaves are on level k . Each node is assigned a binary string of length n , and for 0 ≤ j < 2^i , denote v_ i, j ∈ {0, 1}^n the value assigned to the j -th node on level i . Let x ∈ {0, 1}^n . We perform the following computation to obtain GGM _T[C](x) : we set v_ 0, 0 := x , and for each 0 ≤ i < k , 0 ≤ j < 2^i , we set v_ i+1, 2j := C(v_ i, j )_ [0, n) (i.e., the first half of C(v_ i, j ) ) and v_ i+1, 2j+1 := C(v_ i, j )_ [n, 2n) (i.e., the second half of C(v_ i, j ) ). (We say the nodes (i+1, 2j) and (i+1, 2j+1) are ``children'' of (i, j) .) Finally, we concatenate all values of the leaves and take the first T bits as the output: \[ GGM _T[C](x) := (v_ k, 0 ∘ v_ k, 1 ∘ ... ∘ v_ k, 2^k-1 )_ [0, T) .\]

statement_text: Let f : {0,1}^n → {0,1} be a symmetric Boolean function. Then \[ C _ min (f) = ell _0(f) + n - ell _1(f). \]

paper_title: Instance complexity of Boolean functions
label: cor:symmmaxcmin
statement_text: The only symmetric functions f : {0,1}^n → {0,1} with C _ min (f) = n are the parity function XOR _n and its negation.

paper_title: Instance complexity of Boolean functions
label: thm:symmic
title: Restatement of Theorem
statement_text: Let f : {0,1}^n → {0,1} be a symmetric Boolean function. Then, \[ InstC (f) = frac n C _ min (f) = frac n ell _0(f) + n - ell _1(f) . \]

paper_title: Instance complexity of Boolean functions
statement_text: The only symmetric Boolean functions that are strictly D -instance optimizable are the parity function XOR _n and its negation.

paper_title: Instance complexity of Boolean functions
label: defn:conn
title: Connectivity
statement_text: For a positive integer n > 0 , define the function CONN : binom n 2 → {0,1} as CONN (G) = 1 iff G is connected.

paper_title: Instance complexity of Boolean functions
label: defn:kcl
title: k -Clique
statement_text: For positive integers 0 < k ≤ n , define the function CL _ k : binom n 2 → {0,1} as CL _ k (G) = 1 iff G contains a k -clique as a subgraph.

paper_title: Instance complexity of Boolean functions
label: thm:graph
title: Restatement of Theorem
statement_text: Let n be a sufficiently large positive integer and k be a positive integer satisfying k^3 ≤ n^2/4 . Then, \[ InstC ( CONN ) = frac DT ( CONN ) C _ min ( CONN ) = frac binom n 2 n-1 , qquad InstC ( CL _ k ) = frac DT ( CL _ k ) C _ min ( CL _ k ) = frac binom n 2 binom k 2 . \]

paper_title: Instance complexity of Boolean functions
label: defn:gt
title: Greater-Than
statement_text: For a positive integer n , the Greater-Than function on 2n inputs, denoted GT _n , is defined by GT _n(x_1, ... , x_n, y_1, ... , y_n) = 1 iff the integer whose binary representation is x_n ... , x_1 is strictly larger than the integer whose binary representation is y_n, ... , y_1 .

paper_title: Instance complexity of Boolean functions
label: defn:omb
title: Odd-Max-Bit
statement_text: For a positive integer n , the Odd-Max-Bit function on n inputs, denoted OMB _n , is defined by \[ OMB _n(x_1, ... , x_n) = 1 ⟺ max {i ∈ [n] : x_i = 1 } normal is odd . \] Define OMB (0^n) = 0 .

paper_title: Instance complexity of Boolean functions
label: thm:gtombresults
title: Restatement of Theorem
statement_text: For all positive integers n , we have DT ( GT _n) & = 2n, qquad C _ min ( GT _n) = 2, qquad InstC ( GT _n) ≤ 2 DT ( OMB _n) & = n, qquad C _ min ( OMB _n) = 1, qquad InstC ( OMB _n) ≤ 2.

paper_title: Instance complexity of Boolean functions
label: lem:degdt
title: Folklore
statement_text: Let f : {0,1}^n → {0,1} be a Boolean function. Then DT (f) ≥ deg (f) .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: expl:vs-mc
statement_text: Let τ = {<} be a relational signature with a single binary relation symbol < . Let Γ_ < be the valued τ -structure with domain {0,1} and where < (x,y) = 0 if x < y , and < (x,y) = 1 otherwise.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: expl:mc
statement_text: The problem VCSP (Γ_<) for the valued structure Γ_< from Example models the directed max-cut problem: given a finite directed graph (V,E) (we do allow loops and multiple edges), partition the vertices V into two classes A and B such that the number of edges from A to B is maximal. Maximising the number of edges from A to B amounts to minimising the number e of edges within A , within B , and from B to A . So when we associate A to the preimage of 0 and B to the preimage of 1 , computing the number e corresponds to finding the evaluation map s colon V → {0,1} that minimizes the value Σ _ (x,y) ∈ E < (s(x),s(y)) , which can be formulated as an instance of VCSP (Γ_<) . Conversely, every instance of VCSP (Γ_<) corresponds to a directed max-cut instance. It is known that VCSP (Γ_ < ) is NP-complete (even if we do not allow loops and multiple edges in the input) . We mention that this problem can be viewed as a resilience problem in database theory as explained in Section .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: expl:min-cut
statement_text: Consider the valued structure Γ_ ≥ with domain {0,1} and the binary valued relation ≥ defined by ≥ (x,y)=0 if x ≥ y and ≥ (x,y)=1 otherwise. Similarly to Example , VCSP (Γ_ ≥ ) models the directed min-cut problem, i.e., given a finite directed graph (V,E) , partition the vertices V into two classes A and B such that the number of edges from A to B is minimal. The min-cut problem is solvable in polynomial time; see, e.g., .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
statement_text: Let k ∈ N , let R ∈ mathscr R ^ (k) _C , and let α be a permutation of C . Then α preserves R if for all a ∈ C^k we have R(α(a)) = R(a) . If Γ is a valued structure with domain C , then an automorphism of Γ is a permutation of C that preserves all valued relations of R .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: expl:MCC
statement_text: Let τ = {E,N} be a relational signature with two binary relation symbols E and N . Let Γ_ LCC be the valued τ -structure with domain N where E(x,y) = 0 if x = y and E(x,y)=1 otherwise, and where N(x,y) = 0 if x ≠ y and N(x,y)=1 otherwise. Note that Aut (Γ_ LCC ) is the full symmetric group on N . This group is oligomorphic; for example, there are five orbits of triples represented by the tuples (1,2,3) , (1,1,2) , (1,2,1) , (2,1,1) and (1,1,1) . The problem of least correlation clustering with partial information is equal to VCSP (Γ_ LCC ) . It is a variant of the min-correlation clustering problem that does not require precisely one constraint between any two variables. The problem is NP-complete in both settings .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: lem:cost
statement_text: Let Γ be a valued structure with a countable domain C and an oligomorphic automorphism group. Then for every instance φ(x_1, ... ,x_n) of VCSP (Γ) there exists a ∈ C^n such that the cost of φ equals φ^ Γ (a) .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: thm:fb-NP
statement_text: Let Γ be a countable valued structure with finite signature such that there exists a finitely bounded homogeneous structure B with Aut ( B ) ⊆ Aut (Γ) . Then VCSP (Γ) is in NP.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
statement_text: Let A be a set and R,R' ∈ mathscr R _A . We say that R' can be obtained from R by projecting if R' is of arity k , R is of arity k+n , and for all a ∈ A^k \[R'(a) = inf _ b ∈ A^n R(a,b).\] non-negative scaling if there exists a ∈ Q _ ≥ 0 such that R' = a R ; shifting if there exists a ∈ Q such that R' = R + a . If R is of arity k , then Opt (R) denotes the relation consisting of all minimal-value tuples of R , i.e., \[ Opt (R) := {a ∈ Feas (R) mid R(a) ≤ R(b) for every b ∈ A^k}.\]

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: def:wrelclone
title: valued relational clone
statement_text: Let C be a set. A valued relational clone (over C ) is a subset of mathscr R _C that is closed under forming sums of atomic expressions, projecting, shifting, non-negative scaling, Feas , and Opt ; we will refer to expressions formed this way as pp-expressions . For a valued structure Γ with the domain C , we write le Γ rangle for the smallest relational clone that contains the valued relations of Γ . If R ∈ le Γ rangle , we say that Γ pp-expresses R .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: expl:opt-feas
statement_text: Consider the domain C={0,1,2} and the unary valued relation R on C defined by R(0)=0 , R(1)=1 and R(2)= ∞ . Then the relation Feas (R) cannot be obtained from R by forming sums of atomic expressions, projecting, shifting, non-negative scaling and use of Opt . Similarly, the relation Opt (R) cannot be obtained from R by forming sums of atomic expressions, projecting, shifting, non-negative scaling and use of Feas .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: lem:expr-reduce
statement_text: Let Γ be a valued structure with an oligomorphic automorphism group and a finite signature. Suppose that Δ is a valued structure with a finite signature over the same domain C such that every cost function of Δ is from le Γ rangle . Then there is a polynomial-time reduction from VCSP (Δ) to VCSP (Γ) .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: expl:mc-hard
statement_text: Recall the structure Γ_< from Example . We have seen in Example that VCSP (Γ_<) is the directed max-cut problem. Consider the classical relation NAE on {0,1} defined by \[ NAE := {0,1}^3 \ {(0,0,0), (1,1,1)}.\] Note that \[ NAE (x,y,z) = Opt ( < (x,y)+ < (y,z)+ < (z,x) ).\] Since CSP ({0,1}, NAE ) is known to be NP-hard (see, e.g., ), this provides an alternative proof of the NP-hardness of the directed max-cut problem via Lemma .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: expl:mcc-hard
statement_text: We revisit the countably infinite valued structure Γ_ LCC from Example . Recall that VCSP (Γ_ LCC ) is the least correlation clustering problem with partial information and that Aut (Γ_ LCC ) is oligomorphic. Let Γ_ EC be the relational structure with the same domain as Γ_ LCC and the relation R := {(x,y,z) mid (x=y wedge y ≠ z) vee (x ≠ y wedge y = z)} (attaining values 0 and ∞ ). Note that R(x,y,z) = Opt (N(x,z) + N(x,z) + E(x,y) + E(y,z)). This provides an alternative proof of NP-hardness of the least correlation clustering with partial information via Lemma , because CSP (Γ_ EC ) is known to be NP-hard . Note that we can replace N(x,z) + N(x,z) in the definition of R by Opt (N)(x,z) and that Opt (N) is equal to the classical relation ≠ (attaining values 0 and ∞ ). This shows that even VCSP (N; E, ≠ ) is NP-hard.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
title: pp-power
statement_text: Let Γ be a valued structure with domain C and let d ∈ N . Then a ( d -th) pp-power of Γ is a valued structure Δ with domain C^d such that for every valued relation R of Δ of arity k there exists a valued relation S of arity kd in le Γ rangle such that R((a^1_1, ... ,a^1_d), ... ,(a^k_1, ... ,a^k_d)) = S(a^1_1, ... ,a^1_d, ... ,a^k_1, ... ,a^k_d).

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: prop:pp-hard
statement_text: Let Γ and Δ be valued structures such that Aut (Γ) is oligomorphic and Δ is a pp-power of Γ . Then Aut (Δ) is oligomorphic and there is a polynomial-time reduction from VCSP (Δ) to VCSP (Γ) .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: def:frac-map
title: fractional map
statement_text: Let C and D be sets. A fractional map from D to C is a probability distribution (C^D, B (C^D),ω colon B (C^D) → [0,1]), that is, ω(C^D) = 1 and ω is countably additive: if A_1,A_2, ... ∈ B (C^D) are disjoint, then ω( cup_ i ∈ N A_i) = Σ _ i ∈ N ω(A_i).

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: def:frac-hom
title: fractional homomorphism
statement_text: Let Γ and Δ be valued τ -structures with domains C and D , respectively. A fractional homomorphism from Δ to Γ is a fractional map from D to C such that for every R ∈ τ of arity k and every tuple a ∈ D^k , the expected value E_ω[X] of the random variable X colon C^D → R ∪ { ∞ } given by \[f mapsto R^ Γ (f(a))\] exists and satisfies E_ω[X] ≤ R^ Δ (a).

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: lem:E-exists
statement_text: Let C and D be sets, a ∈ D^k , and R ∈ mathscr R _C^ (k) . If X colon C^D → R ∪ { ∞ } is the random variable given by \[f mapsto R(f(a))\] and Aut (C; R) is oligomorphic, then E_ω[X] exists and E_ω[X] > - ∞ .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: lem:borel-prod
title: see, e.g., or
statement_text: Let S and T be second-countable topological spaces. Then B (S) ⊗ B (T) = B (S × T) .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: lem:comp
statement_text: Let C_1, C_2, C_3 be countable sets. The composition map ∘ colon C_3^ C_2 × C_2^ C_1 → C_3^ C_1 is (Borel-)measurable.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
title: composition of fractional maps
statement_text: Let C_1, C_2, C_3 be countable sets. Let ω_1 be a fractional map from C_1 to C_2 and ω_2 be a fractional map from C_2 to C_3 . Then ω_2 ∘ ω_1 colon B (C_3^ C_1 ) → [0,1] is defined by \[ω_2 ∘ ω_1 (S) := ω_2 ⊗ ω_1 ({(g, f) mid f ∈ C_2^ C_1 , g ∈ C_3^ C_2 , g ∘ f ∈ S}).\]

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: prop:frac-comp
statement_text: Let C_1, C_2, C_3 be countable sets. Let ω_1 be a fractional map from C_1 to C_2 and let ω_2 be a fractional map from C_2 to C_3 . Then the following statements hold. ω_2 ∘ ω_1 is a fractional map from C_1 to C_3 . For every k ∈ N , a ∈ C_1^k , and c ∈ C_3^k , \[ω_2 ∘ ω_1 (mathscr S _ a,c ) = Σ _ b ∈ C_2^k ω_1( mathscr S _ a,b ) ω_2( mathscr S _ b,c ).\] The above property uniquely determines the fractional map ω_2 ∘ ω_1 . The operation ∘ of composition of fractional maps is associative. If Γ_1, Γ_2 , and Γ_3 are valued τ -structures, ω_1 is a fractional homomorphism from Γ_1 to Γ_2 , and ω_2 is a fractional homomorphism from Γ_2 to Γ_3 , then ω_2 ∘ ω_1 is a fractional homomorphism from Γ_1 to Γ_3 .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: prop:frac-hom
statement_text: Let Γ and Δ be valued τ -structures with domains C and D and with a fractional homomorphism ω from Δ to Γ . Then the cost of every VCSP instance φ with respect to Γ is at most the cost of φ with respect to Δ .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: cor:hom-hard
statement_text: Let Γ and Δ be valued τ -structures with oligomorphic automorphism groups that are fractionally homomorphically equivalent. Then VCSP (Γ) and VCSP (Δ) are polynomial-time equivalent.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: prop:frac-hom-expr
statement_text: Let Γ and Δ be valued τ -structures with oligomorphic automorphism groups that are fractionally homomorphically equivalent. Let ω be a fractional homomorphism from Δ to Γ . Let R ∈ le Δ rangle be of arity k and R' ∈ le Γ rangle be the valued relation obtained when the pp-expression for R in Δ is interpreted over Γ . Then for every a ∈ D^k , E_ ω [f mapsto R'(f(a))] ≤ R(a).

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
title: pp-construction
statement_text: Let Γ, Δ be valued structures. Then Δ has a pp-construction in Γ if Δ is fractionally homomorphically equivalent to a structure Δ' which is a pp-power of Γ .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: cor:pp-constr-red
statement_text: Let Γ and Δ be valued structures with finite signatures and oligomorphic automorphism groups such that Δ has a pp-construction in Γ . Then there is a polynomial-time reduction from VCSP (Δ) to VCSP (Γ) .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: cor:OIT
statement_text: Let Γ be a valued structure with a finite signature and oligomorphic automorphism group such that ({0,1}; OIT ) has a pp-construction in Γ . Then VCSP (Γ) is NP-hard.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: prop:pp-constr-rel
statement_text: Let Γ be a valued structure and let B be a relational structure, both with countable domains. Then Γ pp-constructs B if and only if the underlying crisp structure of Γ pp-constructs B .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: lem:pp-trans
statement_text: The relation of pp-constructability on the class of countable valued structures is transitive.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
title: fractional operation
statement_text: Let ell ∈ N . A fractional operation on C of arity ell is a probability distribution ( mathscr O _C^ (ell ) ,B( mathscr O _C^ (ell ) ), ω colon B( mathscr O _C^ (ell ) ) → [0,1] ). The set of all fractional operations on C of arity ell is denoted by mathscr F ^ (ell ) _C , and mathscr F _C := cup_ ell ∈ N mathscr F ^ (ell ) _C .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: def:pres
statement_text: A fractional operation ω ∈ mathscr F _C^ (ell ) improves a k -ary valued relation R ∈ mathscr R ^ (k) _C if for all a^1, ... ,a^ ell ∈ C^k E := E_ω[f mapsto R(f(a^1, ... ,a^ ell ))] exists and E ≤ frac 1 ell Σ _ j = 1 ^ ell R(a^j).

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
title: fractional polymorphism
statement_text: If ω improves every valued relation in Γ , then ω is called a fractional polymorphism of Γ ; the set of all fractional polymorphisms of Γ is denoted by fPol (Γ) .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: expl:id
statement_text: Let π^ell _i ∈ mathscr O ^ (ell ) _C be the i -th projection of arity ell , which is given by π^ell _i(x_1, ... ,x_ell ) = x_i . The fractional operation Id _ell of arity ell such that Id _ell (π^ ell _ i ) = frac 1 ell for every i ∈ {1, ... ,ell } is a fractional polymorphism of every valued structure with domain C .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: expl:aut
statement_text: Let Γ be a valued structure and α ∈ Aut (Γ) . The fractional operation ω ∈ mathscr F _C^ (1) defined by ω(α)=1 is a fractional polymorphism of Γ .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: lem:aut
statement_text: Let R ∈ mathscr R ^ (k) _C and let Γ be a valued structure with domain C and an automorphism α ∈ Aut (Γ) which does not preserve R . Then R ∉ Imp ( fPol (Γ)^ (1) ) .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: lem:easy
statement_text: For every valued τ -structure Γ over a countable domain C we have le Γ rangle ⊆ Imp ( fPol (Γ)) .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
statement_text: Let < be the binary relation on {0,1} and Γ_< the valued structure from Example . By definition, Opt (<) ∈ le Γ_< rangle . Denote the minimum operation on {0,1} by min and let ω be a binary fractional operation defined by ω(min )=1 . Note that ω ∈ fPol ({0,1}; Opt (<)) . However, \[< (min ( 0 1 , 0 0 ) )= < (0, 0) = 1,\] while (1/2) · < (0,1) + (1/2) · < (0,0)= 1/2 . This shows that ω does not improve < and hence < ∉ le ({0,1}; Opt (<)) rangle by Lemma .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
statement_text: An operation f colon C^ ell → C for ell ≥ 2 is called cyclic if f(x_1, ... ,x_ ell ) = f(x_2, ... ,x_ ell ,x_1) for all x_1, ... ,x_ ell ∈ C . Let Cyc _C^ (ell ) ⊆ mathscr O _C^ (ell ) be the set of all operations on C of arity ell that are cyclic.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
statement_text: Let G be a permutation group on the set C . An operation f colon C^ ell → C is called pseudo cyclic with respect to G if there are e_1,e_2 ∈ overline G such that for all x_1, ... ,x_ ell ∈ C e_1(f(x_1, ... ,x_ ell )) = e_2(f(x_2, ... ,x_ ell ,x_1)). Let PC _G^ (ell ) ⊆ mathscr O _C^ (ell ) be the set of all operations on C of arity ell that are pseudo cyclic with respect to G .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
statement_text: Let G be a permutation group with domain C . An operation f colon C^ ell → C for ell ≥ 2 is called canonical with respect to G if for all k ∈ N and a^1, ... ,a^ ell ∈ C^k the orbit of the k -tuple f(a^1, ... ,a^ ell ) only depends on the orbits of a^1, ... ,a^ ell with respect to G . Let Can _G^ (ell ) ⊆ mathscr O _C^ (ell ) be the set of all operations on C of arity ell that are canonical with respect to G .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
statement_text: A fractional operation ω is called pseudo cyclic with respect to G if for every A ∈ B( mathscr O _C^ (ell ) ) we have ω(A) = ω(A ∩ PC ^ (ell ) _ G ) . Canonicity with respect to G and cyclicity for fractional operations are defined analogously.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: def:typetemplate
title: Γ^*_ B ,m
statement_text: Let Γ be a valued structure with signature τ such that Aut (Γ) contains the automorphism group of a finitely bounded homogeneous structure B with a finite relational signature. Let m be at least as large as the maximal arity of the relations of Γ . Let Γ^*_ B ,m be the following valued structure. The domain of Γ^*_ B ,m is the set of orbits of m -tuples of Aut ( B ) . For every R ∈ τ of arity k ≤ m the signature of Γ_ B ,m ^* contains a unary relation symbol R^* , which denotes in Γ_ B ,m ^* the unary valued relation that returns on the orbit of an m -tuple t=(t_1, ... , t_m) the value of R^ Γ (t_1, ... ,t_k) (this is well-defined as the value is the same for all representatives t of the orbit). For every p ∈ {1, ... ,m} and i,j colon {1, ... ,p} → {1, ... ,m} there exists a binary relation C_ i,j which returns 0 for two orbits of m -tuples O_1 and O_2 if for every s ∈ O_1 and t ∈ O_2 we have that (s_ i(1) , ... ,s_ i(p) ) and (t_ j(1) , ... ,t_ j(p) ) lie in the same orbit of p -tuples of Aut ( B ) , and returns ∞ otherwise.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: thm:red-fin
statement_text: Let Γ be a valued structure with a finite signature such that Aut (Γ) contains the automorphism group of a finitely bounded homogeneous structure B . Let r be the maximal arity of the relations of B and the valued relations in Γ , let v be the maximal number of variables that appear in a single conjunct of the universal sentence ψ that describes the age of B , and let m ≥ max (r+1,v,3) . Then there is a polynomial-time reduction from VCSP (Γ) to VCSP (Γ^*_ B ,m ) .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: lem:lift
statement_text: Let Γ be a valued structure with a finite signature such that Aut (Γ) contains the automorphism group G of a finitely bounded homogeneous structure B and let m be as in Theorem . Let χ ∈ fPol (Γ^*_ B ,m ) . Then there exists ω ∈ fPol (Γ) which is canonical with respect to G such that ω^* = χ .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: lem:pc
statement_text: Let G be the automorphism group of a homogeneous structure B with a relational signature of maximal arity at most m . If ω ∈ mathscr F _C^ (ell ) is canonical with respect to G such that ω^* (defined on the orbits of m -tuples of G ) is cyclic, then ω is pseudo cyclic with respect to G .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
statement_text: Let ω be a fractional operation of arity ell on a finite domain C . Then the support of ω is the set Supp (ω) = {f ∈ mathscr O ^ (ell ) _C mid ω(f) > 0}. If mathscr F is a set of fractional operations, then Supp (mathscr F) := cup_ ω ∈ mathscr F Supp (ω).

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: lem:h1-transfer
statement_text: Let Γ and Δ be valued structures that are fractionally homomorphically equivalent. If Γ has a cyclic fractional polymorphism, then Δ has a cyclic fractional polymorphism of the same arity. Suppose that the domains of Γ and Δ are finite. If the set Supp ( fPol (Γ)) contains a cyclic operation, then the set Supp ( fPol (Δ)) contains a cyclic operation of the same arity.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: def:core
title: core
statement_text: A valued structure Γ over a finite domain is called a core if all operations in Supp ( fPol (Γ))^ (1) are injective.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: prop:core
statement_text: Let Γ be a valued structure with a finite domain. Then there exists a core valued structure Δ over a finite domain which is fractionally homomorphically equivalent to Γ .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: lem:cyclic-supp
statement_text: Let Γ be a valued structure over a finite domain. Then Γ has a cyclic fractional polymorphism if and only if Supp ( fPol (Γ)) contains a cyclic operation.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: thm:fin-vcsp-tract
statement_text: Let Γ be a valued structure with a finite signature and a finite domain. If ({0,1}; OIT ) does not have a pp-construction in Γ , then Γ has a fractional cyclic polymorphism and VCSP (Γ) is in P, and it is NP-hard otherwise.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: cor:underl-crisp
statement_text: Let Γ be a valued structure with a finite signature and a finite domain. Let C be the underlying crisp structure of Γ . If ({0,1}; OIT ) does not have a pp-construction in C , then Pol ( C ) contains a cyclic operation and VCSP (Γ) is in P, and it is NP-hard otherwise.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: prop:black-box
statement_text: Let B be a finitely bounded homogeneous structure and let Γ be a valued structure with finite relational signature such that Aut ( B ) ⊆ Aut (Γ) . Let m be as in Theorem . Then the following are equivalent. fPol (Γ) contains a fractional operation which is canonical and pseudo cyclic with respect to Aut ( B ) ; fPol (Γ^*_ B ,m ) contains a cyclic fractional operation; Supp ( fPol (Γ^*_ B ,m )) contains a cyclic operation. Supp ( fPol (Γ^*_ B ,m )) contains a Siggers operation.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: thm:tract
statement_text: If the conditions from Proposition hold, then VCSP (Γ) is in P.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: expl:fin-dual
statement_text: The following query is taken from Meliou, Gatterbauer, Moore, and Suciu ; they show how to solve its resilience problem without multiplicities in polynomial time by a reduction to a max-flow problem. Let μ be the query ∃ x,y,z ( R(x,y) wedge S(y,z) ). Observe that a finite τ -structure satisfies μ if and only if it does not have a homomorphism to the τ -structure B with domain B = {0,1} and the relations R^ B = {(0,1),(1,1)} and S^ B = {(0,0),(0,1)} (see Figure ). We turn B into the valued structure Γ with domain {0,1} where R^ Γ (0,1) = R^ Γ (1,1) = 0 = S^ Γ (0,0) = S^ Γ (0,1) and R^ Γ and S^ Γ take value 1 otherwise. Then VCSP (Γ) is precisely the resilience problem for μ (with multiplicities). In Example we reprove the result from that even with multiplicities, the problem can be solved in polynomial time.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: expl:simple-inf
statement_text: Let μ be the conjunctive query ∃ x,y,z (R(x,y) wedge S(x,y,z)). This query is linear in the sense of Freire, Gatterbauer, Immerman, and Meliou and thus its resilience problem without multiplicities can be solved in polynomial time (Theorem 4.5 in ; also see Fact 3.18 in ). In Example we reprove the result from that this problem remains polynomial-time solvable with multiplicities.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: lem:con-aux
statement_text: Let ν_1, ... ,ν_k be conjunctive queries such that ν_i does not imply ν_j if i ≠ j . Then the resilience problem for ν := ν_1 wedge ... wedge ν_k is NP-hard if the resilience problem for one of the ν_i is NP-hard. Conversely, if the resilience problem is in P for each ν_i , then the resilience problem for ν is in P as well. The same is true in the setting without multiplicities and/or exogeneous relations.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: cor:con
statement_text: Let ν_1, ... ,ν_k be conjunctive queries such that ν_i does not imply ν_j if i ≠ j . Let ν = ν_1 wedge ... wedge ν_k and suppose that ν occurs in a union μ of conjunctive queries. For i ∈ {1, ... , k} , let μ_i be the union of queries obtained by replacing ν by ν_i in μ . Then the resilience problem for μ is NP-hard if the resilience problem for one of the μ_i is NP-hard. Conversely, if the resilience problem is in P for each μ_i , then the resilience problem for μ is in P as well. The same is true in the setting without multiplicities and/or exogeneous relations.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
statement_text: The incidence graph of a relational τ -structure A is the bipartite undirected multigraph whose first color class is A , and whose second color class consists of expressions of the form R(b) where R ∈ τ has arity k , b ∈ A^k , and A models R(b) . An edge e_ a,i,R(b) joins a ∈ A with R(b) if b_i = a . A structure is called incidence-acyclic (also known as Berge-acyclic) if its incidence graph is acyclic, i.e., it contains no cycles (if two vertices are linked by two different edges, then they establish a cycle). A structure is called a tree if it is incidence-acyclic and connected in the sense defined in Section .

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: thm:NT
statement_text: A conjunctive query μ has a finite dual if and only if the canonical database of μ is homomorphically equivalent to a tree. A union of conjunctive queries has a finite dual if and only if the canonical database for each of the conjunctive queries is homomorphically equivalent to a tree.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: def:valued-dual
statement_text: Let B be a τ -structure and σ ⊆ τ . Define Γ( B , σ) to be the valued τ -structure on the same domain as B such that for each R ∈ τ \ σ , R^ Γ( B , σ) (a) := 0 if a ∈ R^ B and R^ Γ( B , σ) (a) := 1 otherwise, and for each R ∈ σ , R^ Γ( B , σ) (a) := 0 if a ∈ R^ B and R^ Γ( B , σ) (a) := ∞ otherwise.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: thm:fin-dual
statement_text: Let μ be a union of incidence-acyclic conjunctive queries with relational signature τ and let σ ⊆ τ . Then the resilience problem for μ with exogenous relations from σ is in P or NP-complete. Moreover, it is decidable whether the resilience problem for given μ and σ is in P. If μ is a union of queries each of which is homomorphically equivalent to a tree and B is a finite dual of μ (which exists by Theorem ), then VCSP (Γ( B ,σ)) is polynomial-time equivalent to the resilience problem for μ with exogenous relations from σ .

label: expl:fin-dual-rev
statement_text: We revisit Example . Consider again the conjunctive query ∃ x,y,z (R(x,y) wedge S(y,z)). The fractional operation ω improves both valued relations R and S (they are submodular ; see, e.g., ) and hence is a cyclic fractional polymorphism of Γ . Combining Theorems and , Example reproves the results from (without multiplicities) and (with multiplicities) that the resilience problem for this query is in P.

paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: expl:path
statement_text: Consider for n ≥ 1 the conjunctive query \[μ := ∃ x_0, ... ,x_n (R_1(x_0,x_1) wedge ... wedge R_n(x_ n-1 ,x_n)).\] Let τ={R_1, ... , R_n} be the signature of μ . We describe a finite dual B of μ . The domain B consists of 2^ n-1 elements v_S , which we index by a subset S of {1, ... , n-1} . Then the dual satisfies R_i(v_S,v_T) for S,T ⊆ {1, ... , n-1} and i ∈ {1, ... ,n} if and only if i < n and i ∉ T , or i > 1 and (i-1) ∈ S . To see that B is indeed a dual of μ , let A be a finite relational τ -structure that does not satisfy μ , and let a ∈ A . Let S_a be the set of all elements i ∈ {1, ... , n-1} such that there exist elements a_ i+1 , ... ,a_n ∈ A such that A models R_ i+1 (a,a_ i+1 ) wedge R_ i+2 (a_ i+1 ,a_ i+2 ) wedge ... wedge R_n(a_ n-1 ,a_n). We claim that a mapsto v_ S_a , a ∈ A , defines a homomorphism h from A to B . Suppose that a,b ∈ A are such that R_j(h(a),h(b)) does not hold in B for some j ∈ {1, ... , n} . This implies that j = n and (n-1) ∉ S_a , or j = 1 and 1 ∈ S_b , or j ∈ {2, ... , n-1} , (j-1) ∉ S_a , and j ∈ S_b . In all three cases, the definition of S_a and S_b and A not models μ imply that R_j(a,b) does not hold in A . This shows that h is a homomorphism. Now suppose that A has a homomorphism to B . We have to show that A does not satisfy μ . It suffices to show that B does not satisfy μ . Suppose for contradiction that there are elements v_ S_0 , ... ,v_ S_n such that B satisfies R_1(v_ S_0 ,v_ S_1 ) wedge ... wedge R_n(v_ S_ n-1 ,v_ S_n ) . Then R_n(v_ S_ n-1 ,v_ S_n ) implies that (n-1) ∈ S_ n-1 . By induction, we obtain from R_i(v_ S_ i-1 ,v_ S_i ) that (i-1) ∈ S_ i-1 for every i ∈ {2, ... , n} . In particular, 1 ∈ S_1 . However, note that R_1(v_ S_0 ,v_ S_1 ) by definition implies that 1 ∉ S_1 . We reached a contradiction, hence, B does not satisfy μ . Let f be the symmetric binary operation that maps (v_S,v_T) to v_ S ∪ T , and let g be the symmetric binary operation that maps (v_S,v_T) to v_ S ∩ T . Define the binary symmetric fractional operation ω by setting ω(f)=ω(g)=frac 1 2 . We claim that ω is a fractional polymorphism of Γ( B , ∅ ) . Let i ∈ {1, ... ,n} . We have to show that for all v_S,v_T,v_P,v_Q ∈ B , it holds in Γ that R_i(v_S,v_T)+R_i(v_P,v_Q) & ≥ R_i(f(v_S,v_P),f(v_T,v_Q)) + R_i(g(v_S,v_P),g(v_T,v_Q)) & = R_i(v_ S ∪ P ,v_ T ∪ Q ) + R_i(v_ S ∩ P ,v_ T ∩ Q ) . First suppose that 1<i<n . If the left-hand side in is equal to 2 , then the disequality holds trivially. Whenever the left-hand side in is equal to 1 , we must have (i-1) ∈ S , (i-1) ∈ P , i ∉ T , or i ∉ Q . Hence (i-1) ∈ S ∪ P or i ∉ T ∩ Q . In the first case, we have R_i(v_ S ∪ P ,v_ T ∪ Q ) = 0 , and in the second case we have R_i(v_ S ∩ P ,v_ T ∩ Q ) = 0 , and in both cases holds. Finally, if the left-hand side in is 0 , then R_i(v_S, v_T)=R_i(v_P, v_Q)=0 . Thus we have (i-1) ∈ S or i ∉ T and at the same time (i-1) ∈ P or i ∉ Q . Therefore, we have (i-1) ∈ S ∩ P , i ∉ T ∪ Q , or both (i-1) ∈ S ∪ P and i ∉ T ∩ Q . It follows that R_i(v_ S ∪ P ,v_ T ∪ Q )=R_i(v_ S ∩ P ,v_ T ∩ Q )=0 . The case that i = 1 and the case that i = n can be treated similarly. Therefore, ω is a cyclic fractional polymorphism of Γ( B , ∅ ) , which by Theorem and Theorem implies that the resilience problem for μ is in P.

statement_text: Consider the 2RPQ μ over the signature τ={R,S,T} given by RS^*T . By Lemma , it has a finite dual. Consider the relational structure B with domain {0,1} and relations R^ B = {(0,0),(1,0)} , S^ B = {(0,0),(1,0),(1,1)} , T^ B = {(1,0),(1,1)} (see Figure ). We argue that B is a dual of μ . paper_title: The Complexity of Resilience Problems via Valued Constraint Satisfaction
label: expl:triad
title: Triangle query
statement_text: Let τ be the signature that consists of three binary relation symbols R , S , and T , and let μ be the conjunctive query ∃ x,y,z (R(x,y) wedge S(y,z) wedge T(z,x) ). The resilience problem without multiplicities for μ is NP-complete , and hence VCSP (Γ_ μ ) is NP-hard (Proposition ). Since the Gaifman graph of μ is NP-complete, the structure H _μ from Theorem exists. Let Γ:=Γ( H _μ, ∅ ) . We provide a pp-construction of ({0,1}; OIT ) in Γ , which also proves NP-hardness of VCSP (Γ) and hence the resilience problem of μ with multiplicities by Corollary . Since Γ is homomorphically equivalent to Γ_μ , this also provides a pp-construction of ({0,1}; OIT ) in Γ_μ (see Lemma ). Let C be the domain of Γ . Denote the relations Opt (R) , Opt (S) , Opt (T) by R^* , S^* , T^* , respectively. In the following, for U ∈ {R,S,T} and variables x,y we write 2 U(x,y) for short instead of U(x,y)+U(x,y) . Let φ(a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h,i) be the pp-expression & R(a,b) + 2 S(b,c) + 2 T(c,d) + 2 R(d,e) + 2 S(e,f) + 2 T(f,g) + 2 R(g,h) + S(h,i) + & T^*(i,g) + S^*(h,f) + R^*(g,e) + T^*(f,d) + S^*(e,c) + R^*(d,b) + T^*(c,a). For an illustration of μ and φ , see Figure . Note that φ can be viewed as 7 non-overlapping copies of μ (if we consider the doubled constraints as two separate constraints) with some constraints forbidden to violate. In what follows, we say that an atomic τ -expression holds if it evaluates to 0 and an atomic τ -expression is violated if it does not hold. Since there are 7 non-overlapping copies of μ in φ , the cost of φ is at least 7 . Every assignment where all atoms in hold, and either every atom at even position or every atom at odd position in holds, evaluates φ to 7 and hence is a solution to φ . Let RT ∈ le Γ rangle be given by \[RT(a,b,f,g) := Opt inf _ c,d,e,h,i ∈ C φ.\] Note that RT(a,b,f,g) holds if and only if R(a,b) holds and T(f,g) does not hold, or T(f,g) holds and R(a,b) does not hold, where the reverse implication uses that H _μ is homogeneous and embeds all finite structures that do not satisfy μ . Define RS ∈ le Γ rangle by \[RS(a,b,h,i) := Opt inf _ c,d,e,f,g ∈ C φ.\] Note that RS(a,b,h,i) holds if and only if R(a,b) holds and S(h,i) does not hold, or S(h,i) holds and R(a,b) does not hold. Next, we define the auxiliary relation widetilde RS (a,b,e,f) to be \[ Opt inf _ c,d,g,h,i ∈ C φ. \] Note that widetilde RS (a,b,e,f) holds if and only if both R(a,b) and S(e,f) hold, or neither R(a,b) and nor S(e,f) holds. This allows us to define the relation \[RR(u,v,x,y):= inf _ w,z ∈ C RS(u,v,w,z) + widetilde RS (x,y,w,z)\] which holds if and only if R(u,v) holds and R(x,y) does not hold, or R(x,y) holds and R(u,v) does not hold. Define M ∈ le Γ rangle as M(u,v,u',v',u'',v''):= Opt inf _ x,y,z ∈ C (R(x,y) + S(y,z) + T(z,x) + RR(u,v,x,y) + RS(u',v',y,z) + RT(u'',v'',z,x) ). Note that R(x,y) , S(y,z) and T(z,x) cannot hold at the same time and therefore (u,v,u',v',u'',v'') ∈ M if and only if exactly one of of R(u,v) , R(u',v') , and R(u'',v'') holds. Let Δ be the pp-power of (C;M) of dimension two with signature { OIT } such that OIT ^ Δ ((u,v),(u',v'),(u'',v'')) := M(u,v,u',v',u'',v''). Then Δ is homomorphically equivalent to ({0,1}; OIT ) , witnessed by the homomorphism from Δ to ({0,1}; OIT ) that maps (u,v) to 1 if R(u,v) and to 0 otherwise, and the homomorphism ({0,1}; OIT ) → Δ that maps 1 to any pair of vertices (u,v) ∈ R and 0 to any pair of vertices (u,v) ∉ R . Therefore, Γ pp-constructs ({0,1}; OIT ) .

statement_text: Let C:{0,1}^n → {0,1}^ 2n be a circuit. Let n, T ∈ N be such that T ≥ 4n and let k be the smallest integer such that 2^kn ≥ T . We perform the following computation to obtain GGM _T[C](x) : we set v_ 0,0 :=x , and for each 0 ≤ i <k, 0 ≤ j < 2^i , we set v_ i+1, 2j :=C(v_ i,j )_ [0,n) (i.e. the first half of C(v_ i,j ) ) and v_ i+1, 2j+1 :=C(v_ i,j )_ [n,2n) (i.e. the second half of C(v_ i,j ) ). Finally, we concatenate all values of the leaves and take the first T bits as the output: \[ GGM _T[C](x) := (v_ k,0 ∘ v_ k,1 ∘ ... ∘ v_ k, 2^k-1 )_ [0,T) . \]

title: Poly-time uniform family of quantum circuits
statement_text: A family of quantum circuits { V_n }_ n ∈ N is said to be uniformly generated in polynomial time if there exists a polynomially bounded function t: N mapsto N and a deterministic Turing machine M acting as follows. For every n -bit input x , M outputs in time t(n) a description of a quantum circuit V_n (consisting of 1 -and 2 -qubit gates) that takes the all-zeros state as ancilla and outputs a single qubit. We say V_n accepts ( rejects ) if measuring its output qubit in the computational basis yields 1 ( 0 ).

statement_text: Let us define three types of quantum circuits: bf Unitary quantum circuit . A unitary quantum circuit consists of a sequence of unitary quantum gates, each of which belongs to some fixed gate set that is universal for quantum computation, such as {normal sc H xspace , normal sc CNOT xspace , normal sc T xspace } . bf Almost-unitary quantum circuit . An almost-unitary quantum circuit generalizes a unitary quantum circuit acting on O(s(n)) qubits by allowing O(s(n)) single-qubit measurement gates normal sc M xspace in the computational basis, which are defined by a pinching channel : See Section 4.1.1 (particularly Definition 4.4) in for further details. This type of channel, also referred to as a completely phase-damping channel, is discussed in . \[Φ^ normal sc M xspace (ρ) coloneqq ket 0 bra 0 Tr rbra * M_0 ρ + ket 1 bra 1 Tr rbra * M_1 ρ , where M_b coloneqq ket b bra b for b ∈ {0,1}.\] bf Isometric quantum circuit . An isometric quantum circuit extends a unitary quantum circuit acting on O(s(n)) qubits by allowing O(s(n)) ancillary gates. An ancillary gate is a non-unitary gate that takes no input and produces a single qubit in the state ket 0 as output. For convenience, we treat almost-unitary quantum circuits as a special case of isometric quantum circuits. More specifically, by applying the principle of deferred measurements (e.g., ) to an almost-unitary quantum circuit, we obtain an isometric quantum circuit in which each measurement gate is simulated by an ancillary gate, and all ancillary qubits are measured at the end. For a promise problem I = ( I _ rm yes , I _ rm no ) , a family of unitary, almost-unitary, or isometric quantum circuits {C_x: x ∈ I } is called s(n) -space-bounded if there is a deterministic Turing machine that, given any input x ∈ I with input length n coloneqq |x| , runs in space O(s(n)) (and hence time 2^ O(s(n)) ) and outputs a description of C_x , where C_x accepts if x ∈ I _ rm yes , rejects if x ∈ I _ rm no , acts on O(s(n)) qubits, and consists of 2^ O(s(n)) gates.

statement_text: An algebraic branching program (ABP) with unrestricted weights of depth D and width ≤ r , on the variables x_1, ... ,x_n , is a directed acyclic graph such that: The vertices are partitioned into D+1 layers V_0, ... ,V_D , so that V_0={s} ( s is the source node), and V_D={t} ( t is the sink node). Further, each edge goes from V_ i-1 to V_ i for some 0< i ≤ D . max |V_i| ≤ r . Each edge e is weighted with a polynomial f_e ∈ F [ overline x ] . The bf (individual) degree d of the ABP is the maximum (individual) degree of the edge polynomials f_e . The bf size of the ABP is the product n · r · d · D . Each s - t path is said to compute the polynomial which is the product of the labels of its edges, and the algebraic branching program itself computes the sum over all s - t paths of such polynomials. The following are restricted ABP variants: An algebraic branching program is said to be bf oblivious if for every layer ell , all the edge labels in that layer are univariate polynomials in a single variable x_ i_ell . An oblivious branching program is said to be a bf read-once oblivious ABP (up bf roABP ) if each x_i appears in the edge label of exactly one layer, so that D=n . That is, each x_i appears in the edge labels in exactly one layer. The layers thus define a bf variable order , which will be assumed to be x_1< ... <x_n unless otherwise specified.

label: ex:example_I4
statement_text: Consider the template (Q;I_4) , where I_4 is defined by \[I_4 mathrel mathop : mathrel mkern -1.2mu = { (x,y,u,v) mid x=y ⇒ u=v}.\] Its CSP is solvable in Datalog (Sections and ). Since CSP xspace ( K _3) is not, and pp-constructions provide Datalog-reductions , it follows that ( Q ;I_4) does not pp-construct K _3 . Hence, its polymorphisms satisfy the pseudo-Siggers identity by the above-mentioned theorem of Barto and Pinsker. However, any polymorphism of I_4 is injective up to dummy variables , and hence cannot satisfy the Siggers identity. This makes it clear that the characterization of tractability of CSPs by the Siggers identity cannot be lifted from finite to infinite domains.

statement_text: theorem sandwichthm Let A be a non-contractible reduct of a countable finitely bounded homogeneous structure B . J is correct as a reduction from CSP xspace ( A ) to PCSP xspace ( S _1, S _2) when limited to instances X with the property that X homomorphically maps to A if and only if X homomorphically maps to a substructure of A of size ≤ n . Every finite cheese for PCSP xspace ( S _1, S _2) pp-constructs K _3 ; thus PCSP xspace ( S _1, S _2) is not finitely tractable. A pp-constructs K _3 if and only if A ' pp-constructs K _3 . If A is a model-complete core, then A ' is a model-complete core as well. If B is Ramsey, then B ' is Ramsey as well.

Since smash A ^ [d] → A ^ [d] / small Aut ( B ) , the structure A ^ [d] _S is a finite cheese for PCSP xspace ( S , A ^ [d] / small Aut ( B ) ) . We claim that CSP xspace ( A ^ [d] _S) is tractable, and hence this PCSP is finitely tractable. To see this, recall from Example that the n -ary minimum operation is a polymorphism of A for every n ≥ 2 . This operation is conservative : min {x_1, ... ,x_n} ⊆ {x_1, ... , x_n} holds for all x_1, ... ,x_n . Hence, its restriction to A_S^2 induces a polymorphism of A _S , which itself induces a polymorphism of A ^ [d] _S through its component-wise action. Since this operation is cyclic, A ^ [d] _S does not pp-construct K _3 , and hence we are done by Theorem . This issue cannot be fixed simply by taking an expansion of A by the inequality relation ≠ because CSP xspace ( A ; ≠ ) is NP-complete .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: def:span-program
title: Span programs
statement_text: A span program consists of the following mathematical objects: The it state space : A Hilbert space H of finite dimension. The it domain : A finite set D , whose elements are referred to as it inputs . The it input-dependent subspaces : to every input x ∈ D , we associate an input-dependent subspace H (x) ⊆ H . The it input-independent subspace : A subspace K ⊆ H . The it initial vector : 0 ≠ |w_0 rangle ∈ K ^ perp . Then, P = ( H , x mapsto H (x), K , |w_0 rangle ) is a span program on D . We make a distinction between positive and negative inputs, as such: x ∈ D is a it positive input , if |w_0 rangle ∈ K + H (x) . x ∈ D is a it negative input , if |w_0 rangle ∉ K + H (x) . Finally, we let f : D → {0,1} be the function that evaluates to 1 if and only if the input x ∈ D is positive. We say that P computes f .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: def:witnesses
title: Span program witnesses
statement_text: Let P = ( H , x mapsto H (x), K , |w_0 rangle ) be a span program on D that computes f . Then, If x ∈ D is a positive input, then every vector |w_x rangle ∈ H (x) that satisfies |w_x rangle - |w_0 rangle ∈ K is a positive witness for x . We write W _+(x, P ) for the set of these vectors. The positive witness complexity for x is the minimal norm-squared of such vectors, and it's denoted by w_+(x, P ) , which is ∞ if such a vector does not exist. If x ∈ D is a negative input, then every vector |w_x rangle ∈ K ^ perp ∩ H (x)^ perp for which lew_xmiddle |w_0 rangle = 1 is a negative witness for x . We write W _-(x, P ) for the set of these vectors. The negative witness complexity for x is the minimal norm-squared of such vectors, and it's denoted by w_-(x, P ) , which is ∞ if such a vector does not exist. We define the positive and negative witness complexity, W_+( P ) and W_-( P ) , respectively, as \[W_+( P ) = max _ x ∈ f^ -1 (1) w_+(x, P ), qquad and qquad W_-( P ) = max _ x ∈ f^ -1 (0) w_-(x, P ),\] and we define the span program complexity, C( P ) , as \[C( P ) = sqrt W_+( P ) · W_-( P ) .\]

title: Properties of scalar multiplication of span programs

W _-(x,α P ) = W _-(x, P )/α , and so w_-(x,α P ) = w_-(x, P )/α . W_+(α P ) = α W_+( P ) , W_-(α P ) = W_-( P )/α , and so C(α P ) = C( P ) . If P computes f , then so does α P .

statement_text: Let G = (V,E) be an undirected graph, with it resistances r : E → [0, ∞ ] . With every edge e ∈ E , we associate a default direction, i.e., it has a head e_+ and a tail e_- . Every function f : E → C that satisfies f_e = 0 if r_e = ∞ is a it flow on G .
