For every ell ∈ [d] , let k_ ell be the maximum number of children of nodes in the (ell -1) th vertex layer. We use a Hilbert space C ^ [k_1] ∪ {bot } ⊗ ... ⊗ C ^ [k_d] ∪ {bot } , with dimension K = (k_1+1) ... (k_d+1) . Every node u in T is connected to its root by a unique path. If u is in the ell th vertex layer, we write u = (j_1, ... , j_ell ) , if u is reached through starting at the root node and taking the j_ ell ' th child at the (ell '-1) th vertex layer, for all ell ' ∈ [ell ] . Moreover, since every leaf u = (j_1, ... , j_d) is uniquely labeled by a singleton {e} , we identify \[ |e rangle := |j_1, ... , j_d rangle .\] Next, let an internal node u ∈ V be labeled by E_u , and let u_1, ... , u_k be its children, labeled by E_ u_1 , ... , E_ u_k . Suppose that G|_ E_ u_1 , ... , G|_ E_ u_k is a parallel decomposition of G|_ E_u , with source and sink nodes s and t . For all j ∈ [k] , we write \[ |ψ_u rangle := Σ _ j=1 ^k frac 1 | |f_ u,j rangle | |j rangle , qquad with qquad |f_ u,j rangle := |f^ min _ G|_ E_ u_j , s, t, r|_ E_ u_j rangle .\] Now, for every ell ∈ [d] , we write the operation E _ ell that for all u = (j_1, ... , j_ ell -1 ) in the (ell -1) th layer of T acts for all j ∈ [k] , \[ E _ ell : |j_1, ... ,j_ ell -1 rangle |j rangle |bot rangle ^ ⊗ (d-ell ) mapsto |j_1, ... ,j_ ell -1 rangle |j rangle |bot rangle ^ ⊗ (d-ell ) , & if u is the root of a tree decomposition , |j_1, ... ,j_ ell -1 rangle |j rangle frac |f_ u,j rangle | |f_ u,j rangle | , & otherwise . \] Similarly, for all ell ∈ [d] , we write U_ ell as the operation that for all u = (j_1, ... , j_ ell -1 ) in the (ell -1) th layer of T acts as \[U_ ell : |j_1, ... ,j_ ell -1 rangle |bot rangle |bot rangle ^ ⊗ (d-ell ) mapsto |j_1, ... ,j_ ell -1 rangle |bot rangle |bot rangle ^ ⊗ (d-ell ) , & if u is the root of a tree decomposition , |j_1, ... , j_ ell -1 rangle |ψ_u rangle |bot rangle ^ ⊗ (d-ell ) , & otherwise . \] Then, we can implement the reflection through C _ G,r in the circuit model with two calls to all the E _ ell 's and U_ ell 's, and widetilde O (d log (K)) auxiliary elementary gates.

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:circulation-space-reflection-implementation
statement_text: Let G = (V,E) be a graph with resistances r : E → R _ >0 , and let T be a tree-parallel decomposition of G , with depth d . For every ell ∈ [d] , let k_ ell be the maximum number of children nodes of vertices in the (ell -1) th vertex layer, and let K = (k_1 + 1) ... (k_d + 1) . Then, we can implement R_ C _ G,r in the QROM-model with widetilde O (|E|K) ⊆ widetilde O (|E|^ d+1 ) bits of QROM, and widetilde O (d log (K)) ⊆ widetilde O (d^2 log |E|) elementary gates.

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
statement_text: Let G = (V,E) be an undirected multigraph with resistances r : E → R _ >0 , and s,t ∈ V with s ≠ t . Let D ⊆ {0,1}^n and for all e ∈ E , let j(e) ∈ [n] and b(e) ∈ {0,1} . We refer to G = (G,j,b,r) as an st -connectivity graph on D , and we say that it computes the function f : D → {0,1} , where f(x) = 1 if and only if s and t are connected along the graph G(x) = (V,E(x)) , where E(x) = {e ∈ E : x_ j(e) = b(e)} . We let w_+(x, G ) = R_ G(x),s,t,r , and w_-(x, G ) = R_ G,s,t,r' ^ -1 , where r'(e) = r(e)^ -1 if x_ j(e) ≠ b(e) , and 0 otherwise. We say that the complexity of G is \[C( G ) = sqrt max _ x ∈ f^ -1 (1) w_+(x, G ) · max _ x ∈ f^ -1 (0) w_-(x, G ) .\] Finally, for any boolean function f : D → {0,1} with D ⊆ {0,1}^n , we write st (f) for the minimal complexity C( G ) of an st -connectivity graph G that computes f .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:st-connectivity
statement_text: Let n ∈ N and D ⊆ {0,1}^n . Every st -connectivity graph G = (G,j,e,r) on D can be turned into a graph composition P on D , such that C( P ) = C( G ) .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: lem:planar-dual-circulation-space
statement_text: Let G = (V,E) be a connected, undirected, planar graph, where every edge e ∈ E has an implicit direction meaning that it goes from e_- to e_+ . Let G^ dagger = (F^ dagger ,E^ dagger ) be a planar dual of G , where every edge e is associated to a dual edge e^ dagger ∈ E^ dagger , that points from the face on the left of e to the face on the right of e , as seen from the perspective of traversing e in its implicit direction. Moreover, let r : E → [0, ∞ ] be resistances on G , and let r^ dagger : E^ dagger → [0, ∞ ] be defined by r^ dagger _ e^ dagger = 1/r_e . Then, by identifying |e^ dagger rangle = |e rangle , and as such identifying H _ G^ dagger = H _G , we find that \[ H _G = C _ G,r ⊕ C _ G^ dagger ,r^ dagger = H _ G^ dagger .\]

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:dual-graph-composition
statement_text: Let G = (V,E) be a connected, undirected graph with s,t ∈ V and s ≠ t , such that G ∪ {(s,t)} is planar. Let G^ dagger = (F^ dagger ,E^ dagger ) be a planar dual of G ∪ {(s,t)} with the dual edge of (s,t) , connecting s^ dagger and t^ dagger , removed. For all e ∈ E we denote its dual edge by e^ dagger , we let P be the span program formed by taking the graph composition of G with the span programs ( P _e)_ e ∈ E , and we let P ^ dagger be the graph composition of G^ dagger with span programs ( ¬ P _e)_ e^ dagger ∈ E^ dagger . Then, ¬ P = P ^ dagger .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: def:logical-compositions
title: AND- and OR-composition
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , and P _1, ... , P _n be span programs on D . We define two special types of graph compositions: Let G be a line graph with n edges, and let s and t be the endpoints. We let P be the graph composition of G with span programs P _1, ... , P _n on the edges, and we write P = wedge_ j=1 ^n P _j . We refer to this as the AND-composition of P _1, ... , P _n . Let G be a graph with 2 nodes, s and t , and n parallel edges between them. We let P be the graph composition with span programs P _1, ... , P _n on the edges, and we write P = vee_ j=1 ^n P _j . We refer to this construction as the OR-composition of P _1, ... , P _n .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:and-or-witness-sizes
title: Witness sizes of AND- and OR-composition
statement_text: Let P _1, ... , P _n be span programs on a common domain D . Then, for all x ∈ D , we have \[w_+ (x, wedge_ j=1 ^n P _j ) = Σ _ j=1 ^n w_+(x, P _j), qquad and qquad w_- (x, wedge_ j=1 ^n P _j ) = [ Σ _ j=1 ^n frac 1 w_-(x, P _j) ]^ -1 ,\] and \[w_+ (x, vee_ j=1 ^n P _j ) = [ Σ _ j=1 ^n frac 1 w_+(x, P _j) ]^ -1 , qquad and qquad w_- (x, vee_ j=1 ^n P _j ) = Σ _ j=1 ^n w_-(x, P _j).\]

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
title: Variable-time search
statement_text: Let P _1, ... , P _n be span programs on a common domain D . Then, \[ P = vee_ j=1 ^n frac P _j W_+( P _j) qquad ⇒ qquad C ( P )^2 ≤ Σ _ j=1 ^n C( P _j)^2.\]

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:variable-time-formula-evaluation
title: Variable-time formula evaluation
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , D ⊆ {0,1}^n , and φ : D → {0,1} be a boolean formula. Let J(φ) be the multiset of the indices being queried by φ , e.g., J((x_ j_1 ∧ x_ j_2 ) ∨ ( ¬ x_ j_1 ∧ ¬ x_ j_2 )) = {j_1,j_2,j_1,j_2} . Let P _1, ... , P _n be span programs on D , such that P _j computes the j th bit of x ∈ D . Then we can build a graph composition P on D of a series-parallel graph G that computes φ with complexity \[C( P )^2 ≤ Σ _ j ∈ J(φ) C( P _j)^2.\] Moreover, in the QROM-model, we can implement the reflection through the circulation space using a QROM with widetilde O (|J(φ)|^ d+1 ) bits, and with widetilde O (d^2 log |J(φ)| ) elementary gates, where d is the depth of the AND-OR-tree representation of φ .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: def:divide-and-conquer
title: Quantum divide and conquer,
statement_text: Let a,b,n ∈ N , Σ a finite alphabet, and Λ a finite parameter space. For all m ∈ N and λ ∈ Λ , let f_m^ λ : Σ^n → {0,1} , f_m^ λ, aux : Σ^n → {0,1} , m_1, ... , m_a ∈ Θ(m/b) , λ_1, ... , λ_a ∈ Λ , and φ_m^ λ : {0,1}^ a+1 → {0,1} be a boolean read-once formula, i.e., where each variable appears exactly once, such that there exists a m_0 ∈ N , such that for all m ≥ m_0 and x ∈ Σ^n , \[f_m^ λ (x) = φ_m^ λ (f_ m_1 ^ λ_1 (x), ... , f_ m_a ^ λ_a (x), f_m^ λ, aux (x)).\] This defines a it quantum divide and conquer strategy for {f_m^ λ }_ m ∈ N , λ ∈ Λ .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:divide-and-conquer
statement_text: Consider a quantum divide and conquer strategy for a family of functions {f_m^ λ }_ m ∈ N , λ ∈ Λ , in the sense of cref def:divide-and-conquer . For all m ∈ N , let P _m^ λ, aux be a span program that evaluates f_m^ λ, aux , and for all m < m_0 , let P _m^ λ be a span program evaluating f_m^ λ . Now, we can build a family of graph compositions ( P _m^ λ )_ m ∈ N , λ ∈ Λ , where for all m ≥ m_0 , P _m^ λ evaluates f_m^ λ , and satisfies \[C( P _m^ λ )^2 ≤ Σ _ j=1 ^a C( P _ m_j ^ λ_j )^2 + C( P _m^ λ, aux )^2.\] Moreover, in the QROM-model, the complexity of implementing the reflection through the circulation space, in the graph composition for P _m^ λ , can be done with a QROM of size widetilde O ( poly (a^ log (m)/ log (b) )) and using widetilde O (( log (m)/ log (b))^2 log (a)) elementary gates.

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:savitch
statement_text: There is an st -connectivity algorithm that solves the directed st -connectivity problem making O( sqrt 2n ^ log (n) ) queries, with widetilde O ( sqrt 2n ^ log (n) ) elementary gates, and using O( log ^2(n)) space.

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
title: Extended learning graphs
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , D ⊆ {0,1}^n , and f : D → {0,1} . We need the following ingredients: A directed acyclic graph G = (V,E) . Labels S : V → 2^ [n] , such that: There is a unique r(G) ∈ V with S(r(G)) = varnothing . For all (u,v) = e ∈ E , there exists a j ∈ [n] such that j ∉ S(u) and S(v) = S(u) ∪ {j} . A weight function w : D × E × {0,1} → R _ ≥ 0 , such that for all (u,v) = e ∈ E , j ∈ [n] such that S(v) = S(u) ∪ {j} and b ∈ {0,1} : For all x,y ∈ D , we have x_ S(v) = y_ S(v) implies w(x,e,b) = w(y,e,b) . For all (x,y) ∈ f^ -1 (1) × f^ -1 (0) , x_ S(u) = y_ S(u) and x_j ≠ y_j implies w(x,e,0) = w(y,e,1) . Finally, for all y ∈ f^ -1 (1) , let p_y : E → R _ ≥ 0 be a unit flow on G , with: A single source node r(G) . The sink nodes are all the nodes v ∈ V for which S(v) contains a 1 -certificate for y . for all e ∈ E , w(y,e,1) = 0 implies p_y(e) = 0 . Then L = (G,S,w,{p_y}_ y ∈ f^ -1 (1) ) is an it adaptive learning graph that computes f . For all x ∈ f^ -1 (0) and y ∈ f^ -1 (1) , respectively, we define \[ell _-(x,L) = Σ _ e ∈ E w(x,e,0), qquad and qquad ell _+(x,L) = Σ _ e ∈ E frac p_y(e)^2 w(y,e,1) ,\] and we define \[ L _-(L) = max _ x ∈ f^ -1 (0) ell _-(x,L), qquad L _+(L) = max _ x ∈ f^ -1 (1) ell _+(x,L), qquad and qquad L (L) = sqrt L _-(L) · L _+(L) .\] Finally, we write XLG (f) as the minimum of L (L) over all adaptive learning graphs L that compute f .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:extended-learning-graphs
statement_text: Let L be an extended learning graph. Then, we can construct an instance of the st -connectivity framework that evaluates the learning graph, with complexity at most L (L) . As such, for all f : {0,1}^n ⊇ D → {0,1} , st (f) ≤ L (f) .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
title: Decision tree + guessing algorithm complexity
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , D ⊆ {0,1}^n and f : D → {0,1} . Let T = (V,E) be a decision tree computing f , and let G : E → {0,1} be a guessing algorithm, such that for every internal node v ∈ V , exactly one of its children is connected with an edge e ∈ E for which G(e) = 1 . Then, we write T (T) for the depth of T , and the G (T) for the maximum number of edges e ∈ E along a path from the root to a leaf that satisfy G(e) = 0 . We call G (T) the guessing complexity of T . Finally, we write \[ sqrt GT (f) = min _ T computing f sqrt G (T) · T (T) .\]

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: def:weighted-decision-tree
title: Weighted-decision-tree complexity
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , D ⊆ {0,1}^n and f : D → {0,1} . Let T = (V,E) be a decision tree computing f , and w : E → R _ ≥ 0 a weight functions on the edges. For every input x ∈ D , let P _x be the path taken on input x , and let overline P _x be the set of edges that have exactly one node in common with the vertices traversed in P _x . Then, we define \[ WDT _+( T ,w) = max _ x ∈ f^ -1 (1) Σ _ e ∈ P _x w_e, qquad WDT _-( T ,w) = max _ x ∈ f^ -1 (0) Σ _ e ∈ overline P _x frac 1 w_e ,\] and WDT ( T ,w) = sqrt WDT _+( T ,w) · WDT _-( T ,w) . Moreover, we let \[ WDT ( T ) = min _ w : E → R _ ≥ 0 WDT ( T ,w), qquad and qquad WDT (f) = min _ T computing f WDT ( T ).\]

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: def:zero-error
title: Zero-error version of the complexity measures
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , D ⊆ {0,1}^n , and f : D → {0,1} . Let T = {T_1, ... , T_k} be a set of decision trees, where every leaf is labeled with 0 , 1 , or tt ? . Let p= (p_1, ... , p_k) be a probability distribution on [k] , such that for all x ∈ D , if we sample T_j with j p , then the probability that it outputs ¬ f(x) is 0 , and the probability that it outputs tt ? is at most 1/2 . Then, we say that T computes f with zero error, and we write \[ sqrt GT ( T ) = max _ j ∈ [k] sqrt G (T_j) · T (T_j) , qquad and qquad sqrt GT _0(f) = min _ T computes f with zero error sqrt GT ( T ).\] and \[ WDT ( T ) = max _ j ∈ [k] WDT (T_j), qquad and qquad WDT _0(f) = min _ T computes f with zero error WDT ( T ).\]

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:weighted-decision-trees
statement_text: Let T = (V,E) be a decision tree, making queries to an n -bit string, having outputs in {0,1,tt ? } , and with a weight function w : E → R _ >0 on the edges. Then, we can construct an instance of the st -connectivity framework that distinguishes whether the output of the tree is 1 or an element of {0,tt ? } with complexity at most WDT ( T ,w) .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:st-to-WDT0
statement_text: Let f : D → {0,1} with D ⊆ {0,1}^n . We have st (f) ≤ sqrt 2 WDT _0(f) .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:phase-estimation-algo
statement_text: Every span program, evaluated on an input x , is also a phase estimation algorithm, and the span program's positive and negative witnesses are negative and positive witnesses of the phase estimation algorithm, respectively.

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:subspace-graph
statement_text: Every graph composition can be turned into a subspace graph with at most the same witness sizes.

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:threshold
title: Threshold functions through the st -connectivity framework
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , and k ∈ {1, ... , n} . Let f_n^k be the threshold function on n bits with threshold k , i.e., f_n^k(x) = 1 if and only if |x| ≥ k . Let x_j be a trivial span program computing the j th bit of the input. Then, for all S ⊆ [n] , we recursively define \[ Th _ S ^ k+1 = vee_ j ∈ S (x_j ∧ k Th _ S \ {j} ^k), qquad and qquad Th _ S ^1 = vee_ j ∈ S x_j.\] Then, Th _n^k := Th _ [n] ^k computes f_n^k , with witness sizes \[w_+(x, Th _n^k) = frac 1 |x|-k+1 , & if |x| ≥ k, ∞ , & otherwise , qquad and qquad w_-(x, Th _n^k) = ∞ , & if |x| ≥ k, frac k(n-k+1) k-|x| , & otherwise . \] Consequently, C( Th _n^k) = sqrt k(n+k-1) , and this is optimal.

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:exact-weight
title: Graph-composition for the exact-weight function
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , k ∈ {1, ... , n-1} , and let f_n^k be the exact-weight function on n bits with weight k , i.e., f_n^k(x) = 1 if and only if |x| = k . We let \[ EW _n^k = k(n+k-1) Th _n^k ∧ ¬ Th _n^ k+1 .\] Then, EW _n^k computes f_n^k , with witness sizes \[w_+(x, EW _n^k) = n + 2k(n-k), & if |x| = k, ∞ , & otherwise , qquad and qquad w_-(x, EW _n^k) = ∞ , & if |x| = k, frac 1 |k-|x|| , & otherwise . \] Consequently, C( EW _n^k) = sqrt n + 2k(n-k) , and this is optimal.

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: lem:gapped-majority
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , D = {x ∈ {0,1}^n : |x| < n/3 ∨ |x| > 2n/3} , and f_n : D → {0,1} be defined as f_n(x) = 1 if and only if |x| > 2n/3 . That is, f_n is the gapped majority function on n inputs. Then, st (f_n) ∈ O(1) , and R _0(f_n) ∈ Ω(n) .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:st-vs-R
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , D ⊆ {0,1}^n and f : D → {0,1} . Then, st (f) ∈ O( R (f)) .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:weighted-decision-tree-complexity
statement_text: Let f : D → {0,1} with D ⊆ {0,1}^n . Then D (f) ≤ WDT (f)^2 .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: cor:R0-WDT02
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , D ⊆ {0,1}^n , and f : D → {0,1} . Then, R _0(f) ≤ WDT _0(f)^2 .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:GT-ub-WDT
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , D ⊆ {0,1}^n , and f : D → {0,1} . Then, sqrt GT (f) ≤ WDT (f)^ 3/2 and sqrt GT _0(f) ≤ WDT _0(f)^ 3/2 .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:GT-sep-WDT
statement_text: Let n ∈ N and f : {0,1}^ 2n+1 → {0,1} be defined as \[f(x) = x_2 ⊕ x_3 ⊕ ... ⊕ x_ n+1 , & if x_1 = 1, x_2 ∨ x_3 ∨ ... ∨ x_ n^2+1 , & if x_1 = 0. .\] Then, WDT (f) ∈ O(n) and sqrt GT _0(f) ∈ Ω(n^ 3/2 ) .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: lem:deterministic-sample
title: Deterministic sample
statement_text: Let Σ a finite alphabet of constant size, m,n ∈ N and y ∈ Σ^m aperiodic, i.e., there does not exist a p ≤ m/2 such that y_ kp+ell = y_ell for all ell ∈ [p] and 0 ≤ k ≤ lfloor (n-ell )/prfloor . Then, there exists a subset J ⊆ [m] and integer 0 ≤ k ≤ m/2 such that |J| ≤ log (m) , and such that if x[j:j+m-1] agrees with y on J , with j ∈ [n-m+1] , then for any non-zero integer max {0,-k} ≤ ell ≤ min {m/2-k,n-m+1} , x[j+ell :j+m-1+ell ] does not agree with y .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:aperiodic-pattern-matching
title: Quantum algorithm for aperiodic pattern matching
statement_text: Let Σ be a finite alphabet of constant size, and y ∈ Σ^m an aperiodic pattern. We can solve the aperiodic pattern matching problem with O( sqrt n log (m) ) queries to the input string x ∈ Σ^n , widetilde O ( sqrt n ) elementary gates, and a QROM of size O(m) .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:pattern-matching
title: Quantum algorithm for pattern matching
statement_text: Let Σ be a finite alphabet of constant size, n,m ∈ N and y ∈ Σ^m be a periodic pattern with period p , and k = lceil m/prceil ≥ 2 (partial) repetitions. Then, we can solve the pattern matching problem with O( sqrt n log (p) ) queries to the input string x ∈ Σ^n .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
title: The OR ∘ pSEARCH -problem
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , and let D _n ⊆ {0,1,*}^n , such that x ∈ D _n if and only if x has exactly one position j(x) ∈ [n] for which x_ j(x) ≠ * . The pSEARCH -problem asks to output the value of x_ j(x) , given query access to x . Next, let m ∈ N , T ∈ {m,m+1, ... ,nm} and let D _T ⊆ D _n^m , such that (x^ (1) , ... , x^ (m) ) ∈ D _T if and only if j(x^ (1) ) + ... + j(x^ (m) ) = T and |overline x | ∈ {0,1} , where \[overline x = x^ (1) _ j(x^ (1) ) ... x^ (m) _ j(x^ (m) ) ∈ {0,1}^m.\] The OR ∘ pSEARCH -problem asks to output |overline x | , given query-access to x ∈ D _T .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:or-psearch
statement_text: There is a quantum algorithm that solves the OR ∘ pSEARCH -problem with O( sqrt T log (T) ) queries, which is tight up to constants, widetilde O ( sqrt T ) elementary gates, and a QROM of size widetilde O (T) .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
title: The Σ^*20^*2Σ^* -problem
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , Σ = {0,1,2} and x ∈ Σ^n . The Σ^*20^*2Σ^* -problem asks whether x is recognized by the regular language Σ^*20^*2Σ^* , i.e., whether there exist j_1,j_2 ∈ [n] such that j_1 < j_2 , x_ j_1 = x_ j_2 = 2 , and x_k = 0 for all k ∈ {j_1+1, ... , j_2-1} .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: thm:202
statement_text: There is a quantum algorithm that evaluates the Σ^*20^*2Σ^* -problem using O( sqrt n log (n) ) queries, and it can be implemented in time widetilde O ( sqrt n ) .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
title: Bounded-depth Dyck language recognition problem
statement_text: Let k ∈ N , and Σ = {tt ( ,tt ) } . For any finite string x ∈ Σ^* , we define w(x) = |x^ -1 (tt ( )| - |x^ -1 (tt ) )| , i.e., the difference of the number of opening and closing brackets in x . The Dyck language of depth k contains all words x ∈ Σ^* , for which w(x) = 0 , and any prefix x' (i.e., any substring at the start of x ) satisfies 0 ≤ w(x') ≤ k . For any even n ∈ N , the depth- k Dyck language recognition problem now asks to determine for a length- n input x ∈ Σ^n , whether it is in the depth- k Dyck language, given query-access to x .

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
statement_text: There exists a graph composition algorithm for recognizing the Dyck language of depths 1 and 2 , making O( sqrt n ) queries and spending widetilde O ( sqrt n ) time.

paper_title: Quantum algorithms through graph composition
label: lem:dyck3-properties
statement_text: Let n ∈ N even, and x ∈ Σ^n . Then x is not a Dyck word of depth 3 if and only if at least one of the following four statements is true: There is a j ∈ [n] such that j is odd, x_j = tt ) , and for all k ∈ [j-1] , x_k = tt ) if and only if k is even. There is a j ∈ [n] such that j is even, x_j = tt ( , and for all k ∈ {j+1, ... , n} , x_k = tt ( if and only if k is odd. paper_title: Collapsing Catalytic Classes
label: def:cspace-variants

statement_text: For a boolean function f , we say a catalytic machine computes f if sf (deterministic machine) for every x , the machine outputs f(x) . sf (non-deterministic machine) for every x , if f(x)=1 then there is a sequence on non-deterministic choices where the machine accepts x , and if f(x)=0 then for any sequence on non-deterministic choices the machine rejects. A sf co-non-deterministic machine must always accept when f(x)=1 and sometimes reject when f(x)=0 . sf (bounded-error randomized machine) for every x , the machine outputs f(x) with probability at least 2/3 over its random choices. sf (unbounded-error randomized machine) for every x , the machine outputs f(x) with probability greater than 1/2 over its random choices.

paper_title: Collapsing Catalytic Classes
statement_text: Let M be a catalytic machine with work space s and catalytic space c . We denote by le π,u rangle the configuration of M where π ∈ {0,1}^c is contained on the catalytic tape and u ∈ {0,1}^s is on its work tape.

paper_title: Collapsing Catalytic Classes
label: definition_config_graphs
title: Configuration graphs
statement_text: The sf configuration graph G _ M,x is the directed acyclic graph where each node corresponds to a configuration of M on input x , where there is a directed edge from le π,u rangle to le π',u' rangle iff le π',u' rangle can be reached from le π,u rangle in one execution step of M . The out-degree of every vertex in G _ M,x is at most 2, and there is some fixed constant d_M depending only on M such that each vertex in G _ M,x has in-degree at most d_M-2 . We call the outgoing edges sf forward edges of le τ,v rangle . The remaining edges of le τ,v rangle are sf backward edges. A halting configuration has no forward edges in G _ M,x . We say an edge (v,v') is labeled with b ∈ {0,1} if it corresponds to a non-deterministic/randomized b -choice of the machine. For deterministic transitions we label the edge with both 0 and 1 . For every catalytic tape τ let G _ M,x,τ be the subgraph of G _ M,x induced on configurations of G _ M,x that are reachable from normal start _ M,x,τ . Clearly G _ M,x,τ has one source node, namely normal start _ M,x,τ , and up to two sink nodes, namely normal acc _ M,x,τ and normal rej _ M,x,τ .

paper_title: Collapsing Catalytic Classes
title: 0 -graph of configuration graphs
statement_text: Given a configuration graph G _ M,x , we let the sf 0 -graph G ^0_ M,x be the undirected graph where only edges with label 0 are retained, and we forget the direction of each edge. Observe that for every τ and v ∈ G _ M,x,τ , G ^0_ M,x (v) is a tree as each node has at most one forward edge corresponding to the edge labeled 0 in G _ M,x . Given a configuration v , we let G ^0_ M,x (v) be the connected component of G ^0_ M,x containing v .

paper_title: Collapsing Catalytic Classes
statement_text: Let v, v' be such that v ∈ G ^0_ M,x (v') . Then G ^0_ M,x (v) = G ^0_ M,x (v') and hence v' ∈ G ^0_ M,x (v) .

statement_text: Each tree in G ^0_ M,x contains at most one halting configuration.

paper_title: Collapsing Catalytic Classes
label: lemma:compressorcompute
statement_text: Let M be a catalytic machine with work space s := s(n) and catalytic space c := c(n) , where log n ≤ s ≤ c ≤ 2^s , and let x ∈ {0,1}^n be an input for M written on the input tape. Let B= 2s and S=2^B , and let τ ∈ {0,1}^c and mathtt tar ∈ {0,1}^B be given on the catalytic tape. There is a catalytic subroutine sc ComputeOrCompress (τ,mathtt tar ) which takes one of the following two actions: If both G ^0_ M,x (normal acc _ M,x,τ ) and G ^0_ M,x (normal rej _ M,x,τ ) are of size at most S/2+1 , then it outputs a directed graph G and two vertices r and t such that the forward reachable graph from r is isomorphic to G _ M,x,τ , with normal start _ M,x,τ mapping to r and normal acc _ M,x,τ mapping to t . Otherwise, it replaces τ by π ∈ {0,1}^c and mathtt tar by (u,j,0^ s- log d_M ) , where u ∈ {0,1}^s and j ∈ [d_M] have the property that sc CountStepsBack (le π,u rangle ,j) replaces π by τ and returns mathtt tar as the number of steps. The subroutine returns a bit indicating which action it took, and the procedure leaves other portions of the tapes unchanged. Furthermore sc ComputeOrCompress (τ,mathtt tar ) uses additional space O(s) .

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
title: Matching
statement_text: Let G = (V, E) be an undirected graph. A sf matching is a set M ⊆ E of edges such that \[ ∀ v ∈ V, \ |E(v) ∩ M| ≤ 1 \] A vertex v ∈ V is matched by M (and otherwise unmatched) if \[|E(v) ∩ M| = 1\] The sf size of the matching M is |M| , and we call a matching sf perfect if every vertex is matched.

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
statement_text: The sf matching function , denoted by MATCH , takes as input an n × n bipartite graph G and returns a matching M in G of maximum size.

statement_text: Let G = (V, E) be a graph. The sf symmetric difference of matchings M_1, M_2 ⊆ E , denoted by M_1 Δ M_2 , is defined as having edges (M_1 smallsetminus M_2) ∪ (M_2 smallsetminus M_1) . Similarly for any matching M and set S ⊆ E , we define M ⊕ S as (M ∪ S) smallsetminus (M ∩ S) .

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
title: Catalytic machines
statement_text: Let s := s(n) and c := c(n) . A sf catalytic Turing machine with space s and sf catalytic space c is a Turing machine M with a read-only input tape of length n , a write-only output tape, a read-write work tape of length s , and a second read-write work tape of length c called the sf catalytic tape , which will be initialized to an adversarial string τ . We say that M computes a function f if for every x ∈ {0,1}^n and τ ∈ {0,1}^c , the result of executing M on input x with initial catalytic tape τ fulfils two properties: 1) M halts with f(x) written on the output tape; and 2) M halts with the catalytic tape in state τ .

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
title: Catalytic classes
statement_text: We define CSPACE [s,c] to be the family of functions computable by catalytic Turing machines with space s and catalytic space c . We also define sf catalytic logspace as CL := cup_ d ∈ N CSPACE [d log n, n^d] Furthermore we define CLP as the family of functions computable by CL machines that are additionally restricted to run in polynomial time for every initial catalytic tape τ .

label: lem:DET-in-cl

label: lem:compute-min-weight-path
statement_text: Let G = (V, E) be a directed graph, let s,t ∈ V be a given source and target vertex, and W: E → Z _ ≤ poly (n) be edge weights such that G does not have any non-positive weight cycles under W . Then there exists a CLP machine which, given (G, s, t, W) , computes the minimum weight of a simple s - t path.

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
title: NC
statement_text: A language L is computable in (uniform) NC if there exists a (uniform) circuit family {C_n}_ n ∈ N such that C_n has size poly (n) , depth log ^ O(1) n , and decides membership in L on all inputs of size n .

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
title: Lossy coding and LOSSYC
statement_text: The sf lossy coding problem is defined as follows: given a pair of algorithms Comp :{0, 1}^n → {0, 1}^ n-1 and Decomp : {0, 1}^ n-1 → {0, 1}^n as input, our goal is to output any x ∈ {0, 1}^n such that Decomp (Comp (x)) ≠ x . Let C be a complexity class. We define LOSSYC as the set of languages reducible to the lossy coding problem whose input algorithms come from the class C . When no class is given, we define LOSSY := LOSSY [ upshape sffamily P xspace ] .

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
statement_text: Let U be a set and W:U → Z be a weight assignment, and let F ⊆ 2^U be a family of subsets of U . We say that W is sf isolating for F if \[ ∃ ! \ S_ unique ∈ F such that W(S_ unique ) = min _ F ∈ F W(F)\] where ∃ ! means that exactly one such set exists.

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace

Let W:E → Z _ ≤ poly (n) be edge weights such that W isolates a size k matching M^k_ unique in G . Then there exists a CLP machine which, given input (G, e ∈ E) and access to W , determines whether e ∈ M^k_ unique .

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
title: Residual Graph
statement_text: Let G = (V = L ∪ R, E) be a bipartite graph, M be a matching in G , and W:E → Z be edge weights. The sf residual graph of M , which we denote by G^M_ residual = (V^M_ residual , E^M_ residual ) , is a directed graph whose vertex set V^M_ residual consists of V plus a new source s and a new sink t . The edge set E^M_ residual consists of the following edges where u ∈ L and v ∈ R : if u is unmatched by M we add an edge (s → u) , and if v is unmatched by M we add an edge (v → t) if (u,v) ∈ M we add an edge (v → u) if (u,v) ∈ E smallsetminus M we add an edge (u → v) We will drop the M superscript in cases where the usage is clear.

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
title: Augmenting Path
statement_text: Let G = (V, E) be a graph, M be a matching in G , and W:E → Z be a weight assignment. A path P = {e_1, ... , e_m} on vertices {v_1, ... , v_ m+1 } is an sf augmenting path with respect to M if: v_1 and v_ m+1 are not matched by M . For all odd i ∈ [m] , e_i ∉ M . For all even i ∈ [m] , e_i ∈ M .

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
statement_text: Let G = (V = L ∪ R, E) be a bipartite graph, M be a matching in G , and W:E → Z be a weight assignment. We define the sf alternating weight function as \[W_ alt ^M(e) vcentcolon = -W(e), &quad if e ∈ M W(e), &quad if e ∉ M \] Furthermore, for residual graph G^M_ residual we define the sf residual weight function as \[W_ residual ^M(e) vcentcolon = 0, &quad if e ∉ E W_ alt ^M(e), &quad otherwise \] Whenever we use weights in G^M_ residual , we are referring to the weights W^M_ residual , while for augmenting paths P with respect to M we use W_ alt ^M .

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
label: fact:augmented-matching
title: Berge's Theorem
statement_text: Let G = (V, E) be a graph, M be a matching in G , and W:E → Z be a weight assignment. Then M is maximum iff there do not exist any augmenting paths with respect to M . Furthermore, for any augmenting path P , M ⊕ P is a matching in G of size |M| + 1 .

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
title: Threshold Edge
statement_text: Let G = (V, E) be a directed graph, s ∈ V be a source vertex, t ∈ V be a target vertex, and W: E → Z be edge weights such that G does not have any non-positive weight cycles under W . We say that an edge e ∈ E is a sf threshold edge if there exist two minimum weight s - t paths P_1, P_2 in G such that e ∈ P_1 and e ∉ P_2 .

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
label: lem:check-whether-k+1-is-isolated

paper_title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
label: thm:lossy-specific
statement_text: There exist NC algorithms A _1 , A _2 which, given a bipartite graph G = (V, E) with as input, have the following behaviour: A _1 outputs NC circuits Comp :{0, 1}^ f(n) → {0, 1}^ f(n) - 1 and Decomp :{0, 1}^ f(n) - 1 → {0, 1}^ f(n) such that both Comp and Decomp have depth polylog (n) and size poly (n) . Furthermore, f(n) ∈ poly (n) . Given any x ∈ {0, 1}^ f(n) such that Decomp (Comp (x)) ≠ x , A _2 outputs a maximum matching of G .

That is, π exchanges 1 and 2 , and π^* exchanges non-star with star. Consider the following equations over bbF _2 : ccc (1) x_1 + x_2 = 1 & (3) x_1^*+x_2 = 1 & (5) x_1 + x_1^* = 1 (2) x_1^* + x_2^* = 1 & (4) x_1+x_2^* = 1 & (6) x_2 + x_2^* = 1 The equations are partitioned into three Γ -orbits. Equation (1) and (2) form an orbit, equation (3) and (4) as well, and equation (5) and (6). The system is unsatisfiable over bbF _2 (and its algebraic closure) because (1)+(4)+(6) is an IPS certificate of unsatisfiability. Nonetheless, there is no linear Γ -symmetric refutation C(vec x, vec y) : Every monomial in such a certificate C(vec x, vec y) would contain exactly one vec y -variable. In order to have C(vec x, vec f) = 1 , there must be a degree- 1 monomial in C(vec x, vec y) , i.e.\ consisting only of a single vec y -variable y_i . But then, the entire orbit of y_i must appear in C(vec x, vec y) due to symmetry. As each orbit of equations has even size and the field has characteristic 2 , the constant terms in C(vec x, vec f) sum up to 0 . statement_text: A matrix M ∈ R ^ n × n is an L -matrix if for all i ≠ j , M _ ij ≤ 0 , and for all i ∈ [n] , M _ ii > 0 . statement_text: For an RDDL matrix M ∈ R ^ n × n , we define the associated weighted graph G = ([n+1], E, w) with an additional dummy vertex n+1 . Finally, for all i ∈ [n] , if the matrix is RDDL, we set w(n+1,i)=0 , and if the matrix is SDDM, we set w(n+1,i)=w(i,n+1) . If for all vertices i ∈ [n] , there is a path in G from i to n+1 with all positive edge weights, then we say G (the graph associated to the RDDL matrix) is connected to the dummy vertex .

statement_text: Let G be an (n, d, λ) -graph with λ < d/50 , and suppose G' ⊆ G satisfies δ(G') ≥ 0.9d . Then for all S ⊆ V(G') , G' \ S has at most |S| connected components, that is, q(G' \ S) ≤ |S| . Therefore, if G' has an even number of vertices then it contains a perfect matching.

paper_title: Refuting Perfect Matchings in Spectral Expanders is Hard
label: lemma:f-factor
title: Regular Subgraph Lemma
statement_text: For every C > 1 there exists d_0 = d_0(C) such that the following holds. Suppose G is an (n, d, λ) graph with λ < ε d and d ≥ d_0 , where ε < 1/100C^ 3/2 . If G' ⊆ G has minimum degree δ( G' ) ≥ d - C , then G' contains a spanning f -regular subgraph for any even 2 ≤ f ≤ d/2 .

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
label: thm:algo-informal
title: Assignment extraction algorithm, informal
statement_text: The search version of the Proof Analysis Problem for Resolution can be solved in deterministic polynomial time whenever the size parameter s is at least n^3 . That is, there is an algorithm that, given a CNF formula φ over n variables and poly (n) clauses and a Resolution refutation π of normal scshape Ref _ s (φ) with s ≥ n^3 , extracts a satisfying assignment for φ in time polynomial in n , s and the size |π| of π , whenever φ is satisfiable.

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
label: thm:krajicek-informal
title: Assignment extraction as information efficiency, informal
statement_text: For every satisfiable CNF formula φ over n variables and poly (n) clauses, \[ info _ Res ( ¬ normal scshape Ref (φ)) ≈ min { Kt (α mid φ) mid φ(α)=1 },\] where info _Q(ψ) coloneq min { Kt (π mid ψ) mid π : Q vdash ψ } is Krajíček's information efficiency function.

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
label: thm:np-hardness-informal
title: NP -hardness of PAP _ EF , informal
statement_text: For every propositional proof system S that p-simulates Extended Frege, the Proof Analysis Problem for S is NP -complete.

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
label: thm:equivalence-PAP-AM-informal
title: Equivalence of analyzability and normal scshape Ref lower bounds, informal
statement_text: Let S be a reasonably strong propositional proof system. Assuming that there is some δ >0 such that TSAT ∉ io SIZE [2^ δ n ] , the following are equivalent: sep=0pt the proof system S is analyzable; for every unsatisfiable 3-CNF formula φ over n variables, every S -proof of the formula ¬ normal scshape Ref _ poly (n) (φ) requires size at least 2^ Ω(n) .

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
label: thm:AM-in-PV-informal
title: Atserias--Müller lower bound in PV_1 , informal
statement_text: The theory PV_1 proves the statement that for every CNF formula φ over n variables and every size parameter s ∈ N , if φ is unsatisfiable and π is a correct Resolution refutation of normal scshape Ref _ s (φ) , then |π| ≥ 2^ Ω(s/n^2) .

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
label: thm:AM-original
title: Atserias--Müller lower bound
statement_text: For every CNF formula φ over n variables and every size parameter s ∈ N , if φ is unsatisfiable and π is a correct Resolution refutation of normal scshape Ref _s(φ) , then |π| ≥ 2^ Ω(s/n) .

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
label: thm:ub-in-res-informal

statement_text: There is a polynomial-size depth-2 Boolean circuit P(α, φ, s) of fan-in 2 that given a CNF formula φ , a satisfying assignment α , and s ∈ N , outputs a Resolution refutation π of normal scshape Ref _s(φ) . paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
label: thm:characterization-informal

statement_text: Let S be a reasonable propositional proof system that simulates Extended Frege. Then, for every sequence { φ_n }_ n ∈ N of unsatisfiable CNF formulas, \[ S vdash _ poly ¬ φ_n qquad if and only if qquad Svdash _ poly ¬ normal scshape Ref (normal scshape Ref (φ_n)).\]

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
label: thm:aut-for-Ref-informal
title: Automatability in terms of normal scshape Ref formulas, informal
statement_text: For every reasonable proof system S that simulates Extended Frege as well as for Resolution itself, sep=0pt S is automatable if, and only if, S is automatable exclusively on normal scshape Ref formulas; S is weakly automatable if, and only if, S is weakly automatable exclusively on normal scshape Ref formulas.

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
label: thm:prop-unprovable-informal
title: Propositional unprovability of Resolution lower bounds, informal
statement_text: Let Q be a reasonable propositional proof system that simulates Resolution. If { φ_n}_ n ∈ N is a sequence of hard unsatisfiable CNF formulas for Q , where φ_n has n variables and size |φ_n|= poly (n) , then sep=0pt the formulas normal scshape Ref _ n^2 (φ_n) over N = poly (n) variables are all unsatisfiable and require size 2^ N^ Ω(1) to be refuted in Resolution; yet, Q does not have polynomial-size refutations of the formulas normal scshape Ref _ N^2 (normal scshape Ref _ n^2 (φ_n)) stating quadratic lower bounds on normal scshape Ref _ n^2 (φ_n) .

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
label: cor:PHP-Ref-ACO-informal

statement_text: For every d ≤ O( log n / log log n) , the formulas normal scshape Ref (normal scshape Ref (normal scshape PHP _n)) are all unsatisfiable but require size exp ( Ω(n^ 1/(2d+1) ) ) to be refuted in depth- d Frege systems.

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem

statement_text: Let T be a consistent first-order theory extending Robinson Arithmetic by a set of polynomial-time recognizable axioms. Then, there exists a sequence of unsatisfiable propositional formulas { ψ_ N }_ N ∈ N described uniformly by a polynomial-time algorithm, where ψ_N has N variables, such that sep=0pt Resolution refutations of the formula ψ_ N require size 2^ N^ Ω(1) ; there exists c > 0 such that the theory T cannot prove Ω(N^c) lower bounds on the Resolution size of these refutations; that is, there is N_0 ∈ N such that the lower bound expressed by the first-order sentence ∀ N ∀ π (N > N_0 ∧ Ref _ Res (ψ_N,π) → |π| > N^c ) is unprovable in T .

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
label: thm:Hastad-PHP

statement_text: Let p ∈ [0, 1) and let N be the number of variables of the normal scshape Ref _s(φ) formula for some CNF formula φ over n variables. paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_text: Let Γ be a constraint language. An instance of sc CSP (Γ) is a tuple I = (V, C ) , where V is a finite set of variables and C a finite set of constraints. We say that A satisfies a constraint C = (R, (x_1, ... , x_k)) if (A(x_1), ... , A(x_k)) ∈ R , and we say that A is a satisfying assignment for I = (V, C ) if A satisfies every constraint in C .

We say that A is a satisfying assignment for I = (V, C , {R_x}_ x ∈ V ) if A satisfies every constraint in C and A(x) ∈ R_x for every x ∈ V .

label: def:factors
title: Factors
statement_text: definition factors For rooted forest T we define the following three kinds of factors: A tree factor is a set V(T_x) for some x ∈ V(T) . We call x the root of the factor. A forest factor is a bf nonempty union of tree factors whose roots are siblings. In particular, a tree factor is also a forest factor but the empty set is not. The set of roots of the tree factors included in the union are called the roots of the factor. If they are not roots of components of T , we define their joint parent as the parent of the factor. Note that We consider two nodes of T siblings when they have a joint parent or if they both roots of components of T . This convention is chosen to remain consistent with the notation of . A context factor is a set U=X \ Y where X is a tree factor and Y is a forest factor whose roots are strict descendants of the root of X . The root of U , denoted by rt(U) , is the root of X and the roots of Y are called the appendices of U . Note that a tree factor is bf not a context factor. We will sometimes refer to X as the base tree factor of U and to Y as the removed forest of U . For clarity we sometimes denote X and Y as X(U) and Y(U) . We also denote the parent of the appendices by pr(U) and let the spine of U , denoted by spine(U) , be the path from rt(U) to pr(U)

statement_text: Consider the quantity (|V(G)|-1)^ 2 = (n-1)^ 2 ≥ 0 for n -vertex graphs G . This is nonnegative and, in fact, a graph motif parameter: Abbreviating \#H = \# Ind (H mathop → G) , we have n = \# K_ 1 and 1 = \# K_ 0 , and (n-1)^ 2 =\# K_ 1 ^ 2 -2\# K_ 1 +\# K_ 0 . Moreover, the quadratic term \# K_ 1 ^2 can be linearized This holds because \# K_ 1 ^2 counts the pairs (u,v) ∈ V(G)^2 , and so does the linear combination 2 \# K_ 2 + 2 \# I_2 + \# K_ 1 , whose summands correspond to the isomorphism type of G[{u,v}] , which is either K_2 , I_2 , or K_1 . As we will elaborate later, graph motif parameters enjoy a general linearization property: Any polynomial combination of induced subgraph counts can be expressed as a unique linear combination. This holds even for ``subobject'' counts under more general notions of objects; see Lemma and Corollary . This motivates our focus on linear combinations. , i.e., expressed as the linear combination \# K_ 1 ^ 2 = 2 \# K_ 2 + 2 \# I_2 + \# K_ 1 . Thus, we have \[ 0 ≤ (\#K_1 - 1)^2 = 2 \#K_2 + 2 \#I_2 - \# K_1 + \# K_0, \] and have constructed a linear combination of induced subgraph counts evaluating to a nonnegative value for every graph G , even though the term \# Ind (K_1 mathop → star ) appears with coefficient -1 .

statement_text: For a fixed graph H , we consider the problem of finding an induced H -copy in a large graph G . The graph G is given as (x, O) where O: Σ^ast → {0,1} is an oracle encoding the edge relation and x is the number of nodes of G written in binary. The nodes of G are 0, ... ,x-1 , written as bit strings of fixed length n . Given two nodes u and v of G , there is an edge between u and v iff O(uv) = 1 . (Since we consider strings of fixed length n , no separation symbol is needed.) In this representation, most of the information about G is stored in the oracle; the input x only encodes the size of the graph, and the running time of oracle Turing machines is measured in terms of x .

paper_title: Which graph motif parameters count?
statement_text: In our example of finding an induced copy of H in the graph G , we start with a binary type-2 relation IsIndSub _H(x,y,O) . The relation interprets y as an encoding of a set Y of k distinct nodes of G with k being the number of nodes of H . The relation then queries the oracle O to obtain the induced subgraph G[Y] . It then checks by brute force whether G[Y] and H are isomorphic. If yes, it returns the value 1 and otherwise 0 . This is clearly polynomial-time computable in |x| . The relation ∃ IsIndSub _H(x,O) now returns 1 if G contains an induced copy of H somewhere , and 0 if G does not contain such a copy. See also Lemma for a more formal proof.

paper_title: An Intrinsic Barrier for Resolving P = NP (2-SAT as Flat, 3-SAT as High-Dimensional Void-Rich)
label: thm: Cubical Complex
statement_text: Let F be a 3-SAT formula with n variables. The set of satisfying assignments S ⊆ {0,1}^n forms a cubical complex C(F) , where: Vertices correspond to satisfying assignments. k -faces correspond to k -dimensional subcubes where all 2^k assignments satisfy F . Topological queries about C(F) (e.g., connectedness, Betti numbers) reduce to 3-SAT instances.

paper_title: An Intrinsic Barrier for Resolving P = NP (2-SAT as Flat, 3-SAT as High-Dimensional Void-Rich)
label: thm:unstructured
statement_text: Let F be a random 3-SAT instance at clause density α>4.26 . Then with probability 1-o(1) : Its solution space S(F) decomposes into 2^ Ω(n) disconnected clusters. The cubical complex of S(F) has exponentially large Betti numbers (e.g.\ β_2(S(F))=2^ Ω(n) ). The primal constraint graph of F has treewidth Ω(n) . In particular, S(F) admits no global ordering or low-dimensional traversal.

statement_text: Let L = SAT and suppose R:L → threesat is a polynomial-time satisfiability-preserving reduction that is cubical and homologically faithful (discussion on this is delayed to Section 5.2 Conditions 1 and 2). If F ∈ L has a solution-space cubical complex S(F) with β_ 2 (S(F)) ≥ f(n) for some f(n)=ω(poly(n)) , then the reduced instance F^ prime =R(F) satisfies \[ β_ 2 (S(F^ prime ) )\ ≥ \ β_ 2 (S(F) )\ =\ Ω(f(n)). \] In particular, the reduction from SAT to 3-SAT does not collapse exponential second Betti numbers.

label: thm:hamiltonian-gap-formal
title: Hamiltonian spectral-gap hardness
statement_text: Let F be a 3-SAT formula on n variables and let S(F) ⊂ {0,1}^n be its solution set. Suppose there exist constants c',c>0 such that \[ β_2 l(S(F) r) ≥ 2^ c' n . \] Let H_F be a physically k -local Hamiltonian acting on n qubits satisfying the following assumptions. (Ground-space encoding) The ground-space of H_F is exactly the linear span of computational-basis states corresponding to satisfying assignments: \[ G := Span {ket x : x ∈ S(F)}, \] and H_Fket ψ =0 for all ket ψ ∈ G . (Cubical-preserving drivers / exponential inter-cluster suppression) Partition S(F)= sqcup_ i=1 ^K C_i into clusters (connected components under single-bit flips) so that K ≥ 2^ c'n . There exists c_1>0 and a (fixed) polynomial p(n) with the following property: for every pair of distinct clusters C_i ≠ C_j and every pair of basis states x ∈ C_i , y ∈ C_j , l|le x | H_F | yrangle r| ≤ p(n) e^ -c_1 n . (Intuitively: all local drivers induce exponentially small matrix elements between different clusters.) (Polynomial locality degree) For every basis state ket x the number of basis states ket y with le x|H_F|yrangle ≠ 0 is at most q(n) for some fixed polynomial q . This holds for any k -local Hamiltonian with k=O(1) . Then there exists a>0 (depending only on c_1,c',p,q ) such that the spectral gap above the ground-space satisfies \[ g(H_F) ≤ 2 e^ -a n . \] In particular the gap is at most exponentially small in n .

label: lem:homology-preservation
title: Homology preservation under gadget duplication / wiring
statement_text: Let K be a cubical complex obtained from a CNF instance (or its solution complex) that contains subcomplexes \[ C_1, ... ,C_M ⊆ K \] (each C_i supported on a small set of variables/clauses, a ``gadget''), and suppose the C_i are pairwise disjoint as subcomplexes of K (or can be made disjoint by the variable-duplication / padding procedure described in later in this Appendix). Let K' be the complex obtained from K by (i) duplicating variable/clauses as needed so that gadget supports become vertex-disjoint, and (ii) adding a linking subcomplex \[ L = cup_ ell L_ell \] (consisting of equality clauses / small wiring gadgets and any expander edges used in the amplification) which attaches to the gadgets in a local, controlled way. Assume the following ``locality and acyclicity'' conditions hold: Each linking component L_ell is contractible (that is, H_j(L_ell )=0 for all j ≥ 1 ). For every i and every linking component L_ell we have that the intersection C_i ∩ L_ell is either empty or contractible (in particular H_j(C_i ∩ L_ell )=0 for all j ≥ 1 ). No (k+1) -cell of K' has support that intersects more than one distinct gadget C_i (equivalently, every (k+1) -cell is incident to cells lying in at most one gadget-support C_i ). Then for every homological degree k ≥ 0 the inclusion i: sqcup_ i=1 ^M C_i hookrightarrow K' induces an injection on H_k , and in particular \[ β_k(K') ≥ Σ _ i=1 ^M β_k(C_i). \] If, moreover, the gadget cycles { [γ_i] } were independent in H_k(K) (so β_k(K)= Σ _iβ_k(C_i) ), then duplication/wiring preserves independence and \[ β_k(K') = β_k(K) = Σ _ i=1 ^M β_k(C_i). \]

label: def:group-action
title: Group action
statement_text: Let G be a group and X be a set. A group action of G on X is a function α: G × X → X , denoted by α(g,x) = g · x , that satisfies the following properties: e · x = x for all x ∈ X , where e ∈ G is the identity element of G , and g · (h · x)=(gh) · x for all g,h ∈ G and x ∈ X .

paper_title: On the Bit Size of Sum-of-Squares Proofs for Symmetric Formulations
title: Orbits, Stabilizers, and Fixed Points
statement_text: Let a group G act on a set X . For x ∈ X , the set Orb_x = {g · x ∈ X \ | \ g ∈ G } is called the G -orbit of x . For x ∈ X , the set Stab_x = { g ∈ G \ | \ g · x = x } is called the stabilizer of x in G . The set of all distinct G -orbits of X is called the quotient set of X by G , denoted X/G . An element x ∈ X is a fixed point if its G -orbit consists only of x , i.e., Orb_x = {x} . Equivalently, x is a fixed point if its stabilizer is the entire group G , i.e., Stab_x = G .

label: def:action-on-poly
title: Action on Monomials and Polynomials
statement_text: Let G be a finite group that can act on the indices 1, ... , n (e.g., a subgroup of S_n ). For g ∈ G and a multi-index α = (α_1, ... , α_n) ∈ N ^n , we define the action of g on α as g · α = (α_ g^ -1 (1) , ... , α_ g^ -1 (n) ) . For a monomial m = x^ α , the action of G on m is defined for any g ∈ G as: g · m := x^ g · α = x_1^ α_ g^ -1 (1) ... x_n^ α_ g^ -1 (n) = x_ g(1) ^ α_1 ... x_ g(n) ^ α_n . This action extends linearly to the set of polynomials R [x_1, ... , x_n] . Thus, for a polynomial p(x) = Σ _ i=0 ^m a_i x^ α_i , the action of g ∈ G on p is defined as g · p = Σ _ i=0 ^m a_i (g · x^ α_i ) . A polynomial p is said to be G -invariant if g · p = p for all g ∈ G . If G=S_n , where S_n is the symmetric group on n elements, the polynomial is called symmetric .

label: th:group_action_additivity_multiplicativity
statement_text: Let G be a finite group acting on polynomials as defined above. For any two polynomials p,q ∈ R [x_1, ... , x_n] and any g ∈ G , the action satisfies: it Additivity: g · (p+q) = g · p + g · q . it Multiplicativity: g · (pq) = (g · p)(g · q) .

label: def:action-on-matrices
statement_text: Let S_n be the symmetric group of permutations of n elements. Every permutation π ∈ S_n of the indices of x_1, ... , x_n induces a permutation π' ∈ S_ ω_n^d on the monomials in the monomial basis x _d . Consider the permutation matrix P_ π' associated to π' , and let Q ∈ S ^ ω_n^d be a symmetric matrix whose entries are indexed by the monomial basis x _d , i.e. Q=(Q_ x^α, x^β ) for x^α, x^β entries of x _d . The action of π ∈ S_n on Q is given by π star Q = P_ π' Q P_ π' ^top . Equivalently, the entries of π star Q satisfy (π star Q)_ x^α, x^β = Q_ π · x^α, π · x^β . Moreover, for any G subgroup of S_n , we say that Q is G -invariant if π star Q = Q for every π ∈ G .

label: th:orbits_pairs_indices_under_symmetric_action
statement_text: Let k=O(1) be a fixed positive integer. Let n_1, n_2, ... , n_k ∈ N be such that Σ _ i=1 ^k n_i = n . paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
statement_text: A Markov process M = (Ω,P) is defined by: A finite state space Ω . A probability transition matrix P ∈ R _ ≥ 0 ^ Ω × Ω , such that every row sums to 1 . If we take a random variable X_0 according to some probability distribution on Ω , and then select a sequence of random variables X_1, X_2, ... such that for all t ∈ N and ω_1,ω_2 ∈ Ω , \[ P [X_t = ω_2 | X_ t-1 = ω_1] = P_ ω_1,ω_2 ,\] then we say that X_0, X_1, X_2, ... is a Markov chain. We say that the Markov chain transition from state ω_1 ∈ Ω into state ω_2 ∈ Ω with probability P_ ω_1,ω_2 .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
statement_text: Let M = (Ω,P) be a Markov process. A distribution π ∈ Δ_ Ω is a it stationary distribution for M if π = π P . A Markov chain is it irreducible if it is possible to reach any state from any other state through a sequence of transitions with non-zero probability. In other words, for all ω_1, ω_2 ∈ Ω , there exists a t ∈ N such that (P^t)_ ω_1,ω_2 > 0 .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: thm:pi-unique
statement_text: If a Markov chain is irreducible, it has a unique stationary distribution, and π_ ω > 0 for all ω ∈ Ω .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
statement_text: Let M = (Ω,P) be a Markov process with stationary distribution π . We say that M is reversible with stationary distribution π if for all ω_1,ω_2 ∈ Ω , we have \[π_ ω_1 P_ ω_1,ω_2 = π_ ω_2 P_ ω_2,ω_1 .\] This condition is referred to as the detailed balance condition. If M is irreducible, then π is unique by cref thm:pi-unique and so we simply say that M is reversible.

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
statement_text: Let G = (V,E) be an undirected graph, with resistances r : E → R _ >0 . Now, let P ∈ R _ ≥ 0 ^ Ω × Ω such that \[P_ vw = Σ _ e ∈ N(v) ∩ N(w) frac r_v r_e , qquad where qquad r_v = [ Σ _ e ∈ N(v) frac 1 r_e ]^ -1 .\] The Markov process M = (V,P) is the it random walk on G with resistances r .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
statement_text: Let G = (V,E) be an undirected graph with resistances r : E → R _ >0 , and let M = (V,P) be the random walk on G with resistances r . Let π ∈ Δ_V be defined by \[π_v = frac R r_v , qquad where qquad R = [ Σ _ v ∈ V frac 1 r_v ]^ -1 .\] Then, M is reversible with stationary distribution π . G is connected if and only if M is irreducible. In that case, π is unique.

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: thm:random-walk-characterization
statement_text: Let M = (V,P) be an irreducible, reversible Markov process, with stationary distribution π . Let G = (Ω,E) be defined as \[E = {{v,w} : v,w ∈ V, P_ vw > 0}, qquad and qquad r_ {v,w} = frac 1 π_vP_ vw .\] Let M' be the random walk on G with resistances r . Then, M = M' .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: def:effective-resistance
statement_text: Let G = (V,E) be an undirected graph, with resistances r : E → R _ >0 . A flow is a function f : E → R . We embed all flows in the flow space C ^E = Span { |e rangle : e ∈ E} by \[ |f rangle = Σ _ e ∈ E f_e sqrt r_e |e rangle .\] We refer to | |f rangle | ^2 as the energy dissipated by f , or simply the energy of f . For any flow f , we define the net-flow δ_f : V → R as \[δ_f(v) = Σ _ e ∈ N_-(v) f_e - Σ _ e ∈ N_+(v) f_e.\] If δ_f equiv 0 , then f is a circulation, and we define the circulation space as C = { |f rangle : f is a circulation } . For any net-flow δ : V → R , the set of corresponding flows f such that δ_f = δ forms an affine subspace, i.e., |f_δ^ min rangle + C . We refer to f_ δ ^ min as the minimum-energy flow with net-flow δ , and we write \[R(G,r;δ) = | |f_ δ ^ min rangle | ^2.\] We refer to this as the effective resistance of net-flow δ in G with resistances r .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
statement_text: Let G = (V,E) be an undirected graph with resistance r : E → R _ >0 . The weighted incidence matrix is the matrix B ∈ R ^ V × E is defined as \[B_ ve = frac 1 sqrt r_e , & if e_- ≠ e_+ ∧ v = e_-, -frac 1 sqrt r_e , & if e_- ≠ e_+ ∧ v = e_+, 0, & otherwise . \] The graph Laplacian L ∈ R ^ V × V is defined as L = BB^T .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: thm:resistance-through-laplacian
statement_text: R(G,r;δ) = δ^TL^+δ , where L^+ is the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse of L .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: thm:laplacian-and-prob-transition
statement_text: Let M = (V,P) be an irreducible, reversible Markov process with stationary distribution π . Let G be the corresponding graph with resistances r . Let L be its Laplacian. Then, \[L = diag (π)(I - P) qquad ⟺ qquad P = I - diag (π)^ -1 L.\]

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
title: Quantum adversary bound for state conversion
statement_text: Let D be some finite domain, and for all x ∈ D , we define |σ_x rangle ∈ V , |τ_x rangle ∈ V and O_x ∈ L ( M ) . Then, P = {( |σ_x rangle , |τ_x rangle ,O_x)}_ x ∈ D is a state-conversion problem, and its adversary bound is the following optimization program: min quad & max _ x ∈ D | |w_x rangle | ^2, s.t. quad & leσ_xmiddle |σ_y rangle - leτ_xmiddle |τ_y rangle = lew_x | ( (I_ M - O_x^ dagger O_y ) ⊗ I_ W ) |w_y rangle , & ∀ (x,y) ∈ D , & |w_x rangle ∈ M ⊗ W , where W is a Hilbert space , & ∀ x ∈ D . We denote the optimal value by ADV (P) . If all the states satisfy | |σ_x rangle | = | |τ_x rangle | = 1 , for all x ∈ D , then we say that this is a unit-norm state-conversion problem, and if the operations O_x are unitaries, we say that P is a unitary-oracle state-conversion problem. For a function f : Σ_1 → Σ_2 , we define |σ_x rangle = |perp rangle and |τ_x rangle = |f(x) rangle , for all x ∈ D , and we abbreviate the optimal value to ADV ({( |bot rangle , |f(x) rangle , O_x)}_ x ∈ D ) = ADV (f, {O_x}_ x ∈ D ) .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
statement_text: A it transducer U is a unitary on V ⊕ H . Let |σ rangle , |τ rangle ∈ V and |w rangle ∈ H . If U performs the mapping |σ rangle ⊕ |w rangle overset U mapsto |τ rangle ⊕ |w rangle , then we say that U transduces |σ rangle to |τ rangle , and we write |σ rangle overset U squigarrow |τ rangle , and we refer to |w rangle as the catalyst for this transduction.

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
statement_text: Let U be a transducer on V ⊕ H . Then, for every |σ rangle ∈ V , there exists a unique |τ rangle ∈ V such that |σ rangle overset U squigarrow |τ rangle . Moreover, the minimal catalyst, i.e., the catalyst |w rangle ∈ H for this transduction of minimal norm is uniquely defined. Finally, the mappings U_ rotatebox [origin=c] -90 squigarrow V : |σ rangle mapsto |τ rangle and U_ squigarrow V : |σ rangle mapsto |w rangle are linear.

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
statement_text: Let U be a transducer on V ⊕ H , and K > 0 . Then, there exists a quantum circuit A that calls U a total of K times, and that implements the mapping \[ | A |σ rangle - U_ rotatebox [origin=c] -90 squigarrow V |σ rangle | ≤ frac 2 |U_ squigarrow V |σ rangle | sqrt K .\]

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
statement_text: Let {σ_x}_ x ∈ D ⊆ V _1 , {τ_x}_ x ∈ D ⊆ V _2 and {O_x}_ x ∈ D ⊆ L ( M ) define a state-conversion problem P . Let { |w_x rangle }_ x ∈ D ⊆ M ⊗ W be a feasible solution to the quantum adversary bound for state conversion. Then, there exists a unitary U acting on ( V _1 ⊕ V _2) ⊕ ( M ⊗ W ) , such that U_x := U · ((I_ V _1 ⊕ I_ V _2 ) ⊕ (O_x ⊗ I_ W )) acts as \[(U_x)_ rotatebox [origin=c] -90 squigarrow ( V _1 ⊕ V _2) : |σ_x rangle mapsto |τ_x rangle , qquad and qquad (U_x)_ squigarrow( V _1 ⊕ V _2) : |σ_x rangle mapsto |w_x rangle .\] Consequently, Q (P) ∈ O( ADV (P)) .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
statement_text: Let M = (V,P) be an irreducible, reversible Markov process, and let G = (V,E) be the corresponding undirected graph with resistance function r , as in cref thm:random-walk-characterization . For any net-flow δ ∈ R ^V , we write R_ eff (P;δ) = R_ eff (G,r;δ) . We also write For all v,w ∈ V , we write R_ eff (G,r;v ↔ w) = R_ eff (G,r;m 1 _v - m 1 _w) , i.e., the effective resistance between vertices v and w . For any two distributions μ,ν ∈ Δ_V , we write R_ eff (G,r;μ ↔ ν) = R_ eff (G,r;μ - ν) . For a distribution μ ∈ Δ_V and a set M ⊆ V , we write \[R_ eff (G,r;μ ↔ M) = min _ ν ∈ Δ_V : ν|_ V \ M equiv 0 R_ eff (G,r;μ ↔ ν).\] We extend all these notations R(G,r; · ) to R(P; · ) as well.

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: lem:fast-forwarding
statement_text: Let M = (V,P) be an irreducible, reversible Markov process, with stationary distribution π . Let ξ ∈ R _V such that Σ _ v ∈ V ξ_v = 0 . We write D = diag (π) , and widetilde ξ = D^ -1/2 ξ . Then, we have the following two consequences: For integer t ≥ 1 , R_ eff (P;ξ) ≤ t · R_ eff (P^t;ξ) . If the spectral gap of P is δ , we have R_ eff (P;ξ) ≤ |widetilde ξ |_2^2/δ .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: lem:fraction-vs-eff-resistance
statement_text: Let t ≥ 1 be an integer. Let M = (V,P) be an irreducible, reversible Markov process, with stationary distribution π ∈ Δ_V . Let σ, ν ∈ Δ_V have disjoint support. Then, Σ _ v ∈ V ν_v^2/π_v ≤ 2R_ eff (P^t; σ - ν) .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: def:state-reflection-problem
title: State-reflection problem
statement_text: Let D be a finite set. For all x ∈ D , let |σ_x^+ rangle , |σ_x^- rangle be two orthogonal vectors in V , and let O_x be an operation on H , such that O_x^2 = I . We refer to the state-conversion problem {( |σ_x^ pm rangle , pm |σ_x^ pm rangle , O_x)}_ x ∈ D as a state-reflection problem, and we write it as R = {( |σ_x^+ rangle , |σ_x^- rangle , O_x)}_ x ∈ D for short. Let w := { |w_x^ pm rangle }_ x ∈ D be a feasible solution to R , satisfying O_x |w_x^ pm rangle = pm |w_x^ pm rangle . We refer to |w_x^+ rangle and |w_x^- rangle as the positive and negative witnesses for x , and similarly to | |w_x^+ rangle | ^2 and | |w_x^- rangle | ^2 as the positive and negative witness sizes for x ∈ D , which write as R ^+_x(w) and R ^-_x(w) .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: thm:reformulation-state-conversion
statement_text: Let P = {( |σ_x rangle , |τ_x rangle , O_x)}_ x ∈ D be a unit-norm unitary-oracle state-conversion problem, with input and output and oracle spaces V _1 , V _2 and H , respectively. For all x ∈ D , we write \[ |σ_x^ pm rangle = frac |σ_x rangle ⊕ pm |τ_x rangle sqrt 2 ∈ V _1 ⊕ V _2, qquad and qquad overline O_x = (X ⊗ I)(O_x ⊕ O_x^ dagger ) ∈ L ( H ⊕ H ),\] where X ⊗ I acting on H ⊕ H swaps both copies of H . Then, R = {( |σ_x^+ rangle , |σ_x^- rangle , overline O_x )}_ x ∈ D is a state-reflection problem, ADV (P) = ADV (R) , and there exists an optimal solution { |w_x^ pm rangle }_ x ∈ D to R such that overline O_x |w_x^ pm rangle = pm |w_x^ pm rangle .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: thm:transducers
title: Explicit implementation of transducers
statement_text: Let R = {( |σ_x^ pm rangle , pm |σ_x^ pm rangle , O_x)}_ x ∈ D be a state-reflection problem, with feasible solution { |w_x^ pm rangle }_ x ∈ D . Let, let A ⊆ V ⊕ H be a subspace such that \[ Span { |σ_x^+ rangle |w_x^+ rangle }_ x ∈ D ⊆ A ⊆ Span { |σ_x^- rangle |w_x^- rangle }_ x ∈ D ^ perp .\] Then, the unitary U = 2Π_A - I is such that U(I ⊕ O_x) implements |σ_x^ pm rangle overset U(I ⊕ O_x) squigarrow pm |σ_x^ pm rangle .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: lem:rescale-state-reflection-problem
statement_text: Let R = {( |σ_x^ pm rangle , pm |σ_x^ pm rangle , O_x)}_ x ∈ D be state-reflection problem. Let D ∈ L ( V ) be an invertible operator, α_ pm ∈ C , and let R' := {(α_+D |σ_x^+ rangle , α_-(D^ -1 )^ dagger |σ_x^ pm rangle , O_x)}_ x ∈ D . Then, any feasible solution w := { |w_x^ pm rangle }_ x ∈ D for a state-reflection problem R can be turned into a feasible solution w' := {α_+ |w_x^+ rangle ,α_- |w_x^- rangle }_ x ∈ D for R' , where x^ -dagger := (x^ -1 )^ dagger . Consequently, \[ ADV (R) ≤ sqrt max _ x ∈ D R _x^+(w) · max _ x ∈ D R _x^-(w) .\]

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: thm:las-vegas-algorithm
statement_text: Let A be a quantum Monte-Carlo algorithm that implements the state-conversion problem given by P = {( |σ_x rangle , |τ_x rangle , O_x)}_ x ∈ D , with run-time given by the random variable T_x , for every x ∈ D . Then, for any choice of (α_t)_ t ∈ N _0 ⊆ R _ >0 , we can implement a feasible solution W := { |w_x^ pm rangle }_ x ∈ D to the corresponding state-reflection problem R := {( |σ_x rangle pm |τ_x rangle , pm ( |σ_x rangle pm |τ_x rangle ), overline O_x )}_ x ∈ D , with complexities \[ W _x^+ = E [ Σ _ t=0 ^ T_x-1 α_t ], qquad and qquad W _x^- = E [ Σ _ t=0 ^ T_x-1 frac 1 α_t ].\] In particular, by choosing α_t = 1 , for all t ∈ N _0 , we obtain W _x^ pm = E [T_x] , and by choosing α_t = t+1 , we obtain W _x^+ = E [T_x(T_x+1)/2] ∈ O( E [T_x^2]) , and W _x^- ∈ O(1 + E [ log (T_x)]) .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: def:hyperedge-problem
title: Hyperedge problem
statement_text: Let V be a finite set, and R = {( |σ_x^ pm rangle , pm |σ_x^ pm rangle , O_x)}_ x ∈ D be a state-reflection problem over V = C ^V . Suppose in addition that we can write for all x ∈ D , \[ |σ_x^+ rangle := δ_x ∈ C ^V, qquad and qquad |σ_x^- rangle = U_x ∈ C ^V,\] such that \[U_x is constant on supp (δ_x), qquad and qquad Σ _ v ∈ V (δ_x)_v = 0.\] Then, we say that R is a hyperedge problem denoted by {(δ_x,U_x,O_x)}_ x ∈ D , and we say that it implements the net-flow δ_x and the potential function U_x through the hyperedge with vertices V .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
statement_text: Let R = {(δ_x, U_x, O_x)}_ x ∈ D , and for all x ∈ D , let C_x ∈ C . Let R' = {(δ_x, U_x + C_xm 1 _V, O_x)}_ x ∈ D . Then, the feasible region of R equals the feasible region of R' .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: thm:hyperedge-from-span-program
title: Hyperedge from a span program
statement_text: Let f : D → {0,1} . For all x ∈ D , we define net-flow δ_x and potential function U_x on {s,t} , as \[δ_x = m 1 _s - m 1 _t, & if f(x) = 1, 0, & f(x) = 0, qquad and qquad U_x = 0, & if f(x) = 1, -m 1 _t, & f(x) = 0. \] On the one hand, let P = ( H , x mapsto H (x), K , |w_0 rangle ) be a span program on D that computes f . Let { |w_x rangle }_ x ∈ D be a set of witnesses for P . We write \[ |w_x^+ rangle = |w_x rangle , & if f(x) = 1, 0, & if f(x) = 0, qquad and qquad |w_x^- rangle = 0, & if f(x) = 1, |w_x rangle , & if f(x) = 0. \] Then, { |w_x^ pm rangle }_ x ∈ D is a feasible solution for the hyperedge problem R = {(δ_x, U_x, 2Π_ H (x) - I)}_ x ∈ D . Conversely, let { |w_x^ pm rangle }_ x ∈ D be a feasible solution to the hyperedge problem R = {(δ_x, U_x, O_x)}_ x ∈ D , where the oracles O_x act on H . We let H (x) be the +1 -eigenspace of O_x . Then, there exists a span program P = ( H , x mapsto H (x), K , |w_0 rangle ) that computes f , with \[C( P )^2 ≤ max {max _ x ∈ f^ -1 (1) | |w_x^+ rangle | ^2, max _ x ∈ f^ -1 (0) | |w_x^- rangle | ^2 }.\]

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: thm:hyperedge-from-database-function
title: Hyperedge from database update and function evaluation
statement_text: Let D be a finite domain, and consider a database update problem with input ξ_x ∈ Σ_I output η_x ∈ Σ_O and oracle O_x satisfying O_x^2 = I , for all x ∈ D . Then, the state-reflection problem R = {( |ξ_x rangle - |η_x rangle , |ξ_x rangle + |η_x rangle , O_x)}_ x ∈ D implementing the database update problem is also a hyperedge problem.

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: thm:known-marked-fraction-recovery
statement_text: Let V be a finite set, and let π ∈ Δ_V . For all x ∈ D in a finite domain D , let M_x ⊆ V , such that P _ v π [v ∈ M_x] = ε , for some fixed ε ∈ (0,1) . We write \[ |ψ_x rangle = frac 1 sqrt ε Σ _ v ∈ M_x sqrt π_v |v rangle ,\] and we define the state-reflection problems R = {( |perp rangle + |ψ_x rangle , |perp rangle - |ψ_x rangle , O_x)}_ x ∈ D and R' = {(m 1 _ perp - frac π|_ M_x ε , m 1 _ perp + m 1 _ M_x , O_x)}_ x ∈ D . Then, the feasible regions for R and R' are identical, and R' is a hyperedge problem.

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: def:generalized-graph-composition
title: Generalized graph composition
statement_text: Let G = (V,E) be a hypergraph, with boundary vertices B ⊆ V , and let D be a finite domain. For every hyperedge e ∈ E , let R^e = {(δ_x^e, U_x^e, O_x^e)}_ x ∈ D be a hyperedge problem. For all v ∈ V and x ∈ D , we write δ_x(v) = Σ _ e ∈ N(v) δ_x^e(v) . Suppose that For all internal nodes v ∈ V \ B , the net-flow vanishes, i.e., δ_x(v) = 0 . The potential function is uniquely defined at every vertex v ∈ V , i.e., U_x^e(v) = U_x(v) , for all e ∈ N(v) . Then, we say that (G,B,(R^e)_ e ∈ E ) is an instance of the generalized graph composition framework, that implements the hyperedge problem R = {(δ_x, U_x, oplus_ e ∈ E O_x^e)}_ x ∈ D on vertex set B .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: thm:generalized-graph-composition
title: Composition of hyperedges
statement_text: Let (G = (V,E),B,(R^e)_ e ∈ E ) be an instance of the generalized graph composition, implementing the hyperedge problem R . For all e ∈ E , suppose that w^e = { |(w^e)_x^ pm rangle }_ x ∈ D is a feasible solution to R^e . For all x ∈ D , let \[ |w_x^ pm rangle := oplus_ e ∈ E |(w^e)_x^ pm rangle .\] Then, w = { |w_x^ pm rangle }_ x ∈ D forms a feasible solution to R , with R _x^ pm (w) = Σ _ e ∈ E R _x^ pm (w^e) , for all x ∈ D .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: thm:graph-composition
title: Generalization of simple graph composition
statement_text: Every instance of graph composition can be turned into an instance for generalized graph composition, with the same witness sizes.

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
label: thm:path-cut-theorem
title: Resistance-cut theorem for function evaluation and database update
statement_text: Let G = (V,E) be a hypergraph, with boundary vertices B ⊆ V and hyperedge problems R^e = {(δ_x^e, U_x^e, O_x^e)}_ x ∈ D for all e ∈ E . Suppose that for every x ∈ D and e ∈ E , the total flow vector δ_x^e has support on at most two vertices, and U_x^e = 1 for those vertices, and 0 everywhere else. Then, for every x ∈ D , we can make a simple graph G(x) = (V,E(x)) , where we include all the edges uv that are connected by the unit flow in the hyperedge problem. Suppose that G(x) connects exactly two boundary vertices {s_x,t_x} . Then, for all x ∈ D , let C_x ⊆ E be a cut that certifies that all the other boundary vertices cannot be reached from s_x or t_x . Then, we can generate an instance to generalized graph composition with witness complexities \[ R _x^+(w) = R_ eff (G(x), e mapsto R _x^+(w^e), s_x ↔ t_x), qquad and qquad R _x^-(w) = Σ _ e ∈ C_x R _x^-(w^e),\] where all w^e 's are feasible solutions to the R^e 's.

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition
statement_text: Let x ∈ {0,1}^n \ {0^n} , and let i(x) be the first index containing a 1 , i.e., i(x) = min {i ∈ [n] : x_i = 1} . The graph composition construction from cref fig:first-marked-index-finding computes i(x) with complexities \[ R _x^+(w) = Σ _ j=1 ^ i(x) - 1 α_j + β_ i(x) , qquad and qquad R _x^-(w) = Σ _ j=1 ^ i(x)-1 frac 1 β_j + frac 1 α_ i(x) .\] Both become O( sqrt i(x) ) , if we choose α_j = 1/ sqrt j and β_j = sqrt j , for all j ∈ [n] , and we have R _x^+(w) ∈ O( log (i(x))) and R _x^-(w) ∈ O(i(x)) , if we choose α_j = 1/j and β_j = 1 , for all j ∈ [n] .

paper_title: Quantum walks through generalized graph composition

statement_text: Let \(F = H ∧ S\) with soft clauses \(S=C_ 1 ∧ ... ∧ C_ m \). statement_text: The cost - SR xspace calculus is a proof system for MaxSAT@ . A derivation of a clause C from a MaxSAT instance \(Γ\) (encoded with blocking variables) is a sequence of clauses \(D_ 1 , D_ 2 , ... , D_ t \) where, \(C ∈ Γ ∪ {D_ i }_ i ∈ [t] \), each \(D_ i \) is either already in \(Γ\) or is deduced from earlier clauses in the sequence using a resolution rule, or D_i is cost - SR xspace w.r.t.\ to \(Γ ∪ {D_ 1 , ... , D_ i-1 }\) with \( Var (D_ i ) ⊆ Var (Γ)\). We only consider the case where no new variables are added via cost - SR xspace rules. To be coherent with , cost - SR xspace should be cost - SR xspace ^- , following the notational convention of adding an exponent with `` - '' to denote SR xspace , PR xspace and SPR xspace when the systems are not allowed to introduce new variables. We ignore that convention to ease an already rich notation. The length of such derivation is \(t\), it i .it e .,\ the number of derived clauses. title: SPDP separation in the compiled (blocked) model
statement_text: Fix (κ,ell )=Θ( log n) and the radius-- 1 block partition B induced by the uniform compiler templates. bf Field convention: The NP-side lower bound uses a coefficient-space identity minor with diagonal entries pm 1 , which is invertible over any field---hence no characteristic restriction is required for the lower bound. The P-side upper bound and Width ⇒ Rank theorem are stated over characteristic 0 (or prime p > poly (n) ) to ensure that multilinearization and polynomial identity arguments hold without cancellation issues. For the separation conclusion, any fixed choice of such a field suffices. Then the following three facts (proved in this manuscript) imply P ≠ NP : bf (P-side compiled upper bound) For every deterministic machine M ∈ DTIME (n^c) , the uniformly compiled family {P_ M,n } satisfies \[ Γ^ B _ κ,ell (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) . \] (Item (1) holds uniformly for all polynomial time bounds by the universal-machine unrolling (Section ), hence applies to every L ∈ P .) bf (NP-side explicit compiled lower bound) There exists an explicit uniform 3 SAT witness family {Φ_n} such that the associated coupled clause-sheet polynomials {Q^ × _ Φ_n } satisfy \[ Γ^ B _ κ,ell (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) ≥ n^ Θ( log n) . \] (The identity minor has pm 1 diagonal entries, so this holds over any field.) (See Theorem and Lemma .) bf (Instance-uniform, witness-free extraction and rank monotonicity) For every instance Φ there is an instance-uniform map T_Φ (depending only on Φ , not on any witness) such that \[ T_Φ(P_ M',N(Φ) ) = Q^ × _Φ quad and quad Γ^ B _ κ,ell (T_Φ(p)) ≤ Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p) \ for all polynomials p. \] Consequently, P ≠ NP .
bounds: DTIME(n^c); \Theta(\log n); poly(n); O(1); n^c; n^{O(1)}; n^{\Theta(\log n)}
