label: thm:observer-separation
title: Observer-class separation under the Global God-Move gauge
statement_text: Fix (κ,ell )=Θ( log n) and the universal gauge Π^star . Then the following two statements hold: bf (Polynomial-time observers have polynomial CEW). For every deterministic polynomial-time machine M ∈ DTIME (n^ c ) , the induced observer O _M satisfies \[ CEW ^ B _ κ,ell ( O _M;n) ≤ n^ O(1) . \] bf (An explicit NP witness family has superpolynomial CEW). There exists an explicit family of NP witnesses {Φ_n} (e.g.\ Ramanujan--Tseitin / identity-minor family) such that the induced observers O _ Φ_n satisfy \[ CEW ^ B _ κ,ell ( O _ Φ_n ;n) ≥ n^ Ω( log n) . \]
bounds: \Theta(\log n); O(1); \Omega(\log n); n^{c}; n^{O(1)}; n^{\Omega(\log n)}

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:p-neq-np-from-observers
title: P ≠ NP (standard complexity consequence)
statement_text: If P=NP , then the NP witness family in Theorem (2) would be decidable by a polynomial-time machine, hence would induce a polynomial-time observer with polynomial CEW, contradicting Theorem (2). Therefore P ≠ NP .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:global-god-move
title: Holographic Upper-Bound Principle
statement_text: There exist a constant C ≥ 1 and a fixed deterministic projection Π_N (uniform per input length N ) such that for every Boolean function f ∈ P , \[ rk _ SPDP (E(f); r(n) ) ≤ n^ O(1) quad for quad r(n) = ( log n)^C, κ ≤ r(n). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:uniform-projection
title: Global God Move / Uniform Projection
statement_text: For every n and κ , there is an explicit, polytime projection Π_n onto the binom n κ monomials m_S = Π _ i ∉ S x_ i,i such that Π_n M_ κ,0 ( perm _n) = I_ binom n κ . In particular, M_ κ,0 ( perm _n) contains an identity minor of size binom n κ , hence Γ_ κ,0 ( perm _n) ≥ binom n κ = 2^ Ω(n) . The map Π_n is uniformly realizable by PAC.compile (n,κ) . The identity claim admits a dual Lagrangian/Farkas certificate: for each S , v = e_ m_S solves Π_n M v = e_S and no y with A^top y = 0 separates e_S , where A = Π_n M .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:main-final
title: Unconditional separation via SPDP collapse vs explicit minor witness
statement_text: There exists an explicit family of 3 CNF formulas {Φ_n} such that for the matched SPDP parameters (κ,ell )=Θ( log n) and the fixed compiled block partition B induced by the uniform compiler templates, the following holds: (bf P-side collapse ) For every deterministic Turing machine M running in time n^ O(1) , the compiled object associated to M and input length n has SPDP rank at most n^ O(1) after applying the canonical restriction/projection pipeline. (bf NP-side non-collapse ) The explicit witness family {Φ_n} yields compiled objects whose SPDP rank is n^ Ω( log n) (in particular, superpolynomial) under the same parameters (κ,ell ) and the same compilation/pipeline. Consequently, P ≠ NP .
bounds: \Theta(\log n); O(1); \Omega(\log n); n^{O(1)}; n^{\Omega(\log n)}

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:semantic-closure-compiled
title: Semantic closure of the compiled normal form under P -decidability
statement_text: Fix the compiler template family C (radius--1 blocks, diagonal basis, and Π^+ ) and parameters (κ,ell )=Θ( log n) . For each Boolean function f_n:{0,1}^n → {0,1} , let C (f_n) denote the compiler's canonical compiled representation of f_n (i.e.\ the unique normal-form output of C on any description of f_n within the admitted source class, modulo the equivalences listed below). The compiler satisfies the following representation invariance properties (as proved in Theorem and Corollary ): bf (Normal-form invariance.) If two admitted source descriptions D,D' compute the same Boolean function f_n , then the canonical compiled outputs C (D) and C (D') are equivalent under a finite sequence of the compiler equivalence moves listed in Definition (Appendix ), i.e. \[ C (D) equiv _ comp C (D'). \] bf (Rank invariance under compiler equivalences.) If P equiv _ comp P' , then \[ Γ^ B _ κ,ell (P') ≤ poly (n) · Γ^ B _ κ,ell (P), \] and the same bound holds with P,P' swapped. In particular, no compiler equivalence can turn an n^ Ω( log n) SPDP-rank lower bound into an n^ O(1) bound. Therefore, if f_n ∈ P , the canonical compiled representation C (f_n) satisfies Γ^ B _ κ,ell ( C (f_n)) ≤ n^ O(1) .
bounds: \Theta(\log n); poly(n); \Omega(\log n); O(1); n^{\Omega(\log n)}; n^{O(1)}

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: CEW - Contextual Entanglement Width
statement_text: For a Boolean function f: {0,1}^n → {0,1} and observer O , the bf Contextual Entanglement Width is: \[ CEW _O(f) = max _ t ≤ 2^n dim ( span {O_t(x) : x ∈ {0,1}^n}) \] where O_t represents the observer's state after t computation steps.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:structural-cew
title: Structural CEW
statement_text: For a compiled program in the diagonal holographic basis, the structural CEW CEW (p) is defined as the maximum, over all time steps t , of the number of block interfaces simultaneously touched by primitive operations at time t , under the fixed, input-independent access schedule produced by the compiler.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:spdp-cew
title: SPDP-based CEW (Appendix-only)
statement_text: In some appendix sections we introduce an alternative, purely algebraic notion of CEW: for fixed derivative parameters (κ,ell ) we define CEW _ κ,ell (p) to be the minimum w such that there exists a universal restriction ρ^star with Γ_ κ,ell (p upharpoonright ρ^star ) ≤ w . This SPDP-based CEW is used only as an equivalent characterisation of low-width behaviour.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: CEW
statement_text: For a straight-line program P on n inputs and window w , with r(n)=( log n)^C , CEW _w(P) is the maximum support size of any intermediate of formal degree ≤ r(n) encountered in window w . The global CEW is CEW (P)=max _w CEW _w(P) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:cew-subadd
title: Subadditivity
statement_text: If P=g(P_1, ... ,P_t) with bounded fan-in t ≤ t_0 , then CEW (P) ≤ C_1(t_0) Σ _i CEW (P_i)+C_2(t_0) n^ c_0 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:cew-mono
title: Monotonicity
statement_text: For any input restriction ρ , CEW (P upharpoonright _ρ) ≤ CEW (P) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:cew-depth4
title: Depth--4/log--degree
statement_text: If f has a size- n^k deterministic circuit, then f admits a ΣΠΣΠ form with each factor multilinear and deg , vars ≤ ( log n)^C , hence CEW (f) ≤ n^ c_2k .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:cew-to-spdp
title: Lifting CEW to SPDP
statement_text: For r(n)=( log n)^C there are a,b>0 with rk _ SPDP (E(f);r(n)) ≤ poly ( CEW (f)) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:spdp
title: SPDP Matrix
statement_text: Let p ∈ Bbb F[x_1, ... ,x_N] and let B={B_1, ... ,B_m} be a partition of {1, ... ,N} into blocks of size ≤ b=O(1) . Fix κ,ell ∈ Bbb N and let rows be indexed by pairs (τ,u) with multi-index τ ∈ Bbb N^N of weight |τ|=κ whose block support satisfies |{j: ∃ i ∈ B_j,\ τ_i>0}| ≤ κ , and u a monomial of degree ≤ ell . Columns are monomials x^β with deg x^β ≤ deg (p)-κ+ell (empty set if negative). Define \[ M^ B _ κ,ell (p) [(τ,u),x^β ] := coeff _ x^β (u · partial ^τ p ), quad Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p):= rank _Bbb F (M^ B _ κ,ell (p) ). \] All basis choices for rows/columns are by default the standard monomial bases; rank is basis--invariant by Lemma . We take the ambient coefficient space to be the multilinear (Boolean) monomial basis modulo le x_i^2-x_irangle , with columns indexed by multilinear monomials of degree at most D:=max {0,deg (p)-κ+ell } (i.e.\ the basis B_ κ,ell of the codimension note).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:rank-equivalence
title: Row--count bound
statement_text: Let p ∈ F [x_1, ... ,x_N] be multilinear. For any ell ∈ N , \[ Γ_ ell ,\ ell (p)\ ≤ \ binom N ell 2^ ell . \] More generally, for arbitrary κ,ell , the number of rows of M_ κ,ell (p) is binom N κ · | Mon _ ≤ ell | , hence Γ_ κ,ell (p) is at most that number.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: True 0/1 Characteristic Polynomial
statement_text: For a Boolean function f: {0,1}^n → {0,1} , the bf characteristic polynomial is: \[ χ_f(x_1, ... , x_n) = Σ _ a ∈ f^ -1 (1) Π _ i: a_i=1 x_i Π _ i: a_i=0 (1-x_i) \] This multilinear polynomial (a sum-of-products form) satisfies: χ_f(a) = 1 if f(a) = 1 χ_f(a) = 0 if f(a) = 0 Each monomial corresponds to exactly one satisfying assignment Monomials are linearly independent under partial derivatives

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Cook-Levin Tableau Polynomial
statement_text: For a Turing machine M running in time T(n) , the bf Cook-Levin tableau polynomial p_M encodes the computation tableau as a constant-degree polynomial with variables for tape bits, state indicators, and head positions. The detailed model-exact construction with constant degree and polynomial SPDP rank is given in Theorem (Section ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Shifted Partial Matrix
statement_text: The bf shifted partial matrix SP _ ell (p, s) for polynomial p , order ell , and shift vector s has entries: \[ SP _ ell (p, s)_ I,x = partial _I p(x + s) \] where I ranges over index sets of size ell .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Observer Frame
statement_text: An bf observer frame is a triple F = (S, R, I) where S is a structured object, R is a resolution class of algebraic operations, and I is an inference operator measuring accessible forms.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:SPDP
title: Shifted--Partial--Derivative rank
statement_text: Let p ∈ F [x_1, ... ,x_n] and κ,ell ≥ 0 . Define \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p) := dim _ F Span { m · partial _S p mid S ⊆ [n], |S|=κ, m monomial ,\ deg (m) ≤ ell }. \] Equivalently, form the SPDP matrix M_ κ,ell (p) whose rows are the coefficient vectors of all m · partial _S p with |S|=κ and deg (m) ≤ ell ; then Γ_ κ,ell (p)= rank _ F M_ κ,ell (p) . paragraph Explicit matrix construction. For complete formal specification, the SPDP matrix M_ κ,ell (p) has: bf Row indices : Pairs (S, m) where S ⊆ [n] with |S| = κ and m is a monomial with deg m ≤ ell . bf Column indices : All monomials in the standard monomial basis of F [x_1, ... , x_n] . bf Entry at (S,m) : The coefficient vector of m · partial _S p when expanded in the monomial basis. In ZFC terms: M_ κ,ell (p) is a finite matrix with entries in F , and its rank is computed via Gaussian elimination (or any equivalent algorithm decidable in ZFC).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:CEW-logn
title: CEW bound for the sorting-network compiler
statement_text: Let N _N be a Batcher odd--even merge sorting network on N wires, realized by radius- 1 comparator tiles in the holographic compiler. Suppose each primitive tile touches at most b ∈ N block interfaces and each comparator involves at most Δ ∈ N such tiles. Then for every time step t lying inside a comparator layer of N _N we have \[ CEW (t) ≤ 2 b Δ. \] If the tag/update phases between comparator layers are implemented by radius- 1 NC ^1 circuits of depth O( log log N) touching at most c_0 interfaces per layer, then there is a constant C>0 such that for all t we have \[ CEW (t) ≤ C log log N. \] In particular, across any polynomial number of accesses the compiled program satisfies CEW (p) ≤ C ( log N)^c for some absolute constants C,c>0 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:profiles
title: Interface-anonymous profiles
statement_text: At any time in the window, each live interface a carries a type τ(a) ∈ T . The profile is the histogram h: T → {0,1,2, ... ,R} given by \[ h(τ) := l|{a:\ τ(a)=τ} r|, qquad so that qquad Σ _ τ ∈ T h(τ) ≤ R. \] Let H(R) be the set of all profiles realizable by some length- κ window execution (for arbitrary κ ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:profile-compression-removes-k
title: Profile compression removes κ -dependence
statement_text: With notation as above, \[ |H(R)| ≤ binom R+m m = R^ O(1) . \] In particular, the number of realizable profiles depends polynomially on R and is independent of the window length κ .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:poly-many-profiles
title: Polynomially many profiles when R= polylog (n)
statement_text: If R ≤ C( log n)^c , then \[ |H(R)| ≤ ( log n)^ O(1) = n^ o(1) . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:profile-subspace
title: Profile subspaces via symmetric tensor powers
statement_text: Fix ell ≥ 0 and a polynomial p in the SPDP construction. We say the coefficient representation is block-factorable if: For each type τ ∈ T there exists a finite-dimensional vector space W_τ (over the base field) of dimension d_τ=O(1) such that each interface of type τ contributes a vector in W_τ , and the contribution of a multiset of interfaces of type τ lies in the symmetric tensor power Sym ^ h(τ) (W_τ) . Define the profile space \[ V_h := otimes_ τ ∈ T Sym ^ h(τ) (W_τ). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:within-profile-dim
title: Within-profile span dimension
statement_text: For each profile h , \[ dim V_h ≤ Π _ τ ∈ T binom h(τ)+d_τ-1 d_τ-1 ≤ (R+1)^ Σ _ τ (d_τ-1) = R^ O(1) . \] If R ≤ C( log n)^c and all d_τ=O(1) , then dim V_h ≤ ( log n)^ O(1) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:width-implies-rank
title: Width ⇒ Rank bound (polynomial via profile compression)
statement_text: Under the compiler construction (Section ), the following hold: (Bounded types) | T |=m=O(1) as in Definition ; (Width bound) the number of live interfaces is at most R throughout; (Within-profile span bound) Lemma applies, so RowSpan ( R _h) ⊆ V_h and dim (V_h) ≤ R^ O(1) (indeed ( log n)^ O(1) when R= polylog (n) ). Then the SPDP rank satisfies \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p) = rank (M_ κ,ell (p)) ≤ Σ _ h ∈ H(R) dim V_h ≤ |H(R)| · R^ O(1) = R^ O(1) . \] In particular, if R ≤ C( log n)^c , then Γ_ κ,ell (p) ≤ ( log n)^ O(1) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:can-map
title: Canonicalization map can ( · )
statement_text: Define can : Win _κ → Win _κ by the following deterministic procedure: bf (Disjoint-support commutation normal form). Reorder the κ derivative steps by repeatedly swapping adjacent steps whose interface supports are disjoint, until the window is in the fixed lexicographic order on the triple ( block index ,\ interface id within block ,\ time index ) . This implements convention (P6) and yields a unique representative of each commutation class. bf (Local word normal form). For each live interface e , let σ_e(w) ∈ Σ^* be the interface-local update word induced by the window w . Replace σ_e(w) by its monoid normal form NF (σ_e(w)) as in convention (P7), and rebuild the corresponding window representation. Let Win ^ can _κ := can ( Win _κ) be the set of canonical windows.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:local-monoid-action
title: Local update words act only through the finite monoid
statement_text: Work in the diagonal local basis (with the fixed block-local normalization Π_+=A ). Each symbol τ ∈ Σ induces a fixed interface-local linear action A_τ on the constant-dimensional interface tensor factors used to form SPDP rows. Extend multiplicatively to words: for u=τ_1 ... τ_t , set A_u := A_ τ_t ... A_ τ_1 . (Compiler note.) Here ``interface'' means the bounded set of boundary variables shared between adjacent blocks/cells in the fixed block partition B (a circuit/constraint interface), not a perceptual interface. If two words u,v ∈ Σ^* represent the same element of the finite transformation monoid M ⊆ Σ^Σ , then A_u = A_v . In particular A_u = A_ NF (u) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:finite-monoid-bounded-nf
title: Bounded normal forms in a finite local monoid
statement_text: There exists a constant q=O(1) depending only on the fixed local model such that: for every word w ∈ Σ^ast , the canonical representative NF (w) has length | NF (w)| ≤ q and induces the same transformation in M as w .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:canonical-windows-rowspan
title: Canonical windows reduction is row-span preserving
statement_text: Let p be any polynomial in the compiled regime, and let M^B_ κ,ell (p) be the blocked SPDP matrix (Definition , block-local specialization). For each window w ∈ Win _κ , let row (w) denote the corresponding SPDP row vector (i.e.\ the coefficient row indexed by the induced derivative/shifting choice). Then for all w ∈ Win _κ , \[ row (w) = row ( can (w)). \] Consequently, \[ RowSpan (M^B_ κ,ell (p) ) = span { row (w): w ∈ Win ^ can _κ}, quad and hence quad Γ^B_ κ,ell (p)\ is unchanged by restricting to canonical windows. \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:profile
title: Interface-anonymous profile
statement_text: The profile of a canonical window is the histogram h:Σ^ ≤ q → N that counts, for each local type word σ ∈ Σ^ ≤ q , the number of live interfaces whose local normal form equals σ . Thus Σ _ σ h(σ) ≤ R .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:perm-invariance
title: Permutation-invariance within blocks
statement_text: If two canonical windows differ only by a permutation of interface identities within the same block partition, then their SPDP row sets are related by left/right multiplication with block-diagonal invertible matrices (depending only on the permutation), hence they contribute the same rank. Consequently, SPDP upper bounds depend only on the profile histogram h from Definition .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:budget
title: Constant local change budget
statement_text: By (P1) and (P7), each live interface undergoes at most q=O(1) local type changes in any canonical window, with q independent of n,κ,ell .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:profile-compression-removes-k
title: Profile compression removes κ -dependence
statement_text: By Lemma (bounded normal forms), fix any canonical window of length κ with R live interfaces. Then there exists a constant q=O(1) , independent of n,κ,ell , such that each live interface i admits a canonical (normal-form) local word σ_i ∈ Σ_ ≤ q of length at most q , where \[ Σ_ ≤ q := cup_ t=0 ^ q Σ^ t qquad and qquad S' := |Σ_ ≤ q | = O(1). \] Consequently, the interface-anonymous profile of the window is completely determined by the histogram \[ h(σ) = l|{ i live in the window : σ_i=σ } r| qquad (σ ∈ Σ_ ≤ q ), \] and the number of realizable interface-anonymous profiles satisfies \[ \# Profiles ≤ binom R+S'-1 S'-1 = R^ O(1) , \] which in particular is independent of κ .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:poly-many-profiles
title: Polynomially many profiles
statement_text: Under the assumptions of Lemma , the set H of realizable interface-anonymous profiles has cardinality |H| ≤ R^ O(1) , independent of κ .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:profile-subspace
title: Profiles generate polylog-dimensional subspaces
statement_text: Let p be the compiled polynomial in the diagonal basis, and fix parameters κ,ell = Θ( log n) and R = C ( log n)^c . For each interface-anonymous profile h (in the sense of Lemma ) there exists a linear subspace V_ h of the SPDP row space such that: All SPDP rows corresponding to mixed partials partial ^ τ p with |τ| = κ and local type statistics matching h lie in V_ h . The dimension of V_ h satisfies \[ dim V_ h ≤ ( log n)^ O(1) ≤ n^ O(1) . \] Consequently, if H denotes the set of all interface-anonymous profiles, then \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p) ≤ Σ _ h ∈ H dim V_ h ≤ ( log n)^ O(1) · | H | ≤ ( log n)^ O(1) · R^ O(1) = n^ O(1) . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:compiled-width-rank
title: Compiled Width ⇒ Rank (profile-compressed form)
statement_text: Let p be the polynomial produced by the NF--SPDP compiler from a width- W , depth- D computation, under a fixed radius-- 1 block partition B and the interface-anonymous (profile-compressed) convention. Fix compiled SPDP parameters (κ,ell )=(K log n,K log n) for any fixed constant K ≥ 1 . Then the compiled (blocked) SPDP rank satisfies \[ Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p)\ ≤ \ R^ O(1) , \] where R=C( log n)^c is the CEW/profile budget parameter in the compiler regime. In particular Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p) ≤ ( log n)^ O(1) ≤ n^ O(1) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:restriction
title: Restriction monotonicity
statement_text: Let ρ be a (block--local) restriction/identification of variables and p':=p upharpoonright ρ . Then for all κ,ell , Γ_ κ,ell (p') ≤ Γ_ κ,ell (p) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:submatrix
title: Submatrix monotonicity
statement_text: If M' is any submatrix of M_ κ,ell (p) obtained by selecting a subset of rows and/or columns, then rank (M') ≤ Γ_ κ,ell (p) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:rank-subadditivity-sum
title: SPDP rank is subadditive under sums
statement_text: For any polynomials p_1, ... ,p_m and fixed parameters (κ,ell ) and block partition B , \[ Γ^ B _ κ,ell ( Σ _ i=1 ^ m p_i ) ≤ Σ _ i=1 ^ m Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p_i). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:affine
title: Affine/basis invariance
statement_text: Let Φ:xmapsto Ax+b with A ∈ GL_N(Bbb F) . Then Γ_ κ,ell (p ∘ Φ)=Γ_ κ,ell (p) for all κ,ell . Moreover, changing the monomial basis within blocks multiplies M_ κ,ell (p) on the left/right by block-diagonal invertible matrices, hence preserves rank.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:basis-invariance
title: Basis invariance
statement_text: Changing the monomial order or coordinate basis multiplies M_ κ,ell (p) on the left/right by invertible matrices; hence Γ_ κ,ell (p) is basis--invariant.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:monotonicity-suite
title: Monotonicity Suite
statement_text: The SPDP rank Γ_ κ,ell (p) satisfies the following properties: bf Restriction monotonicity (Lemma ): For any restriction ρ , Γ_ κ,ell (p upharpoonright ρ) ≤ Γ_ κ,ell (p) . bf Projection monotonicity (Lemma ): Selecting a subset of rows or columns cannot increase rank. bf Affine invariance (Lemma ): For any invertible affine map Φ , Γ_ κ,ell (p ∘ Φ) = Γ_ κ,ell (p) . bf Basis invariance (Lemma ): Changing monomial order or coordinate basis preserves Γ_ κ,ell (p) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:kappa-padding
title: κ -padding does not blow up blocked SPDP rank
statement_text: Let V be a polynomial independent of y_1, ... ,y_κ and let Y:= Π _ j=1 ^ κ y_j . For any ell and any block partition B , \[ Γ^ B _ κ,ell (Y · V)\ ≤ \ Σ _ r=0 ^ min {κ,deg (V)} binom κ r Γ^ B _ r,ell (V). \] In particular, if κ=O( log n) and Γ^ B _ r,ell (V) ≤ n^ O(1) for all r ≤ deg (V) , then Γ^ B _ κ,ell (Y · V) ≤ n^ O(1) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:rank-monotonicity-compiler
title: Rank monotonicity under compiler operations
statement_text: Let p(x) be an SPDP polynomial in variables x=(x_1, ... ,x_N) and fix parameters (κ,ell ) . Consider the following operations, which arise in the radius- 1 compiler and NP-side constructions: Block-local invertible linear change of variables on a subset of variables x_I (the Π^+ transform). Affine relabelling of variables x mapsto A x + b for an invertible matrix A ∈ GL _N( F ) and a fixed vector b ∈ F ^N . Variable restriction x_j gets c to a field constant and coordinate projection that forgets a subset of variables. Introduction of tag constants , i.e.\ adjoining symbols that are treated as fixed field elements and never differentiated with respect to. Local gadget multiplication and PAC projection as used in the compiler: replacing p by q := g · p for a block-local gadget g of bounded degree that depends only on a fixed, constant-size subset of the variables, and then applying the positivity-preserving projection PAC , which by definition is implemented by a finite composition of operations of types up (i) --up (iii) . Then there exists a constant C (depending only on (κ,ell ) and the gadget library, not on p or N ) and parameters (κ',ell ') with κ' ≤ κ+O(1) and ell ' ≤ ell +O(1) such that: Operations up (i) and up (ii) preserve SPDP rank exactly: \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p) = Γ_ κ,ell (p') \] for any polynomial p' obtained from p by a finite composition of block-local basis changes and invertible affine relabellings. Operations up (iii) and up (iv) do not increase SPDP rank: if p' is obtained from p by applying any finite sequence of variable restrictions, coordinate projections, or introductions of tag constants, then \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p') ≤ Γ_ κ,ell (p). \] Operation up (v) is rank-monotone up to a fixed polynomial factor: if q is obtained from p by a single local gadget multiplication followed by a PAC projection, then \[ Γ_ κ,ell (q) ≤ N^C · Γ_ κ',ell ' (p) \] for some constant C and parameters (κ',ell ') as above. In particular, along the bounded-depth compiler pipeline described in Theorem , SPDP rank never grows faster than a fixed polynomial in N times the SPDP rank of the initial polynomial. Moreover, tags are not counted as SPDP variables: they are treated as fixed field constants and never appear in the block partition B , and so they do not contribute to Γ_ κ,ell at any stage.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:classical-observer-equiv
title: Classical--Observer Equivalence
statement_text: The following equivalences hold: P _ classical = P _ observer where P _ observer = {L : ∃ O with CEW (O) ≤ n^c deciding L} NP _ classical = NP _ observer where NP _ observer = {L : ∃ V with CEW (V) ≤ n^c verifying L} The epistemic complexity class EpistemicP = {L : ∃ O observer with bounded resolution deciding L} equals P

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:simulation-overhead
title: Simulation Overhead
statement_text: Let M=(Q,Γ,δ,q_0,q_ accept ,q_ reject ) be a single-tape Turing machine that runs in time t(n) ∈ n^ Θ(1) on inputs of length n . From M we can construct, in time The construction here is meta-level (performed by the proof); it is not counted against the running time of the resulting observer. O(t(n) log n) , an observer O_M= l(S_M,Σ,Δ,s_0,s_ accept ,s_ reject r) such that |S_M| = O l(t(n) log n r) , and on any input x ∈ Σ^n , O_M(x) halts in at most t(n) transitions, yielding the same accept/reject answer as M(x) . Consequently, the TM → Observer translation preserves polynomial running time with at most a logarithmic factor in state-space size and no slowdown in step complexity.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:observer
title: Observer Frame ( CEW Instantiation)
statement_text: Building on Definition A, an Observer with parameter n specializes the observer frame F = (S, R, I) to the CEW setting: tt cew\_limit : N → R - Maximum CEW the observer can handle tt compute : (Fin n → tt Q) → tt Option Q - Symbolic evaluator (partial function) tt sound - Soundness condition: computable functions must have CEW ≤ limit tt monotonic - Observer capacity increases with problem size

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: prop:one-way-implication
title: Interpretive implication (one direction)
statement_text: CEW/SPDP separation as proved in this paper implies P ≠ NP . The converse direction (that P ≠ NP implies CEW/SPDP separation) is not claimed; establishing that would require showing our framework captures all possible P ≠ NP proofs, which is beyond the scope of this work.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:bp-compilation
title: Compilation Lemma (BP simulation of polytime)
statement_text: If L ∈ P is decidable in time n^k , then for each n there exists a deterministic layered BP B_n of length L' = n^ O(k) and width W = n^ O(1) computing χ_L restriction {0,1}^n .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:bp-spdp
title: BP → SPDP, fixed order --- full proof
statement_text: bf Statement. Let B be a deterministic layered BP of length L' and width W over {0,1}^n , and let f be the multilinear polynomial it computes. For any fixed ell ∈ {2,3} , \[ rk _ SPDP ,ell (f) ≤ (C_ell W L')^ d_ell , \] for absolute constants C_ell , d_ell depending only on ell . (For concreteness one may take d_ell = 2ell +2 .)

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:p-polynomial-rank
title: P-languages admit polynomial SPDP rank
statement_text: bf Statement. Let L ∈ P be decidable in time t(n) = n^k . For each fixed ell ∈ {2,3} , there exists c = c(κ,ell ) such that \[ rk _ SPDP ,ell (χ_L) ≤ n^c. \] Equivalently, rk _ SPDP (χ_L) = n^ O(k) for fixed ell .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:p-characterization
title: P ⊆ Low SPDP Rank
statement_text: For every L ∈ P there exists c such that, for all n , \[ rk _ SPDP (L_n) ≤ n^c, \] where L_n is L restricted to inputs of length n .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:sparse-basis
title: Sparse-basis recovery in polytime --- Optional
statement_text: Let f(x_1, ... , x_n) be a degree- d polynomial over a field F with \[ rk _ SPDP ,c (f) ≤ n^6. \] There is a deterministic algorithm running in n^ O(c) time that outputs a monomial basis B of size |B| ≤ n^6 , and the coefficient vector of f in that basis. Consequently, the decision problem computed by f can be solved in time O(n^6) by evaluating the recovered sparse form.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:bridge
title: Partial derivatives form a submatrix
statement_text: For multilinear p and any partition [n] = S sqcup T , \[ rank l( PD _ S,T (p) r) ≤ rank l(M_ SPDP (p) r) = rk _ SPDP ^ all (p). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:non-relativizing
title: Oracle-invariance of SPDP lower bounds
statement_text: There exists an oracle A such that P^A = NP^A , while our SPDP lower bounds remain valid relative to A . Consequently, the proof technique of S 2 (which combines the upper bound P ⊆ LowSPDP with explicit SPDP lower bounds) is oracle-invariant in the sense that the algebraic facts it uses do not depend on oracle access.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:spdp-not-natural
title: Algebraic non-naturality of low SPDP rank
statement_text: For each n , P_ low (n) is (i) not large in the algebraic sense (Zariski-meagre / measure-zero in coefficient space), and (ii) not constructive from truth tables in poly (n) time. Hence the SPDP-rank property used by our framework is not ``natural''.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:general-order-monotonicity
title: General-order monotonicity
statement_text: Let p ∈ F [x_1, ... , x_n] be multilinear and let 0 ≤ ell ≤ n . For a partition [n] = S sqcup T with |S| ≤ ell , let PD _ S,T (p) denote the classical partial-derivative coefficient matrix whose rows are indexed by monomials x^V with V ⊆ T , whose columns are indexed by monomials x^U with U ⊆ S , and whose entries are \[ l( PD _ S,T (p) r)_ V,U := [x^V x^U] p. \] Then \[ max _ substack S ⊆ [n], |S| ≤ ell rank l( PD _ S,T (p) r) ≤ rk _ SPDP ,ell (p). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:transfer-partial-derivative
title: Transfer of known partial -matrix lower bounds
statement_text: If a family {p_n} admits a classical partial-derivative matrix lower bound \[ rank l( PD _ S_n,T_n (p_n) r) = 2^ Ω(n) \] for some S_n ⊆ [n] with |S_n| ≤ ell , then \[ rk _ SPDP ,ell (p_n) = 2^ Ω(n) . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:deterministic-dual
title: Deterministic dual via triple-shift moments (unconditional)
statement_text: There is a deterministic procedure ExtractI that, given a spanning family {f_1, ... ,f_r} of V_n (with r ≤ n^3 ), outputs an index set I = {(i_t,h_t)}_ t=1 ^r ⊆ [r] × [n]^3 with |I|=r such that the r linear functionals \[ L_ (i,h) (v) \ :=\ le v,\ f_i( · +h)rangle qquad l((i,h) ∈ I r) \] achieve full row rank when evaluated on any (r+1) -point support Ω ⊆ {0,1}^n . Using this I , a deterministic algorithm outputs a nonzero w ∈ V_n^ perp in tilde O(n^ 12 ) bit operations. (Here tilde O( · ) hides polylogarithmic factors in the bit-length. The index set I is produced explicitly by ExtractI ; no existential assumption on I is made.)

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:tiny-density
title: Low-rank Boolean functions are exponentially rare
statement_text: Fix constants c,ell >0 . Let \[ F _ n,c \ :=\ { f:{0,1}^n → {0,1}\ :\ rk _ SPDP ,ell (f)\ ≤ \ n^c }. \] Then \[ frac | F _ n,c | 2^ 2^ n \ ≤ \ 2^ -Ω(2^ n ) . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:eval-from-certificate
title: Evaluation from a low-rank certificate
statement_text: Let f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} be a Boolean function and fix an order ell ≥ 0 . Suppose we are given a low-rank certificate for f consisting of: a rank factorization of the order- ell SPDP matrix, \[ M_ell (f) \ =\ U V, quad U ∈ F ^ R × r ,\ \ V ∈ F ^ r × C ,\ \ r= rk _ SPDP ,ell (f), \] where R=Θ(n^ O(ell ) ) and C=2^n ; and an implicit column application routine that, on input x ∈ {0,1}^n , computes V χ(x) in poly (n,r) time, where χ(x) ∈ F ^C is the monomial-evaluation vector χ(x)_m = m(x) . Then f(x) can be evaluated in time poly (n,r) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:cew
title: Multilinear representation and CEW
statement_text: Fix a field F of characteristic 0 or a sufficiently large prime. For a Boolean function f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} , let tilde f ∈ F [x_1, ... ,x_n] be its unique multilinear polynomial that agrees with f on {0,1}^n : \[ tilde f(x) = Σ _ S ⊆ [n] hat f(S) x^S, qquad x^S := Π _ i ∈ S x_i. \] Define \[ CEW (f) \ :=\ max { |S|:\ hat f(S) ≠ 0 } \] (i.e., CEW (f) = deg (tilde f) ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:observer-classes
title: Observer classes
statement_text: For each n , let PolyObs _n \ &:=\ { f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} mid CEW (f) ≤ n^ O(1) }, ExpObs _n \ &:=\ { f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} mid CEW (f) ≤ 2^ Θ(n) }.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: prop:bp-cew
title: BP degree ⇒ polynomial CEW
statement_text: Let B be a deterministic layered branching program (BP) of length L over variables x_1, ... ,x_n with edge labels in {1,x_i,1-x_i} , and let f be its computed function. Then \[ CEW (f) \ ≤ \ L. \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:p-polyobs
title: P ⊆ PolyObs via BP compilation
statement_text: If a language L ∈ P is decidable in time n^k , then for each n the characteristic function χ_L admits a representation with CEW (χ_L) ≤ n^ O(k) . Hence χ_L ∈ PolyObs _n .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:deg-rank
title: Degree bounds columns ⇒ rank bound
statement_text: Let f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} have multilinear degree d= CEW (f) . Fix any constant order ell ≥ 0 . Then \[ rk _ SPDP ,ell (f) \ ≤ \ Σ _ j=0 ^d binom n j . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:exp-rank-linear-cew
title: Exponential SPDP rank ⇒ linear CEW
statement_text: Fix ell ≥ 0 . Suppose a family {f_n} satisfies rk _ SPDP ,ell (f_n) ≥ 2^ γ n for some constant γ>0 . Then \[ CEW (f_n) \ ≥ \ c n \] for some constant c=c(γ)>0 and all sufficiently large n .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:classical-lb-cew
title: Classical partial -LB ⇒ large CEW
statement_text: If {p_n} has rank ( PD _ S_n,T_n (p_n))=2^ Ω(n) for some |S_n| ≤ ell , then CEW (p_n) ≥ Ω(n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:entropy-tight
title: Entropy-tight CEW vs.\ SPDP rank
statement_text: For any ell ≥ 0 and any f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} , \[ min l{ d:\ Σ _ j=0 ^dbinom n j \ ≥ \ rk _ SPDP ,ell (f) r} \ ≤ \ CEW (f) \ ≤ \ n. \] In particular, if rk _ SPDP ,ell (f) ≥ 2^ γ n then CEW (f) ≥ (H^ -1 (γ)-o(1)) n ; conversely, if CEW (f) ≤ δ n then rk _ SPDP ,ell (f) ≤ 2^ H(δ)n .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:epistemic-p
title: Epistemic P
statement_text: EpistemicP (n) is the set of f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} with CEW (f) ≤ n^ O(1) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:epistemic-np
title: Epistemic NP
statement_text: EpistemicNP (n) is the set of f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} for which there exists a polynomial p and a polynomial-time verifier V such that \[ f(x)=1 quad Longleftrightarrow quad ∃ w ∈ {0,1}^ ≤ p(n) \ \ V(x,w)=1, \] and, for each fixed w , the acceptance predicate xmapsto V(x,w) has CEW ≤ n^ O(1) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:observer-hierarchy
title: Observer hierarchy
statement_text: For every n , PolyObs _n ⊊ ExpObs _n .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:epistemic-separation
title: Epistemic P ⊊ NP
statement_text: For all sufficiently large n , \[ EpistemicP (n) \ ⊊ \ EpistemicNP (n). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:resource-bounded-sep
title: Resource-bounded separation
statement_text: Fix any constant derivative order ell ∈ {2,3} . There exists an explicit family {f_n} such that bf (Upper for P ) For every g ∈ P , rk _ SPDP ,ell (g_n) ≤ n^ O(1) and CEW (g_n) ≤ n^ O(1) . bf (Lower for the hard family) rk _ SPDP ,ell (f_n) ≥ 2^ Ω(n) and therefore CEW (f_n) ≥ Ω(n) . bf (Observer separation) EpistemicP (n) ⊊ EpistemicNP (n) (Theorem ), witnessed by {f_n} .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:unique-multilin
title: Unique multilinearization
statement_text: Every f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} has a unique tilde f ∈ F [x_1, ... ,x_n] multilinear with tilde f|_ {0,1}^n =f .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:degree-cew
title: Degree = CEW
statement_text: \[ deg (tilde f) = CEW (f) = max { |S|:\ hat f(S) ≠ 0 }. \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:column-bound
title: Column bound for order- ell SPDP; cf.\ S 4.2
statement_text: If CEW (f)=d , then \[ rk _ SPDP ,ell (f) \ ≤ \ Σ _ j=0 ^d binom n j . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:uniform-monotonicity-ref
title: Uniform monotonicity; cf.\ S 2.6--S 2.7
statement_text: For any partition [n]=Ssqcup T with |S| ≤ ell , the partial-derivative matrix PD _ S,T (f) appears (up to transpose) as a submatrix of the order- ell SPDP matrix. Hence \[ rank ( PD _ S,T (f)) \ ≤ \ rk _ SPDP ,ell (f). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:entropy-tight-ref
title: Entropy-tight CEW ↔ SPDP; cf.\ S 4.2
statement_text: If rk _ SPDP ,ell (f) ≥ 2^ γ n then CEW (f) ≥ (H^ -1 (γ)-o(1)) n ; if CEW (f) ≤ δ n then rk _ SPDP ,ell (f) ≤ 2^ H(δ)n .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:exact-compilation
title: Exact polytime → observer compilation
statement_text: Let M be a polynomial-time decider for L . There exists a layered BP B_n of length n^ O(1) and polynomial width such that the Boolean function f_n=χ_L computed by M at length n equals the function computed by B_n . Consequently, \[ CEW (f_n) ≤ n^ O(1) ,qquad rk _ SPDP ,ell (f_n) ≤ n^ O(1) quad (ell ∈ {2,3}). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:hard-implies-separation
title: Explicit hard family ⇒ observer separation
statement_text: Let {f_n} be the Lagrangian/Tseitin family (see S 6/S 14) with rank ( PD _ S_n,T_n (f_n))=2^ Ω(n) for some |S_n| ≤ ell . Then \[ CEW (f_n) ≥ Ω(n) quad and quad rk _ SPDP ,ell (f_n) ≥ 2^ Ω(n) . \] Hence f_n ∉ PolyObs _n but f_n ∈ EpistemicNP (n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:deterministic-dual-ref
title: Deterministic dual w ∈ V_n^ perp ; cf.\ S 2.7
statement_text: Let V_n be the span of the compiled `` P -side'' evaluations (rows chosen by the fixed triple-shift scheme). There is a deterministic algorithm running in tilde O(n^ 12 ) bit time that outputs a nonzero w ∈ V_n^ perp .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:cert-completeness-soundness
title: Completeness and Soundness of the certificate
statement_text: Let w be as above. Then: bf (Completeness) For every g ∈ P (compiled by the fixed pipeline), le w, g( · +h)rangle =0 for all indexed shifts h ∈ [n]^3 . bf (Soundness) For the hard family f_n (Lagrangian/Tseitin), le w, f_n( · +h_star )rangle ≠ 0 for some fixed h_star ∈ [n]^3 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:non-circular
title: Non-circular evaluation
statement_text: Given a low-rank certificate for g (rank factorization with efficient column application), g(x) can be computed in poly (n, rk _ SPDP ,ell (g)) time (Theorem ). Together with Theorem , the separation uses only algebraic certificates and fixed compilation---no oracle calls to the target function---so the argument is non-circular.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:epistemic-p-matched
title: EpistemicP
statement_text: EpistemicP (n) is the set of f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} computable by an observer that runs in time n^ O(1) and whose intermediate CEW is bounded by n^ O(1) . Let EpistemicP := cup_n EpistemicP (n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:epistemic-np-matched
title: EpistemicNP
statement_text: EpistemicNP (n) is the set of f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} for which there exists a polynomial p and a verifier running in time n^ O(1) such that \[ f(x)=1 quad Longleftrightarrow quad ∃ w ∈ {0,1}^ ≤ p(n) \ V(x,w)=1, \] and for each fixed w , the acceptance predicate xmapsto V(x,w) has CEW ≤ n^ O(1) . Let EpistemicNP := cup_n EpistemicNP (n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: prop:bp-eval-bounds
title: BP length ⇒ CEW/evaluation bounds
statement_text: If a layered BP of length L and width W computes f , then CEW (f) ≤ L and f(x) can be evaluated in poly (n,L,W) time.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:epistemic-classical-equiv
title: Epistemic--classical equivalence
statement_text: \[ EpistemicP =P,qquad EpistemicNP =NP. \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:succinct-index-access
title: Succinct indexing and coordinate access
statement_text: A column index c ∈ C ^B_ κ,ell is succinct if it admits an encoding enc (c) ∈ {0,1}^ O( log n) from which c can be decoded in poly ( log n) time. We say the blocked coefficient representation is coordinate-accessible if there exists a uniform algorithm EvalRow such that, on input ( enc (w), enc (c)) , it outputs the entry row (w)[c] ∈ F in time poly (n) using poly (n) space.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:mmf
title: Materialized multilinear form (MMF)
statement_text: Let C be a succinct index set (here C = C ^B_ κ,ell ). A materialized multilinear form is a pair Rep =( state , Eval ) where: state is a data structure of size poly (n) , Eval is a uniform algorithm that on input ( state , enc (c)) returns the coefficient of basis element c ∈ C in time poly (n) . We call Rep poly-materialized if lvert state rvert ≤ poly (n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:rb
title: Representation bound (RB)
statement_text: A family of blocked SPDP rows { row (w)}_ w ∈ W satisfies a representation bound RB (n) if there is a uniform construction wmapsto Rep (w) such that Rep (w) is poly-materialized and for all c ∈ C ^B_ κ,ell , \[ Eval ( Rep (w), enc (c)) = row (w)[c], qquad with qquad lvert state (w)rvert ≤ RB (n). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:no-giant-poly
title: No implicit expansion / no giant polynomial
statement_text: Assume the compilation/normal-form machinery of the bridge (Theorem ) is instantiated in the fixed blocked basis of M^B_ κ,ell (p) (cf.\ Definition ). Then for every canonical window w produced by the bridge, there exists a poly-materialized representation Rep (w) (Definition ) such that: state (w) has size poly (n) (indeed polylog (n) in the compiled regime), and every coefficient query row (w)[c] is answered by Eval in time poly (n) without enumerating C ^B_ κ,ell or expanding a full monomial list. Equivalently: the bridge never assumes availability of an exponentially large multilinear polynomial as an explicit object; it only uses poly-materialized coordinate access.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:bridge-rb
title: Bridge with explicit RB
statement_text: In the Observer--Classical Bridge of Theorem , all multilinear/coefficient objects manipulated by the observer are to be interpreted as poly-materialized representations satisfying RB (n)= poly (n) in the sense of Definition . In particular, any subsequent use of the bridge in the separation proof does not rely on hidden exponential expansion.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:epistemic-classes-cew
title: Epistemic classes (CEW-bounded observers)
statement_text: Define EpistemicP as the class of languages L ⊆ {0,1}^star for which there exists a uniform family of observer computations { O _n}_ n ≥ 1 such that: ( Correctness ) For all x ∈ {0,1}^n , O _n(x) outputs 1 iff x ∈ L . ( CEW boundedness ) The computation induced by O _n under the canonical compilation has CEW ( O _n) ≤ polylog (n) . ( Materialization discipline ) All multilinear/coefficient objects used by O _n are accessed only via poly-materialized coordinate access as formalized in Subsection . Define EpistemicNP analogously using the standard witness-verifier form internal to the observer model: L ∈ EpistemicNP if there exists a uniform observer-verifier family { V _n} and a polynomial p( · ) such that for all x ∈ {0,1}^n , \[ x ∈ L ⟺ ∃ w ∈ {0,1}^ p(n) \ such that \ V _n(x,w)=1, \] and the compiled verifier computation satisfies the same CEW/materialization conditions.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:epistemic-classical-equivalence-full
title: Epistemic--classical equivalence (fully proved by composition)
statement_text: Assume the Observer--Classical Bridge of Theorem , the CEW equiv SPDP-rank equivalence (Lemma ), and the no--implicit--expansion/materialization discipline (Subsection ). Then \[ EpistemicP = P qquad and qquad EpistemicNP = NP . \] Consequently, \[ EpistemicP ⊊ EpistemicNP quad Longleftrightarrow quad P ⊊ NP . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:licensed-epistemic-reading
title: Licensed epistemic reading of texorpdfstring P ≠ NP P≠NP
statement_text: Assuming the hypotheses of Theorem , the statement P ≠ NP is equivalent to the following observer-capacity claim: There exist languages whose verification is possible for CEW-bounded observers with witnesses ( EpistemicNP ), but whose decision is impossible for any uniformly CEW-bounded observer family ( EpistemicP ). Equivalently: bounded contextual capacity (bounded CEW / polynomial SPDP-rank regime) is insufficient to decide all witness-verifiable tasks.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:epistemic-time-space
title: EpistemicTIME/SPACE
statement_text: For a function f: N → N , \[ EpistemicTIME [f(n)] := { L mid ∃ observer deciding L in O(f(n)) time and with CEW ≤ f(n)^ O(1) }, \] and similarly for EpistemicSPACE by replacing the time bound with a space bound and tracking CEW as an auxiliary representation budget.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:observer-hierarchy-full
title: Observer hierarchy
statement_text: PolyObs _n ⊊ ExpObs _n (as in S 4, Theorem ). Consequently, \[ EpistemicP ⊊ EpistemicNP , \] witnessed by the Lagrangian/Tseitin families (S 6/S 14) whose partial -matrix (hence SPDP) rank is 2^ Ω(n) , implying CEW ≥ Ω(n) (Corollary ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:polytime-upper-bound
title: Polytime upper bound; cf.\ S 2.1
statement_text: If L ∈ P is decidable in time n^k , then for each input length n the characteristic function χ_L satisfies \[ rk _ SPDP ,ell (χ_L) \ ≤ \ n^ O(k) quad for each fixed ell ∈ {2,3}. \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model

statement_text: Let {p_n} be the Lagrangian/Tseitin family (e.g., \#3SAT or expander-Tseitin encodings). If there exist partitions [n]=S_nsqcup T_n with |S_n| ≤ ell such that \[ rank ( PD _ S_n,T_n (p_n)) \ =\ 2^ Ω(n) , \] then \[ rk _ SPDP ,ell (p_n) \ =\ 2^ Ω(n) . \]

label: thm:det-dual-ref
title: Deterministic dual w ∈ V_n^ perp ; cf.\ S 2.7
statement_text: Let V_n denote the span of the compiled `` P -side'' evaluations indexed by a fixed triple-shift scheme. There is a deterministic algorithm running in tilde O(n^ 12 ) bit-time that outputs a nonzero w ∈ V_n^ perp .

statement_text: Given a rank- r factorization M_ell (f)=UV with efficient column application xmapsto Vχ(x) , one can evaluate f(x) in time poly (n,r) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:sep-non-circular
title: Separation, non-circular
statement_text: For L ∈ P , the compiled rows lie in V_n and are annihilated by w ; for the hard family p_n (Theorem ), le w, p_n( · +h_star )rangle ≠ 0 for a fixed index h_star . No oracle access to p_n is used---only algebraic certificates---so the argument is non-circular.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model

title: Blocked rank is at most unblocked rank

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:identity-minor-blocked
title: Identity minor is contained in the blocked SPDP matrix
statement_text: In the NP-side construction (lane family with radius-- 1 blocks), the rows and columns used to form the n^ Θ( log n) identity minor are indexed by block-admissible derivative supports and block-compatible ambient monomials. Hence the exhibited minor lies inside M^ B _ κ,ell (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) , and therefore \[ Γ^ B _ κ,ell (Q^ × _ Φ_n )\ ≥ \ n^ Θ( log n) qquad over any field F . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:uniform-tableau-family
title: Uniform bounded-width tableau family
statement_text: Fix a time exponent c . There exists a finite template set T _c (depending only on the chosen machine normal form and c ) such that for every M ∈ DTIME (n^c) and input length n , the accepting tableau predicate is a width- ≤ 5 CNF Φ_ M,n obtained by tiling the (T(n) × S(n)) tableau with templates from T _c . Moreover, size (Φ_ M,n ) ≤ n^ c_Φ(c) for a constant c_Φ(c) depending only on c .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:tm-support
title: Support lemma
statement_text: For each S with |S| = κ , partial _S P_ M,n is a sum of at most \[ \#{(t,i) : S ⊆ Nbr (t,i)} ≤ C_1 \] local terms, each supported in a neighborhood of size ≤ R_0 := | Nbr (t,i)| = O(1) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:PtoPolySPDP
title: P ⇒ poly - SPDP , model-exact
statement_text: Let M be a deterministic single-tape TM running in time T(n) ≤ n^c . There is a uniform family of constant-degree polynomials {P_ M,n }_ n ∈ N over any field F of characteristic 0 , with \# vars (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) , such that: For all Boolean inputs (x,τ) , P_ M,n (x,τ) = 1 iff τ is a valid accepting tableau of M on x . For (κ,ell ) = (lfloor α log n rfloor , lfloor β log n rfloor ) with any fixed α, β > 0 , \[ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) . \] The mapping n mapsto circuit for P_ M,n is computable in time poly (n) (uniformity).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:sn-cew
title: Sorting-network compiler: locality and CEW
statement_text: Fix N wires and the Batcher odd--even merge sorting network N_N . Compile one logical array access as: Tagging (NC ^1 ): mark the requested address by computing req:=[addr=a] in depth O( log log N) . Forward pass: apply the fixed layers of N_N with key (req,addr) . Local read/update at a fixed position. Reverse pass: apply the inverse layers of N_N . Each comparator acts on an adjacent pair (radius 1 ). Every layer of N_N consists of disjoint comparators. Therefore each layer tiles into disjoint constant-size blocks. The depth of N_N is O( log ^2 N) , and at any time the number of blocks intersecting any cut is O( log N) . Consequently, under the time × tape tiling with step Δ=1 , the contextual entanglement width per logical access satisfies \[ CEW = max {underbrace O( log N) _ network layers , underbrace O( log log N) _ tag/update (NC ^1 ) } = O( log N). \] All gadgets are of constant algebraic degree; the overall compilation preserves radius r=1 .
bounds: O(\log\log N); O(\log^2 N); O(\log N)

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:perm-exp-rank
title: Exponential SPDP rank for perm _n
statement_text: Let X = (x_ i,j )_ 1 ≤ i,j ≤ n be an n × n matrix of indeterminates over a field F (characteristic arbitrary). Let \[ perm _n(X) = Σ _ σ ∈ S_n Π _ i=1 ^n x_ i,σ(i) . \] For any integer κ ∈ {0,1, ... ,n} , consider the SPDP parameters with shift ell =0 (i.e., order κ derivatives and no shift). Then \[ Γ_ κ,0 ( perm _n) ≥ binom n κ . \] In particular, for κ = lfloor n/2 rfloor we have \[ Γ_ lfloor n/2 rfloor , 0 ( perm _n) ≥ binom n lfloor n/2 rfloor = Θ (frac 2^n sqrt n ) = 2^ Ω(n) . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:disjoint-witness
title: Disjoint-witness independence
statement_text: For distinct S, S' ⊆ [n] with |S| = |S'| = κ , the monomial m_S = Π _ i ∉ S x_ i,i appears in partial _S perm _n with coefficient 1 , and does not appear in partial _ S' perm _n . Consequently, the set {partial _S perm _n : |S| = κ} is linearly independent.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:intersection-packing
title: Intersection-bounded packing in binom [n] κ
statement_text: Fix n ∈ N , κ = lfloor w n rfloor with w ∈ (0,1) , and a parameter α ∈ (0,w) . Then there exists a family F ⊆ binom [n] κ such that |S ∩ T| ≤ α n for all distinct S, T ∈ F and \[ | F | ≥ frac binom n κ Σ _ t = lceil α n rceil ^κ binom κ t binom n-κ κ-t ≥ 2^ (H(w) - β(w,α))n - O( log n) , \] where \[ β(w,α) := max _ t ∈ [α n, κ] ( frac κ n H (frac t κ ) + frac n-κ n H (frac κ-t n-κ ) ) = max _ θ ∈ [α/w, 1] ( w H(θ) + (1-w) H (frac w - θ w 1-w ) ). \] Here H(x) = -x log _2 x - (1-x) log _2(1-x) is the binary entropy, and the O( log n) term collects Stirling-type factors.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:shifted-spdp-perm
statement_text: For any fixed w ∈ (0,1) , α ∈ (0, w/2) , and ell = lceil frac 1 4 log n rceil , there is n_0 such that for all n ≥ n_0 and κ = lfloor w n rfloor , \[ Γ_ κ,ell ( perm _n) ≥ 2^ (H(w) - β(w,α))n - o(n) . \] In particular, the lower bound holds with logarithmic shift degree and bounded pairwise intersections.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:god-move-global
title: Global Projection / God-Move (codimension-collapse projection)
statement_text: Let {p_n} be a family of polynomials p_n ∈ F [x_1, ... ,x_ N(n) ] and fix parameters κ,ell ∈ N . We say that {p_n} admits a Global Projection (God-Move) at (κ,ell ) if there exist, uniformly in n : a variable projection φ_n: F [x_1, ... ,x_ N(n) ] → F [y_1, ... ,y_ M(n) ] that is linear (affine is also allowed after homogenization), invertible row/column reindexings P_n,Q_n (permutation/block-invertible matrices), such that the shifted-partial matrix contains an identity block of size R(n) : \[ P_n M_ κ,ell (p_n ∘ φ_n ) Q_n ⊇ I_ R(n) . \] Equivalently, \[ rank _ F M_ κ,ell (p_n ∘ φ_n )\ ≥ \ R(n). \] We call R(n) the revealed identity size . In our applications R(n)=n^ Ω( log n) (often R(n)=binom n κ with κ=Θ( log n) ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:god-move-existence
title: Existence of the God-Move for the hard family
statement_text: There is an explicit hard family {h_n} (e.g.\ the permanent perm _n or a Tseitin/expander-based CNF polynomial) and constants c_0,c_1>0 such that for \[ k= lceil c_0 log n rceil ,qquad ell = lceil c_1 log n rceil , \] the family {h_n} admits a Global Projection (God-Move) at (κ,ell ) with revealed identity size \[ R(n) = n^ Ω( log n) . \] Moreover, the projection φ_n and the reindexings P_n,Q_n are uniformly computable in time poly (n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:god-move-lb
title: Exponential SPDP lower bound
statement_text: Under the hypotheses of Theorem , \[ Γ_ κ,ell (h_n) = rank _ F M_ κ,ell (h_n)\ ≥ \ R(n) = n^ Ω( log n) . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:god-move
title: Global projection / ``God Move'' for perm _n
statement_text: Fix n ≥ 1 and κ ∈ {0, ... ,n} . Let M_ κ,0 ( perm _n) be the SPDP matrix (Definition ) whose rows are partial _S perm _n with |S| = κ (no shifts, ell = 0 ), expressed in the standard monomial basis of F [x_ i,j ]_ 1 ≤ i,j ≤ n . Define the binom n κ ``witness monomials'' \[ m_S := Π _ i ∈ [n] \ S x_ i,i quad (S ⊆ [n], |S| = κ). \] Let C_n := {m_S : |S| = κ} . There is a uniform, polynomial-time computable projection \[ Π_n : Monomials longrightarrow F ^ C_n , quad Π_n( monomial u) = (1_ {u = m_T} )_ T : |T| = κ , \] such that \[ Π_n M_ κ,0 ( perm _n) = I_ binom n κ \] after ordering rows/columns compatibly with {S} and {m_T} . Consequently, M_ κ,0 ( perm _n) has rank at least binom n κ . For κ = lfloor n/2 rfloor this gives Γ_ κ,0 ( perm _n) ≥ binom n lfloor n/2 rfloor = 2^ Ω(n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: prop:zfc-conservativity
title: Conservativity over ZFC
statement_text: The following are definable in first-order ZFC with parameters n ∈ N and a base field F of characteristic 0 or sufficiently large prime: Boolean functions f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} (as their graphs). Multilinear polynomials p ∈ F [x_1, ... ,x_n] and their coefficient vectors (finite functions U ⊆ N ^n → F ). Partial derivatives partial ^ |R| p/partial x_R and their coefficient vectors (defined via finite algebraic recurrences). The order- ell SPDP matrix M_ell (p) : a finite matrix over F with rows indexed by (R,α) ( |R|=ell , deg α ≤ ell ) and columns by monomials x_V , entries [x_V](α · partial ^ |R| p/partial x_R) . Rank of a finite matrix over F (as existence of a largest nonzero minor). Layered branching programs, their path polynomials, and evaluation maps. The subspace V_n spanned by a finite, explicitly indexed family of compiled evaluations, and the orthogonal subspace V_n^ perp w.r.t.\ the fixed inner product le u, grangle = Σ _ x ∈ {0,1}^n u(x)g(x) . The deterministic construction of a nonzero w ∈ V_n^ perp by Gaussian/Bareiss elimination on a finite matrix with entries in F .

label: cor:terminology-alignment
title: Terminology alignment
statement_text: Under these definitions, EpistemicP =P and EpistemicNP =NP . This identification is not used to prove the separation; it serves only to align terminology. (See Subsection for the no--implicit--expansion guarantee.)

title: Algebraic separation
statement_text: Let V_n and w_n be as above. There exists a fixed index h_star in the finite index set used to generate the P -side rows (e.g., a triple shift) such that, for all sufficiently large n , \[ le w_n, p_n( · +h_star )rangle \ ≠ \ 0, \] while for every f ∈ P and every allowed index h one has le w_n, f( · +h)rangle =0 for all sufficiently large n .

statement_text: There exists a language L with L ∈ NP \ P , and, for all sufficiently large n , every polynomially bounded observer O (bounded time and bounded CEW/representation degree) fails to compute some explicit high-rank characteristic function f_n^star :{0,1}^n → {0,1} satisfying rk _ SPDP ,ell (f_n^star ) ≥ 2^ Ω(n) (fixed ell ∈ {2,3} ). label: thm:observer-equivalence
title: Formal observer equivalence
statement_text: Let sf FiniteObs denote the class of uniform deterministic polynomial-time procedures. Define the following observer principle: ( Observer Separation Principle ) There exists a language L^star ∈ NP such that no finite observer decides L^star , i.e. \[ ( ∃ L^star ∈ NP)\ ( ∀ O ∈ sf FiniteObs )\ [ O does not decide L^star ]. \] Then bf (OSP) is logically equivalent to P ≠ NP .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:holographic-completion-equivalence
title: Holographic completion equivalence (formal)
statement_text: Fix a uniform encoding leΦrangle of 3 CNF instances and a uniform boundary map B( · ) computable in polynomial time (the ``holographic boundary view''). Define: ( Holographic Completion Principle ) There is no polynomial-time algorithm that, given only B(leΦrangle ) , decides satisfiability for all Φ , i.e. \[ ( ∀ A ∈ P)\ ∃ Φ\ such that \ A(B(leΦrangle )) ≠ sf SAT (Φ). \] If B is information-preserving in the sense that sf SAT (Φ) is decidable from B(leΦrangle ) in polynomial time iff sf SAT ∈ P , then bf (HCP) is logically equivalent to P ≠ NP .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:perm-derivatives
title: Derivatives = minors of complements; exact form
statement_text: Fix an integer κ with 0 ≤ κ ≤ n . Let R,C ⊆ [n] be row/column sets with |R|=|C|=κ . For any bijection π: R → C , let \[ S_π\ :=\ {(i,π(i)): i ∈ R}. \] Then \[ partial _ S_π Perm _n(X)\ =\ Perm _ n-κ l(X[R^c, C^c] r), \] i.e., the (n-κ) × (n-κ) principal complement minor permanent on the remaining rows R^c and columns C^c . If S ⊆ [n] × [n] is not the graph of a partial matching (i.e., two pairs in S share a row or a column), then partial _S Perm _nequiv 0 .

title: Distinct complements ⇒ disjoint supports ⇒ independence
statement_text: Fix κ . For each pair of sets R,C ⊆ [n] with |R|=|C|=κ , define \[ p_ R,C (X)\ :=\ Perm _ n-κ l(X[R^c, C^c] r). \] Then the family {p_ R,C }_ |R|=|C|=κ is linearly independent over any field: each p_ R,C involves only the variables indexed by R^c × C^c , and for distinct pairs (R,C) ≠ (R',C') these supports are disjoint.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:3sat-partial-derivative-lb
title: partial -matrix lower bound for \#3 SAT encodings; explicit family
statement_text: There exists an explicit family {φ_n} of 3-CNFs on n variables (e.g., Tseitin/expander encodings, see S 6 / S 14) and a sequence of partitions [n]=S_nsqcup T_n with |S_n|=Θ(n) such that the classical partial-derivative matrix satisfies \[ rank l( PD _ S_n,T_n (χ_ φ_n ) r)\ =\ 2^ Ω(n) . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:3sat-spdp-lb
title: Exponential SPDP rank for χ_ φ_n at order |S_n|
statement_text: With {φ_n} and {S_n} as in Theorem and κ_n:=|S_n|=Θ(n) , \[ rk _ SPDP , κ_n (χ_ φ_n )\ ≥ \ 2^ Ω(n) . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:multilinear-interpolation
title: Multilinear interpolation / ``characteristic'' polynomial
statement_text: For a Boolean function f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} , its multilinear interpolation p_f ∈ F [x_1, ... ,x_n] is p_f(x)\ :=\ Σ _ a ∈ {0,1}^n : f(a)=1 Π _ i: a_i=1 x_i Π _ j: a_j=0 (1-x_j). Then p_f is multilinear and satisfies p_f(a)=f(a) for every a ∈ {0,1}^n .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:tseitin-spdp-lb
title: Tseitin SPDP rank on expanders
statement_text: Let {G_n} be an explicit family of d -regular Ramanujan expanders on n vertices with girth Ω( log n) . Let Φ_n be the Tseitin 3CNF obtained from G_n by the standard parity constraints and XOR-to-3CNF gadgetization, and let χ_ Φ_n be its characteristic multilinear polynomial over any field of characteristic 0 or sufficiently large prime. Then there exist constants c,C>0 such that, for r(n)=( log n)^C , \[ rk _ SPDP , r(n) (χ_ Φ_n )\ ≥ \ n^c. \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:disjoint-packing
title: Linear-size variable-disjoint clause subfamily
statement_text: Let Φ be a 3 CNF in which every variable appears in at most Δ clauses. Let m:=| Cl (Φ)| . Then there exists a clause subfamily C_ disj ⊆ Cl (Φ) such that: the clauses in C_ disj are pairwise variable-disjoint (no shared variables), and |C_ disj |\ ≥ \ m/(3Δ) . In particular, if m=Θ(n) and Δ=O(1) , then |C_ disj |=α n for some constant α>0 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:Qphi-times
title: Coupled verifier sheet polynomial
statement_text: Let Φ be a 3-CNF verifier sheet with clause gadgets {V_C(u)}_ C ∈ Φ , where each V_C(u) is multilinear in the verifier variables u and satisfies: V_C(u)=0 iff clause C is satisfied (under the intended local decoding). Introduce coupling selector variables z=(z_C)_ C ∈ Φ , one per clause, and define the coupled verifier polynomial \[ Q_Φ^ × (u,z) := Π _ C ∈ Φ l(1 - z_C · V_C(u)^2 r). \] We also define the activated coupled sheet for any clause-set S ⊆ Φ by the restriction \[ Q_ Φ, S ^ × (u) := Q_Φ^ × (u,z) |_ z_C=1\ (C ∈ S ),\ z_C=0\ (C ∉ S ) = Π _ C ∈ S l(1 - V_C(u)^2 r). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:qphi-coupled
title: Coupled verifier sheet polynomial (refined, unconditional)
statement_text: Let Φ be a 3 -CNF verifier sheet with clause set Cl (Φ) produced by the (verifier-sheet) arithmetization/compilation procedure. For each clause C ∈ Cl (Φ) , let B_C denote the set of clause-local gadget variables introduced for C (pads/tags/selectors/internal wires, as applicable), and write u_ B_C for the tuple of variables in B_C . We adopt the compiler convention that these clause-local namespaces are disjoint: \[ B_C ∩ B_ C' = ∅ qquad (C ≠ C'). \] (Any global assignment/interface variables are not included in any B_C and may be shared across clauses.) Let V_C(u_ B_C ) be the associated clause gadget polynomial. We require (by construction of the fixed constant-size clause gadget) that: V_C is multilinear in the clause-local variables u_ B_C ; deg (V_C)=O(1) uniformly; V_C is not a constant polynomial in u_ B_C . Introduce coupling selector variables z=(z_C)_ C ∈ Cl (Φ) , one per clause, and define the coupled sheet polynomial \[ Q^ × _Φ(u,z) := Π _ C ∈ Cl (Φ) l(1 - z_C · V_C(u_ B_C )^2 r). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:tag-monomial-exists
title: Existence of a block-local tag monomial
statement_text: Under Definition , for each clause C ∈ Cl (Φ) there exists a monomial τ_C(u) supported only on variables from B_C such that \[ [τ_C] V_C(u_ B_C )^2 ≠ 0. \] Fix one such τ_C for each clause C .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:unit-clause-tag
title: Unit clause-local tag monomial
statement_text: For each clause C , the fixed clause gadget polynomial V_C(u_ B_C ) contains a designated clause-local tag variable t_C ∈ B_C with coefficient +1 , i.e. \[ [t_C] V_C = 1. \] Consequently, \[ [t_C^2] V_C(u_ B_C )^2 = 1. \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:syntactic-k-selector
title: Syntactic κ -selector
statement_text: Fix κ=lceil α log nrceil . A selector family F _κ(Φ) is the set of all κ -subsets S ⊆ Cl (Φ) . When a single subset is needed, we use a purely syntactic choice, e.g.\ the first κ clauses in the canonical ordering. All constructions below use only syntactic data (clause indices), never satisfiability.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:effective-degree
title: Effective degree under κ -selector differentiation
statement_text: Let κ=lceil α log nrceil . For any S ⊆ Cl (Φ) with |S|=κ , the polynomial \[ R_S(u,z)\ :=\ partial _ z_S Q_Φ^ × (u,z) qquad and its z -constant part qquad r_S(u)\ :=\ R_S(u,z) |_ z=0 \] satisfy \[ deg _u(r_S)\ ≤ \ 2 (max _C deg V_C) · κ\ =\ O( log n). \] Hence the SPDP regime κ=Θ( log n) and ell =Θ( log n) is compatible with the coupled sheet lower bound (only O( log n) u -degree is ever needed).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:rank-monotone-linear
title: Coefficient-space rank monotonicity under linear maps
statement_text: Let L be any F -linear operator on polynomials that acts by fixed linear combinations of coefficients (e.g.\ restriction of variables, projection/deletion of columns, taking a coefficient slice, or applying a fixed partial derivative). Then for every polynomial p and every (κ,ell ) , \[ Γ_ κ,ell (L(p))\ ≤ \ Γ_ κ,ell (p). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:syntactic-extraction
title: Syntactic extraction of coupled sheets
statement_text: Assume the compiler produces a polynomial P_ M',n (u,z,v) such that \[ P_ M',n (u,z,v)\ =\ Q_Φ^ × (u,z)\ +\ R_ M',Φ (v) \] after the standard variable partition into verifier variables (u,z) and auxiliary variables v , where Φ is the 3 -CNF instance and R_ M',Φ depends only on v . Let π_ u,z denote the syntactic projection (restriction) setting all v -variables to 0 .
