Then for the verifier-restricted machine M' deciding 3SAT, the compiled polynomial satisfies bf Guard (no extraction from Φ alone). The extraction operator T_ Φ is applied only to the compiled machine-exact polynomial P_ M',n produced by the assumed polytime decider M' on input length n ; it is not an operator that outputs Q^ × _ Φ from Φ in isolation. The compiled polynomial satisfies \[ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M',n ) ≤ n^ O(1) \] by the P-side width ⇒ rank upper bound (Theorem ). By the coupled extraction map (Lemma ), \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) \ ≤ \ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M',n ) \ ≤ \ n^ O(1) . \] On the other hand, by the coefficient-space identity minor for coupled sheets (Theorem , which applies to Q^ × _ Φ_n ), \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _ Φ_n )\ ≥ \ n^ Θ( log n) , \] a contradiction for large n . Hence P ≠ NP .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:uniform-extraction-verifier-sos
title: Uniform Block-Local Extraction of the Verifier SoS
statement_text: There exists a deterministic, instance-uniform map \[ E : (Φ, M) longmapsto (Q^ × _Φ, P_ M,n ) \] with the following properties: bf P-side compilation. For any polytime decider M of 3SAT, the compiler produces P_ M,n with \[ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) , quad κ, ell = Θ( log n). \] bf Verifier extraction. For each 3SAT instance Φ with n variables and m clauses, the map extracts Q^ × _Φ (the coupled clause-gadget SoS polynomial, Definition ) such that \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _Φ) ≤ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) . \] bf Block-locality. The extraction T_Φ : P_ M,n mapsto Q^ × _Φ decomposes as a finite composition of block-local operations (restriction, projection, affine relabeling, basis change), each operating within radius O(1) blocks. bf NP-side lower bound. For sufficiently hard 3SAT instances Φ_n (derived from the permanent via Valiant--Vazirani reduction or direct construction), \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) ≥ n^ Θ( log n) . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:sheet-extract
title: Clause-sheet separability and extraction
statement_text: In the instrumented compilation, the coupled verifier sheet occupies disjoint blocks tagged sf VER . Selecting rows whose derivatives touch only sf VER variables (including coupling selectors z ) and projecting to columns supported on sf VER blocks yields a block-supported submatrix. By Lemma , this projection cannot increase rank, and after the instance-uniform affine relabeling of literal pads, the extracted polynomial equals Q^ × _Φ exactly.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:oracle-invariance
title: Oracle-invariance of SPDP rank
statement_text: Let p ∈ F [x_1, ... ,x_n] be any polynomial and κ,ell ≥ 0 . For any oracle O ⊆ {0,1}^* (or any Turing-relativized model), define the ``relativized'' SPDP rank Γ_ κ,ell ^O(p) to be the rank of the same shifted partial-derivative matrix M_ κ,ell (p) computed over F (i.e., the definition does not refer to oracle answers). Then \[ Γ_ κ,ell ^O(p) = Γ_ κ,ell (p) quad for all O. \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:non-largeness
title: Non-largeness of high-SPDP property
statement_text: For κ(n), ell (n) = O( log n) and any fixed α > 0 , there is c > 0 such that \[ Pr _ f U({0,1}^ 2^n ) [f ∈ P _n] ≤ 2^ -c · 2^n \] for all sufficiently large n . In particular, P _n is not large in the Razborov--Rudich sense.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:natural-avoided
title: Non-largeness achieved unconditionally
statement_text: The SPDP-based property P _n is unconditionally non-large (Theorem ). In the Razborov--Rudich framework, non-largeness is the key condition preventing a ``natural'' proof from succeeding against PRF-computable functions. We mention this only as context; bf no cryptographic assumption enters our separation proof.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: prop:algebraic-oracle-invariance
title: Formal insensitivity to algebraic oracles for fixed p
statement_text: Let A be any algebraic oracle (collection of low-degree polynomials in fresh variables Z ). For a fixed base polynomial p(x) independent of Z , define p^A(x,Z) := p(x) (i.e., the oracle does not modify p ). Then \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p^A) = Γ_ κ,ell (p). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Permanent monomial
statement_text: Fix n ≥ 1 . For σ ∈ S_n , define the monomial \[ m_σ(x) = Π _ i=1 ^n x_ i,σ(i) , \] where we regard the variable x_ i,j as the single variable x_ (i-1)n+(j-1) in a flattened index.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:perm-overlap
title: Overlap structure of permanent monomials
statement_text: For σ, τ ∈ S_n : If x_ i,σ(i) = x_ j,τ(j) (as flattened variables), then i = j and σ(i) = τ(i) . vars (m_σ) = vars (m_τ) iff σ = τ . vars (m_σ) ∩ vars (m_τ) = { x_ i,σ(i) : σ(i) = τ(i) } .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:perm-distinct-values
title: At least 2^ n-1 distinct Boolean evaluations
statement_text: There exist 2^ n-1 Boolean n × n matrices whose permanent values are pairwise distinct.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Constants
statement_text: f equiv 0 ⇒ p = 0 takes value set {0} ⇒ valrank (p) = 1 . f equiv 1 ⇒ p = 1 takes value set {1} ⇒ valrank (p) = 1 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Single bit
statement_text: f(x) = x_i ⇒ p(x) = x_i ∈ {0,1} ⇒ valrank (p) = 2 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: AND
statement_text: f(x_1,x_2) = x_1 wedge x_2 ⇒ p = x_1 x_2 ∈ {0,1} ⇒ valrank (p) = 2 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Parity
statement_text: A convenient multilinear extension is \[ p_ PAR _n (x) = Π _ i=1 ^n (1 - 2x_i). \] On {0,1}^n , each factor is pm 1 , and the product is (-1)^ Σ _i x_i ∈ {pm 1} . Hence the value set is {-1, +1} ⇒ valrank (p) = 2 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Majority, n = 2k+1
statement_text: Let MAJ _ 2k+1 (x) = 1 [ Σ _i x_i > k] and p_ MAJ its multilinear extension. For Hamming weight t ∈ {0, ... ,2k+1} , the restriction of p_ MAJ to the weight- t layer is constant and equals the probability (over a uniformly random completion consistent with fixing those t ones) that a random point has majority 1. As t varies from 0 to 2k+1 , these constants form a strictly monotone list with exactly k+2 distinct values (from 0 up to 1 in steps that occur at the threshold), hence valrank (p) = k+2 = Θ(n) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: det _2
statement_text: p = x_ 11 x_ 22 - x_ 12 x_ 21 . On {0,1}^4 , each monomial is in {0,1} , so values are {-1,0,1} ⇒ valrank (p) = 3 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: perm _2

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: perm _3
statement_text: It is classical that perm _3 on {0,1}^9 attains exactly the integers 0,1, ... ,6 (e.g., all-ones matrix has value 3! = 6 ; identity has 1; sparse choices yield 0,2,3,4,5 ). Hence valrank (p) = 7 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Triangle
statement_text: p_triangle = x_ 12 x_ 13 x_ 23 ∈ {0,1} ⇒ valrank (p) = 2 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: 4-clique
statement_text: p_ K_4 = Π _ 1 ≤ i < j ≤ 4 x_ ij ∈ {0,1} ⇒ valrank (p) = 2 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Inner-product mod 2
statement_text: Define \[ p_ IP _n (x,y) = Π _ i=1 ^n (1 - 2x_i y_i). \] Since each factor is pm 1 on {0,1}^ 2n , the range is {pm 1} ⇒ valrank (p) = 2 .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Disjointness
statement_text: \[ p_ DISJ _n (x,y) = Π _ i=1 ^n (1 - x_i y_i) ∈ {0,1} ⇒ valrank (p) = 2. \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: obs:rank-dichotomy
title: Refined dichotomy
statement_text: Under value diversity valrank ( · ) : Many basic Boolean functions (AND/OR/XOR, IP mod 2, DISJ) have valrank = 2 . Symmetric threshold functions (e.g., Majority) have polynomial valrank . Algebraically rich counting functions such as Permanent exhibit exponential growth in the number of distinct values on {0,1}^d .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:oracle-invariance-appg
title: Oracle invariance of SPDP-rank
statement_text: For any oracle O and Boolean f with multilinear extension p_f , \[ SPDP-rank ^O(p_f) = SPDP-rank (p_f). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:rank-gap-persists
title: Rank-gap persists under relativization
statement_text: If the separation is proved purely by a rank gap--- ∀ g ∈ P : poly-rank and ∃ f : exp-rank---then those inequalities remain true in every relativized world O . (This is a method statement, not a class-separation claim.) (See also S 29.8.1.)

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Syntactic vs algebraic divergence
statement_text: With an oracle O_ perm answering perm (M) , the syntactic complexity of perm changes (now in P ^ O_ perm ), while its algebraic SPDP-rank witness remains exponential. (Discussion: S 25.4.4, S 29.9, App. A.4.)

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:low-rank-rare
title: Low SPDP-rank is exponentially rare
statement_text: Fix derivative order ell and c ∈ N . There exists c_0 > 0 such that, for uniform f : {0,1}^n → {0,1} , \[ Pr [ SPDP-rank _ell (p_f) ≤ n^c] ≤ 2^ -c_0 2^n . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:prg-resistance-concise
title: PRG-resistance of low-rank
statement_text: Under the truth-table model (strings of length 2^n ), low-rank functions are computationally indistinguishable from PRG outputs for poly-size distinguishers; advantage ≤ 2^ -Ω(2^n) . (Proof: S 2.4.2, App. A.M, App. A.O.)

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:non-naturality-concise
title: Non-naturality
statement_text: The property `` SPDP-rank _ell (p_f) ≥ 2^ Ω(n) '' fails largeness and so is non-natural in the Razborov--Rudich sense. (See S 2.4.2, App. A.O, and summary S 29.8.2.)

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:inherently-algebraic
title: Inherently algebraic; method does not algebrize
statement_text: SPDP lower bounds talk about the multilinear p_f and linear-algebraic independence over a base field (and extensions). These arguments are not captured by standard algebrizing frameworks for relativized classes. (Discussion: S 2.4, App. A.3--A.4, S 29.9.2--29.9.3.)

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:perm-exp-rank-appendix
title: Permanent has exponential SPDP-rank
statement_text: For every integer n ≥ 4 , \[ spdp\_rank ( perm _n) ≥ binom n lceil n/3 rceil = 2^ Ω(n) . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Monomial isolation
statement_text: For S ≠ S' , the monomial m_S does not appear in partial _ S',τ_ S' perm _n .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Linear independence
statement_text: The set \[ { partial _ S,τ_S perm _n : S ∈ binom [n] κ } \] is linearly independent over the base field. Reason: each polynomial in the family contains its ``signature'' monomial m_S that does not occur in any other member; a nontrivial linear relation would force the coefficient of m_S to vanish, contradiction.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:rank-test
title: Storjohann-Wiedemann Rank Test
statement_text: Given a matrix M ∈ Q ^ m × n with entries of bit-size at most B , there exists a deterministic algorithm that computes rank (M) in time O(mn^ ω-1 · log ^2(nB)) where ω < 2.373 is the matrix multiplication exponent.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:canonical-window-vocabulary
title: Canonical window vocabulary
statement_text: Fix the radius-- 1 compiler template family (finite local tile alphabet, neighborhood shape, block partition B , diagonal-basis conventions, administrative tag scheme, and the fixed gauge Π^+ ). The canonical window vocabulary is the finite template language determined by these fixed compiler parameters, in which compiled objects are represented as multisets/sequences of local constraints indexed by canonical window coordinates, with deterministic tie-breaking conventions for ordering and naming.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:admitted-source-descriptions
title: Admitted source descriptions
statement_text: A source description D (machine/circuit/tableau description) is admitted if the compiler front-end contains an explicit deterministic normalization map \[ Win (D) ∈ L _ win \] into the canonical window vocabulary L _ win (Definition ), computed using only syntactic rewrites that preserve the computed Boolean function (e.g.\ standard uniform simulation steps, fixed template expansion, and deterministic naming/order conventions).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:window-normalization-degrees
title: Front-end determinism: only (E1)--(E4),(E6) remain after window normalization
statement_text: Let D_1,D_2 be admitted source descriptions computing the same Boolean function f_n . Then their normalized window forms Win (D_1) and Win (D_2) differ only by the syntactic degrees of freedom listed in Definition , i.e., moves (E1)--(E4) and (E6) (and padding only if explicitly invoked).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:compiler-equivalence-moves
title: Compiler equivalence moves
statement_text: Fix the compiler template family Comp (radius-- 1 blocks, diagonal basis, and Π^+ ). We write p equiv _ comp p' (or p p' ) if p' is obtained from p by a finite sequence of the following moves (and their inverses where applicable): bf (E1) Block-local invertible changes. Blockwise invertible linear changes of variables within blocks, and block-local variable renamings (permutations) consistent with the block partition B . bf (E2) Tag specialization / administrative normalization. Deterministic specialization, coalescing, or elimination of administrative tags introduced by the compiler front-end, in a way that preserves the Boolean semantics of the compiled instance. bf (E3) Deletion of identically-zero components (only). Removal of constraints/cells whose compiled polynomial is identically 0 after deterministic normalization. No other notion of ``semantically inactive'' is permitted. bf (E4) Commutation / reordering of independent cells. Reordering (permutation) of commuting factors, independent cells, or disjoint local constraints, including deterministic tie-breaking conventions. bf (E6) Positive-cone closure Π^+ . Applying the canonical ``positive-cone'' linear map Π^+ used in the final canonicalization layer. By definition of the compiler, Π^+ is chosen block-local and invertible on each block, hence is a special case of (E1) (recorded separately because it is used repeatedly in the narrative).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:padding-equivalence
title: Padding equivalence (optional, not in core)
statement_text: Write p equiv _ pad p' if p' is obtained from p by applying the (uniform) round-trip NC ^0 padding transformation from Theorem (or its inverse), together with the induced renaming of auxiliary variables. This move is not part of the core equivalence equiv _ comp and contributes at most a poly (n) factor to rank.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:each-move-rank-exact
title: Core compiler moves preserve blocked SPDP rank exactly
statement_text: If p equiv _ comp p' (i.e.\ p' is obtained from p by moves (E1)--(E4), (E6)), then \[ Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p') = Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:padding-rank-benign
title: Padding is rank-benign up to poly (n)
statement_text: If p equiv _ pad p' , then \[ Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p') ≤ poly (n) · Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p) quad and quad Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p) ≤ poly (n) · Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p'). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:canonical-compiled-rep
title: Canonical compiled representative
statement_text: Fix the compiler pipeline Comp ( · ) described in S , including the final canonicalization layer (tag normalization, block-basis choice, and Π^+ application). For an admitted source description D , write \[ NF (D)\ :=\ Comp (D) \] for the compiler output after canonicalization.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:I1-normal-form-invariance
title: (I1) Normal-form invariance
statement_text: Let D_1,D_2 be admitted source descriptions computing the same Boolean function f_n . Then NF (D_1) NF (D_2) . Equivalently, the compiler output is well-defined as a normal form modulo .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:I2-representation-invariance
title: (I2) Representation invariance of SPDP rank
statement_text: Under the hypotheses of Theorem , \[ Γ^ B _ κ,ell ( NF (D_1)) = Γ^ B _ κ,ell ( NF (D_2)). \] If padding is additionally invoked, the two ranks are within a poly (n) factor by Lemma .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:finite-family
title: Finite compiled formula family F_ n,c
statement_text: Fix a runtime exponent c . Let F_ n,c be the set of all bounded-width CNF constraints generated by instantiating the compiler's local templates over all legal placements (time layer, tape index, and local neighborhood) in the Cook--Levin tableau for computations of length ≤ n^ c .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:enumerability
title: Enumerability bound
statement_text: For fixed template library T and fixed c , the family F_ n,c can be enumerated in time n^ O(c) , and |F_ n,c | ≤ n^ O(c) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:hoeffding-bernstein
title: Hoeffding-Bernstein MGF bound
statement_text: Let X be a real-valued random variable such that E [X] = μ and |X - μ| ≤ b almost surely. Then for every |t| ≤ 1/b , \[ E [exp (t(X - μ))] ≤ exp (frac t^2σ^2 2 ) \] where σ^2 = Var (X) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:spdp-rank-hard
title: Hardness of exact SPDP rank on succinct inputs
statement_text: Fix SPDP parameters (κ,ell ) with κ ≥ 1 . Consider the function problem \[ RANK _ SPDP : f longmapsto Γ_ κ,ell (f), \] where f is specified by a succinct arithmetic (or Boolean) circuit computing its multilinear extension p_f . Then RANK _ SPDP is \#P-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: prop:low-rank-not-large
title: Low-rank property is not large
statement_text: For each fixed k there exists a constant c_k ∈ (0,1) such that, for all sufficiently large n , at most 2^ c_k 2^n Boolean functions on n variables satisfy P_ rank ,k (f) . In particular, P_ rank ,k is not large in the Razborov--Rudich sense.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:spdp-appg
title: SPDP Matrix
statement_text: Let p ∈ Bbb F[x_1, ... ,x_N] and let B={B_1, ... ,B_m} be a partition of {1, ... ,N} into blocks of size ≤ b=O(1) . Fix κ,ell ∈ Bbb N . Rows are indexed by pairs (τ,u) with multi-index τ ∈ Bbb N^N of weight |τ|=κ whose block support supp _ B (τ):={j: ∃ i ∈ B_j,\ τ_i>0} satisfies | supp _ B (τ)| ≤ κ , and u a monomial of degree ≤ ell . Columns are monomials x^β with deg x^β ≤ deg (p)-κ+ell (empty set if negative). Define \[ M^ B _ κ,ell (p) [(τ,u),x^β ] := coeff _ x^β (u · partial ^τ p ), qquad Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p):= rank _Bbb F (M^ B _ κ,ell (p) ). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:width-to-rank-appg
title: Width ⇒ Rank at κ,ell =Θ( log n)
statement_text: Let p be a constant-degree multilinear polynomial with contextual entanglement width CEW (p) ≤ R:=C( log n)^c for absolute constants C,c>0 . If deg (p)-κ+ell <0 then M_ κ,ell (p)=0 . Otherwise, for κ,ell =Θ( log n) we have Γ_ κ,ell (p) ≤ n^ O(1) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:splitter-appg
title: Combinatorial isolating family for κ -sets
statement_text: Let [N] index variables/blocks with N=Θ(n) and fix κ=α log n for any constant α>0 . There exists a family H ={h_1, ... ,h_t} of hash functions h_j:[N] → [m] with m:=c_0 κ^2 and t:=c_1(κ log N+10) (absolute constants c_0,c_1 ) such that for every κ -subset S ⊆ [N] there is some j with h_j injective on S .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:isolator
title: DEPRECATED - Isolating Family for additive sheet
statement_text: Let N be the number of clause--blocks/variable--pads in Q_ Φ_n and let κ=α log n for a fixed α>0 . There exists a family H of κ -perfect hash functions h:[N] → [κ] of size \[ | H | ≤ C_0 κ^κ log N = n^ O(1) \] with the following property: for every κ -subset S ⊆ [N] there is an h ∈ H that is injective on S . For each S choose the unique monomial x^ β(S) that selects, in the SoS clause gadget for Q_ Φ_n , exactly the κ literal--wires indexed by S and no others (feasible because each block exposes private pads and the gadgets are block-separable). Then the SPDP submatrix with rows indexed by the κ -tuples S and columns by the x^ β(S) is the identity. Consequently, \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q_ Φ_n ) ≥ binom N κ = n^ Θ( log n) . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:identity-minor-appg
title: DEPRECATED - Identity minor for additive clause SoS
statement_text: Let Q_ Φ_n =1- Σ _ C ∈ Φ_n V_C(x)^2 be the clause-violation SoS for a fixed 3 SAT family with bounded degree and clause locality (e.g., Ramanujan/Tseitin-based). With κ=α log n and ell =β log n , there exist sets R , C of size binom N κ =n^ Θ( log n) such that M_ κ,ell (Q_ Φ_n )[ R , C ] is the identity matrix.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:tphi-appg
title: Rank-monotone extraction
statement_text: There exists an instance-uniform, block-local transformation T_Φ such that T_Φ(P_ M,n )=Q_ Φ_n and for all κ,ell , Γ_ κ,ell (T_Φ(P_ M,n ) ) ≤ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M,n ) . The transformation is witness-free in the sense of Lemma .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:identity-minor-explicit
title: Explicit identity minor and absence of cancellations
statement_text: Let Φ_n be the Ramanujan--Tseitin instance on a fixed d -regular expander G_n = (V_n,E_n) with |V_n| = m and |E_n| = N = Θ(n) , and let p_n be the associated multilinear polynomial in edge-variables {x_e : e ∈ E_n} constructed above. For parameters κ = α log n and ell = β log n as in the main text, there exist: a set R of binom N κ = n^ Θ( log n) SPDP rows, indexed by mixed partials partial ^ τ concentrating on κ -tuples of vertices with pairwise disjoint neighbourhoods, and a matching set C of binom N κ columns, indexed by monomials x^ α selecting one incident edge per such vertex, such that the submatrix M(p_n)[R,C] is a signed identity matrix. In particular, rank M(p_n) ≥ binom N κ and there are no cancellations among the corresponding monomials.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:spdp-matrix-formal
title: SPDP matrix
statement_text: Let F be a field and p ∈ F [x_1, ... , x_N] a polynomial. Fix parameters κ, ell ∈ N with κ ≤ N . Define: S _κ := {S ⊆ [N] : |S| = κ} (the set of all κ -subsets of variable indices), T _ell := { monomials m in x_1, ... , x_N : deg m ≤ ell } , For S ∈ S _κ , define the partial derivative operator partial _S := Π _ i ∈ S frac partial partial x_i , For m ∈ T _ell , define the shift operator x^m : p mapsto m · p . The bf SPDP matrix M_ κ,ell (p) is the matrix with rows indexed by (S, m) ∈ S _κ × T _ell and columns indexed by monomials in the standard monomial basis, where the (S,m) -th row is the coefficient vector of m · partial _S p expressed as a linear combination of monomials. The bf SPDP rank is defined as \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p) := rank _ F M_ κ,ell (p). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:cew-formal
title: CEW and additive composition law
statement_text: Let p be a polynomial representing a Boolean function or circuit. The bf Contextual Entanglement Width CEW (p) is the minimal w such that after a universal restriction ρ_star (defined via deterministic switching lemma), the SPDP rank satisfies \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p upharpoonright ρ_star ) ≤ w \] for fixed parameters (κ,ell ) = Θ( log n) . For compositional systems (e.g., layered circuits), CEW satisfies the bf additive composition law : \[ CEW (f ∘ g) ≤ CEW (f) + CEW (g) + O(1), \] where the O(1) accounts for interface gadgets.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:batcher-network
title: Batcher odd--even merge network
statement_text: The bf Batcher sorting network for N inputs is a fixed comparison network defined recursively: bf Base case : For N = 1 , the network is trivial (identity). bf Recursive case : For N > 1 , split into two halves of size lceil N/2 rceil and lfloor N/2 rfloor , recursively sort each half, then merge using the odd--even merge gadget. The network has: bf Depth : D(N) = O( log ^2 N) , bf Width : Constant (each comparison gate operates on exactly 2 wires), bf Size : S(N) = O(N log ^2 N) comparisons.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:compiled-width-rank
title: Compiled Width ⇒ Rank via profile compression (load-bearing)
statement_text: Under the compiler setting of Section (bounded type set |T|=O(1) , radius-- 1 locality, and at most R= polylog (n) live interfaces throughout the sweep), the compiled SPDP rank satisfies \[ Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p) ≤ R^ O(1) = ( log n)^ O(1) quad for (κ,ell )=Θ( log n). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:restriction-monotonicity
title: Restriction monotonicity
statement_text: Let p ∈ F [x_1, ... , x_N] and ρ : F ^N → F ^ N' be a restriction (fixing some variables to constants). Then \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p upharpoonright ρ) ≤ Γ_ κ,ell (p). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:submatrix-monotonicity
title: Submatrix monotonicity
statement_text: If M' is a submatrix of M_ κ,ell (p) obtained by selecting a subset of rows, then \[ rank (M') ≤ Γ_ κ,ell (p). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:basis-Piplus-invariance
title: Block-local affine/basis invariance and Π^+
statement_text: Let p ∈ Bbb F[x_1, ... ,x_N] and fix κ,ell . Suppose a block-local change of variables x mapsto Ax+b acts on each block by an invertible linear map A (so det A ≠ 0 on each block), and let Π^+ denote the fixed positive-cone map used in the compilation (acting block-locally and invertibly on the column space induced by the local basis). Then left/right multiplication of M_ κ,ell (p) by the corresponding block-diagonal change-of-basis matrices is invertible, hence \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p) = Γ_ κ,ell (p ∘ (Ax+b) ) = Γ_ κ,ell (Π^+[p] ). \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:basis-invariance-appg
title: Basis invariance
statement_text: The rank Γ_ κ,ell (p) does not depend on the choice of monomial ordering or coordinate system (up to linear isomorphism).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: prop:monotonicity-parameters-cumulative
title: Monotonicity in parameters (cumulative variant)
statement_text: Fix an ambient coefficient convention (monomial bases) for each parameter choice. If ell ' ≥ ell then Γ_ κ,ell (p) ≤ Γ_ κ,ell ' (p) . If κ' ≥ κ then Γ_ ≤ κ,ell (p) ≤ Γ_ ≤ κ',ell (p) .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
title: Splitters / κ -perfect hash family
statement_text: A family H of functions h:[N] → [L] is κ -injective if for every κ -subset S ⊆ [N] there exists h ∈ H such that h|_ S is injective (i.e., assigns distinct colors in [L] to all elements of S ).

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:k-injective-family
title: Existence of small κ -injective families
statement_text: Fix κ ≤ c log n and set L:=2κ . There exists a κ -injective family H={h_1, ... ,h_T} with \[ T = O (κ log N ) \] such that for every S ∈ binom [N] κ some h_t is injective on S .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:private-literal-unique
title: Private literal uniqueness
statement_text: For each witness block B_i used in the NP construction, there exists a designated literal pad variable ell _i such that: ell _i occurs in the NP polynomial Q_ Φ_n only inside the unique local gadget factor associated with B_i , and no other local gadget contains ell _i .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:private-linear-unique
title: Private literal appears linearly and uniquely
statement_text: For each witness block B_i , the local gadget factor has the form \[ G_i(ell _i, y_i) = ell _i + H_i(y_i), \] where y_i are the remaining variables of the block and H_i does not contain ell _i . In particular, [ell _i]G_i=1 and no other monomial of G_i has the same support as ell _i .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:pi-plus-unit
title: Π^+ -normalization gives unit private coefficients
statement_text: There is a fixed, block-local invertible linear change of variables Π^+ (chosen once for the compiler/gadget family) such that, after applying Π^+ to each witness block, the designated private literal ell _i appears with coefficient +1 in the corresponding local gadget polynomial, and no other monomial in that local gadget shares the same support as the private monomial used in the identity-minor construction.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:no-cross-interference
title: No cross-interference (off-diagonal vanishing)
statement_text: Let S ≠ S' be two κ -sets of blocks. Let x_ β(S) be the private column monomial constructed from the private literals of S . Then the coefficient of x_ β(S) in the row polynomial corresponding to (S',u') is zero: \[ [x_ β(S) ] (u' · partial _ S' Q_ Φ_n )=0. \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:identity-minor-k-injective
title: Identity minor from κ -injective coloring
statement_text: Let Q^ × _Φ be the coupled NP-side SoS polynomial (Definition ) with clause/witness block layout and block-local, radius- 1 gadgets. Fix κ=Θ( log n) and let H be a κ -injective family as in Lemma with L=2κ . Then there exists a set I of row/column indices of size \[ |I| ≥ binom N' κ quad for some quad N'=Θ(N), \] such that the submatrix of M_ κ,ell (Q^ × _Φ) indexed by I × I is the identity. Consequently, \( Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _Φ) ≥ binom N' κ = n^ Θ( log n) . \)

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: lem:splitter-appg-duplicate
title: Splitter for κ -windows with private monomials
statement_text: There exist absolute constants c_0,c_1>0 and, for all N,κ with 1 ≤ κ ≤ c_0 log N , a family F ⊆ [N] choose O(κ) of size ≤ N^ c_1 such that for every κ -set S ⊆ [N] there is F ∈ F with |S ∩ F|=1 . Moreover, given S and F with |S ∩ F|=1 , there is a monomial x^β using only variables in F such that x^β appears in the (S,u) -row of M_ κ,0 (Q_ Φ_n ) with nonzero coefficient, while for any S' ≠ S in [N] choose κ the (S',u') -row has zero coefficient on x^β .

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:np-identity-minor-formal-appg
title: Identity minor for M_ κ,0 (Q_ Φ_n )
statement_text: For κ = Θ( log n) and N=Θ(n) , there exists a column subfamily C and a row subfamily R = {(S,1): S ∈ [N]choose κ } such that the submatrix M_ κ,0 (Q_ Φ_n )[ R , C ] is the identity matrix of size binom N κ . Consequently, \[ Γ_ κ,0 (Q_ Φ_n ) ≥ binom N κ = n^ Θ( log n) . \]

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: prop:zfc-formalizability
title: ZFC Formalizability
statement_text: All mathematical objects, constructions, and theorems in this proof are definable within ZFC (Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory with the Axiom of Choice) using only: bf Finite combinatorics : Finite sets, sequences, and functions over N , Q , and finite fields. bf Polynomial algebra : Polynomials over Z and Q with finitely many variables. bf Linear algebra : Finite-dimensional vector spaces and matrix rank over Q (computable via Gaussian elimination). bf Turing machines : Finite automata with explicit transition functions and tape alphabets. bf No non-constructive steps or uses of Choice beyond ZF are required. All existence proofs provide explicit constructions or algorithms.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: cor:lean-embedding
title: Lean 4 Embedding
statement_text: Each lemma and theorem in S S -- can be represented in the Lean 4 proof assistant using: tt Matrix.rank from Mathlib's linear algebra library for SPDP rank computation. tt MvPolynomial for multivariate polynomials over Q or finite fields. tt Finset and tt Fintype for finite combinatorics (subsets, derivatives, etc.). tt Nat.log and asymptotic lemmas for complexity bounds. Appendix outlines the Lean formalization structure with type signatures.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: thm:non-algebrizing-collapse
title: Non-algebrization of the compiled SPDP collapse principle
statement_text: Fix (κ,ell )=Θ( log n) and a fixed block partition B . There exists an algebraic oracle A such that the following fails relative to A : centerline (Compiled SPDP collapse) ^ A : every M ∈ P ^ A compiles to Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) . In particular, any separation route whose P-side hinge is the compiled SPDP collapse lemma is not an algebrizing proof technique.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
label: def:finite-observer-boundary

label: Def: Lnn
statement_text: An L _p -formula F is in negation normal form ( nnf , in short), if it is defined by the following grammar: \[ F:= p mid ¬ p mid F_1 wedge F_2 mid F_1 vee F_2 \] Similarly, an L _u -formula F is in * -negation normal form ( * -nnf , in short), if it is defined by the grammar: \[ F:= p mid ¬ p mid F_1 wedge F_2 mid F_1 vee F_2 mid F_1 * F_2 \] We write L _ nn and L ^*_ nn for the sets of nnf- and * -nnf-formulas.

Note that these initial sequents are not meant to be used as axioms and hence using their substitutions are not allowed in G . Moreover, G includes the cut rule.

paper_title: Fine-Grained Complexity for Quantum Problems from Size-Preserving Circuit-to-Hamiltonian Constructions
title: Multi-control-NOT gate and Toffoli gate
statement_text: A multi-control gate, denoted by C^ksc not , is a quantum gate that acts on k+1 qubits. Let C be a k -qubit register and T be a one-qubit register. paper_title: Fine-Grained Complexity for Quantum Problems from Size-Preserving Circuit-to-Hamiltonian Constructions
label: def:klocalH
title: Local Hamiltonian
statement_text: We say a Hamiltonian H acting on n qubits is k -local if H can be written as H = Σ _ i=1 ^m H_i for m= poly (n) and for all i , the following holds. H_i is a Hamiltonian. H_i non-trivially acts on at most k qubits. |H_i| ≤ poly (n) .

paper_title: Fine-Grained Complexity for Quantum Problems from Size-Preserving Circuit-to-Hamiltonian Constructions
label: def:LHP
title: k -local Hamiltonian ( krm - LH ) problem
statement_text: The local Hamiltonian problem is a decision problem that asks whether the ground-state energy of a k -local Hamiltonian is greater or less than given energy thresholds. bf Inputs: a k -local Hamiltonian H such that acting on n qubits where k=O(1) , and two energy thresholds E_ yes ,E_ no satisfying E_ no -E_ yes ≥ Ω(1) . bf Outputs: YES, if there exists a quantum state ket ψ ∈ C ^ 2^n such that leψmiddle rvertH middle lvert ψ rangle ≤ E_ yes . NO, if leψmiddle rvertH middle lvert ψ rangle ≥ E_ no for all ket ψ ∈ C ^ 2^n . In other words, the krm - LH problem asks to decide whether λ(H) ≤ E_ yes or λ(H) ≥ E_ no . We say an algorithm A _ LH solves krm - LH (H, E_ yes , E_ no ) if A _ LH decides (H,E_ yes ,E_ no ) correctly.

paper_title: Fine-Grained Complexity for Quantum Problems from Size-Preserving Circuit-to-Hamiltonian Constructions
label: def:QPF
title: Approximating quantum partition function of k -local Hamiltonian ( krm - QPF ) problem
statement_text: The quantum partition function problem is to approximate the partition function of a k -local Hamiltonian up to a multiplicative error under a certain temperature. bf Inputs: a k -local Hamiltonian H acting on n qubits where k=O(1) , an inverse temperature β ≤ poly (n) , and an error parameter δ ∈ (0,1) . bf Outputs: widetilde Z ∈ R such that (1-δ)Z ≤ widetilde Z ≤ (1+δ)Z, where Z:= tr [e^ -β H ] . We say an algorithm A _ QPF solves krm - QPF (H, β, δ) if A _ QPF outputs such widetilde Z on the inputs H, β, δ .

paper_title: Fine-Grained Complexity for Quantum Problems from Size-Preserving Circuit-to-Hamiltonian Constructions
label: def:kCNF
title: Conjunctive normal form (CNF) formula
statement_text: Let Φ be a Boolean formula that consists of n variables x_1,x_2, ... , x_k . We say Φ is a k CNF formula if Φ is in the form of m= poly (n) smaller formulas connected by wedge . Each smaller formula contains at most k variables, and the variables are connected by vee . To be more precise, Φ=φ_1wedge φ_2 wedge ... wedge φ_m where m= poly (n) , and for all i ∈ [m] , the following constrains hold. φ_ i = (ell _ i,1 vee ell _ i_2 vee ... vee ell _ i,k_ i ) , where ell _ i,p can be x_j or ¬ x_j for all p ∈ [k_i] and j ∈ [n] . k_i ≤ k . For each j ∈ [n] , x_j and ¬ x_j do not appear in φ_i at the same time; x_j , ¬ x_j appears in φ_i at most once. We say φ_i is a clause of Φ for all i ∈ [m] .

paper_title: Fine-Grained Complexity for Quantum Problems from Size-Preserving Circuit-to-Hamiltonian Constructions
label: def:kSAT
title: Satisfiability for krm - CNF ( krm - SAT ) problem
statement_text: The satisfiability problem is a decision problem that asks whether there is an assignment satisfying the given k CNF formula. bf Inputs: a krm - CNF formula Φ that contains n variables. The number of clauses of Φ is m= poly (n) . bf Outputs: YES, if there exists an assignment x ∈ {0,1}^n such that Φ(x)=1 . No, if Φ(x)=0 for all x ∈ {0,1}^n . We say an algorithm A _ SAT solves krm - SAT (Φ) if A _ SAT decides Φ correctly.

statement_text: Let P and Q be two problems and A _Q be an oracle that solves Q with probability greater than frac 2 3 . Let p( · ) and q( · ) be two non-decreasing functions. We say P is (p,q) reducible to Q if for all ε , there exist ξ , an algorithm A _P , a constant d , and an integer r(n) such that the algorithm A _P that can black-boxly assess to A _Q takes an instance of P with size n and satisfies the following. A _P solves P with probability greater than frac 2 3 . A _P runs in d · p(n)^ 1-ξ time. A _P produces at most r(n) instances of Q adaptively. Σ _ i=1 ^ r(n) (q(n_i))^ 1-ε ≤ d · (p(n))^ 1-ξ , where n_i is the size of the i th instance of problem Q that is produced by A _P .

label: theorem:main
statement_text: Let x ∈ {0,1}^n be an input and U_x be a QMA verification quantum circuit U_x acting on N qubits, and suppose U_x consists of T = poly (n) gates. If there exists a quantum proof ket ψ such that Pr [U_x accepts ket ψ ] ≥ 1-ε_ err , then λ(H_x) ≤ ε_ err . If Pr [U_x accepts ket ψ ] ≤ ε_ err for any quantum proof ket ψ , then λ(H_x) ≥ frac 1 2 -ε_ err .

label: lem:U_compute_Phi
title: A quantum circuit can compute krm - CNF
statement_text: For any positive integer k and c>0 , for all n ∈ N , for any krm - CNF formula Φ that contains n variables and m=O(n^c) clauses, there exists a quantum circuit U_Φ that acts on n input qubits and at most 2c log n +2 ancilla qubits, and U_Φ consists of at most 34c^2 n^c log ^2 n + (70k+2)n^c + 35c log n elementary gates such that U_ Φ ket x _ in ⊗ ket 0 _ anc =ket Φ(x) _ out ⊗ ket ψ_x _ overline out for all x ∈ {0,1}^n , where ket ψ_x is some quantum state depending on x . The construction of U_ Φ can be done in poly (n) time. It is worth noting that an alternative quantum circuit for computing k CNF appears in , Corollary 10. That construction has width k + 2 l(lceil log n rceil + lceil c log n rceil r) and size at most 4 × 3^ lceil log _2 n rceil + lceil c log _2 n rceil - 1 . However, its circuit size is O(n^ c+1 ) , whereas ours is O(n^ c log ^2 n) . This gap impacts the locality of the resulting Hamiltonian, which is why cref lem:U_compute_Phi is necessary for our results.

statement_text: Let U be a unitary and ket u_θ be U 's eigenstate satisfying that Uket u_θ =e^ iθ ket u_θ . Let CU^d be the control- U^d operator, where d ∈ N . label: def: nash convergence
statement_text: We describe several definitions, from most basic to most demanding. statement_text: Let φ be a dynamic. φ is Nash-convergent if for every game G and for all mixed strategy profiles x ∈ X_G , the limit lim _ t → ∞ φ(x,t) exists and is a Nash equilibrium of G . title: ε -sc RePolymatrix
statement_text: In a general polymatrix game, there are n players with m_i actions for player i ∈ [n] . Let a_i ∈ [m_i] be the action of player i . The payoff of player i from the sub-game associated with player j ≠ i is determined by the matrix A^ ij , where player i gets a payoff of A^ ij _ a_i a_j from this subgame if i plays a_i and j plays a_j . Given the actions of all agents (a_1, ... , a_n) , the utility of player i is equal to Σ _ j ≠ i A^ ij _ a_i a_j . We make the following additional assumptions to restrict the class of polymatrix games we use in our reductions: Each player has exactly two actions: a_i ∈ {0, 1} for all i . All the payoffs are from the set {0, 1, 2} : A^ ij ∈ {0, 1, 2}^ 2 × 2 for all i and j ≠ i . All payoff matrices are either diagonal or anti-diagonal: for every i and j ≠ i , either A^ ij _ 01 = A^ ij _ 10 = 0 or A^ ij _ 00 = A^ ij _ 11 = 0 . The game is it bipartite : We can view the polymatrix game as a directed graph, where the vertices are the players, and there is an edge from player j to player i if A^ ij ≠ 0 . We assume that the underlying undirected graph of this directed graph is bipartite. The it in-degree is at most two: The payoff of any player depends upon at most two other players, i.e., for every player i , there exist at most two players k and k' such that A^ ij = 0 for all j ∉ { k, k' } . The it out-degree is at most two: Any player can affect the payoff of at most two other players, i.e., for every player i , there exist at most two players k and k' such that A^ ji = 0 for all j ∉ { k, k' } . The ε -sc RePolymatrix problem is to find an ε -WSNE of a polymatrix game satisfying the assumptions given above, for a given ε > 0 .

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: def:xor_gadget
title: XOR Gadget
statement_text: Let p be a nonnegative integer. The color defblue XOR gadget of order p is a graph containing two paths (a_1, ... , a_ p ) and (b_1, ... , b_ p ) which are called the color defblue rails of the XOR gadget. In addition, for i ∈ {1, ... , p} , the XOR gadget contains vertex disjoint paths of length two with a_i and b_i as endpoints. A color defblue subtour of the XOR gadget is a spanning path with two endpoints in the set {a_1, a_p, b_1, b_p} . For convenience, when p = 0 , both the XOR gadget of order zero and its only subtour are defined to be the empty graph.

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: obs:xor_external_edges
statement_text: For the XOR gadget assigned to an H -vertex x , one subtour in the gadget is incident to the left and right first-set edges of x , and another subtour in the gadget is incident to the closest door to x_r and the right second-set edge of x . These two subtours are identical, if the order of the gadget is at most one. Otherwise, they are distinct.

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: lem:partialedgeorientation
statement_text: Let F=(V,E) be a graph of maximum degree 5. Then we can compute in polynomial time a partition of E into two disjoint sets E_1 and E_2 and an orientation overrightarrow E_2 of the edges in E_2 such that (V, E_1) is a disjoint union of stars and each vertex in (V, overrightarrow E_2 ) has out-degree at most two.

statement_text: Let τ be a tour of G and α be a gadget in G . Then a subtour of τ in α is a subtour of α .

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: lem:end_doors
statement_text: For any tour of G and any H -vertex x , the tour contains either both the door incident to x_ ell and the closest door to x_r or none of them. Further, these two doors are in the tour, if and only if the left and right first-set edges of x are not in the tour.

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: obs:strict_iff_standard
statement_text: Let α be a parity gadget in G , τ be a tour of G , and x be a related H -vertex of α . Then α is strict at x in τ , if and only if the subtour of τ in α is standard.

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: lem:tour_edges
statement_text: For any standard tour of G and any H -vertex x , exactly one of these cases holds: The first-set case: The tour uses the left and right first-set edges of x and does not use any doors or the right second-set edge of x . It also uses the subtour in the XOR gadget assigned to x incident to the left and right first-set edges. Further, all parity gadgets related to x are disengaged at x . The second-set case: The tour uses all the doors and the right second-set edge of x and does not use the left and right first-set edges of x . It also uses the subtour in the XOR gadget assigned to x incident to the right second-set edge of x and the closest door to x_r . Further, all parity gadgets related to x are engaged at x .

paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
label: lem:x-change
statement_text: For an H -vertex x , an x -change is a swap of at least k edges. Further, it is a swap of exactly k edges, if and only if the x -change only involves standard subtour changes.

title: Cellular automaton
statement_text: A cellular automaton is formally defined as a quadruplet (d, S, N, f) : The integer d ≥ 1 is the dimension of the space on which the cellular automaton operates. S ≠ ∅ is a finite set called the set of states . The neighbourhood N is a v -tuple of distinct vectors of Z ^d . For N = (x_1, . . ., x_v) , vectors x_i are the relative positions of the neighbour cells with respect to a given center cell. The states of these neighbours are used to compute the new state of the center cell. The local function of the cellular automaton f: S^v → S gives the local transition rule.

statement_text: A relational propositional proof system is a binary relation \(Q ⊆ {0,1}^* × {0,1}^*\), where {0,1}^* denotes the set of all finite binary strings, such that: \(Q\) is p-time decidable; for any \(w, α\), if \(Q(w,α)\) holds then \(α ∈ TAUT \); for any \(α ∈ TAUT \), there is a \(w ∈ {0,1}^*\) such that \(Q(w,α)\) holds. The second condition gives the soundness of \(Q\) and the third its completeness.

title: p-simulation
statement_text: Let P and Q be two propositional proof systems. A p-time function f : {0,1}^* → {0,1}^* is a p-simulation of Q by P if and only if for all strings w, α , \[ Q(w,α) → P(f(w,α), α). \] If such f exists, we say that P p-simulates Q .

paper_title: Lower Bounds on Inverse Cellular Automata via Proof Complexity
label: ex:pigeonhole
title: Pigeonhole principle
statement_text: Consider the following CNF formula ¬ onto PHP _n , consisting of clauses over propositional variables p_ ij , where linebreak i ∈ [n+1] and j ∈ [n] : vee_j p_ ij , one clause for each i ; ¬ p_ i_1 j ∨ ¬ p_ i_2 j , one clause for each triple i_1 < i_2 and j ; ¬ p_ i j_1 ∨ ¬ p_ i j_2 , one clause for each triple i and j_1 < j_2 ; vee_i p_ ij , one clause for each j . The variable p_ ij is intended to express that pigeon i is assigned to hole j . The clauses in (1) and (4) assert that every pigeon is assigned to some hole and that every hole contains at least one pigeon, respectively. Clauses in (2) and (3) enforce that no two pigeons are assigned to the same hole and that no pigeon is assigned to more than one hole. Clearly, ¬ onto PHP _n is unsatisfiable, since the number of pigeons exceeds the number of holes. In fact, the formula remains unsatisfiable even if only clauses (1) and (2) are retained. This weaker principle is known as the weak pigeonhole principle , denoted ¬ PHP _n . We introduce this example because of the following well-known result due to Ajtai, which establishes super-polynomial lower bounds for bounded-depth Frege proofs. Let d ≥ 2 and let 0 < δ < 5^ -d . Then for all sufficiently large n the following holds. Every F_d -refutation of ¬ ontoPHP _n (that is, every F_d -proof of bot from linebreak ¬ ontoPHP _n ) contains at least 2^ n^δ pairwise different subformulas. In particular, any such refutation has size at least 2^ n^δ .

statement_text: There exists an algorithm that, given an automatic structure M and a first order formula φ(x_1, ... , x_n) , builds an automaton A _ φ such that for all a_1, ... , a_n ∈ M we have M models φ(a_1, ... , a_n) if and only if A _ φ accepts (a_1, ... , a_n) . In particular, the first order theory of any automatic structure M is decidable.

paper_title: Automatic constraint satisfaction problem
label: Dfn:AutCSP
statement_text: bf (Automatic constraint language) \ Let A be a finite automaton over D . Define the following set of relations Γ_ A = {R_1, \ R_2, \ ... } , where R_k=L( A ) ∩ D^k and k ∈ N . We call a language of relations Γ an bf automatic constraint language if Γ=Γ_ A for some finite automaton A .

paper_title: Automatic constraint satisfaction problem
statement_text: bf (AutCSP instance) \ We call the tuple (V, D, C , A ) an bf AutCSP instance I or bf an automatic CSP instance , where V is a set of variables, D is a finite domain, C is a finite set of constraints, and A is a finite automaton over D . Here a bf constraint is a tuple le s rangle =(s_ i_1 , ... ,s_ i_k ) of variables from V that in the context of constraint satisfaction instance is viewed as the formula R_k(s_ i_1 , ... , s_ i_k ) . \ Sometimes we write the constraint le s rangle as le s , R_krangle , -- consistent with the notations in the CSP literature, where R_k is a relation symbol of arity k .

paper_title: Automatic constraint satisfaction problem
statement_text: Let I=(V, D, C , A ) be an automatic CSP instance. The bf size of the instance I is defined in two ways: bf The automaton is a part of the input: The size of the representation of I is |V|+| C |+| A | , where | C | = Σ _ le s , Rrangle ∈ C | s | . bf The automaton is a fixed parameter: The size of the representation of I is |V|+| C | , where | C | is defined as above. So, A is not part of the input.

paper_title: Automatic constraint satisfaction problem
statement_text: Based on the representations of AutCSP instances, we define the following classes of CSP. bf The automatic constraint satisfaction problem , written bf AutCSP , is the problem of finding solutions to instances I=(V, D, C, A ) where the automaton A is counted as a part of the input. The constraint satisfaction problem that corresponds to Γ_ A is denoted by bf AutCSP( A ) . For the AutCSP( A ) instances, the automaton A is a fixed parameter and it is not part of the input. Hence we can write these instances in the form (V, D, C ) as Γ_ A is given by A .

paper_title: Automatic constraint satisfaction problem
label: eg:boolean
statement_text: In these examples D={0,1} is Boolean: Consider CSP (Γ) , where Γ consists of finitely many relations of pairwise different arities. This is an AutCSP as finite languages are regular . Let A _ NAE be an automaton, see Figure , recognizing NAE =overline 0^* + 1^* , where NAE stands for not-all-equal. For all k ≥ 1 , the relation R_k in Γ_ A _ NAE consists of all k -tuples (d_1, ... , d_k) such that d_i ≠ d_j for some i and j . The CSP ( NAE ) is NP-complete . Since CSP ( NAE ) reduces in linear time to AutCSP ( A _ NAE ) , the problem AutCSP ( A _ NAE ) is NP-hard. Consider the automaton A _ ODD recognizing language ODD = {α ∈ (0+1)^*: α has an odd number of 1s } . In any instance of the AutCSP ( A _ ODD ) , each constraint has the form x_1+ ... +x_n=1 mod 2 . Solving such constraints is in P.

paper_title: Automatic constraint satisfaction problem
label: Prop:$NP$-complete
statement_text: The following are true: The AutCSP is in NP. The problem AutCSP ( A ) is in NP for any automaton A . Moreover, there exists a automaton A ' such that AutCSP( A ') is NP -complete.

paper_title: Automatic constraint satisfaction problem
label: Thm:1-constraint
statement_text: Let A be an automaton over the Boolean domain D = {0,1} such that L( A ) = NAE _3^* , where NAE _3 := D^3 \ {000,111} . \ Then AutCSP ( A ) restricted to single constraints is NP-complete.

paper_title: Automatic constraint satisfaction problem
label: dfn:polymorphisms
statement_text: Let R be a relation of arity k on D . A bf polymorphism of R is an operation f:D^t → D that satisfies the following condition. For all tuples (x_ 1,1 , ... , x_ 1, k ) ∈ R , ... , (x_ t,1 , ... , x_ t, k ) ∈ R we have (f(x_ 1,1 , x_ 2,1 , ... , x_ t,1 ), ... , f(x_ 1,k , x_ 2,k , ... , x_ t,k )) ∈ R . The operation f:D^t → D is called a bf polymorphism of a language Γ if f is a polymorphism for every relation R in Γ .

paper_title: Automatic constraint satisfaction problem
label: dfn:Pol-Inv
statement_text: Let Γ be a language and let F be a set of operations on D . We introduce the following two sets: Pol (Γ)={fmid f is a polymorphism of Γ} . Inv ( F )={Rmid every f ∈ F is a polymorphism of R} . When F ={g} is a singleton, we write Inv (g) instead of Inv ( F ) . Likewise, if Γ={R} is a singleton, we write Pol (R) .

paper_title: Automatic constraint satisfaction problem
title: Schaefer's Dichotomy
statement_text: Let Γ be a (possibly infinite) set of relations over D = {0,1} . Then CSP( Γ ) is polynomial-time solvable iff one of the following is a polymorphism of \ Γ : the constant operations \ 0 : x mapsto 0 and \ 1 : x mapsto 1 . the binary AND operation ∧ : (x,y) mapsto x ∧ y . the binary OR operation ∨ : (x,y) mapsto x ∨ y . the majority operation Maj : (x,y,z) mapsto ( x ∧ y) ∨ (x ∧ z) ∨ ( y ∧ z). the minority operation Minor : (x,y,z) mapsto x ⊕ y ⊕ z , where ⊕ denotes addition modulo 2. Otherwise, it is NP-complete.

paper_title: Automatic constraint satisfaction problem
statement_text: Let Γ be a (possibly infinite) language on a finite domain. Then the CSP( Γ ) is in P if and only if \ Γ has a Sigger's polymorphism. Otherwise, it is NP-complete.

label: Prop: poly-eg
statement_text: Set X={ 0 , 1 , ∧ , ∨ , Maj, Minor} . For each f ∈ X there exists an automaton A _f over D={0,1} such that L( A _f) is infinite and f is the only polymorphism of L( A _f) .

label: Thm:deciding-polymorphism
statement_text: The following are true: Given a k -ary operation f : D^k → D and a finite automaton A , it takes O(| A |^ k+1 ) time to decide whether the constraint language Γ_ A has f as its polymorphism Fix an integer b ≥ 0 . statement_text: Let n ∈ N and Γ be a constraint language containing k -ary relations over the domain [q] . For even- r , |V(S_i Δ S_ i+1 )| = r for any i ∈ [2q] and W_i = ∅ for any i ∈ [2q] ; For odd- r , |V(S_i Δ S_ i+1 )| = 2r-1 , and |W_i|=1 for any i ∈ [2q] ; (Closed-walk) S_1 = S_ 2q+1 ; (At least 2 -steps) Each hyper-edge (underlying random variable) appears in at least two steps; Equivalently, we view it as a walk of length- (2q) such that at each step- t ∈ [2q] , we move from the left boundary U_t = S_t to the right boundary V_ t = S_ t+1 = U_ t+1 with potential intermediate-set W_t ; For even- r , each step traverses exactly 1 hyper-edge (viewed as an ordered-tuple) that contains V(S_tΔ S_ t+1 ) ; for the odd- r , each step traverses along 2 hyper-edges incident to U_A ∪ V_A ∪ W_t and U_B ∪ V_B ∪ W_t where we assume that U_A, U_B are equal partitions for S_ t \ S_ t+1 and V_A, V_B for S_ t+1 \ S_t as prescribed by the intermediate set. color blue bf (Jeff: adjust as needed) Each hyper-edge appears in at least two steps.

statement_text: For each step- t in a trace walk, for each hyperedge g_e that appears in the matrix entry corresponding to the step- t (the single edge in the even case, and two edges in the odd case), we assign them the following labels, F -Step: a hyperedge that is making its first appearance in the walk; L -Step: a hyperedge that is making its final appearance in the walk; H -Step: a hyperedge that is making its middle appearance (neither first nor final) in the walk.

statement_text: For any step- t in the trace-walk, and any edge e that appears in step- t , we define F -step: assign a factor of B_ ev (e,t) = p ; H/L -step: assign a factor of B_ ev (e, t) = 1 .

statement_text: For any walk P , recall that val (P) coloneqq mathop E _G [ Π _ i ∈ [2q] M_ S,ell [S_i, S_ i+1 ] ] = Π _ e = (I,J) ∈ E(P) mathop E _G[(G_e)^ mul _P(e) ] , we have \[ val (P) ≤ Π _ e ∈ E(P) p \] where E(P) is collection of (hyper)-edges traversed by the walk P , and mul_P(e) denotes the multiplicity/number of times e is traversed in P .

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
label: lem:marginal
statement_text: Suppose a k -CSP is t -wise ν -independent. For any instance J = (V, C) , variable subset S ⊆ V , constraint C ∈ C such that normal size V(C) ∩ (V(C \ set C) ∪ S) ≤ t , \[ π_S (μ_J) = π_S (μ_ J \ C ). \]

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
label: independent-lp
statement_text: Let t ≥ 2 . If a k -CSP is t -wise independent, then except with probability o_ n;k (1) , a random instance of the CSP with n variables and Δ n constraints has an LP hierarchy solution of level Ω_k(n/(Δ^ 2/(t-1) log Δ)) .

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
label: lem:cond-indep
statement_text: Let S,T be subsets of variables of an instance J = (V, C) , and R be an (S,T) -separator in J . Consider picking a random assignment b from μ_J . Then b_S and b_T are conditionally independent given b_R .

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
label: lem:global-markov
statement_text: Let K be the collection of cliques in a graph G = (V, E) . Suppose a distribution μ over D^V is proportional to Π _ K ∈ K f_K , where f_K is a K -junta for K ∈ K . For any vertex subsets S,T ⊆ V and (S,T) -separator R ⊆ V , μ_S and μ_T are conditionally independent given μ_R .

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
statement_text: Let t ≥ 2 . If a k -CSP is t -wise independent, then except with probability o_ n;k (1) , a random instance of the CSP with n variables and Δ n constraints has an SoS solution of degree Ω_k(n/(Δ^ 2/(t-1) log Δ)) .

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
statement_text: Let t ≥ 2 , and ρ be a distribution over R . Given any k -CSP (D, R) , except with probability o_n(1) , a random ρ -instance of the CSP with n variables and Δ n constraints has an SoS solution of degree Ω_k(n/(Δ^ 2/(t-1) log Δ)) and of value opt _t (ρ) + o_n(1) .

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
statement_text: Suppose J = (V, C) is an instance, W ⊆ V, q ∈ A_W . Define μ_ J,q to be the distribution of a random assignment b from μ_J , conditioned on b_W = q .

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
label: lem:extensible
statement_text: Suppose a k -CSP is t -wise independent. For any instance J = (V, C) , variable subsets W ⊆ S ⊆ V , satisfying assignment q ∈ A_W to W , constraint C ∈ C such that normal size V(C) ∩ (V(C \ set C) ∪ S) ≤ t , we have μ_ J,q is well defined if and only if μ_ J \ C,q is, and \[ π_S (μ_ J,q ) = π_S (μ_ J \ C,q ). \]

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
label: thm:cblpaip
statement_text: Let k ≥ 3 . Suppose a k -CSP is pairwise independent and lax. Then, for any constraint density Δ > 0 , with uniformly positive probability, a random instance of the CSP with n variables and Δ n constraints has a solution in the C(BLP+AIP) hierarchy of level Ω(n) .

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
label: thm:sdpaip
statement_text: Let t ≥ 2 . If a k -CSP is t -wise independent and t -wise neutral for AIP, then except with probability o_ n;k (1) , a random instance of the CSP with n variables and Δ n constraints with replacement has an SDP+AIP hierarchy solution of level Ω_k(n/(Δ^ 2/(t-1) log Δ)) .

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals

statement_text: Consider a system of linear equations Ax=b in unknown x ∈ R ^d , where A ∈ {0,1}^ m × d and b ∈ {0,1}^d have zero-one entries. If the system has a solution, then it has a rational solution x^star ∈ Q ^d such that |x^star |_1 ≤ m^ m+1 .

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
label: eq:efron-stein

statement_text: Let ν^k be a product distribution over D^k . Given a subset S ⊆ [k] , define Y_S to be the vector space of S -juntas Z_S to be the subspace of Y_S orthogonal to all the subspaces of proper subsets of S : \[ Z_S coloneqq Y_S ∩ span set Y_T | T ⊊ S ^perp quad under ν^S. \] The subspaces set Z_S | S ⊆ [k] are mutually orthogonal under ν^k and together they span L^2(ν^k) . The Efron--Stein decomposition is the orthogonal decomposition L^2 (ν^k) = oplus_ S ⊆ [k] Z_S quad under ν^k.

statement_text: Given a distribution μ over D^k having density f wrt ν^k , π_Q (μ) has density f^ ⊆ Q vert _Q wrt ν^Q for any Q ⊆ [k] .

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals

statement_text: Let Φ= Q .φ be a QBF, v ∈ Var _ ∀ ( Φ ) , and E = Var _ ∃ ( Q ) ∩ D _ preceq ( v ) , and let A and Q ' be defined as above. For every function f : [N] → [0,1] and ε > 0 , σ can be used to produce an estimate widehat μ (f) ∈ [0,1] for μ_M(f) coloneqq E _ w Unif (M) f(w) s.t. \[ Pr _ σ [|widehat μ (f) - μ_ M (f)| ≥ ε+ frac λ α ] ≤ 2exp (-Ω(ε^2 α^2 t)). \] ( widehat μ (f) is a deterministic function of σ .)

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: thm:densub:sparse hard
statement_text: For constant ε>0 , any randomized streaming algorithm which returns v ∈ [0,1] such that (1-ε) · maxden _ G ≤ v ≤ maxden _ G or returns a set S ⊆ V such that den _ G parens * S ≥ (1-ε) · maxden _ G with probability at least 2/3 requires Ω(n log n) bits of space.

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: cl:denseSquare
statement_text: Let n ∈ N , π : {0,1}^n → {0,1}^n be a permutation, and x ∈ {0,1}^n and i ∈ [n] . Let G be the graph created if Alice runs Cref alg:densub:sparse hard:alice-reduction with input π and Bob runs Cref alg:densub:sparse hard:bob-reduction with input (x,i) . Then: If (π(x))_i = 1 , then G contains exactly one square (i.e., a 4 -cycle), and the rest of the connected components are single edges and length- 3 paths; hence, maxden _ G ≥ 1 . If (π(x))_i = 0 , then the connected components of G are single edges and length- 3 paths; hence, maxden _ G ≤ frac 34 .

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: cl:density of not square
statement_text: Consider a graph with a single 4 -cycle (i.e., a square) and all other connected components consisting of single edges and length- 3 paths. Take the set of vertices in the 4 -cycle to be C . For any set S ≠ C , den _ G parens * S < 0.9 .

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: thm:densub:dense alg
statement_text: There exists an insertion-only streaming algorithm which, given an undirected graph G = (V, E) on n vertices and m ≥ α n^2 edges and ε ∈ (0,1) , outputs S ⊆ [n] which has den _ G parens * S ≥ (1-ε) · maxden _ G in O(frac n ε^2α^4 ) bits of space with probability at least 2/3 .

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
statement_text: There exists an insertion-only streaming algorithm which, given an undirected simple graph G = (V, E) on n vertices and m ≥ α n^2 edges and ε ∈ (0,1) , outputs S ⊆ [n] which has den _ G parens * S ≥ (1-ε) · maxden _ G in O(frac n ε^2α^4 log frac 1 ε α^2 ) bits of space and O( log n) amortized update time with probability at least 2/3 .

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: claim:densub:maxden-lb
statement_text: Let G=(V,E) be an undirected multigraph on n vertices with m edges. Then \[ maxden _ G ≥ frac m n. \]

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: claim:densub:S-m/n-lb
statement_text: Let G=(V,E) be an undirected multigraph on n vertices with m edges. Then \[ abs * arg max _ substack S ⊆ V S ≠ ∅ den _ G parens * S ≥ frac m n. \]

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: thm:densub:dense hard
statement_text: For constant ε > 0 , any randomized streaming algorithm which outputs a set S ⊆ V such that den _ G parens * S ≥ (1-ε) · maxden _ G for input graph G on n vertices and m = Θ(n^2) edges with probability at least 2/3 requires Ω(n) bits of working space.

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: def:densub:dense hard:disjoint
statement_text: Let γ ∈ [0,1] . Two graphs G and G' on [n] are γ -disjoint if for every T ⊆ [n] , it is not simultaneously the case that den _ G parens * T ≥ γ maxden _ G and den _ G' parens * T ≥ γ maxden _ G' .

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: thm:densub:dense hard:instances
statement_text: There exists α, C > 0 such that the following holds. For ε_0 coloneqq tfrac 14 and every 0 < ε < ε_0 , let n ∈ N be sufficiently large. Then there exists a set G such that: Each G ∈ G is an undirected simple graph on [n] with ≥ α binom n 2 edges. |G| ≥ 2^ Cn/ε . For every G ≠ G' ∈ G , G and G' are (1-ε) -disjoint (in the sense of Cref def:densub:dense hard:disjoint ).

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
statement_text: Let 0 < ε < frac 12 . Suppose T ⊆ [n] satisfies den _ K (S) parens * T ≥ (1-ε) maxden _ K (S) . Then d(1_S,1_T) ≤ 4ε , where d( · , · ) denotes the normalized Hamming distance.

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: thm:maxcsp:dense alg
statement_text: Let k,q ∈ N . There exists an insertion-only streaming algorithm which, given an instance Φ on n vertices with m ≥ α n^k constraints and ε ∈ (0,1) , outputs x : V → [q] which has val _ Φ parens * x ≥ (1-ε) · opt _ Φ in O(frac n ε^2α^2 ) bits of space with probability at least 2/3 .

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: thm:altForCSP
statement_text: Let k,q ∈ N . paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: thm:sim-alg
statement_text: For every ε> 0 and N ∈ N , there exists an insertion-only streaming algorithm which, given as input a sequence of insertions to two sets A, B ⊆ [N] , outputs \[ v ∈ frac |A ∩ B| |A ∪ B| pm ε \] with probability at least 2/3 in O(1/ε^2 + log N) bits of space.

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: prelim:twowise
title: 2 -wise independent hash permutation family
statement_text: Let N be a prime. Let x_1 ≠ x_2 ∈ [N] and y_1 ≠ y_2 ∈ [N] . For c Unif ({1, ... ,N-1}) and d Unif ({0, ... ,N-1}) , letting h_ c , d : [N] → [N] : x mapsto c x + d , \[ Pr _ c , d [h_ c , d (x_1)=y_1 wedge h_ c , d (x_2)=y_2] = frac 1 N(N-1) . \]

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: lem:calc
statement_text: Let N be prime and let h_ c,d : [N] → [N] be the random hash function in Cref prelim:twowise . For every set S ⊆ [N] and t ∈ N , for the random variable X_S coloneqq abs * braces * w ∈ S : h_ c,d (w) ≤ t , we have: \[ E X_S = frac |X| t N and Var X_S ≤ E X_S. \]

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
statement_text: For every ε, α > 0 and N ∈ N , there exists an insertion-only streaming algorithm which, given as input a sequence of insertions to two sets A, B ⊆ [N] , assuming |A ∪ B| ≥ α N , outputs \[ v ∈ frac |A ∩ B| |A ∪ B| pm ε \] in O(1/(αε^2) + log N) bits of space and O(1) time (in arithmetic operations) per update with probability at least 2/3 .

paper_title: Streaming Complexity Separations for Dense and Sparse Graphs
label: thm:rare-alg
statement_text: For every ε, α > 0 and N,k ∈ N , there exists an insertion-only streaming algorithm which, given as input a sequence of insertions to a multiset S ⊆ [N] , letting S_k denote the number of distinct elements in S of multiplicity k and D the total number of distinct elements in S , assuming D ≥ α N , outputs \[ v ∈ frac S_k D pm ε \] with probability at least 2/3 in O( log k/(αε^2) + log N) bits of space and O(1) time (in arithmetic operations) per update. The multiplicity of an element can be unbounded.

paper_title: Multi-Prover Interactive Proof Systems with Leakage
label: lem:parallel_repetition
title: Parallel repetition theorem
statement_text: For any two-prover game G = (π, X × Y , A × B , V ) such that ω_c(G) = 1-ε for 0<ε ≤ frac 1 2 , \[ ω_c(G^ ⊗ N ) ≤ (1-ε^c)^ Ω(frac N s ) enspace , \] where s= log | A × B | +1 and c is a universal constant.

paper_title: Multi-Prover Interactive Proof Systems with Leakage
title: AM
statement_text: We say a language L is in AM if and only if for an input z ∈ {0,1}^* , there exists a single-prover one-round interactive proof system satisfying the following properties: Verifier's messages are sampled uniformly at random from {0,1}^ p(|z|) for some polynomial p . If z ∈ L , the verifier accepts with probability at least frac 2 3 . If z ∉ L , the verifier accepts with probability at most frac 1 3 .

paper_title: Multi-Prover Interactive Proof Systems with Leakage
statement_text: Any language recognized by single-prover constant-round interactive proof systems is in AM .

paper_title: Multi-Prover Interactive Proof Systems with Leakage
title: NEXP
statement_text: We say a language L is in NEXP if and only if there exist polynomials p,q and a deterministic classical algorithm A satisfying the following properties: For all x,y the algorithm A runs in time 2^ p(x) on input (x,y) . If x ∈ L , there exists a string y of length 2^ q(|x|) such that the algorithm A given x and y accepts. If x ∉ L , then for all strings y of length 2^ q(|x|) , the algorithm A given x and y rejects.

paper_title: Multi-Prover Interactive Proof Systems with Leakage
label: def:mip
title: MIP
statement_text: We say a language L is in MIP _ c,s [q,a] if and only if, for z ∈ {0,1}^* , there exists a family of non-local games G_z = (π, X × Y , A × B , V ) satisfying the following properties: The question size is q and the answer size is a . There is an algorithm running in poly (|z|) -time, given z , to sample questions (x,y) ∈ X × Y from π . There is an algorithm running in poly (|z|) -time, given z and (x,y,a,b) ∈ X × Y × A × B , to output V (a,b|x,y) ∈ {0,1} . If z ∈ L , ω_c(G_z) = c If z ∉ L , ω_c(G_z) ≤ s .

paper_title: Multi-Prover Interactive Proof Systems with Leakage
label: def:mip*
title: MIP ^* , Definition 5.29 in

There is an algorithm that runs in poly (|z|) -time, given z and (x,y,a,b) ∈ X × Y × A × B , to output V (a,b|x,y) ∈ {0,1} . If z ∈ L , ω_q(G_z) = 1 . If z ∉ L , ω_q(G_z) ≤ frac 1 2 .

paper_title: Multi-Prover Interactive Proof Systems with Leakage

Each one of the constraints is a projection constraint, meaning that for every e ∈ E there is a map φ_ecolon Σ_L → Σ_R such that Φ_e = {(σ,φ_e(σ)) | σ ∈ Σ_L} enspace .

statement_text: A language L is in MIP ^ → _ c,s [q,a,ell ] if and only if there exists a two-prover one-round interactive proof for L , in which the verifier V runs in time poly (|x|) for every instance x ∈ {0,1}^* and satisfies the following properties: Completeness: If x ∈ L , then after exchanging one round of messages first with P_1 and then with P_2 , the verifier V accepts with probability at least c . Soundness: If x ∉ L , for every set of malicious provers P_1 and P_2 , in which P_1 is allowed to send ell bits to P_2 after receiving the question from V , the verifier will accept with probability at most s . Additionally, the question size is q bits, and the answer size is at most a bits.
