paper_title: Optimal Inapproximability of Generalized Linear Equations over a Finite Group
title: Max-E k -LIN _ S (G)
statement_text: Consider a multiset of linear equations (C_1,C_2, ... , C_m) over variables {x_1,x_2, ... ,x_n|x_i ∈ G} for a group G . Each constraint consists of a tuple of exactly k literals and will be considered satisfied when their sum/product over G is in S ⊆ G . The Max-E k -LIN _ S (G) problem is to find an assignment to {x_1,x_2, ... ,x_n} that maximizes the number of satisfied constraints.

paper_title: Optimal Inapproximability of Generalized Linear Equations over a Finite Group
label: thm:main
statement_text: Fix any finite group G and S ⊆ G . Let H_S is the smallest normal subgroup such that [G,G] ⊆ H_S S ⊆ gH_S for some g ∈ G , i.e., S is a subset of some coset of H_S . then the problem Max-E k -LIN _ S (G) is approximable within a factor of frac |S| |H_S| on satisfiable instances. Furthermore, if S^ -1 S generates H_S , assuming P ≠ NP , for every ε>0 , it is NP -hard to approximate Max-E k -LIN _ S (G) within a factor of frac |S| |H_S| +ε .

paper_title: Optimal Inapproximability of Generalized Linear Equations over a Finite Group
label: def:label-cover
title: Label Cover
statement_text: An instance Ψ=(U,V,E,[L], [R],{π_e}_ e ∈ E ) of the Label Cover constraint satisfaction problem consists of a bi-regular bipartite graph (U,V,E) , alphabets [L] and [R] and a surjective projection map π_e : [L] → [R] for every edge e ∈ E . Given a labeling ell : U → [L], ell :V → [R] , an edge e = (u,v) is said to be satisfied by ell if π_e(ell (u)) = ell (v) . Ψ is said to be satisfiable if there exists a labeling that satisfies all the edges. Ψ is said to be at most δ -satisfiable if every labeling satisfies at most a δ fraction of the edges.

paper_title: Optimal Inapproximability of Generalized Linear Equations over a Finite Group
label: thm:LChard
title: Hardness of Label Cover
statement_text: For every r ∈ N , there is a deterministic n^ O(r) -time reduction from a 3 - SAT\ instance of size n to an instance Ψ=(U,V,E,[L],[R], {π_e}_ e ∈ E ) of Label Cover \ with the following properties: |U|,|V| leqslant n^ O(r) ; L,R leqslant 2^ O(r) ; Ψ is bi-regular with degrees bounded by 2^ O(r) . YES Case : If the 3 - SAT\ instance is satisfiable, then Ψ is satisfiable. NO Case : If the 3 - SAT\ instance is unsatisfiable, then Ψ is at most 2^ -r -satisfiable.

paper_title: Optimal Inapproximability of Generalized Linear Equations over a Finite Group
title: Layered Label Cover

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
statement_text: For every non-trivial symmetric Boolean predicate R , the following hold. If R has arity at most 4 , then the asymptotic growth of NRD _ n (R) is determined exactly. If R has arity 5 , then the asymptotic growth of NRD _ n (R) is determined exactly for all predicates except, up to bit-flip symmetry, Bit-flip symmetry identifies R ⊆ {0,1}^r with overline R:={1-x:x ∈ R} . For symmetric predicates, this sends W to r-W:={r-w:w ∈ W} and preserves NRD xspace _n . See Cref sec:prelims . the two predicates R_ 023 and R_ 124 with W (R_ 023 ) ={0,2,3} and W (R_ 124 ) ={1,2,4} . For each R ∈ {R_ 023 ,R_ 124 } , we obtain Ω(n^2) ≤ NRD _ n (R) ≤ O(n^3) .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: thm:intro-tbalanced
title: Upper-Bound criterionxspace ; informal Cref thm:t-balanced-main
statement_text: theorem infupper Let R ⊆ {0,1}^r and let t ≥ 1 . Then R is t -balanced if and only if every falsifying tuple f ∉ R is captured by a multilinear polynomial of degree at most t over some commutative ring with identity. Consequently, every n -variable instance of CSP xspace (R) has an equivalent subinstance with O(n^t) constraints, and hence NRD _ n (R) =O(n^t) .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: ex:nae-upper-1
statement_text: Consider R= NAE _3 , so W (R) ={1,2} . The falsifying tuples are 000 and 111 . The polynomial p(x)=(x_1+x_2+x_3-1)(x_1+x_2+x_3-2) vanishes on all tuples of Hamming weight 1 or 2 , and is nonzero on tuples of Hamming weight 0 or 3 . Thus this degree- 2 polynomial captures both falsifying tuples. For t=2 , the lift is ν_2(x)=(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_1x_2,x_1x_3,x_2x_3) . The lifted relation R^ (2) consists of the six vectors obtained from the accepting tuples: \[ c|c x & ν_2(x) hline 100 & (1,0,0,0,0,0) 010 & (0,1,0,0,0,0) 001 & (0,0,1,0,0,0) 110 & (1,1,0,1,0,0) 101 & (1,0,1,0,1,0) 011 & (0,1,1,0,0,1). \] The falsifying tuples lift to ν_2(000)=(0,0,0,0,0,0) and ν_2(111)=(1,1,1,1,1,1) . After multilinearization, p becomes p(x)=2-2(x_1+x_2+x_3)+2(x_1x_2+x_1x_3+x_2x_3) , which is a linear expression in the lifted coordinates. This illustrates why degree- t capturing polynomials can be studied through linear conditions after the degree- t lift.

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
title: Continuing Cref ex:nae-upper-1
statement_text: The previous example showed the polynomial side of the lift. We now use the same relation to illustrate the integer-span test actually used in the implementation. The two rejected lifted points are ν_2(000)=(0,0,0,0,0,0) and ν_2(111)=(1,1,1,1,1,1) . To test 2 -balancedness, we check whether either rejected point lies in the integer span of the accepted lifted points after adding a leading 1 coordinate. For b=ν_2(000) , membership would mean that there are integers z_ 100 ,z_ 010 ,z_ 001 ,z_ 110 ,z_ 101 ,z_ 011 such that \[ Σ _ a ∈ R^ (2) z_a ext (a)= ext (b)=(1,0,0,0,0,0,0). \] Looking at the three degree- 2 coordinates forces z_ 110 =z_ 101 =z_ 011 =0 . Then the three degree- 1 coordinates force z_ 100 =z_ 010 =z_ 001 =0 , contradicting the leading-coordinate equation Σ _a z_a=1 . Hence ext (ν_2(000)) is not in the integer span. Similarly, for b=ν_2(111) , the three degree- 2 coordinates force z_ 110 =z_ 101 =z_ 011 =1 . The degree- 1 coordinates then force z_ 100 =z_ 010 =z_ 001 =-1 . But the leading-coordinate sum is then -1-1-1+1+1+1=0 , not 1 . Hence ext (ν_2(111)) is also not in the integer span. Therefore neither rejected lifted point lies in the integer span, so the integer-span test certifies that NAE _3 is 2 -balanced.

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
statement_text: The predicate NAE _3 defines OR xspace _2 after pinning one coordinate to 0 : the constraint { NAE _3,(x,y,0)} is false exactly on (x,y)=(0,0) and true otherwise. Thus it behaves as { OR xspace _2,(x,y)} . Since OR xspace _2 has non-redundant instances of size Ω(n^2) , this gives an Ω(n^2) lower bound.

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
title: Lower-bound criterionxspace ; informal Cref thm:carbonnel-lower-bound
statement_text: Let R ⊆ {0,1} ^r and let 2 ≤ k ≤ r . If OR xspace _k ∈ le Rrangle _ fg , then NRD _ n (R) =Ω(n^k) .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: ex:kcube
statement_text: For example, when k=2 , the input rows are indexed by 11,10,01 . The operation f_2 has arity 3 and is defined on the following column types: \[ c|c column & f_2( column ) hline 000 & 0 111 & 1 110 & 0 001 & 1 101 & 0 010 & 1. \] Here 110 and 101 are the two coordinate columns of the nonzero 2 -cube, and 001 and 010 are their complements. As a concrete failure, take R= NAE _3 , so W (R) ={1,2} . Consider the following three input rows, indexed by 11,10,01 : \[ c|ccc|c & coord. 1 & coord. 2 & coord. 3 & weight hline 11 & 1 & 1 & 0 & 2 10 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1 01 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 1. \] All three rows belong to NAE _3 . Now look at the columns: they are 110 , 101 , and 000 . By the table above, f_2 maps these columns to 0 , 0 , and 0 , respectively. Hence the coordinatewise output is 000 , which does not belong to NAE _3 . Therefore f_2 does not preserve NAE _3 , and thus gives the lower bound NRD _ n ( NAE _3) =Ω(n^2) .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
statement_text: Consider again the case k=2 . The column types in the domain of f_2 are 000,111,110,001,101,010 , with outputs 0,1,0,1,0,1 , respectively. Suppose R= NAE _3 , so W (R) ={1,2} . Since R has arity 3 , a multiplicity vector assigns three coordinates among these six column types. Take the multiplicity vector that uses 110 once, 101 once, and 000 once, and uses all other column types zero times. The three input rows then have weights 2,1,1 : the row indexed by 11 sees the entries 1,1,0 , the row indexed by 10 sees 1,0,0 , and the row indexed by 01 sees 0,1,0 . All these weights lie in W (R) ={1,2} . The output row has entries 0,0,0 , hence output weight 0 , which does not lie in W (R) . Therefore this multiplicity vector witnesses failure of preservation, and the lower-bound criterionxspace succeeds for R= NAE _3 and k=2 .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
title: Relative balancedness
statement_text: Let A ⊆ X ⊆ {0,1} ^N . We say that A is balanced relative to X if for every odd integer m ≥ 1 and every tuple a^ (1) ,a^ (2) , ... ,a^ (m) ∈ A , it holds that if the coordinatewise alternating sum u := a^ (1) - a^ (2) + a^ (3) - ... - a^ (m-1) + a^ (m) belongs to X , then u ∈ A .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: def:tbal
title: t -lift and t -balancedness
statement_text: Fix integers r ≥ 1 and t ≥ 1 , and let S_ r,t :={S ⊆ [r]:1 ≤ |S| ≤ t} . The degree- t lift is the map ν_t:{0,1}^r → {0,1}^ S_ r,t defined by ν_t(x)_S:= Π _ i ∈ S x_i . For a relation R ⊆ {0,1}^r , let X_t:=ν_t({0,1}^r) and R^ (t) :=ν_t(R) . We say that R is t -balanced if R^ (t) is balanced relative to X_t .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
title: Capturing polynomial
statement_text: Let R ⊆ {0,1} ^r and let f ∈ {0,1} ^r \ R . A polynomial p over a ring E captures f with respect to R if \[ p(y)=0 quad for all y ∈ R, qquad and qquad p(f) ≠ 0. \] Equivalently, we may write p\ captures _R\ f .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: lem:bal-latt
statement_text: Let A ⊆ X ⊆ {0,1} ^N , and define ext (v) := (1,v) ∈ Z ^ N+1 . Then the following are equivalent. A is balanced relative to X . For every u ∈ X , if ext (u) ∈ span _ Z l({ ext (a): a ∈ A} r), then u ∈ A .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: thm:linrel
statement_text: Let A ⊆ X ⊆ {0,1} ^N . Then the following are equivalent. A is balanced relative to X . For every u ∈ X \ A , there exists a prime-power q_u := p^a (for some prime p ) and a linear polynomial ell _u(z_1, ... ,z_N)=α_0+α_1 z_1+ ... +α_N z_N over Z /q_u Z such that ell _u\ captures _A\ u . Moreover, if A is not balanced relative to X , then there exists some u ∈ X \ A that is not capturable by any linear polynomial over any commutative ring with identity.

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: thm:t-balanced-main
statement_text: Let R ⊆ {0,1}^r and let t ≥ 1 . Then the following are equivalent. R is t -balanced . For every f ∈ {0,1}^r \ R , there exists a prime-power q_f and a multilinear polynomial p_f over Z/q_fZ of degree at most t such that p_f captures f with respect to R . Moreover, if R is not t -balanced , then there exists f ∈ {0,1}^r \ R that is not captured by any degree- ≤ t multilinear polynomial over any commutative ring with identity.

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: thm:cjp-general-capture
title: Theorem 3.5,
statement_text: Let R ⊆ {0,1} ^r be a fixed Boolean relation. Suppose that for every u ∈ {0,1} ^r \ R , there exists a ring E_u which is either Q or a Z /q_u Z for some q_u ∈ N _ >1 and a polynomial p_u over E_u of degree at most t such that p_u captures u with respect to R . Then there exists a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a set of R -constraints on n variables, outputs an equivalent subset of O(n^t) constraints.

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: cor:t-balanced-sparsification
statement_text: Let R ⊆ {0,1} ^r be t -balanced , with t ≥ 1 . Then every instance of CSP xspace (R) on n variables has an equivalent subinstance with O(n^t) constraints.

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: thm:balanced-nrd
statement_text: Let R ⊆ {0,1} ^r be t -balanced , with t ≥ 1 . Then NRD _ n (R) =O(n^t).

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: def:fgppdef
title: fgpp-definition
statement_text: Let Γ be a constraint language over a finite domain D , and let R ⊆ D^m be a relation. We say that R is fgpp-definable from Γ if there is a formula \[ R(x_1, ... ,x_m)equiv ∃ y_1, ... ,y_q ψ(x_1, ... ,x_m,y_1, ... ,y_q), \] where ψ is a conjunction of constraints over Γ together with functional guards of the form Q_g(u,v) , where gcolon D → D is a unary map and \[ Q_g:={(a,g(a)):a ∈ D}. \] We write le Γ rangle _ fg for the set of all relations fgpp-definable from Γ .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
title: Polymorphism pattern and pattern partial operation
statement_text: A polymorphism pattern of arity s is a set of pairs \[ ((x_1, ... ,x_s),x), \] where (x_1, ... ,x_s) is a tuple of variables and x is one of the variables appearing in it. Given a finite domain D , the interpretation of such a pattern P on D is the partial operation f_P^D defined as follows: its domain consists of all tuples of the form \[ (φ(x_1), ... ,φ(x_s)) \] arising from a pair ((x_1, ... ,x_s),x) ∈ P and an assignment φ of the variables to D , and on such a tuple we set \[ f_P^D(φ(x_1), ... ,φ(x_s)):=φ(x). \] A partial operation obtained in this way is called a pattern partial operation .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
title: Pattern partial polymorphisms
statement_text: Let R ⊆ D^r be a relation and let f be a k -ary partial operation on D . We say that f is a partial polymorphism of R if for every choice of tuples t^ (1) , ... ,t^ (k) ∈ R such that f is defined coordinatewise on these tuples, the tuple obtained by applying f coordinatewise also belongs to R . If in addition f is a pattern partial operation, then we call it a pattern partial polymorphism of R . For a constraint language Γ , we write p^2Pol (Γ) for the set of all pattern partial polymorphisms of every relation in Γ .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: thm:carbonnel-duality
title: Carbonnel
statement_text: Let Γ_1,Γ_2 be finite constraint languages over the same finite domain. Then \[ p^2Pol (Γ_1) ⊆ p^2Pol (Γ_2) qquad Longleftrightarrow qquad Γ_2 ⊆ le Γ_1rangle _ fg . \] In particular, for a relation R and any relation S over the same domain, \[ S ∈ le {R}rangle _ fg qquad Longleftrightarrow qquad p^2Pol ({R}) ⊆ p^2Pol ({S}). \]

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: def:universal-k-cube
title: Universal k -cube pattern
statement_text: Fix k ≥ 2 . Let c_1, ... ,c_ 2^k-1 be the lexicographic ordering of the tuples in {x,y}^k \ {(y, ... ,y)} with respect to y>x . The universal k -cube pattern P_k^u of arity 2^k-1 is the set of pairs (t_i,y) for all 1 ≤ i ≤ k , where \[ t_i := l(c_1[i],c_2[i], ... ,c_ 2^k-1 [i] r). \] Its interpretation on the Boolean domain is denoted by f^ {0,1} _ P_k^u .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: thm:carbonnel-lower-bound
statement_text: Let R be a relation of arity r over a finite domain D , and let 2 ≤ k ≤ r . If f^D_ P^u_k ∉ p^2Pol ({R}) , then NRD _ n (R) =Ω(n^k) .

paper_title: Non-Redundancy of Low-Arity Symmetric Boolean CSPs
label: thm:positive-nrd
statement_text: Let D be a domain of size |D|=q , let Γ be a fixed finite constraint language containing r -ary relations over D . Let U be a finite set of unary maps D → D containing the identity map. Then, for every n ≥ 1 , we have NRD ^ simp _ n (Γ) ≤ NRD ^ + _ n (Γ) ≤ NRD ^ lit _ n (Γ) ≤ NRD ^ simp _ O_ r,q (n) (Γ) . Consequently, for fixed D,Γ , and U , the three models have the same asymptotic non-redundancy up to constant-factor changes in the number of variables.

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: def:balance
statement_text: A Boolean predicate P ⊆ {0,1}^r is balanced if for all k ∈ N and all tuples t_1, hdots , t_ 2k+1 ∈ P (some possibly equal), if we compute (over Z ) the r -tuple \[ t := t_1 - t_2 + t_3 - ... + t_ 2k+1 \] and t ∈ {0,1}^r , then t ∈ P .

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: thm:main
title: Informal version of Theorem
statement_text: Assume that P is an I -substructure of Q and that CSP (P) has an infinite family of (|E|^ ε , I) - shrinking instances . Then, NRD (Q, n) = Ω(n^ frac 1 1-ε ) .

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: thm:boolbck-intro
title: Informal version of Theorem
statement_text: Every non-trivial projection of BoolBCK | BoolBCK ^ + has a super-linear NRD lower bound.

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: def:NRD
statement_text: Given a predicate P ⊆ D^r , we say that an r -uniform hypergraph H = (V, E) is a non-redundant (NRD) instance of CSP (P) if for every edge e ∈ E , there exists an assignment ψ_e : V → D such that ψ_e satisfies e' for every e' ∈ E \ {e} , but ψ_e does not satisfy e . We define NRD (P, n) to be the size of the largest non-redundant instance of CSP (P) on n vertices.

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: def:conditional-nrd
statement_text: Given predicates P ⊊ Q ⊆ D^r , we say that an r -uniform hypergraph H = (V, E) is a (conditionally) non-redundant instance of CSP (P mid Q) if for every edge e ∈ E , there exists an assignment ψ_e : V → D such that ψ_e P -satisfies e' for every e' ∈ E \ {e} , but e is Q \ P -satisfied by ψ_e . We define NRD (P mid Q, n) to be the size of the largest non-redundant instance of CSP (P mid Q) on n vertices.

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: lem:NRD-triangle
title: Triangle inequality
statement_text: For any predicates P ⊊ Q ⊊ R ⊆ D^r and n ∈ N , we have that \[ NRD (P mid R, n) ≤ NRD (P mid Q, n) + NRD (Q mid R, n). \] In particular, if R = D^r , we have that \[ NRD (P, n) ≤ NRD (P mid Q, n) + NRD (Q, n). \]

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: def:projection
statement_text: Consider predicates P ⊊ Q ⊆ D_1^ r_1 and R ⊊ S ⊆ D_2^ r_2 . Given a sequence I = (I_1, hdots , I_ r_2 ) of subsets of [r_1] , we say that P mid Q is an I -substructure of R mid S if there exist maps {g_j : D_1^ I_j → D_2 mid j ∈ [r_2]} (called the witnessing maps ) such that the following two conditions are true. ∀ x ∈ P &, (g_1(π_ I_1 x), g_2(π_ I_2 x), hdots , g_ r_2 (π_ I_ r_2 x)) ∈ R, ∀ x ∈ Q \ P &, (g_1(π_ I_1 x), g_2(π_ I_2 x), hdots , g_ r_2 (π_ I_ r_2 x)) ∈ S \ R.

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: prop:projection-compact
statement_text: Consider predicates P ⊊ Q ⊆ D_1^ r_1 and R ⊊ S ⊆ D_2^ r_2 . Given a sequence I = (I_1, hdots , I_ r_2 ) of subsets of [r_1] , we have that that P mid Q is an I -substructure of R mid S if and only if there exists a map Σ : Q → S subject to the following conditions Σ(P) ⊆ R and Σ(Q \ P) ⊆ S \ R . For all i ∈ [r_1] and j ∈ [r_2] , if i ∉ I_j and x, y ∈ Q differ only in coordinate i , then Σ(x)_j = Σ(y)_j .

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: def:shrink
statement_text: Given an r -partite hypergraph H = (V_1, hdots , V_r, E) , a family of sets I of subsets of [r] , and a parameter λ ≥ 1 , we say that H is (λ, I) -shrinking if for all I ∈ I , we have that |π_I E| ≤ |E| / λ . We say that H is λ -shrinking if H is (λ, I) -shrinking for all I ⊊ [r] .

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: def:projection-hypergraph
statement_text: Given an r -partite hypergraph H = (V_1, hdots , V_r, E) and a family of sets I = (I_1, hdots , I_ell ) of subsets of [r] (possibly with repetition), define the ell -partite projection hypergraph pr _ I H = (π_ I_1 E, hdots , π_ I_ell E, pr _ I (E)) , where \[ pr _ I (E) = { pr _ I e := (π_ I_1 e, hdots , π_ I_ell e) mid e ∈ E}. \]

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: lemma:projection-NRD
statement_text: Consider predicates P ⊊ Q ⊆ D_1^ r_1 and R ⊊ S ⊆ D_2^ r_2 . Given a sequence I = (I_1, hdots , I_ r_2 ) of subsets of [r_1] , assume that that P mid Q is an I -substructure of R mid S with witnessing maps g_1, hdots , g_ r_2 . If H = (V_1, hdots , V_ r_1 , E) is a non-redundant instance of CSP (P mid Q) , then pr _ I H = (π_ I_1 E, hdots , π_ I_ r_2 E, pr _ I (E)) is a non-redundant instance of CSP (R mid S) .

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: thm:shrink-lb
statement_text: Consider predicates P ⊊ Q ⊆ D_1^ r_1 and R ⊊ S ⊆ D_2^ r_2 . Given a sequence I = (I_1, hdots , I_ r_2 ) of subsets of [r_1] , assume that that P mid Q is an I -substructure of R mid S . Further let H_1 = (V_1, E_1), H_2 = (V_2, E_2), hdots be an infinite sequence of non-redundant instances of CSP (P mid Q) with the following properties. Assume there exists absolute constants C_1, C_2, ε > 0 (with ε < 1 ) such that the following conditions hold for all i ≥ 1 : H_i is (C_1 · |E_i|^ -ε , I) -shrinking, and 1 ≤ |E_ i+1 | / |E_ i | ≤ C_2 . Then, NRD (R mid S, n) = Ω(n^ frac 1 1-ε ), where Ω hides constant factors dependent on |E_1|, C_1, C_2, r_1,r_2, ε.

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: cor:richness
statement_text: Consider predicates P ⊊ Q ⊆ D_1^ r_1 and R ⊊ S ⊆ D_2^ r_2 with P,R ≠ ∅ . Given a sequence I = (I_1, hdots , I_ r_2 ) of subsets of [r_1] of size at most c , assume that that P mid Q is an I -substructure of R mid S . Assume that NRD (P mid Q, n) = Ω(n^ α ) , then \[ NRD (R mid S, n) = Ω(n^ α/c ). \]

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: prop:girth-6
title: Lemma 4.3
statement_text: A bipartite graph G = (V_1, V_2, E) is a non-redundant instance of CSP (C_6^ * mid C_6) if and only if G has girth at least 6 .

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances
label: def:box-product
statement_text: Given predicates P_1 ⊊ Q_1 ⊆ D^ r_1 and P_2 ⊊ Q_2 ⊆ D^ r_2 , we define their box product (P_1 mid Q_1) boxtimes (P_2 mid Q_2) = (P_3 mid Q_3) with P_3 ⊊ Q_3 ⊆ D^ r_1+r_2 as follows. Q_3 &:= Q_1 × Q_2 = {(t_1, hdots , t_ r_1 , t'_ 1 , hdots , t'_ r_2 ) : t ∈ Q_1, t' ∈ Q_2} P_3 &:= (P_1 × Q_2) ∪ (Q_1 × P_2).

paper_title: Super-linear Lower Bounds for CSP Non-Redundancy via Shrinking Instances

However, there are 64m^5 agents in A_ e,* but only 32m^5 goods in G_e , demand is greater than supply, a contradiction. Thus the prices of G_e is positive. This also implies that only agents with positive utility for them will be assigned these goods. Since all goods in G_e need to be sold, and can be sold only to agents in A_ e,* , A_ e,2,ell , A_ e,3,ell , A_ e,4,ell who have positive utility for it, where each of them has a budget of 1+ε , therefore we have p(G_e) ≤ frac (64m^5 + 50m)(1+ε) 32m^5 = 2+O(1/m^4). Similarly, G_ v,3 have positive prices and therefore can only be sold to agents in A_v and A_ e,1 where e=(v,k) for some k (there can only be a constant number of such edges since the out-degree of each vertex is bounded). Thus by market clearance, we have p(G_ v,3 ) ≤ frac (5m^ 10 + Θ(48m^3))(1+ε) 2m^ 10 = 5/2 + O(1/m^7).

label: thm:feasible-relative-consistency
statement_text: Let S ⊇ S^1_2 be finitely axiomatized and sequential, and let φ be true. If EA vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + φ , then there is a polynomial p such that S sststile n^ O(1) Con _ S (p(n)) → Con _ S + φ (n) . In particular, S sststile n^ O(1) Con _ S + φ (n) .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: conj:HRC

statement_text: Let S ⊇ S^1_2 be a sound, finitely axiomatized sequential theory, and let φ be a true sentence. We expect the non-simulation implications of bf HRC /bf FR , bf KH , and related conjectures to extend to sound effective theories beyond the finitely axiomatized sequential class; no corresponding biconditional characterization is claimed there.

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: conj:feasible-reflection
statement_text: (bf Feasible Reflection (FR) ) Let S ⊇ S^1_2 be a sound, finitely axiomatized, sequential theory, and let φ be a true sentence. If S sststile n^ O(1) Con _ S + φ (n) , then EA vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + φ .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption

statement_text: For a sound theory S ⊇ S^1_2 , the following are equivalent. There exists a true sentence φ such that, for every constant c > 0 , Scenternot sststile n^c Con _ S + φ (n) . For all sufficiently large k and every constant c > 0 , Scenternot sststile n^c Con _ S^1_2 + φ_ BB (k) (n) .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: conj:kolmogorov-hardness
statement_text: (bf Kolmogorov Hardness (KH) ) Let S ⊇ S^1_2 be a sound, finitely axiomatized, sequential theory. For every x ∈ R in the standard model, one has S sststile n^ O(1) Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) if and only if EA vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) . We expect the hardness direction of bf KH to extend to sound computably axiomatized ambient theories, whose sufficiently long true randomness facts remain inaccessible by Chaitin incompleteness.

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: theoremHRCImpliesKH

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: thm:robustness
statement_text: Let U,U' be universal machines with Kolmogorov invariance constant c=c(U,U') , so that |K_U(x)-K_ U' (x)| ≤ c for every x . Fix d ≥ 3 and write R_U^ (d) :={x:K_U(x) ≥ |x|-d log |x|} . Then, for all sufficiently long x , \[ x ∈ R_U^ (d) Longrightarrow x ∈ R_ U' ^ (d+1) qquad and qquad x ∈ R_ U' ^ (d) Longrightarrow x ∈ R_U^ (d+1) . \] Consequently, the density estimates and conclusions depending only on those estimates are robust under changing the universal machine, after increasing the logarithmic-deficiency parameter and disregarding finitely many lengths.

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: def:simulation-game
title: Simulation game
statement_text: Let C_ fs be the class of sound, finitely axiomatized sequential theories extending S^1_2 , and let Φ be a family of true sentences. In the game G(Φ) , Nature selects S ∈ C_ fs ; the Theorist, seeing S , selects φ ∈ Φ . Nature wins the round if S sststile n^ O(1) Con _ S + φ (n) , and the Theorist wins if, for every constant c , Scenternot sststile n^c Con _ S + φ (n) . Exactly one player wins each round.

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: def:explanation
title: Explanation and hidden information
statement_text: A position (S,φ) is explained if EA vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + φ ; the EA -proof is the explanation, a certificate any third party can check without reference to the internals of S . Nature holds hidden information at (S,φ) if Nature wins at an unexplained position.

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: prop:explained-wins
title: Explained positions are Nature wins
statement_text: If S is finitely axiomatized and sequential and the position (S,φ) is explained, then Nature wins at (S,φ) , by the canonical strategy: the explanation yields an interpretation of S + φ in S , whose proof translation supplies the required bounded-consistency proofs.

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: thm:ph-density
statement_text: Assume bf SETH-K-PH . For every i ≥ 1 , let t_i be the time bound supplied by the assumption. Then: (Explicitness.) The predicate Q_i^ t_i is an explicit language in Π_ i+1 ^p \ P ^ Π_i^p . In particular, it witnesses Π_i^p ≠ Π_ i+1 ^p . (Density.) Its YES-set widehat R_i^ t_i has density at least 1 - n^ -d inside {0,1}^n . Thus almost every length- n string is a YES-instance. (Sparse-side localization.) Every polynomial-time Π_i^p -oracle machine that is correct on all of widehat R_i^ t_i for all sufficiently large n must err, for infinitely many n , on some string in the sparse complement overline widehat R_i^ t_i .

If a polynomial-time Turing machine M with oracle access to Π_i^p correctly decides Q_i^t , then, for every sufficiently long string x ∈ R_i ∩ widehat R_i^t , the theory T_i , rather than T_ i+1 , certifies that M accepts x and that this acceptance is correct for Q_i^t(x) .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: thm:liu-pass-main
title: Liu--Pass
statement_text: For every polynomial time bound t satisfying t(n) ≥ (1 + δ)n for some constant δ > 0 , one-way functions exist if and only if K^t is mildly hard on average over the uniform distribution: there is a polynomial p such that no probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm computes K^t(x) correctly on more than a 1 - 1/p(n) fraction of strings x ∈ {0,1}^n for all sufficiently large n .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: ass:avg-boundary-reflection-main
title: bf Average-Case Boundary Reflection
statement_text: There exist a computable polynomial time bound t , a polynomial N(n) , and a polynomial-time samplable ensemble D = {D_n} supported on R_t ∩ {0,1}^n such that both Pr _ x D_n [x ∈ R] and Pr _ x D_n [x ∈ R_t \ R] are bounded away from 0 uniformly in n , and such that the following reflection principle holds: if some probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm decides E_ S (x,N(n)) on x D_n with success probability 1 - o(1) , then for almost every x D_n with x ∈ R , one has EA + Con _ S vdash x ∈ R .

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
label: ass:boundary-calibration-main
title: bf Boundary Calibration
statement_text: The ensemble D , the threshold N(n) , and the time bound t are chosen so that two conditions hold. First, on D the boundary-exposure predicate E_ S ( · ,N(n)) tracks t -time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity up to a polynomial-time computable reindexing. Second, this correspondence bridges D to the uniform distribution on which Liu--Pass operates: any average-case algorithm computing K^ t over the uniform distribution on {0,1}^n that is strong enough to violate the Liu--Pass hardness condition yields, through the reindexing, a 1 - o(1) -success heuristic for E_ S ( · ,N(n)) on x D_n .

label: prop:dnp-payoff

statement_text: Suppose there is an efficient algorithm that has non-negligible advantage in solving LPN with n variables, t samples, and noise rate n^ -α for some constant α < 1 . Then, for any constant β > 0 such that α + β < 1 , and m = O(t^2n^ 2β ) , there are efficient algorithms algS and algD such that, for any A ∈ F _2^ m × n , either algS can decode the code generated by A from random noise of rate n^ -(α+β) , or algD can distinguish noisy codewords of the dual of this code from random for noise rate n^β/m .

statement_text: lemma certifyball [Certify] There is a randomized procedure that, given a set \(K ⊆ B(c,r)\) and parameters \(Δ,τ,δ ∈ (0,tfrac 13 )\), runs in time \[ O (frac d Δ^ 2 τ log (frac 2|K| δ ) · |K| ) \] and, with probability at least \(1-δ\), does one of the following: returns a point \(k^* ∈ B(c,r)\) such that \[ |B (k^*, sqrt 1-Δ^4 r ) ∩ K | ≥ Ω(Δ^2) · τ |K|, \] certifies that \(K\) is \((Δ',τ)\)-pseudo-random, where \(Δ'=Θ(Δ)\). We refer to this procedure as \(sc Certify _ Δ,τ,δ \).

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: lem:ps_randomification
statement_text: lemma partition [Performance guarantees of sc Partition , Cref alg:partition ] For any r_0 , Δ ≤ 1/3 and any dataset K ⊂ B(c, r) , |K| ≤ n , sc Partition produces a decomposition K of K K = sqcup_ i=1 ^ N K_i such that K_i ⊂ B_i = B(c_i, r_i) and at least one of the two holds: K_i is (B_i, Δ, τ) -pseudo-random. r_i < r_0 . The algorithm is successful with probability at least 1 - frac 1 n^2 , has runtime O (frac d Δ^ 4 τ^2 · |K| log (n ) · frac log (r/r_0) Δ^4 ) and outputs a partition of size at most qty (frac log |K| Δ^2 · τ )^ Oqty (frac log frac r r_0 Δ^4 )

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: lem:ps_rand_coreset
title: Coresets for pseudo-random datasets
statement_text: Assume that K' is (B(c', r'), Δ, τ) -pseudo-random, r' ≤ r, τ ≤ frac 1 2 , |K'| ≤ n . Then there is a randomized procedure that runs in time O(|K'|^2 · d) and outputs tilde K ' ⊂ K' such that with high probability 1 - frac 1 poly (n) for any fixed |q|_2 ≤ r qty | exp (K', q) - 2 exp (tilde K ', q)| ≤ O (e^ r^2(1 + Δ) · log n · frac exp (K', q) |K'| ) .
bounds: O(|K'|^2 \cdot d); poly(n); exp(K', q); exp(\tilde{K}', q)

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: lem:small_r_coreset
title: Coresets for low radius datasets
statement_text: Assume that K' is contained in B(c', r') , r' ≤ r / 2 , |K'| ≤ n . Then there is a randomized procedure that runs in time O(|K'|^2 · d) and outputs tilde K ' ⊂ K' such that with probability 1 - frac 1 poly (n) for any fixed |q|_2 ≤ r qty | exp (K', q) - 2 exp (tilde K ', q)| ≤ O (e^ r^2 · log n · frac exp (K', q) |K'| ) .
bounds: O(|K'|^2 \cdot d); poly(n); exp(K', q); exp(\tilde{K}', q)

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: lem:fast_2_compress
statement_text: [Performance guarantees of Cref alg:fast_2_compress ] For any K ⊂ B(c, r) , |K| ≤ n , Δ ≥ (frac log log n log n )^ 1/4 , Cref alg:fast_2_compress outputs tilde K ⊂ K , weight function w_x ∈ {1, 2} |tilde K | ≤ 3|K|/4 such that with high probability 1 - frac 1 poly (n) for any fixed |q|_2 ≤ r |exp (K, q) - exp (tilde K , w, q) | ≤ O (e^ r^2(1 + Δ) · qty (frac log |K| Δ^2 )^ Oqty (Δ^ -4 ) · log n · frac exp (K, q) |K| ), where exp (tilde K , w, q) coloneqq Σ _ x ∈ tilde K w_x e^ le x, qrangle is the weighted KDE. The runtime of Cref alg:fast_2_compress is \[O (max {|K|^2d, frac d Δ^ 4 |K| log n · frac 1 Δ^4 } )\] and the probability of success is 1 - frac 1 poly (n) .

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: lem:merge-reduce-w
title: Weighted Merge-and-Reduce
statement_text: Let A be a black-box offline algorithm which takes as input a dataset K ⊂ B(0,r) , |K| ≤ n , and returns widetilde K ⊂ K , |widetilde K | ≤ 3|K|/4 , weight function α_x ∈ {1, 2} such that with probability 1 - frac 1 poly n , for any fixed q ∈ B(0, r) , |exp (K, q) - exp (tilde K , α, q) | ≤ O (e^ r^2(1 + o(1)) · n^ o(1) · frac exp (K, q) |K| ). Let T(m) denote the runtime A on inputs of size m . Assume that the space complexity of A is O(m) . Algorithm A can be adapted to process K as a stream. At every step j of the stream, it maintains a weighted coreset C_j of the j first elements of the stream K_j . Let w_x^j denote the weight of a point x ∈ C_j and w^j -- the weight function. We have with probability 1-frac 1 poly (n) , for any fixed q ∈ U and desired error ε ∈ (0, 1) , \[ | exp (K_j,q)-exp (C_j, w^j, q) | ≤ ε · exp (K_j, q). \] The size of the coreset, runtime and memory are defined in terms of the it block size of the algorithm b \[ |C_j| ≤ O (b log ^2 (frac |K_j| b ) ), quad runtime = O (T(b) · log ^2 (frac |K_j| b ) ), quad space = O (b log ^2 (frac |K_j| b ) ), \] and the block size b is defined by the desired error ε \[ b = frac e^ r^2(1 + o(1)) · n^ o(1) ε . \]

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: lem:reduction_big_r
statement_text: Let S_ n, d, r, ε denote a deterministic upper bound on the space, measured in bits, of a (randomized) data structure for the Streaming KDE problem with parameters n, d, r, ε and a failure probability 1/100 . Assume that d = ω( log n), r^2 = Θ( log n) , n < frac exp (r^2 p 1 - C sqrt frac log n d ) 16 ε for some constant C , there exists a communication protocol with a message size S_ n, d, r, ε + o(n) which solves the tt INDEX _ 2n, n problem with probability at least 9/10 .

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: lem:taylor_embed_memory
statement_text: Let t < d . There exist embeddings ψ_A, ψ_B such that \[ abs l le Σ _ k ∈ K_ x ψ_A(k), ψ_B(q) r rangle - exp _ ≤ t (K_ x , q) ≤ ε exp (K_ x , q), \] and that Σ _ k ∈ K_ x ψ_A(k) can be stored in O(frac (d+t)^t t! log ^2 n) bits of space.

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: lem:signal_bound
statement_text: For any t < r^2 and any k_j from a sphere of radius r , we have exp _ >t (k_j, k_j) ≥ frac 1 2 e^ r^2 .

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: lem:variance_bound
statement_text: For any t > ( log n)^ 1 - o(1) , any fixed k_j from a sphere of radius r , and for uniformly random i.i.d. draws of v_1, ... , v_n from a sphere of radius r , we have bf Var normalfont llbrack exp _ >t ({v_1, ... , v_n}, k_j) rrbrack = Oqty (nfrac (2r)^ 4t d^t t! ).

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: th:const_r_ub_lb_attn
title: Formal version of Cref remark:const_r_attn
statement_text: Assume that r = log ^ o(1) n , log n ≤ d ≤ log ^a n for some constant a > 1 and n^ -100 < ε < n^ -c for any constant c > 0 . Then the Attention problem can be solved using tilde O qty (qty (frac 1 ε )^ 1 - frac 1 a + o(1) ) memory. Furthermore, this bound is tight for any d ≥ log ^a n , a > 2 , i.e. there is a tilde Ω qty (min qty n, qty (frac 1 ε )^ 1 - frac 1 a - o(1) ) lower bound for the streaming space complexity.

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: th:big_r_ub_lb_attn
title: Formal version of Cref remark:big_r_attn
statement_text: Assume that r^2 = Ω( log n) , i.e. e^ r^2 = n^ Ω(1) . Then the Attention problem can be solved using tilde O qty (frac e^ r^2(1 + o(1)) ε ) memory. Furthermore, this bound is almost tight for any d = ( log n)^ 1 + Ω(1) and r^2 < frac log n 2 , i.e. there is a tilde Ω qty (min qty n, frac e^ r^2(1 - o(1)) ε ) lower bound for streaming space complexity.

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: def:weighted-kde
title: Weighted Softmax KDE problem
statement_text: The algorithm receives key-weight pairs (k_1, w(k_1)) ... , (k_n, w(k_n)) ∈ R ^d × R in a stream and at every point j = 1, ... , n , given any fixed q ∈ R ^d , outputs an estimate widehat exp (K_ j , w_j, q) of exp (K_ j , w_j, q) that satisfies |widehat exp (K_ j , w_j, q) - exp (K_ j , w_j, q)| ≤ ε · exp (K_ j , q) with probability at least 1-δ for some δ ∈ (0, 1) for any fixed query q . Here K_ j =(k_1, ... , k_ j ) is the sequence of keys received by time j , w_ j =(w(k_1), ... , w(k_ j )) is the sequence of weights received by time j , |w(k)| ≤ 1 for all k ∈ K , and exp (K, w, q) := Σ _ k ∈ K w(k) exp (k, q).
bounds: exp(K_{j}, w_j, q); exp(K_{j}, q); exp(K, w, q); exp(k, q)

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: lem:weighted_embed_memory
title: Weighted version of Cref lem:embed_memory
statement_text: Let γ(k, q) := Σ _ l = 0 ^ t a_l \<k, q>^l for some t and a_l . Then there exist embeddings ψ_1, ψ_2 such that for any K ⊂ R ^d with |k|_2 ≤ r for all k ∈ K , any q ∈ R ^d with |q|_2 ≤ r , and any weights {w(k)}_ k ∈ K with |w(k)| ≤ 1 for all k ∈ K , we guarantee \[qty | l le Σ _ k ∈ K w(k) ψ_1(k), ψ_2(q) r rangle - Σ _ k ∈ K w(k)γ(k, q)| < δ,\] and the weighted aggregate Σ _ k ∈ K w(k)ψ_1(k) can be stored in O l(frac (d+t)^ t t! log frac |K| · (d+t)^ t · max _l |a_l| · max {r, 1}^t δ r) bits of space.

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: lem:weighted_streaming_coreset
title: Weighted version of Cref lem:simple_coreset , specialized to γ = exp
statement_text: Let U × V ⊂ R ^d × R ^d be a predefined subset of the domain. There is a randomized algorithm sc BaseCompress ' which receives as inputs K ⊂ U and any weights {w(k)}_ k ∈ K with |w(k)| ≤ 1 . sc BaseCompress '(K, {w(k)}_ k ∈ K ) outputs widetilde K ⊂ K such that |widetilde K | ≤ |K|/2 and for any q ∈ V , with probability 1 - δ , \[ | exp (K, w, q) - 2 exp (widetilde K , w, q) | ≤ O ( sqrt max _ u ∈ U exp (u, u) · max _ v ∈ V exp (v, v) · log (|K|/δ) ).\] sc BaseCompress '(K,w) runs in O(|K|^2 · T) time, where T is the maximum time to access exp (k,q) .
bounds: exp(K, w, q); exp(\widetilde{K}, w, q); exp(u, u); exp(v, v); O(|K|^2 \cdot T); exp(k,q)

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
statement_text: Assume that r = log ^ o(1) n , log n ≤ d ≤ log ^a n for some constant a > 1 and ε < n^ -c for any constant c > 0 . The Weighted Softmax KDE problem (cref def:weighted-kde ) can be solved using tilde O qty (qty (frac 1 ε )^ 1 - frac 1 a + o(1) ) memory. If, on the other hand, r^2 = Ω( log n) , equivalently e^ r^2 = n^ Ω(1) , then the Weighted Softmax KDE problem can be solved using tilde O qty (frac e^ r^2(1 + o(1)) ε ) memory.

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: l:tokde
statement_text: If there exists a streaming algorithm that solves the weighted Softmax KDE problem (cref def:weighted-kde ) with parameters n, d, ε , r using S(n, d, ε , r) space, then there exists a streaming algorithm that solves the Attention problem (cref def:streaming-attn ) with parameters n, d, tilde O ( ε ), r using tilde O (S(n, d, ε , r)) space.

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: def:random-kde-instance
title: Random KDE Instance
statement_text: Let x ∈ {0,1}^ 2n be a binary vector with exactly n ones. Let K ⊂ R ^d be a set of 2n points drawn i.i.d.\ from a rotationally invariant distribution, independently of x . Let K_ x be the set of points indexed by the ones of x . A random KDE instance is an instance of the streaming KDE problem (cref def:streaming-kde ) in which the keys k_1, ... , k_n are the points in K and the query q is chosen from K . Vector q is chosen to be one of the keys k_i ∈ K ; the position in the dataset i is independent of the randomness of K .

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: l:fromkde
statement_text: Assume r^2 < frac log n 2 . If there exists a streaming algorithm that solves the attention problem (cref def:streaming-attn ) with parameters 2n, d, ε , r using S(2n, d, ε , r) space, then there exists a streaming algorithm that solves the streaming KDE problem on random instances (cref def:random-kde-instance ) with parameters n, d, ε ', r using S(2n, d, ε , r) space, where ε ' = ε · O (e^ O(r^2 sqrt frac log n d ) ) .

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
label: lemma:certify
title: , Lemma 58
statement_text: There is a randomized procedure that, given a set K ⊆ S^ d-1 and parameters Δ,τ,δ ∈ (0,tfrac 13 ) , runs in time \[ O (frac d Δ^ 2 τ log (frac 2|K| δ ) · |K| ) \] and, with probability at least 1-δ , does one of the following: returns a point k^* ∈ S^ d-1 such that \[ |B (k^*, sqrt 2(1 - Δ^2) ) ∩ K | ≥ Ω(Δ^2) · τ |K| \] or certifies that the set K is (Δ',τ) -pseudo-random, where Δ' = Θ(Δ) .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: obs1
statement_text: Any vertex v ∈ V(G) \ V(C) is adjacent to at most two vertices on V(C) , and these neighbors must be non-consecutive.

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: AdjacencyX_1
statement_text: Let X_1,Y_1 ∈ {A_1,B_1,C_1,D_1,E_1 } . Each X_1 is independent. Furthermore, X_1 is complete to Y_1 if X_1 and Y_1 are not consecutive, otherwise, X_1 and Y_1 are independent.

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
title: Two neighbors
statement_text: Let X_2 ⊆ V(G) be the set of vertices having exactly two non-consecutive neighbors on the cycle: A_2 : adjacent to {b, e} , B_2 : adjacent to {a, c} , C_2 : adjacent to {b, d} , D_2 : adjacent to {c, e} , E_2 : adjacent to {d, a} .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
title: Zero neighbor vertices
statement_text: Let X_0 ⊆ V(G) be the set of vertices at distance 2 from V(C) . A_0 is a set of vertices adjacent to A_2 , and similarly we define B_0,C_0,D_0,E_0 . Note that every vertex x of distance two from C is not adjacent to any vertex in A_1 ∪ B_1 ∪ C_1 ∪ D_1 ∪ E_1 , which will be proved later.

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: lem:distance-2
title: Distance Lemma
statement_text: When G is connected then every vertex v ∈ V(G) is at distance at most 2 from C .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: X1-X2-dichotomy
title: Layer 1 and Layer 2 Dichotomy
statement_text: If none of X_1, X_2, Y_1 is empty, where X_1 and Y_1 are not consecutive (i.e. (X_1,X_2,Y_1)=(A_1,A_2,C_1) then X_2=X^1_2 ∪ X^2_2 so that X^2_2 is complete to X_1 and independent from Y_1 , and X^1_2 is complete to Y_1 and independent from X_1 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: A1~A2--B2
statement_text: Suppose X_1,X_2 and Y_2 are not empty where X_2 and Y_2 are consecutive. Let X^2_2 be a subset of X_2 with neighbors in X_1 . Then X^2_2 is complete to Y_2 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: A1!~A2--B1!~B2--C1
statement_text: Suppose X_1, X_2, Y_1, Y_2, Z_1 are non-empty where X_1 and X_2 are independent, Y_1 and Y_2 are independent, and Z_1 is not next to X_1, Y_1 . Then X_2 and Y_2 are independent.

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: B0!~A1
statement_text: Every vertex x of distance two from C is not adjacent to any vertex in A_1 ∪ B_1 ∪ C_1 ∪ D_1 ∪ E_1 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: 2-disjoint-cycle
statement_text: Let G be a connected (P_6, C_3) -free graph. If G contains two vertex-disjoint induced 5-cycles C^1 and C^2 , then there exists at least one edge with one endpoint in V(C^1) and the other in V(C^2) .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: A1-C2
statement_text: Suppose X_1 and Y_2 are not empty where X_1,Y_1 are not consecutive (i.e. A_1 and C_2 are not empty or A_1 and D_2 are not empty). Then for every two vertices x_1,x'_1 ∈ X_1 , N(x_1) ∩ Y_2 = N(x'_1) ∩ Y_2 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: A1~C2_2
statement_text: Suppose X_1 and Y_2 are not empty where X_1 and Y_1 are not consecutive (e.g. A_1 and C_2 ). Then Y_2= Y^1_2 ∪ Y^2_2 so that X_1 and Y_2^2 forms a clique and X_1 ∪ Y^1_2 is independent.

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: A1-D2-C2
statement_text: Suppose X_1,Y_2,Z_2 (say A_1,D_2,C_2) are not empty where X_1 is not consecutive with Y_1 and not consecutive with Z_1 ( Y_1,Z_1 consecutive). Then Y_2=Y^2_2 ∪ Y^1_2 , and Z_2=Z^1_2 ∪ Z^2_2 so that : X_1 is complete to Y^2_2 and Z^2_2 . X_1 is independent of Y^1_2 and Z^1_2 . Z^1_2 and Y^2_2 form a complete bipartite graph. Y^1_2 and Z^2_2 form a complete bipartite graph.

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: A0-A2-B2
statement_text: If X_0 , X_2 , and Y_2 ( X_2,Y_2 are consecutive) are not empty then the following hold. For every two vertices a_0,a'_0 ∈ X_0 with a common neighbor in X_2 , N(a_0) ∩ Y_2 = N(a'_0) ∩ Y_2 . For every two vertices a_0,a'_0 ∈ X_0 with a common neighbor in Y_2 , N(a_0) ∩ X_2 = N(a'_0) ∩ X_2 . For every two vertices a_2,a'_2 ∈ X_2 with a common neighbor in X_0 , N(a_2) ∩ Y_2 = N(a'_2) ∩ Y_2 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: chain-switch
statement_text: Let a_1, a_2 ∈ V_j and b_1, b_2 ∈ V_ j+1 . Suppose that a_1b_1 ∈ E(H) , a_2b_2 ∈ E(H) , and b_1a_2 ∈ E(H) , but a_1b_2 ∉ E(H) (a `Z' shape). Then: N(b_2) ∩ V_ j+2 ⊆ N(b_1) ∩ V_ j+2 , N(a_1) ∩ V_ j-1 ⊆ N(a_2) ∩ V_ j-1 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: 2K2
statement_text: Let a_1, a_2 ∈ V_j and b_1, b_2 ∈ V_ j+1 . Suppose a_1b_1 ∈ E(H) and a_2b_2 ∈ E(H) form an induced 2K_2 (i.e., a_1b_2 ∉ E(H) and a_2b_1 ∉ E(H) ). Then \[ N(a_1) ∩ V_ j-1 =N(a_2) ∩ V_ j-1 qquad and qquad N(b_1) ∩ V_ j+2 =N(b_2) ∩ V_ j+2 . \]

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: lem:alternate-chain
statement_text: Suppose H_j , H_ j+1 , and H_ j+2 are proper chain graphs with alternating inclusion directions ( L → R , R → L , and L → R respectively). Then the adjacent bipartite graphs H_ j-1 and H_ j+3 must be complete bipartite graphs.

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: disconnected
statement_text: Suppose H_j is not connected. Then H_ j-1 and H_ j+1 are both complete bipartite graphs.

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: 2K2-structure
statement_text: Suppose H_j is connected and contains two independent edges a_1b_1 and a_2b_2 . Then H_j is partitioned into A_1, A_2, A_3 where A_1 and A_2 are connected and contain a_1b_1 and a_2b_2 (respectively), and A_1 and A_2 are independent. A_3 is complete to both A_1 and A_2 . Furthermore, N(A_1) ∩ V_ j-1 = N(A_2) ∩ V_ j-1 ⊆ N(A_3) ∩ V_ j-1 and N(A_1) ∩ V_ j+2 = N(A_2) ∩ V_ j+2 ⊆ N(A_3) ∩ V_ j+2 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: OCT-chain-chain-chain
statement_text: Let H_j, H_ j+1 , H_ j+2 be chain graphs. Suppose X is a set of vertices from V_ j ∪ V_ j+1 ∪ V_ j+2 such that H \ X is bipartite, i.e. X is an OCT. Then X is a vertex cover for H[V_ j ∪ V_ j+1 ] or X is a vertex cover for H[V_ j+1 ∪ V_ j+2 ] .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: lem:OCT-2K2
statement_text: Let H_ j = H[V_j ∪ V_ j+1 ] be connected and contain an induced 2K_2 . Suppose X is a minimum OCT for G containing vertices from V_ j-1 , V_ j , V_ j+1 , and V_ j+2 . Then X must contain a vertex cover for H_ j-1 , H_j , or H_ j+1 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: OCT-independent
statement_text: Let H_ j have more than one connected component. Suppose X is a minimum OCT containing vertices from V_ j-1 , V_ j , V_ j+1 , V_ j+2 . Then X must contain a vertex cover in H_ j-1 or in H_j or in H_ j+1 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: tm:ring-cut
title: Bottleneck Cut
statement_text: Let H be a (P_6, C_3) -free graph consisting of a ring of 5 vertex sets V_1, ... , V_5 where every vertex lies on a 5-cycle. The size of the Minimum Odd Cycle Transversal of H is equal to the minimum size of a Vertex Cover among the five bipartite subgraphs induced by consecutive sets (V_i, V_ i+1 ) . \[ OCT(H) = min _ i=1 ^5 { τ(H[V_i ∪ V_ i+1 ]) } \] where τ(G) denotes the vertex cover number.

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: lem:mvc-local
title: Local MVC optimality
statement_text: Let W_r=(Δ_1, ... ,Δ_5) be a (cleaned) 5 -ring instance and let H=G[Δ_1 ∪ ... ∪ Δ_5] . If S is a minimum OCT of H and S ∩ (Δ_1 ∪ Δ_2) ≠ ∅ , then there exists a minimum OCT S' of H such that S' ∩ (Δ_1 ∪ Δ_2) is a minimum vertex cover of the bipartite graph H[Δ_1 ∪ Δ_2] .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: lem:ring-extraction
title: Ring extraction
statement_text: If G_ S contains a 5 -cycle, then after at most a constant number of refinements we obtain a cleaned 5 -ring W=(Δ_1, ... ,Δ_5) such that H=G[Δ_1 ∪ ... ∪ Δ_5] contains an induced C_5 and every vertex of H lies on an induced C_5 in H .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: lem:safe-branching
title: Safe branching
statement_text: Algorithm 1 is complete under its preference rule: for every instance G , at least one root-to-leaf branch explored by the algorithm is consistent with an optimal OCT of G .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: thm:algo-P6
statement_text: Algorithm 1 runs in polynomial time and outputs a minimum odd cycle transversal of a (P_6,C_3) -free graph G .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
label: thm:pk-approx
statement_text: Let k ≥ 6 be an integer. There is a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a P_k -free graph G , outputs an OCT, S such that |S| ≤ (k-3) · OPT (G) when k is even and |S| ≤ (k-2) · OPT (G) when k is odd. Here OPT (G) denotes the size of a minimum OCT of G .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs

Suppose the simulator is exact, that is P = P^star , and let q_t be as in cref eq:relaxation-mgf-strategy . Then, for any history S_ 1:t-1 , we have \[ E _ X_t P_t^star ( · mid X_ 1:t-1 ) exp ( sup _ Y_t [η E _ hat Y_t q_t m 1 { hat Y_t ≠ Y_t} + η Rel (S_ 1:t ) ] ) ≤ exp ( η Rel (S_ 1:t-1 ) ). \] Thus, conditioned on S_ 1:t-1 , E _ X_t sup _ Y_t Φ_t ≤ Φ_ t-1 , and therefore, {Φ_t}_ t ≤ T is a supermartingale.

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lemma:idealized-regret
statement_text: lemma IdealizedRegret Let cF be a VC dimension d class. Then, for every η > 0 , an algorithm that plays according to cref eq:relaxation-mgf-strategy achieves the following expected regret bound in the agnostic setting: \[ E _ P^star Reg (cF ,T) lesssim sqrt dT + frac 1 η KL dvr * P^star P + η T. \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: prop:closed-form
statement_text: proposition ClosedFormStrategy For a history S_ 1:t and a covariate X_t , let G _ y (W^t) := sup _ f ∈ cF [ Σ _ s=t+1 ^T ε_s frac 2f(X_s)-1 2 - L_ t-1 (f) - m 1 {f(X_t) ≠ y} ]. Then, q_t as in cref eq:relaxation-mgf-strategy can be written as \[ q_t(S_ 1:t-1 , X_t) = frac 1 2 + frac 1 2η log (frac E exp (η G _ 1 (W^t)) E exp (η G _ 0 (W^t)) ) \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lemma:mse-bound
statement_text: lemma MSEBound For an arbitrary history S_ 1:t-1 , an arbitrary covariate X_t , and η ≤ 1 , we have \[ E [(hat q_t - q_t)^2 ] lesssim frac v_t N , quad where quad v_t := max _ y ∈ {0,1} frac E exp (2η G _ y (W^t)) ( E exp (η G _ y (W^t)) )^2 , \] is the normalized variance of the exponential moment.

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lemma:v-eta
statement_text: lemma VEtaBound For an arbitrary history S_ 1:t-1 , an arbitrary covariate X_t , and η ≤ 1 , we have \[ v_t ≤ exp (2η) E exp (2η sup _ f Σ _ s= t+1 ^T ε_s frac 2f(X_s) - 1 2 ) lesssim exp (O(η sqrt dT + η^2 T) ). \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lemma:reg-mgf-intermediate
statement_text: lemma RegMGFIntermediate Let cF be a VC dimension d class. Then, an algorithm that plays according to cref eq:plug-in with N samples per step and inverse temperature η achieves the following regret bound E _ P^star Reg (cF ,T) lesssim sqrt dT + η T + frac 1 η KL dvr * P^star P + T sqrt frac exp (O(η sqrt dT + η^2 T)) N .

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: cor:sim-families
statement_text: corollary LearnabilitySublinearKL Let cP be a family of processes with cR (cP ) ≤ o(T) , and cF a bounded VC dimension class. Then, there exists a (possibly inefficient) algorithm that achieves sublinear agnostic regret for every P^star ∈ cP . Moreover, for every D ∈ bbN , there exists cP with cR (cP ) ≤ D ∧ T and a VC class of dimension 1 , such that any algorithm suffers regret Ω(D ∧ T) even in the realizable setting.

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
title: Time-bounded samplable distribution
statement_text: Let p colon N → N be a time bound. Then, distribution P ∈ Δ(Σ^ ∞ ) is p -time samplable iff there exists a program π such that, for every t ≥ 1 and s Unif ({0,1}^ p(t) ) , we have U^ p(t) (π, 1^ t \# s) P_ 1:t . For a distribution P ∈ Δ(Σ^ ∞ ) , let \[ K^p(P) = min {|π| colon U^ p(t) (π, 1^ t \# s) P_ 1:t for every t ≥ 1, where s Unif ({0,1}^ p(t) ) } \] be the (time-bounded) Kolmogorov complexity of P if P is p -time samplable.

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: thm:universal-dist
title: Universal samplable distribution
statement_text: theorem UniversalDist Let p colon N → N be a time-constructible bound. There exists a time bound p'(t) = poly (p(t)) and a sequence of measures {μ^t}_ t ≥ 1 , with each μ^t ∈ Δ (Σ^*) samplable in time p'(t) that satisfy the following. For any p -time samplable distribution P and any x ∈ cX ^t we have \[ log frac P_ 1:t (le x rangle ) μ^t(le xrangle ) ≤ K^p(P) + 2 log K^p(P) + O(1). \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: thm:samplable-nature
statement_text: theorem SamplableNature Suppose the distribution P^star of nature is p -time samplable (as per Cref def:samplable ). Let cF be any class of VC dimension d . Then, there exists an algorithm that, given access to a realizable ERM oracle w.r.t. cF , runs in time poly (T^d, p(T)) and for any f^star ∈ cF , achieves regret \[ E Reg (cF , T ) lesssim d log (T) + d · 2^ K^p(P^star ) + 2 log K^p(P^star ) . \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: thm:lds
statement_text: theorem ThmLDS Let cF be a class of VC dimension d , and let R, B ≥ 1 and σ > 0 be arbitrary. There is a poly (n, T) -time algorithm that, given access to an agnostic ERM oracle for cF , the noise scale σ , and the magnitude bound B , achieves expected regret \[ E Reg (cF , T) lesssim sqrt dT (1 + sqrt n^3 log (nBT(R/σ + 1) ) ) \] in the agnostic setting, simultaneously for every P^star = P^ A^star with A^star ∈ Θ satisfying ρ(A^star ) ≤ 1 and initial state X_0 ∈ cB (0,R) .

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: thm:glauber
statement_text: theorem ThmGlauber Let cF be a class of VC dimension d , and let B ≥ 1 . There is a poly (n, T, B) -time algorithm that, given access to an agnostic ERM oracle for cF , achieves expected regret \[ E Reg (cF , T) lesssim sqrt dT · (1 + sqrt n^2 log (BTn) ) \] in the agnostic setting, simultaneously for every P^star = P^ θ^star with θ^star ∈ Θ and initial state X_0 ∈ {0,1}^n .

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: def:vc
title: VC dimension
statement_text: For a binary class cF ⊂ {0,1}^ cX , the VC dimension of cF is the largest integer d for which there exists a subset {x_1, ... ,x_d} ⊂ cX such that, for any labels y_1, ... ,y_d ∈ {0,1} , there exists f ∈ cF such that f(x_t) = y_t for every t ∈ [d] .

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lemma:sauer-shelah
title: Sauer--Shelah Lemma
statement_text: For a binary class cF with VC dimension d , and any finite set S ⊂ cX , the number of distinct labelings of S by functions in cF is at most \[ Σ _ i=0 ^d binom |S| i ≤ (frac e |S| d )^d. \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
title: Littlestone Dimension
statement_text: Let cF ⊂ {0,1}^cX be a binary class of functions. The Littlestone dimension is the largest integer d such that the following holds. There exists a tree x such that, for any choice of signs ε_1, ... ,ε_d ∈ {pm 1} there exists a function f ∈ cF such that \[ f(x_t(ε_ 1 , ... ,ε_ t-1 )) = frac ε_t + 1 2 , \] for every t ∈ [d] .

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: prop:littlestone-hardness
statement_text: Let cF ⊂ {0,1}^cX be a class of infinite Littlestone dimension, and let x be a depth- T Littlestone tree. Consider nature's strategy that first samples ε_t Unif ({pm 1}) independently for each t ∈ [T] . Then, at step t ∈ [T] , the nature presents the learner with X_t = x_t(ε_1, ... ,ε_ t-1 ) labeled by Y_t := (ε_t + 1)/2 . Then, any learner suffers T/2 regret in this setting.

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: Let x be a depth- T tree. We say that a function f is consistent with the path (ε_1, ... ,ε_T) in x iff \[ f(x_t(ε_1, ... ,ε_ t-1 )) = frac ε_t + 1 2 . \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lemma:mult-pinkser
statement_text: For any P, Q ∈ Δ([0,1]) , we have \[ E _ Q X ≤ 3 E _P X + 4 KL dvr * P Q . \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lemma:kl-markov
statement_text: For any P,Q , λ > e we have \[ P_ P [frac d P d Q > λ ] ≤ frac KL dvr * P Q log (λ/e) \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lemma:log-plus
statement_text: For any P,Q we have \[ E _ P log ^+ (frac d P d Q ) ≤ KL dvr * P Q + 1. \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lemma:price-of-sampling
statement_text: Let cF _d be the class as defined in cref eq:d-dim-thresholds . For any N ∈ N and for any learning algorithm that draws at most N unconditional samples from P^star , there exists a choice of P^star and f^star ∈ cF _d such that \[ E Reg (cF _d, T) gtrsim frac T (d ∧ N) N . \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: Let cF _1 be as in cref eq:d-dim-thresholds . For every D ∈ N , there exist a family cP _D of distributions over cX ^T and a simulator P such that: max _ P^star ∈ cP _D KL dvr * P^star P ≤ D ∧ T . For any learning algorithm, even one granted full knowledge of P , there exists P^star ∈ cP _D and a labeling f^star ∈ cF _1 for which \[ E Reg (cF _1, T) ≥ frac D ∧ T 2 . \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lemma:kl-sampling-lb
statement_text: Let cF _1 be as in cref eq:d-dim-thresholds . For any N ≥ 2 , D ∈ N , and for any learning algorithm that draws at most N unconditional samples from P , there exists a choice of (P, P^star ) with KL dvr * P^star P ≤ D and f^star ∈ cF _1 such that \[ E Reg (cF _1, T) gtrsim T ( frac D log (N) ∧ 1 ) \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lem:talg-regret
statement_text: Let tilde Y_1, ... , tilde Y_T denote the predictions of widetilde Alg . Then it holds that E [ Σ _ t=1 ^T m 1 { tilde Y_t ≠ Y_t } ] = frac T 2 , where the expectation is over the randomness of widetilde Alg and the choice of cF .

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lem:talg-alg
statement_text: With probability at least 1-6J^ 3/2 TN/K^ 1/4 - N/M (over the execution of Alg , widetilde Alg , and the choice of cF ), the execution of Alg is identical to that of widetilde Alg .

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lem:close-uniform
statement_text: Fix any subset cK ⊂ [K] and step j ∈ [J] , and set ε= frac 2j |cK | K . Then with probability at least 1- sqrt ε over the execution of widetilde Alg up to step j and the choice of cF , the distribution of the tuple of functions (h_k)_ k ∈ cK conditioned on scrF \^j is sqrt ε -close to uniform in total variation distance.

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: prop:approx-agnostic-lb
statement_text: proposition ApproxAgnosticLB Consider the class cF of thresholds on the unit interval [0,1] . Then, for any D ∈ [T] , and for any algorithm, there exists a pair (P, P^star ) such that KL dvr * P^star P = D , and the algorithm suffers regret ≥ sqrt D T in the agnostic setting.

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lemma:lds-compressor
statement_text: Let P be as defined in cref eq:universal-dist-lds . Then, for any A^star ∈ Θ with ρ(A^star ) ≤ 1 and X_0 ∈ cB (0, R) , we have \[ KL dvr * P^ A^star ( · mid X_0) P( · mid X_0) ≤ O (n^3 log (nBT(R/σ + 1) ) ). \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lemma:matrix-power-growth
statement_text: For any A ∈ bbR ^ n × n with ρ(A) ≤ 1 and any s ≥ 1 , \[ | A^s |_ op ≤ n · ( | A |_ op + 1)^ n-1 · s^ n-1 . \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: prop:lds-cond-sampler
statement_text: For any X_0, X_ 1:t , exact conditional sampling from P( · mid X_ 1:t , X_0) , where P is as in cref lemma:lds-compressor , can be implemented in poly (n, T) time per sample.

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: lemma:glauber-compressor
statement_text: For any T ≥ 2 , θ^star ∈ Θ , and X_0 ∈ {0,1}^n , we have \[ KL dvr * P^ θ^star ( · mid X_0) P( · mid X_0) lesssim p log (BTn). \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: prop:glauber-cond-sampler
statement_text: For any X_0 ∈ {0,1}^n , conditional sampling from P( · mid I_ 1:t , X_ 1:t , X_0) , where P is as in cref lemma:glauber-compressor , can be implemented in poly (n, T, B, 1/δ) time per sample, to within total-variation error δ .

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: Consider any class cF with infinite Littlestone dimension, and consider the Littlestone tree of depth T . Let P^star be a distribution that samples a uniform path X in the Littlestone tree, and, for each t ≤ T-1 , set Y_t := 1 iff X_ t+1 is the right child of its parent (and sample Y_T randomly). This strategy of nature forces any learner to have ≥ T/2 regret.

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: assumption:adaptive-labels
statement_text: For every t ∈ [T] , the distribution X_ t+1:T mid (cH _t, Y_t, hat Y_t) is given by P^star ( · mid X_ 1:t ) .

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: Let cF be the class of thresholds on the [0,1] interval. For any N ≥ 1 , and for any learning algorithm that draws at most N unconditional samples, there exists a choice of a distribution P^star , a choice of realizable labels satisfying cref assumption:adaptive-labels such that \[ E [ Σ _ t=1 ^T m 1 {f^ star (X_t) ≠ hat y _t} - inf _ f ∈ cF Σ _ t=1 ^T m 1 {f^ star (X_t) ≠ f(X_t) } ] ≥ T/8. \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
label: thm:cond-oracle-eff-adaptive-labels
statement_text: Let cF be a class of VC dimension d . Suppose the labels satisfy cref assumption:adaptive-labels . Then, there exists an algorithm that, given access to an agnostic ERM oracle over cF and a conditional sampling oracle O ^ cond _ P , achieves expected regret bound: \[ E Reg (cF ,T) lesssim sqrt dT (1 + KL dvr * P^star P ) , \] in both realizable and agnostic settings. Moreover, the algorithm runs in poly (T) time.

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: def:noninteracting
title: Non‑interacting coalition
statement_text: A coalition C ⊆ N is non‑interacting if, for every i ∈ C , the payoff u_i does not depend on σ_ i' for any i' ∈ C \ {i} (equivalently, in a polymatrix game, C is an independent set of the interaction graph). For a non‑interacting coalition, u_i(y_i,σ_ -i ^t)=u_i(y_C,σ_ -C ^t) for all i ∈ C , so the aggregate deviation--regret R ^ y_C _ C coincides with the joint coalitional deviation--regret Σ _t Σ _ i ∈ C (u_i(y_C,σ_ -C ^t)-u_i(σ^t) ) in which the whole coalition deviates simultaneously.

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: def:edre
title: Static EDRE
statement_text: A profile σ^star is a static (ε) ‑EDRE if \[ max _ a_i u_i(a_i,σ^star _ -i ) \ ≤ \ u_i(σ^star )+ε quad for all i. \] A strict EDRE sets ε=0 .

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: def:dynamic-edre
title: Dynamic EDRE properties
statement_text: Fix L>0 and consider entropic MD with either: constant steps 0<η ≤ 1/L (Lyapunov monotonicity and selection to the fixed‑point set; when that set is a singleton, pointwise convergence holds for 0<η<1/L ), or diminishing steps η_t=η_0/ sqrt t with η_0>0 (deviation‑regret). We say that a static EDRE σ^star satisfies the dynamic properties if: bf (Deviation–regret) Under (B), for each fixed coalition C and fixed deviation y_C , from any interior initial condition (or under fixed exploration), for each horizon T ≥ 1 , with probability at least 1-δ , max _ 1 ≤ τ ≤ T \ R ^ y_C _ C (τ) &\ ≤ \ 2|C| sqrt 2Tln frac 4T δ [-1mm]&quad +\ sqrt T g[ frac 1 η_0 Σ _ i ∈ C D_ KL (y_iVert σ_i^1) + η_0 |C| g]. bf (MD selection / invariance) Under (A), for any interior start, \[ dist l(σ^ t , Fix ( MD _η) r)\ longrightarrow \ 0, qquad and we require σ^star ∈ Fix ( MD _η). \] If the fixed‑point set is a singleton, then for 0<η<1/L we have σ^t → σ^star .

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: prop:strict-edre-subset-ne
title: Strict EDRE ⟺ NE
statement_text: A profile is a strict EDRE if and only if it is a mixed Nash equilibrium.

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: lem:eq-iter2
statement_text: The game admits pure Nash equilibria (1,1) and (2,2) (both weak ), and (3,3) is a strict pure Nash equilibrium.

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: lem:sep-conv-iter2
title: Potential descent and fixed points
statement_text: Entropic MD on an L ‑smooth cost potential satisfies \[ Ψ(σ^ t+1 )-Ψ(σ^t) ≤ l(-tfrac 1 η +L r) D_ KL (σ^ t+1 Vert σ^t). \] Hence for 0<η ≤ 1/L , the potential Ψ(σ^t) is non‑increasing. If 0<η<1/L , then also Σ _ t D_ KL (σ^ t+1 Vert σ^t)< ∞ , so |σ^ t+1 -σ^ t |_1 → 0 and every ω –limit point of {σ^t} is a fixed point of the MD map. If the fixed‑point set is a singleton, convergence is pointwise for 0<η<1/L .

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: lem:sep-regret-iter2
title: Joint coalitional regret at a held profile
statement_text: Suppose play is held at the fixed point (2,2) for T rounds. The (interacting) coalition C={1,2} with fixed deviation y_C=(3,3) accrues joint coalitional deviation--regret Σ _t Σ _ i ∈ C (u_i(y_C,σ_ -C ^t)-u_i(σ^t) )=T , which exceeds the bound of Definition (i) for large T .

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: cor:sep-edre-iter2
title: Selection non‑uniqueness in the congestion example
statement_text: In the congestion game above, the MD fixed‑point set contains multiple pure points (e.g., (1,1) and (2,2) ; in fact (3,3) is also a NE). Unless the potential is strictly concave (it is not here), Definition (ii) yields set‑valued (Cesàro) selection rather than a singleton. Hence a given NE (e.g., (2,2) ) need not be the uniquely selected outcome from all interior initials; Nash equilibria need not coincide with EDRE under singleton‑selection.

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: lem:regret
title: High‑probability, all prefixes with diminishing steps
statement_text: Assume utilities in [0,1] . Let players run entropic mirror descent with steps η_t=η_0/ sqrt t for any η_0>0 . From any interior initial state ( min _aσ_i^1(a)>0 for all i ), for any fixed coalition C and deviation y_C , \[ max _ 1 ≤ τ ≤ T \ R ^ y_C _ C (τ) ≤ 2|C| sqrt 2Tln frac 4T δ + sqrt T g[ frac 1 η_0 Σ _ i ∈ C D_ KL (y_iVert σ_i^1) + η_0 |C| g] quad with probability 1-δ. \] The same bound holds under a fixed exploration mixture p_i^t=(1-γ)σ_i^t+γ u_i with γ>0 .

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: lem:tight
title: Order‑tightness of the template
statement_text: For every constant c<1 there is a sequence of payoff (gradient) vectors in [0,1] , realizable within a two‑player zero‑sum interaction, against which entropic MD with steps η_t=η_0/ sqrt t incurs unilateral deviation--regret at least c sqrt T with probability 1-δ for all large T . Hence the Θ( sqrt T) rate of Lemma cannot be improved in general by the OMD analysis.

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: def:exact-pot
title: Exact potential game
statement_text: A finite game admits an exact potential Φ if \[ u_i(a'_i,a_ -i )-u_i(a) = Φ(a'_i,a_ -i )-Φ(a) quad ∀ i,a_i',a. \]

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: def:strict-concave
title: Strict concavity
statement_text: A differentiable Φ on Δ(A) is strictly concave if Φ(λ x+(1-λ)y)> λΦ(x)+(1-λ)Φ(y) for all x ≠ y and λ ∈ (0,1) .

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: lem:uhc
title: Well‑defined proximal map
statement_text: Assume the payoff potential Φ is concave on Δ(A) and fix λ>0 . For each σ , the problem \[ T _λ(σ)= arg max _ σ' ∈ Δ(A) l[Φ(σ')-λ D_ KL (σ' |σ) r] \] has a unique maximizer (since -D_ KL ( · |σ) is strictly concave), hence T_λ is a single‑valued map. Moreover, T_λ is continuous by Berge's Maximum Theorem (strict concavity yields continuity of the argmax map).

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: lem:kakutani-to-NE
title: Interior proximal fixed point ⇒ unilateral optimality
statement_text: Let Γ be an exact‑potential game with concave multilinear extension Φ . If σ^star ∈ T _λ(σ^star ) for some λ>0 and σ^star lies in the relative interior of Δ(A) , then σ^star is a constrained stationary point of Φ on Δ(A) ; in particular, for every player i , all actions in supp (σ_i^star ) have equal payoff and no unilateral deviation yields a higher payoff, so EDRE(i) holds with ε=0 . For a boundary (e.g.\ pure) fixed point of MD _η , optimality is checked directly: a pure profile is a fixed point of the multiplicative‑weights map iff the played action is a best response, which is exactly the Nash condition.

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: thm:exist-edre
title: Existence
statement_text: Every finite exact‑potential game admits at least one profile satisfying Definition with ε=0 (a Nash equilibrium). Under the step‑size regimes in Definition , item (i) holds, and item (ii) holds relative to the fixed‑point set as stated therein. When that fixed‑point set is a singleton, EMD converges pointwise for 0<η<1/L .

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: thm:global-md
title: Global convergence of EMD
statement_text: With constant step 0<η ≤ 1/L and an interior initialization, EMD on an L ‑smooth cost potential Ψ satisfies \[ Ψ(σ^ t+1 )-Ψ(σ^ t )\ ≤ \ l(-tfrac 1 η +L r)D_ KL (σ^ t+1 |σ^ t ), \] so {Ψ(σ^ t )} is non‑increasing (strictly decreasing when η<1/L ). For 0<η<1/L , every ω –limit point of {σ^t} is a fixed point of the MD map, and dist (σ^t, Fix ( MD _η)) → 0 . If the fixed‑point set is a singleton, then σ^t converges to it. (Pure strategies are fixed points of the multiplicative‑weights map; from interior starts they are not attained in finite time but can arise as limits.)

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: cor:singleton-fp
title: Singleton fixed‑point set
statement_text: If Fix ( MD _η) is a singleton, then the EDRE selected by Definition (ii) is unique, and for 0<η<1/L the iterates converge to it from any interior initialization.

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: def:robust-edre
title: Robustly selected EDRE
statement_text: A static EDRE σ^star ∈ Fix ( MD _η) is robustly selected under constant‑step EMD ( 0<η<1/L ) if its basin B(σ^star )={σ^1 ∈ int Δ(A):\ σ^t → σ^star } has positive Lebesgue measure.

paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
label: prop:unstable-excluded
title: Linearly unstable equilibria are EDRE but not robustly selected
statement_text: Let σ^star be an interior fixed point of MD _η that is hyperbolic and linearly unstable ---the Jacobian D MD _η(σ^star ) on the tangent space of Δ(A) has spectral radius >1 . Then its basin B(σ^star ) has Lebesgue measure zero; hence σ^star is a static EDRE but is not robustly selected. Consequently, from Lebesgue‑almost‑every interior initialization the EMD limit (when it exists) is a linearly stable fixed point; in an exact‑potential game these are the local maximizers of the payoff potential Φ .

title: Period‑doubling bifurcation
statement_text: For the map , the interior equilibrium p^star =G_0/G_1 has multiplier \[ T_η'(p^star ) = 1-η G_1 p^star (1-p^star ), \] which decreases monotonically in η and equals -1 at the threshold \[ η_ PD = frac 2 G_1 p^star (1-p^star ) . \] Hence p^star is linearly stable for η<η_ PD and loses stability through a period‑doubling (flip) bifurcation at η=η_ PD , after which a stable 2 ‑cycle appears. This is a one‑dimensional codimension‑one bifurcation; it is not a Neimark--Sacker bifurcation (the state space is one‑dimensional, so there is no complex multiplier pair and no invariant circle).

Then the map T_η of possesses a period‑three orbit \[ x_1 xrightarrow T_η x_2 xrightarrow T_η x_3 xrightarrow T_η x_1, qquad x_1&=0.000197784073392 ... , x_2&=0.025773667425 ... , x_3&=0.674028548501 ... , \] with x_1<x_2<x_3 (verified: |T_η^3(x_1)-x_1|<10^ -30 and |T_η(x_1)-x_1|>2 × 10^ -2 , so the period is exactly three). title: Stationary effective Hamiltonian and hard window
statement_text: There is a round index t_0 and a window W =[t_0,t_1] such that, for t ∈ W , the per-round losses are (up to an additive constant) a fixed local operator, L(s)=H_star +o(1) for s ≤ t , so that the cumulative loss defines a stationary effective Hamiltonian H_ eff (t)=frac 1 t Σ _ s ≤ t L(s)=H_star +o(1), qquad β_ eff (t)=η t . Let A _ class be any randomized classical algorithm that, given only the classical description of the loss L(t) at some round t ∈ W with t ≥ t_0 , outputs in polynomial time a sample whose distribution is within total-variation distance τ<tfrac 12-ε_ prep of the distribution from which DQMW-Sample draws its round- t sample. Then the existence of such a polynomial-time A _ class would yield a polynomial-time classical sampler for the BCL distribution μ^star to within total-variation distance τ+ε_ prep <tfrac 12 . Under the standard hardness assumption that no such efficient classical sampler for μ^star exists (on pain of collapsing the polynomial hierarchy), no such classical algorithm A _ class can exist. Consequently, there is no efficient classical algorithm that can simulate the sampling step that supplies the loss feedback to the multiplicative-weights update of DQMW-Sample in the hard window W .
