Then the additional regret attributable to hardware noise satisfies Δ Regret _ noise (T) ≤ frac C δ γ_0 T, where C=C(d) depends on the Hilbert-space dimension d=2^n only through the norm-equivalence constant relating the trace norm to the loss functional [see below]; in particular C is dimension-free whenever the losses satisfy |L(t)|_ op ≤ 1 . Under the balanced schedule γ_0(T)=Θ( sqrt T ) , Δ Regret _ noise (T) = O l(δ sqrt T r), so the noise-induced regret is sublinear in T and DQMW-Sample remains asymptotically no-regret for any fixed δ>0 .

statement_text: A propositional proof system P is given by a polynomial-time algorithm V: {0,1}^* × {0,1}^* → {0,1} , known as its verifier, such that for every CNF formula F , \[ ∃ Πcolon V(F,Π) = 1 ⟺ F is unsatisfiable .\] Given two propositional proof systems P , Q , with verifiers V_P and V_Q , we say that P polynomially-simulates Q , written P ≥ _p Q , if there is a polynomial-time computable function f such that V_Q(F, Π) ⇒ V_P(F, f(F, Π)) for all F and Π .

statement_text: Let C_1, ... C_m, D be a collection of clauses. paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:reflection
statement_text: For a proof system P with verifier V , its reflection principle is the family of tautologies \[ Refl _ P,n,m,s (F,Π,x) := ¬ Proof _ n,m,s (F,Π) vee SAT _ n,m (F,x)\] where Proof _ n,m,s is a formula (using the definition of V_ n,m,s ) asserting that Π is a P -proof that F is a tautology, and SAT _ n,m is the CNF formula claiming that x is a satisfying assignment to F . This captures the soundness of the proof system P : it asserts that if Π is a P -proof of F then every assignment satisfies F . If the parameters n, m, s are clear from context, then we will suppress the subscripts and call the formula Refl _P . A Σ^q_1 -formula is a quantified boolean formula of the form ∃ vec y G(x, y) , where G is unquantified. The reflection principle for Σ^q_1 -formulas is defined similarly by changing SAT (F,x) to SAT _ Σ^q_1 (F,x) , asserting that F , a Σ^q_1 -formula, is satisfied by assignment x . The formula SAT _ Σ^q_1 (F,x) may itself be written as a Σ^q_1 -formula in the natural way. We will denote this version of reflection as Σ^q_1 - Refl _P .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: The proof system [EF, Resolution ] is defined as follows. If F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ ... ∧ C_m is an unsatisfiable CNF formula, then a refutation in [EF, Resolution ] of F is given by a pair (C, Π) , where C is an implicit encoding of a Resolution refutation of F , and Π is an Extended Frege proof that C is correctly encoded.

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: A relation R ⊆ { 0,1 } ^* × { 0,1 } ^* is Total , if for all x ∈ { 0,1 } ^* there is a y ∈ { 0,1 } ^* such that (x, y) ∈ R . Polynomially bounded , if there is a polynomial ell (n) such that for all (x, y) ∈ R , |y| ≤ ell (n) . An NP search problem is a polynomial-time computable, polynomially bounded relation R ⊆ { 0,1 } ^* × { 0,1 } ^* . The class of all total NP search problems is denoted TFNP .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:tfnp-cnf-encoding
statement_text: Let R ∈ TFNP and let n, ell be positive integers. Define V_ R, n, ell to be a polynomial-size circuit such that V_ R, n, ell (x, y) = R(x, y) . If the parameters n and ell are clear from context, then we will omit them and write V_R(x, y) .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:mapping-reduction
statement_text: Let R, S ∈ TFNP . A mapping reduction from R to S is given by two polynomial-time computable functions f and g such that for all x, y ∈ { 0,1 } ^* , \[S(f(x), y) ⇒ R(x, g(y)).\] If R is mapping reducible to S we write R ≤ _m S .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: The iterlong problem, also denoted iter , is defined as follows. For any positive integer n , let ell (n) = n^ O(1) be a polynomially-bounded input parameter. The input to the problem is a size parameter 1^n and a circuit S: { 0,1 } ^n × { 0,1 } ^ell → { 0,1 } ^ell of size polynomial in n . Given n and S , a string y ∈ { 0,1 } ^ell is a valid solution if either y = 0^ell , if S(x, 0^ell ) = 0^ell , or y ≠ 0^ell , if S(x, y) <_ lex y , or y ≠ 0^ell , if S(x, y) >_ lex y and S(x, S(x, y)) = S(x, y) . Above <_ lex denotes the usual lexicographic ordering on strings. The class of all search problems mapping reducible to iterlong is denoted by PLS .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: If F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ ... ∧ C_m is an unsatisfiable CNF formula, the false-clause search problem Search _F associated with F is the total relation \[ Search _F := { (x, i) ∈ {0,1}^n × [m]: C_i(x) = 0 }.\]

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: Let n be a positive integer. A black-box search problem is any total relation \[R^ dt _n ⊆ { 0,1 }^ n × O_n,\] where O_n is a polynomial-sized set of feasible solutions. The class TFNP ^ dt contains all sequences R^ dt = { R^ dt _n }_n of black-box search problems such that the following holds: there is a universal constant c such that for each input length n , and each o ∈ O_n , there is a O(( log n)^c) -depth decision tree T_o satisfying T_o(x) = R^ dt _n(x,o) .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:formulation
statement_text: Let S^ dt _m ⊆ {0,1}^m × O_S, R^ dt _n ⊆ {0,1}^n × O_S be black-box search problems. A decision-tree reduction from S^ dt _m to R^ dt _n is given by functions f = {f_i: { 0,1 } ^m → {0,1}}_ i ∈ [n] and g = {g_o: { 0,1 } ^n → O_S}_ o ∈ O_R each computable by decision trees T_ f_i , T_ g_o , such that for every x ∈ {0,1}^m and o ∈ O_R , (T_f(x), o) ∈ R^ dt ⇒ (x, T_ g_o (x)) ∈ S^ dt . where T_f(x) denotes the n -bit string obtained by evaluating T_ f_1 (x), ... ,T_ f_n (x) . The depth of the reduction is the maximum depth of any of the decision trees { T_ f_i }_i ∪ { T_ g_o }_o . The complexity of the reduction to be: \[ Σ _ i=1 ^n |T_ f_i | + Σ _ o ∈ O_S |T_ g_o |.\] We extend this definition to sequences as follows. If R ^ dt = {R^ dt _n} is a sequence of search problems, then R^ dt (S^ dt _m) is the minimum complexity of a reduction from S^ dt _m to any problem in R^ dt . If S^ dt = {S^ dt _m} is also a sequence of search problems, then we write S^ dt ≤ ^ dt _m R ^ dt if R ^ dt (S^ dt _m) is polynomially-bounded in m .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: Let N = 2^k be a positive integer. The problem iter _N^ dt is defined as follows. As input, for each element u ∈ [N] , we are given a successor s_u ∈ [N] , interpreted as naming the successor node of u , and which we can think of as being encoded by a string of k bits. The goal of the search problem is to output any of the following 1 if s_1 = 1 hfill (inactive distinguished source) u ≠ 1 , if s_u < u , hfill (decreasing successor) u , if u is active and s_u is a proper sink. hfill (proper sink)

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:unsat-cnf
statement_text: Let F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ C_2 ∧ ... ∧ C_m be a CNF formula. The formula UNSAT _F(x_1, ... , x_n, z_1, ... , z_m) is defined to be \[ UNSAT _F(x, z) := ( vee_ i=1 ^m z_i ) ∧ wedge_ i=1 ^m ( ¬ z_i ∨ ¬ C_i).\] If F = { F_i }_i is a sequence of unsatisfiable CNF formulas, then let UNSAT _ F = { UNSAT _ F_i }_i be the corresponding sequence of formulas.

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: If F is a polynomial-time uniform sequence of unsatisfiable CNF formulas, then UNSAT _ F , interpreted as a total search problem, is in FP .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:non-uniform mapping reduction
statement_text: Let R ∈ TFNP and let F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ ... ∧ C_m be an unsatisfiable CNF formula. Let ell (n) denote the polynomial upper bound on the length of any solution to R on inputs of length n . A non-uniform mapping reduction from Search _F to R is given by two circuits C : {0,1}^n → {0,1}^s, D : { 0,1 } ^n × { 0,1 } ^ ell (s) → { 0,1 } ^m , such that R(C(x), y) ⇒ UNSAT _F(x, D(x, y)).

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: Let n, m be positive integers, let R ∈ TFNP , and let F(x_1, ... , x_n) = wedge _ i=1 ^m C_i be a CNF formula. Let ell be a polynomial bound on the certificate length of R . If R ∈ TFNP and F(x_1, ... , x_n) = wedge _ i=1 ^m C_i , then Reduction _ R, n, m, S, s (C, D, F) is the boolean formula defined as follows. We introduce several helper formulas which can easily be represented in CNF. isCkt _S(C) is satisfied iff the variables in C encode a valid boolean circuit with S gates. Eval _ n, S, s (C, x, t) is satisfied iff C encodes a boolean circuit with n inputs, S gates, and s outputs, and t ∈ { 0,1 } ^s is the output of C on input x ∈ { 0,1 } ^n . Then Reduction _ R, n, m, S, s (C, D, F):= \[ isCkt (C) ∧ isCkt (D) ∧ Eval (C, x, x') ∧ Eval (D, (x, y), z) ∧ Eval (V_R, x', y) → UNSAT _F(x, z).\] For readability, we have omitted parameter subscripts above, and we will continue to do so when those parameters are clear from context. The circuit C has n inputs, S gates, and s outputs, and the circuit D has n+ell (s) inputs, S gates, and m outputs.

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:ef-mapping-r

For any unsatisfiable CNF formula F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ ... ∧ C_m , a refutation of F in le EF, R rangle is given by an EF -provable reduction from Search _F to R . Formally, such a reduction is a tuple (C, D, Π) , where (C, D) are circuits computing a non-uniform mapping reduction from Search _F to R , and Π is an Extended Frege proof of a boolean formula Reduction _R(C, D, F) .

statement_text: If R ∈ TFNP , then we say R is EF -provably inside of FP if for every input length n , there is a polynomial-size circuit A and a polynomial-size Extended Frege proof of the formula Eval (A, x, y) ∧ Eval (V_R, (x, y), b) ∧ b , where V_R is understood to encode the polynomial-time verifier for the relation R .

statement_text: The class Σ^q_0 = Π^q_0 consists of all (quantifer-free) propositional formulas. The class of Σ^q_1 formulas are of the form ∃ x_1, ... ,x_n A(x_1, ... ,x_n,y) where A(x,y) ∈ Σ^q_0 , and y=y_1, ... ,y_m .

Then \[G_1 vdash ∃ i (llbracket i = 1 rrbracket ∨ ... ∨ llbracket i = m rrbracket ) ∧ ( (llbracket i = 1 rrbracket → ¬ C_1) ∧ ... ∧ ( llbracket i = m rrbracket → ¬ C_m) ).\] This is the quantified version of the UNSAT _F formula of Definition Cref def:unsat-cnf , and it is near identical to the first-order formula UNSAT _F used to define Reduction _iter . statement_text: WrongProof _P:= { WrongProof _ P,n,m,s }_ n,m,s is the false clause search problem associated with the unsatisfiable formula ¬ Refl _P , which asserts that a formula has both a P -proof and a falsifying assignment. Formally, WrongProof _ P,n,m,s (x,z) :&= UNSAT _ ¬ Refl _ P,n,m,s (x,z) &= UNSAT _ Proof _ P,n,m,s (x,z_1) ∨ UNSAT _ ¬ SAT _ n,m (x,z_2), Recalling that we use a one-hot encoding in UNSAT , z_1 are the bits that represent the clauses of Proof , while z_2 are those belonging to SAT . As well, x=(α,F,Π) is a tuple encoding an assignment, a formula (claimed to be a tautology), and a proof Π . Recall from Cref def:unsat-cnf that this is a problem in TFNP .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:pk
title: Gentzen's PK: Propositional Calculus
statement_text: Let all formulas be propositional and under the DeMorgan basis. A PK proof uses the following rules. \[ l l (Ax) inferrule *[right=Ax] A → A & (Cut) inferrule *[right=Cut] Γ → A Δ, A → B Γ, Δ → B (WL) inferrule *[right=WL] Γ → A Γ, B → A & (WR) inferrule *[right=WR] Γ → A Γ → A, B (CL) inferrule *[right=CL] Γ, A, A → B Γ, A → B & (CR) inferrule *[right=CR] Γ → A, A Γ → A (EL) inferrule *[right=EL] Γ, A, B, Δ → C Γ, B, A, Δ → C & (ER) inferrule *[right=ER] Γ → A, B, Δ Γ → B, A, Δ (neg L) inferrule *[right=neg L] Γ → A, Δ Γ, ¬ A → Δ & (neg R) inferrule *[right=neg R] Γ, A → Δ Γ → ¬ A, Δ (and L) inferrule *[right=and L] Γ, A, B → Δ Γ, A wedge B → Δ & (and R) inferrule *[right=and R] Γ → A, Δ Γ → B, Δ Γ → A wedge B, Δ (or L) inferrule *[right=or L] Γ, A → Δ Γ, B → Δ Γ, A vee B → Δ & (or R) inferrule *[right=or R] Γ → A, B, Δ Γ → A vee B, Δ \]

statement_text: Let F be a PK -derivation from initial formulas F_1, ... ,F_k over variables p_i . Let e be a variable not among the p_i variables of F . An extension rule is the inference, → e ↔ A , for A a formula over variables p_i . We say that e is an extension variable .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
label: def:G
title: G and G_i Subsystems
statement_text: We adapt Frege to allow quantified formulas introduced by the following rules: \[ l l ( ∀ -left ) inferrule * A(B), Γ → Δ ∀ x A(x), Γ → Δ & ( ∀ -right ) inferrule * Γ → Δ, A(p) Γ → Δ, ∀ x A(x) ( ∃ -left ) inferrule * A(p), Γ → Δ ∃ x A(x), Γ → Δ & ( ∃ -right ) inferrule * Γ → Δ, A(p) Γ → Δ, ∃ x A(x) \] For the ∀ -right and ∃ -left rules, the variable p is called an eigenvariable and cannot appear in the bottom sequent. The G proof system is simply PK with these additional rules. For i ≥ 0 , G_i is a restriction of G to only allow cuts on (Σ^q_i ∪ Π^q_i ) -formulas. (That is, the cut rule for G_i can only be applied to formulas with at most i alternations of ∀ and ∃ quantifiers.) While the G systems can prove validity of general QBF formulas, it is also interesting to understand their strength with respect to Boolean formulas. Since G (and even G_1 ) has all of EF rules plus additional rules, G can trivially p-simulate EF (with respect to Boolean formulas). And it is known that the tree-like version of G_1 , called G_1^* is p-equivalent to EF. On the other hand, it is unknown whether or not G_1 is stronger than EF (with respect to Boolean formulas), and it is generally conjectured to be more powerful wrt p-simulations.

title: Proofs, Satisfiability, and Reflection Principles
statement_text: For a proof system P (a polynomial-time verifier) and parameters n,m,s , a reflection principle for P is a CNF formula \[ Refl _P:= Proof _P(F,Π, s) ⊃ SAT (F,X), \] where SAT is the VPV -predicate stating that F is a formula satisfied by the truth assignment X . As well, Proof _P is a VPV -predicate which is true iff Π is a P -proof of F . Such a formula can be obtained, for example, by taking the Cook-Reckhow translation of the verifying Turing Machine for P -proofs. Reflection principles establish the soundness of a proof system. The satisfiability predicate and reflection principles may be generalized to quantified boolean formulas in the natural way, by changing the SAT predicate to be SAT _ Σ^q_1 equiv ∃ |W| < |F| SAT (F,X,W) , where values for W are substituted into existentially quantified variables of F . We refer to this reflection as Σ^q_1 -reflection.

statement_text: theorem MainDict Let U be an integer. Let Ω( log log U/ log U) ≤ ε<1/4 be a parameter The constraint on ε may seem strange. statement_text: Let U and V be parameters with log V ≤ O( log U) . label: def:vl_word_RAM
title: Variable-Length Word RAM Model
statement_text: In the variable-length word RAM model with boldmathbf word size w , the memory is a collection of 2^w words. At any point in time, each word is either boldmathbf idle or boldmathbf active . When a word is active, it can store as its boldmathbf content a bit string of length at most w . In unit time, an algorithm in the variable-length word RAM model can perform the following operations: Activate a word and set its content to be empty. Deactivate a word. Write to/Read the content of an active word. When we read an active word, the memory returns the length of its content as well as the content itself. Perform arithmetic or bitwise operations on two w -bit integers. Note that the memory is not responsible for remembering which words are active. If the queried word of some type 1 (resp. 2, 3) operation is currently active (resp. idle), the behaviour of the memory is undefined. We say that a data structure in the variable-length word RAM model is boldmathbf legitimate if it never causes undefined behavior. The boldmathbf space usage of the memory in the variable-length word RAM model with word size w is defined to be (total length of word contents) +C_ retr · log w · (\# of active words) , where C_ retr is a sufficiently large constant. We say that a data structure has boldmathbf address limit M , if it only ever accesses the first M words, regardless of its input.
